Title: An Introduction to Rhetoric and Storytelling
Description:
CONTENT:
The seminar "Introduction to Rhetoric & Storytelling" offers a journey into the one of the oldest sciences and arts, providing a blend of historical context, theoretical frameworks, and practical applications. The seminar's emphasis on group discussions and hands-on exercises ensures that students not only grasp the underlying theories but also acquire the practical skills necessary for effective communication. 
Furthermore, the seminar aims at incorporating an ethical perspective on persuasive communication. In an era where credibility and trust are of paramount importance, both in society and business, this seminar highlights the need of and offers insight into impactful yet responsible communication.

OBJECTIVES:
In this Rhetoric and Storytelling Seminar at students can expect to learn about various aspects of rhetoric and storytelling from both a theoretical and practical perspective. This may include:
1.	Understanding the principles of rhetoric: Students will delve into the classical and modern theories of rhetoric, examining concepts such as ethos, pathos, and logos, as well as rhetorical devices and strategies.
2.	Analyzing narrative structures: Students will explore different narrative structures and techniques used in storytelling across various mediums, including literature, film, and digital media.
3.	Examining cultural and historical contexts: The seminar may involve studying how rhetoric and storytelling have evolved over time and how they are influenced by cultural, social, and political contexts.
4.	Critiquing persuasive communication: Students will learn to critically analyze persuasive communication, including speeches, advertisements, and propaganda, to understand how rhetoric is used to shape beliefs and attitudes.
5.	Exploring storytelling techniques: Through readings, videos, discussions, and assignments, students will explore different persuasive methods and apply them in their own pitch.

The students will gain an overall view of a relevant topic, which enables them to recognize interdisciplinary and intercultural connections. Further they will foster their ability to make presentations, to work in a team, knowledge and experience in project management and, within the scope of the possibilities to marketing and management qualifications.

Title: Analog and Mixed-Signal Circuit Design
Description:
CONTENT:
•  Specifics of semiconductor process technology and devices for the building of integrated circuits
•  Transistor level circuits and the implementation in CMOS technology: amplifier, current and voltage reference, power supply as well as clock generation, regulation and distribution, A / D and D / A converters
•  Non-idealities and their compensation: operating point, frequency response (with feedback), how to optimize for disturbances (parasitic, power supply and common mode rejection, ...) and error sources (variability, noise, ...)

OBJECTIVES:
Upon successful completion of the module, students are able to understand the concepts and structures of transistor level integrated analog and mixed-signal circuit design. They are able to size devices and set operating points of basic circuit functions like operational amplifiers, clocks, references, power supplies and A/D or D/A converters. Students are able to describe basic interaction between circuit specifications and the sizing and structure of the circuit.

Title: Analogelektronik
Description: CONTENT: Diese regulär im Wintersemester für Studierende im Bachelorstudiengang für das Lehramt an beruflichen Schulen angebotene Pflichtlehrveranstaltung wird ergänzt durch Übungen und einem Praktikum im darauffolgenden Sommersemester und bildet ein zweisemestriges Modul. Die Modulveranstaltung "Analogelektronik“ gibt einen Überblick über die grundlegenden Konzepte und Methoden der analogen Schaltungstechnik. Ausgehend vom Atomaufbau werden anhand der elektronischen Bandstruktur die unterschiedlichen Beiträge von elektrischen Ladungsträgern zur Leitfähigkeiten wiederholt. Qualitative und quantitative Berechnungen der Bauteiledimensionierungen in der Schaltungstechnik unter Berücksichtigung anwendungsbezogener Randbedingungen, Fertigungstoleranzen, etc. für die behandelten passiven wie aktiven Bauelemente und Schaltungen werden vorgestellt und durchgeführt. Grundlagen der Elektrotechnik (Überblick zur Wiederholung relevanter Teilgebiete der Lehrveranstaltung „Technische Elektrizitätslehre“) Passive elektronische Bauelemente (R, C, L) ○ Charakterisierung von passiven elektronischen Bauelementen sowie von analogen Schaltungen durch geeignete Kennlinien, Bode-Diagramme, etc. ○ Elektronische Filterschaltungen mit passiven Bauelementen Physikalische Grundlagen der Elektronik ○ Elektronische Bändermodelle und Ladungstransport in Festkörpern für Isolatoren, Halbleiter sowie Metalle ○ Beweglichkeit von Ladungsträgern, Phononen (Gitterschwingungen) und andere Streumechanismen Halbleiterdioden ○ Aufbau, Wirkungsweise, Kennlinien, charakteristische Kenngrößen, Arbeitspunkteinstellungen für Halbleiterdioden ○ Exemplarische Beispiele für Halbleiterdioden (p(i)n-Dioden, Gleichrichterdioden, VariCap, Photodioden, …) ○ Z-Dioden & Spannungsstabilisierung mit Z-Dioden ○ Suppressordioden Transistoren und Grundschaltungen mit Transistoren ○ Aufbau, Wirkungsweise, Kennlinien, charakteristische Kenngrößen, Arbeitspunkteinstellungen, etc. von Bipolar- und Feldeffekttransistoren ○ Gleichsignalverhalten ○ DC-Ersatzschaltbilder ○ Arbeitspunkteinstellungen ○ Leistungshyperbeln ○ Thermische Einflüsse und Stabilität von Bipolartransistoren ○ Gegenkopplungen ○ Transistoren als Schalter und in Kippstufen ○ Kleinsignalverhalten ○ AC-Ersatzschaltbilder ○ Frequenzverhalten ○ Berechnung wichtiger Verstärkerkenngrößen Operationsverstärker (OpAmp) ○ Eigenschaften und Kenngrößen idealer und realer OpAmps ○ Grundschaltungen mit OpAmps ○ Gegenkopplung, Mitkopplung ○ Addierer, Subtrahierer ○ Differenzierer, Integrierer ○ Aktive Filter ○ Schmitt-Trigger OBJECTIVES: Nach dem Vorlesungs- und Übungsteil des Moduls sind die Studierenden in der Lage mit angemessenem fachlichem Niveau, verschiedene Kompetenz- und Anforderungsbereiche in der analogen elektronischen Schaltungstechnik zu planen und zu dimensionieren. Nach der Teilnahme an diesem ersten Teil (Wintersemester) der Modulveranstaltungen sind die Studierenden in der Lage, ○ die grundlegenden Begriffe, Definitionen, mathematischen Methoden, Konzepte und Zusammenhänge zu passiven und aktiven Bauelemente und Schaltungen in der analogen elektronischen Schaltungstechnik zu verstehen und anzuwenden, ○ den Aufbau und die Funktion der wichtigsten elektronischen Bauelemente zu erläutern, ○ die halbleiterphysikalischen Grundlagen elektronischer Bauelemente zu verstehen, ○ Fertigkeiten in der Modellbildung und in der Formulierung mathematisch-elektrotechnischer Ansätze zu den bearbeiteten Themengebieten der analogen elektronischen Bauelemente und Schaltungen anzuwenden, zu lösen bzw. unter Anwendung von vereinfachten Kompaktmodellen und Ersatzschaltbildern zumindest näherungsweise zu lösen ○ wesentliche Kenndaten von elektronischen Bauelementen aus Datenblättern zu verstehen, zu interpretieren und für anwendungsbezogene Schaltungen auszuwählen, ○ grundlegende elektronische Schaltungen mit passiven und aktiven elektronischen Bauelementen zu berechnen und die Bauteile geeignet zu dimensionieren. Die Modulleistung besteht aus zwei schriftlichen Abschlussklausuren, einer praktischen Prüfung und den Studienleistungen (im Laborpraktikum), die regulär jeweils am Ende des zugehörigen Semesters erbracht werden. In den Klausuren soll nachgewiesen werden, dass die in den Lehrveranstaltungen des Moduls behandelten Zusammenhänge verstanden wurden, in begrenzter Zeit Aufgaben gelöst und die Methoden angewandt werden können. Alle Teilprüfungen können Aufgabenstellungen zu allen Themenbereichen des Moduls enthalten. Erlaubte Hilfsmittel: Mit Ausnahme eines nicht programmierbaren Taschenrechners (keine Grafikfunktion, keine komplexen Operationen, kein Abspeichern von Formeln) sind keine Hilfsmittel zugelassen! Für Details relevant ist Modulbeschreibung zur Lehrveranstaltung.

Title: Analyse ökologischer Daten - Einführung in multivariate Verfahren
Description:
CONTENT:
Block course:
Thematically, the module course is particularly suitable for students who deal with the evaluation of ecological data sets from the fields of vegetation ecology and animal ecology and their interactions with abiotic environmental factors as part of internships, project work and theses (e.g. Bachelor's, Master's and doctoral theses).

Monday (introduction to the tidyverse)
- Handling of the statistical software R with RStudio (packages of the 'tidyverse' such as 'tidyr', 'dplyr', 'stringr', 'forcats', etc.).
- Graphical representation of analysis results with 'ggplot2'
- Short introduction to Open Science
Tuesday (ordinations)
- PCA
- NMDS
- RDA
Wednesday (Functional Diversity)
- Harmonize species names with database
- Selection and download of functional plant traits
- Calculation Community-Weighted Mean (CWM)
- Calculation of Functional Dispersion (FDis)
Thursday (Environment-plant community-trait relationship)
- Statistical analysis of the relationship between species composition and environmental variables
- Statistical analysis of the relationship between environmental variables and functional plant traits using species compositions (CWM regression, Fourth-corner approach)
Friday
- Presentation of the results (= examination)

OBJECTIVES:
After successfully completing this module, students will be able to understand and apply multivariate evaluation methods and the analysis of functional diversity. They have an important basis for scientific work. In addition, students will be able to statistically evaluate their own ecological data sets and interpret the evaluation results.

Title: Analyse- und Arbeitstechniken im Labor
Description:
CONTENT:
Students will learn in 3 separate tests analytical methods and techniques in the laboratory. Students learn under the guidance of academic staff the methodology of statistical experimental design (Design of Experiments. They learn how to determine, the influence of process parameters. Furthermore, the participants learn Raman spectroscopy known as non-destructive analysis method. In addition, the ability to operate a scanning electron microscope (SEM),
a central analyzing tool for surface metrology is developed. The use illustrates the effects of the different imaging methods on different samples reverse engineering of a semiconductor chip). Specifically, the following topics are covered in the tests: Design of Experiments, Raman spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy

OBJECTIVES:
After the successful completion of this module the part6icipants is able to
- Apply the methodology of the "Design of Experiment" to determine the influence of process parameters on an overall process
- To design experiments that are suitable to obtain the desired information
- master orthogonal arrays for industrial troubleshooting
- develop efficient tests
- perform regression analysis to analyze the results and perform process / product improvements
- understand the fundamentals of Raman spectroscopy
- perform Raman analysis on selected samples and analyze (evaluate)Raman signals of carbon nanotubes, diamond, silicon and solvents -
- understand the operation of a scanning electron microscope and operate one
- understand the imaging result as an interaction of the electron with the features of a sample
- use a scanning electron microscope a to analyze samples
Skills: ['Analytical thinking and structured problem solving', 'Statistical experimental design', 'Raman spectroscopy', 'Laboratory techniques']

Title: Analyse und Design zellulärer Netzwerke
Description:
CONTENT:
This lecture is an introduction to the basic principles of "Systems Biology". This discipline analyzes biochemical systems  from an engineering perspective. By analyzing how the structure of a biochemical system relates to its performance in terms of efficiency, reaction times and similar parameters, systems biology aims to explain why cells work the way they do and point thew way towards their modification for industrial and biomedical application. The most relevant techniques covered will be analysis of time hierarchies, sensitivity analysis and feedback loops.

OBJECTIVES:
After completing this module, the student should be able to understand the basic motiffs participating in the regulation of biochemical processes and have the knowledge to perform fundamental analyses such as estimation of time constants, calculation of local and global sensitivities. These tools can be used to suggest modifications in biotechnological applications.

Title: Analyse und Interpretation von Geoinformationen in der Erdbeobachtung
Description:
CONTENT:
The course introduces the concept of the Earth as an integrated system and the role of Earth observation in monitoring dynamic processes in the geo-, hydro-, bio-, and anthroposphere. Students learn the fundamentals of spatial, spectral, and temporal resolution, and are introduced to multiple types of remote sensing techniques. Key focus areas include the interpretation of satellite imagery, application examples such as flood monitoring and urban development, and exploration of open-access Earth observation data sources.

Topics include:
- Introduction to the Earth system and its spheres
- Remote sensing principles (resolution, spectral characteristics)
- Case studies in environmental monitoring
- Data access platforms and tools (e.g., Google Earth Engine)
- Basics of literature research and scientific reading in EO

OBJECTIVES:
After participating in the module, students will be able to:
- Understand the principles of various remote sensing techniques and explain their applications.
- Interpret and analyze remote sensing imagery and derived data.
- Identify appropriate Earth observation datasets for environmental or geographical monitoring.
- Apply remote sensing knowledge to real-world problems and case studies.
- Navigate and utilize remote sensing data platforms and tools for scientific investigation.
Skills: ['GIS software', 'Earth observation', 'Remote sensing', 'Spatial resolution', 'Spectral resolution', 'Temporal resolution']

Title: Analysis of Epigenomic Data
Description:
CONTENT:
Epigenetic modifications, such as DNA methylation or histone modifications, have a central role in the regulation of gene expression and in the preservation of genome integrity. Next Generation Sequencing (NGS) technologies now allow us to measure the genome-wide patterns of various epigenetic modifications at unprecedented resolution. These technologies have opened up novel research avenues in basic and applied plant biology, including studies of development, stress response and natural variation.                                                                                                                                           In the framework of this practical course students will work under close supervision on current research topics in plant epigenetics and epigenomics. Students will be aquainted with high-throughput sequencing technologies, data files, various software packages, and low level programming tasks. Students will aquire insights into the broader research topic through personal studies of relevant literature.

OBJECTIVES:
This practical course will enable students to work independently on realistic research questions in the field of plant epigenetics and epigenomics.                                                                                                                   Upon successful completion of this module students will be able to:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                1) Distunguish mainstream measurement approaches such as chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by sequencing (ChIP-seq) and whole genome bisulphite sequencing (WGBS-seq)                                                2) understand the structure of the data files produced by sequencing machines                                                3) apply a number of software tools for analyzing ChIP-seq and WGBS-seq data                                              4) interpret the output from the data analysis                                                                                                       5) query the results to answer specific biological questions

Title: Analysis of High-Throughput Datasets for Biologists
Description:
CONTENT:
Lectures will give insight into how biological knowledge can be generated from modern omic technologies (transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic) and illustrate different ways of analyzing such data.
Practicals will consist of 1) how to use many freely available computing tools to work more powerfully and effectively 2) computer exercises that will enable the participants to apply statistical methods to the analysis of large scale biological data 3) gain knowledge on how to utilize existing biological databases in their research.

OBJECTIVES:
Scientists find themselves facing exponentially larger data sets and analyses without suitable tools to deal with them. Many biologists end up using spreadsheet programs for most of their data-processing tasks and spend hours clicking around or copying and pasting, and then repeating the process for other data files.
The aim of this course is to familiarize students with advanced data analysis methodologies and provide hands-on training on the latest available tools for the analysis of high throughput data sets. It will provide biologists with basic knowledge on what information can be found and where, as well as how can the information be
accessed/retrieved. A variety of examples of use, which a user might require for a research, will be presented.
===

Module 1: Introduction to Python and basic data exploration
-Simple manipulations; numbers and vectors

Title: Analytic methods applied agricultural systems data
Description:
CONTENT:
The Analytic methods applied to agricultural systems data module (accompanying the block module Data Science for agricultural systems) focuses on theoretical and practical aspects of data science in the context of agricultural and livestock systems, particularly with respect to environmental and productivity analyses. In particular, two types of data form the main foci: field experiments and surveys of agricultural enterprises & ;farms derived from interviews with agricultural workers (farmers). The emphasis is on the applied, analytical, and exploratory aspects of data science; underlying statistical concepts are only briefly summarized. Material is heavily-dependent on applications and exercises performed in R software, and include: basic data exploration and summation, estimation and testing of statistical models (e.g. simple regressions, treatment effects), factor analysis (e.g. using principal components analysis) and clustering. Basic GIS concepts will similarly be taught (using QGIS), including applications for how GIS can inform and complement the analysis of data using R software.  Students will apply their knowledge through ungraded interactive seminars and a project report and presentation worth 100% of the final grade (50% written report, 25% R scripts, 25% presentation). The report is based on a dataset chosen by students involving analysis performed in R and (optionally) GIS. The datasets will be provided by the lecturers.

OBJECTIVES:
Upon successful completion of this module, the students are able to:

•	Understand key concepts involved in the design of field or survey experiments pertinent to given research objective(s)
•	Understand and apply statistical methods for experimental and survey data analysis appropriate to a  research objective(s)
•	Discern appropriate analytical methods to answer questions related to experimental research
•	Develop algorithms (R code) to analyse data and apply GIS tools to analyse field experiments and survey data
•	Generate original research findings from existing datasets,
•	Communicate findings through a project report, with accompanying presentation and supplementary data and script files

Title: Analytics in Manufacturing
Description:
CONTENT:
The module overviews key advanced analytics techniques, relevant for manufacturing applications and beyond (e.g., disaster relief, logistics). The course puts especial emphasis on solving complex managerial decision-making problems that heavily rely on data. Additionally, the module discusses the ethical dimension of using methods of data analytics for managerial decision-making. The module is structured as follows:
• Introduction to linear programming.
• Simplex method, duality theory.
• Introduction to integer programming: Modeling, time-space networks, min-cost flow problems, enumeration techniques (branching, bounding, cutting).
• Relaxations and decompositions (Lagrange relaxation, column generation, Benders decomposition, logic-based Benders decomposition).
• Overview of AI-based combinatorial heuristics.
• Introduction to quantum computing

OBJECTIVES:
The course aims to equip managers with an in-depth undestanding of advanced analytics methods to solve challenging, data-driven decision-making problems. They will be able to meaningfully complex decompose problems into subproblems, setup feedback loops to ensure that the algorithmic solution converges to optimality; they learn how to control for optimality gaps. They will be able to design algorithms that can handle uncertainty and dynamically incoming information.

Title: Angewandte Philosophie und Umweltethik für Naturschutz, Landschafts- und Umweltplanung
Description:
CONTENT:
On the basis of varying timely topics, the seminar provides an introduction into the foundations of environmental aesthetics, environmental ethics, and the philosophy of science/ecology. Major topics are, e.g.: Which colloquial and scientific perceptions and ideas of nature exist? Which values are connected to these various ideas? Which methods are adequate to capture these values?

Topic in winter 2020/21: 
Conflict analysis and evaluation im biological conservation: philosophical issues

Conservation conflicts are not conflicts between humans and nature, but between different humans with different interests, values, and concepts of nature. The seminar asks how such conflicts can be analysed and how different alternatives in dealing with nature may be evaluated. This does in our case not relate to more technical methods and procedures such as landscape assessment methods or other methods of "classical" conservation indices (e.g. rarity), but to philosophical, fundamental questions that arise in the analysis of conservation conflicts. These questions are in part are of an ethical nature, but also involve those about which – often implicit – images or visions of nature exist (and which effects they have), or by which approaches we can assess and understand specific conservation conflicts in their very complexity. Next to some basics about value categories and the analysis of argumentations in a conservation context the focus will be on three methodological approaches:  the popular ecosystem services approach, an approach on the evaluation of conflicts from the perspective of environmental ethics, and the less well-known approach of societal relationships with nature, which attempts to capture the complexity of dealing with nature beyond a methodology focusing only on interest and values. The different approaches for the analysis of conservation conflicts (and partly towards their solution) will be illustrated by case studies.

A  course of lectures on „Philosophy of Science and Environmental Ethics“ (T. Heger) will complement the seminar (also 2 SWH, see seperate announcement)

OBJECTIVES:
After participating in the courses of the module, students will be able to understand different approaches of environmental ethics and to apply them to current subjects of landscape planning and biological conservation. They will be able to understand basic concepts of the philosophy of science and of the meta-theory of ecology (such as the differences between normative and descriptive, and between scientifically-causal and  aesthetically-moral). They will be able to critically evaluate professional publications and contribute substantially to professional discussions. They also will have the skills to apply different methods of text analysis. Their skills to write scientific texts of different forms will have improved as well as those to conduction scientific discussions.

Title: Angewandte Simulation und Modellbildung in der Fertigungstechnik
Description:
CONTENT:
The aim of the course "Virtual Process Design (Focus: Metal Forming and Casting)" is to present the most important concepts of virtual methods and simulation in the design of industrial manufacturing processes,  with particular regard to the fields of metal forming and casting. 

In the first part of the lecture, the fundamentals, motivation and history of simulation are reviewed in detail. In particular, the basics of the finite element method (FEM) are addressed along with the definition of the constitutive law and the failure behaviour of metals. In addition, an overview of material characterization methods for metal forming, cutting and casting is presented.

The second part of the lecture deals with the application of the presented virtual methods to typical industrial problems. The workflow of the forming, cutting and casting simulation are presented and different industrial standard tools are shown. 

The course is completed by some exercise sessions and guest lectures from simulation experts from the industry.

OBJECTIVES:
After attending the course, students get an overview of important simulation tools and virtual methods used in the industry in the fields of metal forming, cutting and casting. They develop an understanding of characterization methods and are able to select the most suitable ones for depending on the application. Furthermore, they are able to assess the suitability of virtual simulation tools and methods with respect to industrial applications as well as to plan the design of a forming process.

Title: Angewandte Statistik
Description:
CONTENT:
The Applied Statistics module imparts knowledge of central statistical methods for analyzing multi-factorial experimental designs as well as the preparation, presentation and interpretation of associated characteristic values. The course focuses on the multi-factorial analysis of variance with or without repeated measures as well as multiple regression and its application within the framework of the general linear model. Factor analysis methods are used for the explorative processing of multivariate data sets. As an alternative to classical hypothesis testing, an introduction to Bayesian statistical inference is given. Statistical analysis is demonstrated using R and RStudio. In parallel to the statistical methods, important aspects of experimental design are covered.

OBJECTIVES:
After participating in the module course, students are familiar with central statistical procedures for the evaluation of multi-factorial experimental designs and are able to

• ... apply multi-factorial methods (multi-factorial ANOVA with and without repeated measures, multiple regression) to new data sets.
• ... interpret the associated results.
• ... assess the suitability of a method for testing a specific question.
• ... trace relationships in multivariate data sets back to underlying constructs using exploratory factor analysis.
• ... understand the differences between classical hypothesis tests and the Bayesian statistics approach.

In addition, students can formulate their own questions with several independent variables in an implementation-oriented manner, plan the implementation in concrete terms, select suitable methods for exploration and statistical evaluation, carry out the data collection independently, and prepare, present, and discuss the results adequately.

Title: Angewandte Systembiotechnologie
Description:
CONTENT:
The module takes the form of practical work (laboratory work). This includes the practical design of the experiment, including preparation of the reactor, cultivation of bacteria, independent sampling, and final cleaning. A script, containing essential information, is provided for data evaluation and mathematical modelling. The internship is carried out as a block internship over several days. The students are given the task of cultivating a modified bacterial strain (with two gene constructs that lead to different fluorescence) in an experiment with a 1-liter bioreactor, collecting data and integrating them into a mathematical model.
In the first half of the internship, a bio-reactor run is started and samples are taken and evaluated. Since the gene constructs result in fluorescence, the amount of the two proteins can be easily estimated. Further learning content of the practical work is sterile work, as well as analytical methods for the determination of sugar and alcohols. The data should then be used for a simple mathematical model, which takes place in the second half of the internship. The metabolic model is set up and analyzed in a Matlab environment using the COBRA toolbox (constrained based reconstruction and analysis). The model combines the data with a mechanistic representation of the processes taking place in the cell and enables a quantitative description of the processes. The focus is on the description of the intracellular metabolic flux when, at the same time, the bacteria starts synthesizing the heterologous protein. On the one hand, the students should be able to learn and apply the role of the FBA (flux balance analysis) and also take into account information about the cellular resource distribution via the two fluorescence markers. In this way, they learn to cultivate bacteria/microorganisms on a laboratory scale, to quantitatively record metabolic performance by measuring substrate, product and biomass processes and to combine the data with a stoichiometric model.

OBJECTIVES:
After participating in this internship, the students are able to cultivate bacteria/microorganisms on a laboratory scale, to quantitatively record the metabolic performance by measuring substrate, product and biomass processes and to combine the data with a stoichiometric model.

Title: Annäherungen an die Konservierung von ARCHITEKTUROBERFLÄCHE
Description:
CONTENT:
The aim is to provide a historical overview of the development of the concept and the practice of designing and maintaining "architectural surfaces". The current state of the art will be defined and sustainable future perspectives for the practice of old buildings will be described. An overview of historical conservation methods for architectural surfaces using the example of the removal and transfer of wall painting as a conservation method represents the starting point for a discussion about the values and compatibility of "traditional" and "industrial" (building) materials and their processing techniques and ageing behaviour. Subsequently, practical questions of care and repair as well as conservation and reconstruction will be discussed. Preventive conservation strategies, monitoring and adapted methods of documentation are understood as a contribution and integral part of the discussion on sustainability in building practice. On-site lectures in the Munich area complement the format.

OBJECTIVES:
After completing the module, students will be able to

Title: Antennas for Space and Aeronautics Applications
Description:
CONTENT:
Part I: Space
- Fundamentals of outer space
- Requirements, challenges and applications of antennas in space
- Antennas for space exploration
- Antennas for GEO and focus on multibeam antennas: adaption of reflector antennas for multibeam behaviour
- Antennas for MEO and focus on Global Navigation Satellite Systems: design methods for satellite antennas and ground reference stations
- Antennas for LEO and focus on megaconstellations and cubesat antennas: concepts of beamsteering antennas and design techniques for ground terminal antennas

Part II: Aeronautics
- The world of aeronautics: from jumbo jets to UAVs
- Antennas for Communication Systems: focus on satellite communication and ground communication (VHF/HF/ATC) and concepts of HF antennas integration
- Antennas for Sensor Systems: focus on weather, primary/secondary surveillance radars and radioaltimeters and design techniques of radar arrays
- Antennas for Navigation Systems: focus on satellite navigation, augmentation systems (GBAS/SBAS) and terrestrial navigation (DME/VOR/Loran), with design techniques for airborne antenna installed performance and ground antennas

OBJECTIVES:
At the end of the module, the students know the specific peculiarities of space and aeronautic environments and their impact on antenna systems. They understand the main antenna types used in space and aeronautics for different applications and are able to evaluate the antenna technology most suitable for each application and perform preliminary antenna system dimensioning.

They understand antenna placement issues, can determine trade-offs in antenna systems and are able to remember, understand and apply various antenna parameters to describe and assess the performance of an antenna. Moreover, they are able to develop implementation guidelines for antenna systems for navigation and communication.

Title: Antriebssystemtechnik für Fahrzeuge
Description:
CONTENT:
The drive line system is the heart of every automobile and remains a central element of modern vehicles, even in the context of increasing electrification. The module Systems Engineering for Vehicle Drive Lines covers content on internal combustion engine and electric vehicle drive lines, with an emphasis on the transmission. The module introduces the requirements, core tasks, assemblies and components of vehicle drive lines. The expertise of the following topics are promoted by means of lectures and supplementary practical insights into current development trends in the field of drive line systems engineering:

- Concepts of internal combustion engine drive lines as well as electric powertrains
- Basic design parameters of transmissions
- Transmission systematics, components and assemblies of the automotive drive line
- Hybrid and fully electrified powertrain systems
- Vibrations and noise of the powertrain
- Resource and energy efficiency of the drive line
- Service Life of the drive line

The lecture content is enlarged by exciting presentations by guest speakers from industry.

OBJECTIVES:
After participating in the module, students will be able to...
- ...classify established drive line concepts.
- ...highlight core tasks of a drive line.
- ...characterize transmission systems of internal combustion engine drive lines and electric powertrains.
- ...describe components and assemblies of vehicle transmissions.
- ...describe vibration excitation sources in drive lines and identify transfer paths.
- ...analyze the power loss behavior of different drive lines and evaluate influences on efficiency.
- ...differentiate life-limiting damage types in transmissions and to evaluate the load-bearing capacity of the components.
Skills: ['Vehicle dynamics', 'Powertrain systems', 'Electrification', 'Systems engineering', 'Internal combustion engines', 'Electric vehicles']

Title: Anwendung strömungsmechanischer Berechnungsverfahren in Flugtriebwerken
Description:
CONTENT:
- Review of the basic equations of fluid mechanics.
- Overview of calculation methods used in turbomachinery
- Introduction to S1 and S2 methods
- Methodical basics of blade and annulus geometry generation
- Introduction to 3D CFD methods of multi-stage turbomachinery
- Importance and implementation of turbomachine-relevant meshing aspects and meshing techniques
- Turbomachinery-specific boundary conditions: Wall treatment, non-reflecting edges, rotor-stator interface.
- Turbulence and transition modeling in the context of multistage simulation
- Interdisciplinary CFD aspects: Flutter and forced-response evaluation of blades, heat transfer calculations.
- Frequency domain methods for transient treatment of flow in multi-domain arrangements
- Post-processing of result data from steady-state and time-accurate engine simulations
- Introduction to numerical optimization and probabilistic approaches
- Introduction to Lattice-Boltzmann methods

OBJECTIVES:
Nach der Teilnahme am Modul Anwendung strömungsmechanischer Berechnungsverfahren in Flugtriebwerken haben die Studierenden ein grundlegendes Verständnis für moderne, computergestützte Verfahren zur Strömungssimulation von Flugtriebwerken.

Sie kennen wichtige Aspekte aus der Vorbereitung, der Durchführung und der Auswertung von Finite-Volumen-Verfahren. Zudem werden Turbomaschinen-spezifische Aspekte zur Behandlung von Randbedingungen, zur Turbulenzmodellierung und zu Frequenzbereichsverfahren erläutert. Die Studierenden kennen die vielseitigen Möglichkeiten, aber auch die Grenzen  gängiger CFD-Verfahren. Die Vorlesung vermittelt den Studierenden das notwendige Wissen, um später selbst erfolgreich CFD-Simulationen durchführen zu können. Darüber hinaus beherrschen die Studierenden die mathematischen Grundlagen der Strömungsmechanik.

Title: Applied Citizen Participation
Description:
CONTENT:
1. Introduction to Participation and the Seminar Challenges:
The first module serves as an interactive introduction to the topic and is based on the questions: What is public participation? Why is it important in urban and mobility planning? Why is interdisciplinary and cross-stakeholder mobility planning important? Subsequently, real life problems relating to participation and mobility in the Munich metropolitan region will be analyzed. These form the basis for the following seminar components.

2. Facilitation of Transformative Participation Processes:
The aim of this module is to provide answers to the question: "What transformative process design do participation processes need in order to make the mobility transition culturally sustainable?" and "What methods and building blocks enable successful participation?". Here, students acquire knowledge about methods and building blocks for successful participation from participation experts. In addition, answers to the question "How can the success of participation be made measurable?" are developed.

3. Taking on the Challenge: Participation Strategy Development
Throughout the week, students work on a participation strategy to tackle their real-life challenge. The expert sessions, mentoring from lecturers (from the Chair of Urban Structure and Transport Planning), and peer learning are key elements of this process.

4. Presentation of the Participation Strategy & Concluding Session
On the last day of the block seminar, the student groups present their solutions to the real-life challenge in front of an expert audience (scientists, participation experts, challenge providers).
Finally, a discussion and lessons learned session will be held to conclude the block seminar.

OBJECTIVES:
After participating in the project week, students will be able to
- Understand different forms of participation
- Analyze different levels of participation
- Evaluate participation methods and processes
- Give scientific presentations to communicate the results of their research
- Develop their own participation methods and processes
- Develop solutions for a Mobility Participation Challenge in interdisciplinary teams
- Flexibly solve unforeseen problem situations in interdisciplinary teams
- Continuously reflect on the methods they have learned with regard to sustainable development

Title: Applied Data Analytics and Machine Learning in Python
Description:
CONTENT:
The practical course "Applied Data Analytics and Machine Learning in Python" aims to impart basic skills and abilities in the application-oriented handling of machine learning methods, data mining and Python programming. For this purpose, basic Python knowledge of syntax and common Python frameworks from data analysis and machine learning will be taught or refreshed firstly. It is followed by an introduction to the basic concepts, methods, and algorithms of machine learning and modeling. The acquired background knowledge is then transferred to application-oriented problems from control engineering, process control and quality monitoring by conceptualizing, modeling and implementing solutions for various complex use cases.

OBJECTIVES:
After participating in the practical course, students will be able to
•	understand the basic theoretical principles of machine learning, specifically reinforcement learning and unsupervised learning, from an application-oriented perspective. 
•	use Python and common Python frameworks for data analysis and machine learning, and to design and implement suitable pipelines for data analysis independently. Students will learn to read and understand Python-specific online documentation on open source code, analyze the code behind it, and apply common Python frameworks (e.g., Tensorflow, Keras, scikit-learn). Computational thinking will be strengthened. 
•	understand complex control problems, Big Data, and Machine Learning problems in an appropriate representation form (flowchart, state diagrams) and implement them in Py-thon.
•	model and develop a control task for an automation system as a reinforcement learning task for a given problem. 
•	assess and critically evaluate the use, effort, and challenges of reinforcement learning for decision making and optimization of automation engineering tasks.

Title: Applied Regression Analysis
Description:
CONTENT:
The course will be taught using a lecture and seminar style. Students will each work on their datasets based on regression methods discussed in class.

OBJECTIVES:
After successful completion of this course, students will have learned important methods used in the regression analysis of data. They will understand basic concepts of the linear regression model and its properties and understand, explain and critically reflect on selected advanced topics such as the analysis of non-linear data, duration data, panel data, and multilevel analysis, and have gained the ability to discuss and elaborate on methods to deal with the problems of endogeneity and sample selection. Students will have built a basic understanding of the theoretical basis of these methods, but the focus of the course is on the application of the methods to data sets.

Title: Applied Regression
Description:
CONTENT:
Applied regression studies the fundamentals of models of association of randomly observed outcomes and fixed covariates for the purpose of inference and prediction. Contextual data scientific applications emphasize potential pitfalls and solutions or preventive measures to the pitfalls. Specific inferential models include Normal linear and nonlinear regression for continuous outcomes, logistic regression for binary outcomes and Poisson regression for count outcomes and rates. Real world data applications typically encounter missing data, and hence the course includes definitions and solutions for handling this problem, including imputation. Machine learning models are large data generatlizations of regression models that do not make modeling assumptions and focus primarily on classification or prediction. These models are covered at the end of the course.

OBJECTIVES:
Upon successful completion of the course, students will be able to solve real-world applications by identifying the appropriate regression modeling strategy; diagnose problems in regression analyses, including assumption failures and outlier detection; program and effectively visualize data in the R statistical package.

Title: Applied Strategy and Organization
Description:
CONTENT:
Professor Dr. Axel Stepken is the Chairman of the Board of Management of TÜV SÜD AG. The focus of his lecture is on understanding the necessary prerequisites and measures for the successful implementation of an internationalization strategy and transformation in the context of digitalization.

Relevant market-driven growth drivers, corporate strategies, corporate culture, concepts of complex organizations and leadership, as well as the impact of digitalization on business models, work-life balance, talent acquisition, knowledge management, organizational structure, and IT landscape will be discussed.

Professor Dr. Stepken will openly share his professional experiences with strategic and organizational challenges and present digitalization and its effects on international business activities.

Through independent study of academic literature, students will additionally acquire foundational knowledge in strategy planning and implementation on their own.

OBJECTIVES:
Participants are able to assess the key aspects and challenges for the successful implementation of internationalization strategies in the context of digitalization. These include organizational development, corporate culture, customer orientation, and knowledge management with a particular focus on digital transformation, as well as disruptive business models and the impact on work-life balance and the IT landscape.

8)	to apply principles of study planning and conduct to their own research question
9)	to develop a study design (including literature review / analysis / ethics)

Die aktive Mitarbeit der Studierenden wird erwartet und gefördert.

The course will introduce the different material classes’ keys for understanding and conserving architectural surfaces. Furthermore, the methodologies and strategies behind their scientific study will be define. The students will acquaint themselves with the chemistry of historical materials, from binding media (inorganic and organic) to fillers/additives and colourants, their degradation paths, and the state-of-the-art technologies currently used to document, monitor and characterize them. The influence of climate conditions on historical materials and the concept of preventive conservation will be explained. Sustainable technical and cultural strategies for the preservation of complex historical objects/surfaces require an integrative approach that combines science-based investigation (documentation, research, analysis, and evaluation) with architectural planning. To be able to work together on interdisciplinary basis an effort to understand and be familiar with other complementary disciplines should be done. Thus, the Heritage science discipline and the role of the different professional figures involved in cultural heritage studies will be defined.

OBJECTIVES:
-	After successfully completing module, students are able
-	to understand why it is so important to conserve our cultural heritage.

-	to understand the meaning and importance of an interdisciplinary approach in cultural heritage studies.

-	to name materials of historical and artistic interest.

-	to name the physicochemical behaviour of historical materials and describe their degradation path.

-	to understand the influence of the microclimate conditions on historical materials and define the concept of preventive conservation.

-	to name state-of-the-art technology currently applied and developed for cultural heritage studies.

-	to understand the analytical challenges and boundaries conditions in studying valuable and highly heterogeneous objects/surfaces.
Skills: ['Material science', 'Chemistry', 'Analytical thinking and structured problem solving', 'Research-oriented mindset']

Title: Architektur- und Designtheorie
Description:
CONTENT:
Exhibitions have internationally influenced the development of architecture since the beginning of the 20th century. Due to their public nature they are an effective form to convey ideas and concepts to a broad public and to change the general perception of architecture. Ranging from the Werkbund exhibition in Cologne to the current Architecture Biennale in Venice, the lecture intends to provide a survey of important milestones of architectural history by means of specific examples, focusing on exhibitions that have taken a direct position towards current questions. They will deal with building exhibitions as well as architectural exhibitions, with some formats complementing each other. Central questions are directed at the concept, implementation, design, conveyance, criticism and the consequences of these exhibitions. An additional aspect of examination is the possible exploitation of architectural exhibitions for propaganda purposes. The lecture aims at gaining an understanding of the complex theory and practice of architectural exhibitions as a specific design task by means of comparing analyses.

OBJECTIVES:
Participants learn to critically deal with complex issues with their own observation and on the basis of literature, and to discuss them during a presentation. Thus they learn to phrase their own theses, practice structured argumentation and to defend the positions they have developed in front of a larger public. Students will also be taught how to edit texts and the proceedings of visual presentation, in order to qualify for independent scientific work.

Title: Architekturmuseum
Description:
CONTENT:
After seizing power in January 1933, the National Socialists destroyed democracy within a few months. On the basis of the law for the "restoration of the professional civil service" of April 7, 1933, so-called non-Aryans and political enemies were dismissed. The newly founded Reich Chamber of Culture did not accept Jewish architects and architects who did not comply with the Nazi ideology; this was effectively tantamount to a professional ban. Professional associations such as the Association of German Architects (BDA) were "brought into line". As a result, around 500,000 people fled Germany, Austria and parts of Czechoslovakia during the rule of the Nazi system. Nearby Switzerland was one of the first destinations for refugees. The "neutral" country had already repeatedly granted asylum to politically persecuted people in the past, for example Georg Büchner, Gottfried Semper, August Bebel, and Vladimir Ilyich Lenin. Other centers of emigration were England, Sweden, Turkey, and China.

The seminar will investigate the fates of architects and artists who had to emigrate, and will examine the extent to which exile influenced their work. The seminar will conclude with a review and outlook on current migration movements caused by climate change, violence, and war. An excursion to Zurich to the former places of exile is planned.

OBJECTIVES:
After successful participation in the module, students are able to explain and assess architectural-historical contexts.

Title: Architekturvermittlung (Architecture and the Making of Modern Iran
Description:
CONTENT:
In the 20th century, architecture played a central role in defining national identity, driving modernization, and shaping cultural transformation. In Iran, particularly during the Pahlavi era (1925–1979), architecture was not merely about constructing buildings; it served as a platform for reimagining the nation’s past and envisioning its future. This course examines the role of architecture in shaping modern Iran during this period, focusing on both prominent Iranian architects and international figures such as Alvar Aalto, Louis Kahn, Kenzo Tange, and Hans Hollein. It explores how their work, through state commissions, cultural projects, and urban development plans, reflected Iran’s ambitions to modernize, celebrate its heritage, and engage with global architectural networks.

The course will reference architecture in different visual media: architectural drawings and models, paintings and visual art, literature and texts, videos and movies, photography and music. Students will develop analytical skills and the ability to describe and critique architecture through different media.

Title: Ausgestattet mit Ausstrahlung - Mein Standing. Meine Stimme. Mein Auftritt - für Frauen
Description:
CONTENT:
Sprechen ist mehr als schlaue Worte, es ist meine Stimmmelodie und meine Aussprache, es ist mein ganzes Auftreten. Schneller und direkter erlebbar wird dies bei Videomeetings oder wenn wir uns selber hören. Entscheidend ist dabei oft nicht das, was ich sage, sondern das Wie. Denn ich habe eine ganz bestimmte Vorstellung, wie ich wirken will auf mein Publikum. Doch wie geht das, dass ich damit im Augenblick und auch im Nachhinein damit einverstanden bin? 

Der Workshop wendet sich insbesondere an Frauen. Er möchte sie ermutigen, ihren Standpunkt und ihre Haltung als Frau wahrzunehmen, sich auszuprobieren und zu behaupten. Aber es geht auch darum, Rückmeldungen anderer zu bekommen und mit diesen aktiv zu arbeiten, diese positiv zu nutzen. 
Bei diesem Workshop werden wir nicht NUR ÜBER die Stimme etwas HÖREN, wir werden sie trainieren und mit ihr auf unsere Stimmungen hören. Wir werden Situationen schaffen, bei denen unser Standpunkt gefragt und herausgefordert ist. Spielerisch und ernst werden wir den Tücken und Chancen der nonverbalen und der verbalen Kommunikation auf die Spur kommen, indem wir uns selbst erleben und das Erlebte reflektieren.
Kommunikation beginnt bei meinem Selbst-bewusstsein. Welche Wahrnehmung habe ich für mich und für mein Gegenüber und wie authentisch bin ich in dem was ich tue. Durch Körperübungen bzw. im Videotraining schauen wir nach unseren Bewegungen, Haltungen, Ressourcen und Begabungen. Wir nehmen uns Raum für Stimmübungen und schaffen Situationen für freies und erarbeitetes Sprechen.

OBJECTIVES:
Am Ende dieser 2 Tage kann jede Teilnehmerin eine Portion Selbstbewusstsein für sich in Anspruch nehmen. Sie weiß um ihr Auftreten, ihre Stimmgewaltigkeit und weiß diese für einen Auftritt vorzubereiten. Sie erlebt sich selbst im Videomeeting und weiß gelernte Tricks immer wieder abzurufen. Durch Selbstreflexion und Rückmeldungen aus der Gruppe kann jede immer wieder an sich arbeiten, wenn Persönlichkeit und Auftreten gefragt sind. Das gilt für Videomeetings wie auch bei Präsenzauftritten.

Title: Automaten und formale Sprachen
Description:
CONTENT:
Automata and formal languages are at the heart of all fields of computer 
science. This course recalls, deepens and extends the notions of automata theory 
covered in introductory courses at bachelor level, like transformations between 
different classes of automata, and minimization algorithms.  

The module introduces automata as a data structure for storing and manipulating 
sets and relations. Data structures are characterized by the operations they offer for 
accessing and maintaining data. In the case of automata these are the boolean 
operations, union, intersection and complement, together with important operations 
on relations, like projections and joins. The module presents implementations of 
these operations using deterministic and nondeterministic automata. It then describes 
applications in areas like string matching and automatic verification, for which special 
class of automata are introduced and analyzed. The last part of the module deals 
with automata on infinite words, with applications to the verification of liveness 
properties.

OBJECTIVES:
On successful completion of this course, students will be able to

* apply automata to describe, store, and manipulate finite or infinite sets and relations
* assess whether a given set or relation is representable by automata
* use automata-based algorithms to solve simple problems in areas like 
pattern-matching and verification, selecting the most adequate automata class 
for each problem
* assess the algorithmic complexity of automata algorithms

Title: Automatische Ausführung von Prozessmodellen
Description:
CONTENT:
Prozessmodelle sind eine Möglichkeit, Prozesse zu dokumentieren, zu erfassen, zu kommunizieren und in ausführbare Programme zu übersetzen. Wenn diese Prozesse manuell in Programme übersetzt und ausgeführt werden, kann es zu Abweichungen zwischen der Prozessausführung und dem Prozessmodell kommen. Um das zu vermeiden, können Prozessmodelle so verfeinert werden, dass diese direkt und automatisch übersetzbar und ausführbar sind. Dazu muss das ursprüngliche Prozessmodell erweitert werden, indem der Datenfluss sowie die hinter den Aktivitäten  verborgenen Funktionalitäten genau spezifiziert werden. Anschließend können Instanzen eines Prozessmodells mithilfe einer Prozessengine ausgeführt werden. Dies verhindert Abweichungen zwischen der Prozessausführung und dem modellierten Verhalten.

In diesem Kurs wird zuerst ein Prozessmodell zu einer textuellen Beschreibung erstellt, das danach analysiert und verfeinert wird. Anschließend werden die Funktionalitäten, die hinter den Aktivitäten im Prozessmodell stehen, implementiert. Dann werden aus dem verfeinerten Prozessmodell Instanzen erstellt und unter Verwendung der vorher implementierten Funktionalitäten ausgeführt.

OBJECTIVES:
Verstehen der Unterschiede zwischen ausführbaren Prozessmodellen und Prozessmodellen, die lediglich zur Dokumentation, Erfassung und Kommunikation erstellt werden. Erstellen eines ausführbaren Prozessmodells.
Skills: ['Process modeling', 'Business process management', 'Workflow automation', 'Software development', 'EAI software']

Title: Automatisierungstechnik
Description:
CONTENT:
Das Modul umfasst die Themengebiete Automatisierungstechnik und Regelungstechnik.

Automatisierungstechnik:
- Grundlagen – Automatisierungsebenen (Sensoren, Aktoren, SPS, SCADA)
- Kommunikation (digitale Datenübertragung, Topologien, Zugriffsverfahren, OSI Referenzmodell, IT Security, Standards)
- Fließbilder (Arten, Symbolik, MSR-Schnittstellen)
- SPS Programmierung (Petri-Netze, Binär-/Ablaufsteuerungen, IEC Sprachen)
- Virtuelle Inbetriebnahme (Simulationsmodelle, Verhaltensmodelle, Praxisbeispiel)
- Robotik (Aufbau, Programmierung & Steuerung, Kinematik)
- Übergeordnete Systeme (Prozessleittechnik, Fertigungsmanagement, ERP Software)
- Zukunftstrends (Internet of Things (IoT), Block Chain, Maschinelles Lernen
- Praktische Übung – Programmierung und virtuelle Inbetriebnahme einer „Cocktailmischanlage“ mit batchorientierten, kontinuierlichen und diskreten Modulen

Regelungstechnik:
- Prinzip der Regelung - Beispiele für (nicht-) technische Regelungsaufgaben
- Beschreibung dynamischer Systeme im Zeit- und Frequenzbereich (Systemantwort, Differentialgleichung, Übertragungsfunktion)
- Regelkreis, Beispiele für Regelstrecken und Regler
- Eigenschaften von Regelkreisen(Regelgüte, Stabilität, Führungs- und Störverhalten)
- Entwurf einschleifiger Regelkreise im Frequenzbereich und Zustandsraum
- weitere Regelkreise: Mehrgrößenregelung, modellbasierte Reglung, Fuzzy-Regler, Neuro-Regler
- kurze Einführung in Simulink sowie praktische Übungen zur Systemidentifikation und Reglerauslegung mit Simulink

OBJECTIVES:
Nach der Teilnahme an den Modulveranstaltungen kennen und verstehen die Studierenden die Grundlagen der Prozessautomation und Regelungstechnik. Sie sind in der Lage, für eine gegebene Problemstellung eine Automatisierungslösung zu konzipieren. Grundvoraussetzungen hierzu sind, die geeigneten Komponenten auszuwählen, das System zu analysieren und durch ein geeignetes Modell zu beschreiben. Die Studierenden sind in der Lage, darauf aufbauend das adäquate Konzept zur Projektierung der Steuerung bzw. Regelung auszuwählen und anzuwenden. Neben dieser Fach- und Methodenkompetenz erweitern die Studierenden ihre Selbstkompetenz, da sie nach erfolgreicher Teilnahme am Modul befähigt sind, komplexe Problemstellungen in mathematische Ausdrücke zu überführen. Darüber hinaus sind die Studierenden auch in der Lage, in ihrem Berufsalltag mit Ingenieuren anderer Fachrichtungen (insb. Elektrotechnik, Informatik) kompetent zu kommunizieren.
Skills: ['Automation technology', 'Control systems', 'Sensors and transducers', 'Actuators', 'PLC programming', 'SCADA', 'Industrial communication', 'IT Security']

Title: Autonome Systeme
Description:
CONTENT:
Autonomous systems will cover concepts, principles and algorithms for modern mobile autonomous systems operating in the physical world (e.g., autonomous cars, drones). The lecture will provide knowledge and tools from a broad spectrum of disciplines. Topics will include mathematical foundation, kinematics and dynamics, sensing, state estimation, computer vision, perception, environment representation (SLAM), control and motion planning for mobile systems. Title: Autonomous Drone Racing Project Course
Description:
CONTENT:
In this course, students will work in teams of 2 on an autonomous drone racing project. The project will include algorithm development, software implementation, and real-world robot experiments in the field of robot learning and control.

Students will gain hands-on experience in robot learning and control by developing their own comprehensive hardware/software solution for autonomous drone racing on crazyflie drones. The teams work jointly on the challenge to not only teach robotics problem-solving skills, but also project management and teamwork.

The final mark is composed of:
(1) quality of the software implementation and results of the final robot demonstration (40%)
(2) a written report summarising the results (30%, length of report: up to 3 double-column pages per team member)
(3) a presentation followed by questions and a discussion (30%, length of presentation: 5 minutes per team member).

OBJECTIVES:
Students will learn to independently solve robotics control and learning problems. This includes analysing the problem, developing a project plan, exploring appropriate solutions, and demonstrating the results on real robot hardware. Students will also learn to work efficiently as a team, document their approach, and communicate their results.
Skills: ['Autonomous systems', 'Drone technology', 'Robot learning', 'Control systems', 'Algorithm development', 'Software implementation', 'Python', 'MATLAB']

Title: Basics Sustainability Campus Heilbronn
Description:
CONTENT:
The consistent overstepping of planetary boundaries by humans is the cause of many environmental problems and social tensions regionally, globally and between generations. For sustainable development in the sense of a fair distribution of resources, an interdisciplinary approach to solutions and the consideration of the interrelationships of social, ecological and economic factors and actors are indispensable. The course "Basics Sustainability" teaches the most important sustainability models and analysis methods for sustainable development. From environmental and resource economics, basic methods for a fair distribution of environmental goods as well as environmental policy instruments and tools for sustainable spatial design are presented. With regard to materiality, the goal is the use of renewable raw materials for the production of materials and products, the recycling or pollutant-free landfilling of existing products and materials, and the optimization of natural processes from a material and energy point of view. Against the background of climate change, students learn about current technologies and developments and assess measures in the field of renewable energy systems in the context of grid expansion, energy distribution and storage technologies.

1. General principles of sustainability
1.1 Introduction to sustainability
1.2 Social transformation
1.3 Corporate responsibility
1.4 Sustainability management
1.5 Life cycle assessment
1.6 Education for sustainable development

2. Economic framework for sustainability
2.1 Fundamentals of resource, environmental and public good economics
2.2 Sustainability policy
2.3 Game theory and behavioural economics in the context of sustainability
2.4 Economics of climate change
2.5 Sustainable regional development

3. Materiality and sustainability
3.1 Resource consumption and finiteness
3.2 Primary/secondary biomass and material cycles
3.3 Materials from renewable resources
3.4 Recycling and biorefinery concepts

4. Energy and sustainability
4.1 Introduction to energy and sustainability
4.2 Climate change and greenhouse effect
4.3 Fundamentals of selected technologies
4.4 Future energy systems

OBJECTIVES:
General principles of sustainability: At the end of the module students know about the interrelationships of social, ecological and economic factors and actors and are able to apply basic sustainability models and analysis methods.

Economic framework of sustainability: Students know methods of environmental and resource economics and are able to assess the use of sustainability policy instruments.

Materiality and sustainability: Students understand the material cycles of the earth and the production of materials from renewable raw materials and the recycling and disposal of products.

Energy and sustainability: Students understand the basics of climate change. They know about current technologies and developments and are able to assess measures in the field of regenerative energy systems in the context of grid expansion, energy distribution and storage technologies.

Title: Batteriespeicher
Description:
CONTENT:
The lecture Battery Systems provides basic knowledge of various energy storage technologies. Electrochemical contents are presented in a general manner and across technologies. In particular, present energy storage technologies such as lead-acid batteries or lithium-ion batteries are presented with their characteristics, function and design. The topics are presented in the context of current questions and challenges within applications in the field of electromobility and stationary energy storage systems.

Topics:

- Introduction, terms and definitions
- Introduction to electrochemistry
- Basic thermodynamics (equilibrium conditions)
- Kinetics and overpotentials (voltage under current flow)
- Electrochemical double layer
- Diffusion processes and consecutive reactions
- Cell design
- Primary and secondary systems
- Lead acid batteries
- Lithium batteries in general, lithium-ion batteries in particular
- Post-lithium-ion-batteries (lithium-sulfur and lithium-air)
- Optimization of batteries for diffrent requirements

The institute for electrical energy storage technology offers an excursion as part of the lecture.

OBJECTIVES:
After this lectrue, students should have basic knowledge about electrochemical energy storage technology. This includes electrochemical coherences of thermodynamics, charge and mass transport as well as kinetics. In the focus of current research and development, students will be able to characterize and design different energy storage systems.
Skills: ['Energy storage systems', 'Electrochemical engineering', 'Battery technology', 'Lithium-ion batteries', 'Lead-acid batteries']

Title: Battery Applications
Description:
CONTENT:
Today, batteries are essential in a wide range of applications, from powering portable electronics to electric vehicles and grid-scale energy storage systems. Advancements in battery technology have enabled these applications by increasing the longevity of batteries, as well as reducing their size, weight, and cost. However, despite these remarkable advancements, battery technology remains the limiting factor. To fully harness the potential of this technology, efficient utilization is crucial, allowing us to maximize the benefits of available resources. This requires developing a tailored system design and operational strategy for each specific application.

Within the framework of the lecture, the required methods will be studied and applied in the exercises.
Contents:
- Battery technology
- Portable devices
- Mobility (electric vehicle, boats, railway, planes, space etc.)
- Stationary application

OBJECTIVES:
A comprehensive understanding of battery technology and its various applications.
Upon successful completion of the module, students are able to:
- Evaluate the suitability of different battery technologies for specific applications, such as consumer electronics, electric vehicles, and stationary energy storage.
- Analyze the performance of a battery system, including energy density, power density, cycle life, and safety considerations.
- Design (size, thermal, electric, lifetime) of battery systems for different applications
- Evaluate the cost-effectiveness of different battery system designs and identify strategies for optimizing system performance while minimizing costs.
- Assess the battery systems and their applications in terms of sustainability and social influence.
- Explain the current state of battery technology and discuss emerging research and development trends.
Skills: ['Battery technology', 'Energy storage systems', 'Electric vehicles', 'Portable electronics', 'Grid-scale energy storage']

Title: Baudokumentation
Description:
CONTENT:
Das Modul „Baudokumentation“ erstreckt sich über zwei Semester und besteht aus Teil I „Historisches Bauen“ im WiSe und Teil II im SoSe „Bauaufnahme“.

Der erste Teil des Moduls vermittelt vertieftes Grundwissen zu Einzelthemen des historischen Bauens und Konstruierens, verschiedenen Bauaufnahmetechniken und Methoden der Analyse historischer Bauten so-wie die Fähigkeit zur eigenständigen Analyse und zeichnerische Dokumentation eines historischen architektonischen Einzelelements am gebauten Objekt.

Der zweite Teil des Moduls vermittelt die praktische Anwendung von traditionellen und modernen technik-gestützten Methoden der Bauaufnahme und Baudokumentation einschließlich der selbstständigen Konzep-tion eines objektspezifischen Dokumentations- und Aufmaßprogrammes. In der Arbeit am Objekt werden historische Bauformen und Baukonstruktionen im architektonischen Gesamtzusammenhang erkannt und analysiert sowie verformungsgerechte Planzeichnungen und fotografische und textlichen Dokumentationen eines historischen Bauobjekt erstellt.

OBJECTIVES:
Vertiefte Grundkenntnisse historischer Bauweisen, Grundkenntnisse verschiedener Methoden der Baudokumentation sowie vertiefte Grundkompetenzen zur Erstellung eines verformungsgerechten Handaufmaßes.

Title: Be the Change - Wie Sie Veränderungen anstoßen und ins Tun kommen
Description:
CONTENT:
Course language is German / Kurssprache ist Deutsch 

Welcome to the inspiring Be the Change seminar! In this seminar we will focus on change processes in the context of sustainability. We want to empower you to initiate change processes to make a positive difference in your life and in the world around you. The aim is to provide you with the necessary knowledge about "change" and to guide you to self-reflect on your attitudes and current behaviour in relation to your individual living environment and your own values. Through your own change project, which you will work on for 30 days, you will gain valuable experience and evaluate and reflect on it together with the other participants. The topic of the change project can be chosen freely.

Our aim is to focus on the questions "How can I make a difference?" and "How can I interest and involve others in my project?" and to promote goal-oriented communication between different stakeholders. You will be empowered to create your own plans to achieve your goals and encouraged to be part of the solution to different challenges.

The Be the Change seminar includes the following content modules and methods

Self-reflection and goal-setting:
You learn to identify and reflect on your own needs and goals. You will sharpen your awareness of areas in need of change and create problem awareness.
You will increase your self-efficacy to work positively on change processes. You will learn to overcome obstacles and maintain your inner motivation.
Reflect on your own role in the change process within your personal sphere of influence. You will recognise your influence and become aware of how you can initiate change.

Communicating effectively:
You will learn how to communicate your ideas clearly and logically in order to get others on board with your vision.
You will learn to be sensitive to the needs and perspectives of others and to communicate change effectively.

Sustainability and continuous growth:
Change is not a one-off process, but an ongoing journey. You will learn how to implement sustainable change in your life and how to continue your personal growth. You will be given practical tools and techniques to initiate and successfully implement change.
You will have the opportunity to apply your learning directly to a change project and receive valuable feedback.

OBJECTIVES:
After participating in the seminar "Be the Change," you will be motivated to drive your own change processes. You will be able to:
- Reflect on and analyze your value systems. You will gain a deeper understanding of your personal beliefs and values and be able to consciously use them in your change processes.
- Motivate yourself and others to implement change. You will learn techniques to strengthen your intrinsic motivation and to successfully inspire and motivate others.
- Identify your areas of responsibility in your personal and professional life where you want to create sustainable change. You will identify your areas of influence and work specifically to bring about positive change.
- Analyse your own role as a change agent and apply this to your areas of influence. You will recognize your skills and strengths as a change agent and know how to use them effectively in your personal and professional areas of life.
- Communicate your own concerns in a way that is appropriate to your target group in order to create awareness of problems in others and to stimulate behavioral change. You will learn to convey your messages clearly and convincingly and to win other people over to your visions.
- Examine arguments in discussions for their plausibility, evaluate them and respond to them constructively and goal-oriented. You will improve your ability to analyse rational arguments and to counter them convincingly.
- Know the mechanisms of persuasive argumentation and apply them to your own argumentation. You will learn techniques to make your argumentation powerful and convincing.
- You will get to know different methods and learn how to use them in a targeted way to bring about sustainable change.
- Develop sustainable goals for change processes and implement them. You will learn to formulate clear and measurable goals and to develop strategies to successfully achieve these goals.

Title: Behavioral Economics
Description:
CONTENT:
This course provides a general introduction to behavioural economics and discusses its relevance to applications in a variety of contexts. In this course, the students will first learn the foundations of traditional theories and models of economics. Building on these foundations they will subsequently learn and analyse how behavioral economics moves away from these models, by relaxing traditional assumptions. 
The emphasis of this course is to explain, through state-of-the-art methods of analysis, how people and firms actually behave in practice and be able to explain behaviors that seem at face value ‘irrational’. Specific topics covered in this course include:
1. Behavioral economics overview
2. Principles of experimental economics
3. The standard economic model: consumer theory
4. Reference dependence and departures from the standard model
5. Decisions under risk and uncertainty
6. Intertemporal choice
7. Interaction with others: game theory
8. Behavioral game theory and social preferences
9. Behavioral economics and policy

OBJECTIVES:
By the end of the course, students will be able to better understand decision processes and commonly observed decision biases in a variety of applications, such as in the domain of financial investments, medical decisions and in behaviors related to the environmental economics and to bioeconomy. Moreover, they will be able to understand and design choice architectures supporting (better) decision making.

Title: Behavioral Public Economics
Description:
CONTENT:
In this course combines public economics with recent contributions of behavioral economics. Students will learn how to apply findings from behavioral economics to the public sector. This course will combine standard models from text books with recent academic papers. We will cover classic theories, their behavioral extensions, and empirical studies. Cover topics will be:
- Welfare Analysis
- Taxation
- Public Goods / Externalities
- Political Economy (Politicians and Voting)
- Public Policy (Savings, Poverty, Health, Environment)

OBJECTIVES:
After attending the module, students will understand current topics in Public Economics and know the relevant insight from behavioral economics. Title: Benachteiligung in der beruflichen Bildung
Description:
CONTENT:
Der Schwerpunkt des Seminars "Benachteiligung in der beruflichen Bildung" liegt auf der Sensibilisierung der Studierenden für Problemlagen von Lernenden an beruflichen Schulen, sodass Eingangsvoraussetzungen der Lernenden anhand fundierter Informationen gezielt beurteilt werden können und in der Folge ein effektives Verständnis über individuelle Lernvoraussetzungen entsteht. Die Studierenden sollen für Problemlagen sensibilisiert werden, die auf der Mikro-, Meso- und Makroebene auftreten und den Lernerfolg beeinflussen können. Inhaltlich rekurrieren sich die im Seminar erfassten Problemlagen insbesondere auf den Einfluss der Ressourcenausstattung von Lernenden auf den Lern- bzw. Ausbildungserfolg. Neben der Kenntnis dieser Problemlagen sollen die Studierenden im Seminar ebenfalls dazu befähigt werden, Möglichkeiten zu reflektieren, die einen anforderungsgerechten Umgang mit heterogenen Voraussetzungen der Lernenden ermöglichen. Der gewählte Fokus resultiert insbesondere daraus, dass die Ressourcenausstattung bzw. die soziale Herkunft als zentrale Ursache für die Benachteiligung von Lernenden in beruflichen Lehr-Lernprozessen angesehen werden kann.

OBJECTIVES:
Nach dem Seminar sind die Teilnehmer/-innen erstens in der Lage,…
… Ursachen für Leistungsunterschiede bezüglich sozial heterogener Gruppen zu benennen, Erklärungsansätze zu verstehen und Benachteiligung ebenenübergreifend zu analysieren,
… gesellschaftliche und systembedingte Faktoren, die zur Reproduktion sozialer Ungleichheit führen, zu verstehen und die Effektivität von Handlungsmöglichkeiten auf der Mikro- und Mesoebene zu reflektieren, sowie
… zentrale Komponenten des Lernerfolgs (inkl. Lernbedingungen) auf der Mikroebene zu verstehen und Handlungsoptionen zur Verringerung von Benachteiligung theoriegeleitet zu analysieren und anzuwenden.     

Nach den Seminaren sind die Teilnehmer/-innen zweitens in der Lage,...
... einschlägige Fachinhalte nach wissenschaftlichen Kriterien anhand von Forschungsfragen eigenständig aufzuarbeiten und diese auf bestimmte (Lehr-Lern)Situationen anzuwenden.                                          
...lernförderliche Präsentationen zur Optimierung der Verarbeitungskapazität des Arbeitsgedächtnisses auszuarbeiten, sowie inhaltliche und formale Vorgehensweisen unter Berücksichtigung aktueller kognitionspsychologischer Modellvorstellungen zu begründen.
