Es könne verschieden Beratungsansätze sowie die aktuellen und zukünftigen Aufgabenfelder von beruflicher Beratung in Gesundheit und Pflege wiedergegeben und eingeordnet werden. Die Studierenden können Beratungsgespräche nach Beratungsansätzen führen, dabei Gesprächstechniken gezielt anwenden, auch im schulischen Bereich, und Ihre Beiträge und den Lernprozess reflektieren.

Title: Berechenbarkeit und Unvollständigkeit
Description:
CONTENT:
Der Kurs bietet eine Einführung zu den Grundbegriffen der Berechenbarkeitstheorie, zu den Gödelschen Unvollständigkeitssätzen und zu anderen wichtigen Sätzen der modernen Logik, welche die Grenzen der formalen Systeme aufzeigen.

Der Kurs ist folgendermaßen aufgebaut:
1. Algorithmen, Turingmaschinen, Berechenbarkeit
2. Peano Arithmetik: das elementare formale System PA
3. Gödelschen Unvollständigkeitssätze
4. Philosophische Interpretationen der Gödelschen Sätzen
5. Satz von Tarski (Undefinierbarkeit der Wahrheit)
6. Satz von Church (Unentscheidbarkeit der Arithmetik und der elementaren Logik)

OBJECTIVES:
Tiefes Verständnis der Unvollständigkeitssätze. Die Studierenden wissen am Ende des Semesters, was "semantische Vollständigkeit", "Syntaktische Unvollständigkeit", "Entscheidbarkeit" und "Unentscheidbarkeit" bedeuten.

Title: Bestand als Bedingung
Description:
CONTENT:
Abriss und Neubau stellen nach wie vor die Standardlösung dar, um schnell auf sich ändernde programmatische Anforderungen an ein Gebäude zu reagieren. Dabei wird die Wirtschaftlichkeit häufig über langfristige ökologische, soziale und historische Bedeutung gestellt. Gebäude aus den Boomjahren der Nachkriegszeit weisen weitreichende ökologische und kulturelle Implikationen auf, machen fast ein Drittel des Gebäudebestands in Europa aus und genießen häufig nicht den besten Ruf. Bei genauerer Betrachtung erweist sich ein Gebäudetyp als besonders prototypisch für die Bauten der Boomjahre: das Warenhaus. Es ist nicht nur baukonstruktiv rational und typologisch effizient organisiert, sondern verkörpert auf programmatischer Ebene auch eine kapitalistische Idee jener Zeit des Wirtschaftswunders: die Demokratisierung des Konsums. 
In diesem Seminar wird argumentiert, dass die Herausforderung des Bauens im Bestand nicht nur eine technische, sondern auch eine Frage der Wahrnehmung ist. Kann Architektur auch bedeuten, weniger zu bauen und stattdessen Wissen zu generieren, um ideologisch und wirtschaftlich motivierte Abrisse zu vermeiden? Über den reinen Erhalt hinaus bedarf es Strategien zur Dokumentation, Analyse und Bewertung, um den Entwurfsprozess fundiert zu informieren und uns stärker in Richtung einer zirkulären Baupraxis zu bewegen. 
Über das Medium der Zeichnungen sollen das adaptive Potenzial und Werte verschiedener Fallstudien entschlüsselt und Schichten von Dauerhaftigkeit und Transformierbarkeit sichtbar gemacht werden. Ziel ist es, die Werte und Potentiale des baulichen Bestands bewusster wahrzunehmen und Gebäude entsprechend zu verstehen und zu repräsentieren. Die Arbeit erfolgt in Gruppen zu dritt und beinhaltet Recherche- und Zeichenarbeit.

OBJECTIVES:
Nach Abschluss des Kurses sind die Studierenden in der Lage…
•	… die historische und zeitgenössische Bedeutung sowie die Herausforderungen des Umgangs mit dem Bestand zu bewerten.
•	… den Aufbau unterschiedlicher konstruktiver Systeme und den Wert des anthropogenen Lagers zu verstehen.
•	… sich mit dem baulichen Erbe der Nachkriegsmoderne methodisch und kritisch auseinanderzusetzen.

Title: Bestandsanalyse - Einfach Umbauen
Description:
CONTENT:

OBJECTIVES:

Description:
CONTENT:

Dazu werden sowohl gesammeltes Anschaunugsmaterial bestimmt, als auch Freilandübungen durchgeführt. die Merkmale der ca. 20 wichtigsten Pflanzenfamilien der einheimischen Flora
- Überblick über die Gehölzfamilien mit Beispielen zu Nutzung und Ökologie z.B. Ausbreitung-.

OBJECTIVES:
Nach der Teilnahme an der Modulveranstaltung haben die Studierenden vertiefte Artenkenntnisse in der einheimischen Gehölzflora und häufig verwendeten nicht heimischen Gehölzen. Sie können die Gehölze  an ihren Merkmalen erkennen, benennen und charakterisieren. Eine Auswahl von Gehölzen können sie sicher ohne Bestimmungshilfe identifizieren. Darüber hinaus haben Sie Kenntnisse zu Nutzung und Ökologie (z.B. Ausbreitungsformen).

Title: Bestimmung von Insekten
Description:
CONTENT:
The module covers the most important characteristics for the identification and differentiation of various insect groups. In addition to various identification keys, the critical use of mobile apps for identification as well as molecular methods as identification tools are presented and their use in various application areas and research fields is taught. The knowledge will be applied in exercises in the laboratory and in the field to teach the most important insect orders with identification keys and apps in more depth.

OBJECTIVES:
Upon successful completion of the module, students will be able to recognize and distinguish the most important insect groups in the laboratory as well as in the field. They will also know the most important identification characteristics for the different insect groups, and they are able to identify insects down to family, genus and, if necessary and possible, species level using traditional and modern identification keys and methods. In addition, the students learn the critical use of so-called "identification apps" and gain insight into today's applications of taxonomic knowledge in the digital world.

Title: Betonkonstruktionen im Hoch- und Ingenieurbau
Description:
CONTENT:
- Load paths, bracing, and idealization of reinforced concrete structures 
- Non-linear analysis of structures  
- Design for Serviceability Limit State (crack control, deflection control) 
- Design for restraint forces, minimum reinforcement areas 
- Fire safety design 
- Design for special load cases (earthquake, impact and explosion) 
- Pre-cast construction

OBJECTIVES:
Participating this module enables the student to design and to idealize concrete structures (mainly high-rise constructions) and to examine the results out of numerical calculations by obtaining simplified procedures. The student has an understanding of the load transfer, the impact and opportunities of the bracing elements and the interaction of individual components of the overall system. Furthermore the student is able to apply different methods for the rearrangement of internal forces and to apply nonlinear methods.
For the serviceability limit state the student is able to apply direct calculation methods (crack, deflection). In addition, the student understood the basics of structural design for special load cases and the load case of fire and is able to apply those methods. Also an insight into the use of prefabricated structures is given.
Skills: ['Reinforced concrete design', 'Structural analysis', 'Fire safety engineering', 'Earthquake engineering']

Title: Betriebswirtschaftslehre
Description:
CONTENT:

- Warenwirtschaftssysteme und Beschaffung: Wareneingang, Angebotsvergleiche, Anschaffungskostenermittlung, Bedarfsermittlung, Beschaffungsvorgänge.
- Lieferantenmanagement: Vergleichsrechnungen zwischen Lieferanten und zwischen Eigenproduktion und Fremdbezug
- Lagerhaltung: Lagerkennzahlen, Soll-Ist-Abweichungen, Lagerkostenermittlung
- Kostenrechnung: Kostenarten-, stellen-, trägerrechnung, Deckungsbeitragsrechnung, Ziel- und Prozesskostenrechnung, Break-even-Analyse, Kosten- und Erlösmanagement
- Buchführung/Bilanzierung: doppelte Buchführung, Grundlagen der Bilanzierung nach HGB
- Personalwirtschaft: Personalführung, Personalentlohnung, Personalentwicklung

OBJECTIVES:
Nach erfolgreichen Abschluss des Moduls sind die Studierenden in der Lage, die wichtigsten Mechanismen und Konzepte der für eine spätere Tätigkeit als Lehrer für Ernährungs- und Hauswirtschaftswissenschaft relevanten Bereiche der Betriebswirtschaftslehre anzuwenden und deren Zusammenhänge und Interaktionen in einem Betrieb für Ernährung oder Hauswirtschaft einzuschätzen. Hierdurch sollen die Studierenden befähigt werden, diese Inhalte Schülern zu vermitteln und neuere Erkenntnisse selbständig sich zu erarbeiten.

Description:

Title: Bildung und Nachhaltigkeit mit dem Fokus auf Bewegung und Sport
Description:
CONTENT:
Das Modul gliedert sich in ein Seminar und eine begleitende Übung.

Im Seminar werden folgende Inhalte vermittelt:
-	Grundlagenwissen zu den Themen Nachhaltigkeit, nachhaltige Entwicklung, Bildung für nachhaltige Entwicklung im schulischen Kontext, aktuelle globale Herausforderungen, Anspruch an Bildungsinstitutionen
-	Analyse des schulischen Lehrplans für das Fach Sport hinsichtlich (a) Bildung für nachhaltige Entwicklung und (b) Nutzung alternativer, naturnaher Lernsettings (für den Sportunterricht und darüber hinaus)
-	Nutzung naturnaher, alternativer Lernsettings für Erziehungs- und Bildungsprozesse
-	Kennenlernen des Konzepts des „Draußenunterichts“
-	Erkennen, erfahren und gestalten alternativer Lernräume im Sportunterricht (außerhalb normierter Sportstätten)
-	Gefährdungsbeurteilung und Sicherheitsmaßnahmen

In der Übung werden die Inhalte in Lehrversuchen umgesetzt. Dabei geht es um das Erleben, Erfahren (Lernebene), Anleiten (Lehrebene), und Reflektieren (Lehr- und Lernebene) von exemplarischen Unterrichtsversuchen gemäß den Seminarinhalten.

Settings
Die Durchführung des Moduls findet teilweise in der Sporthalle, im Seminarraum und an alternativen Lernräume (drinnen und draußen) statt.

OBJECTIVES:
Nach dem Besuch des Moduls sind die Studierenden in der Lage:
-	Die Grundbegriffe und theoretischen Hintergründe einer nachhaltigen Entwicklung sowie einer Bildung für nachhaltige Entwicklung zu erklären.
-	Aktuelle globale Herausforderungen zu beschreiben und Konsequenzen für die Lebens- und Lernwelt Schule als Bildungsinstitution zu bestimmen.
-	Didaktisch und fachlich fundierte, lehrplanbezogene Unterrichtsstunden für Bildung für nachhaltige Entwicklung im Sportunterricht zu planen, durchzuführen und auszuwerten.
-	Alternative, naturnahe Lernorte und deren didaktisches Potential zu erkennen, zu gestalten und zu nutzen.
-	Gefahrengeneigte Bewegungsfelder mittels Gefährdungsbeurteilung systematisch zu bewerten, um daraus Sicherheitsmaßnahmen (Hilfestellung, Verwendung von Schutzausrüstung, Material Sicherheitscheck, etc.) abzuleiten und in Unterrichtsversuchen anzuwenden.

Title: Bildverarbeitung in der Physik
Description:
CONTENT:
This course will cover a wide range of advanced techniques used for image processing and image reconstruction, with a special focus on physical science applications. Following a problem-solving philosophy, the course will motivate all techniques and fundamental concepts with problems drawn from real-life applications.

Each class will address a specific technique, yet all will be linked by recurrent essential topics including Fourier analysis, linear algebra, iterative techniques, maximum likelihood and convex optimization. In addition to the two-hour classes, a weekly one-hour exercise session will take place to answer questions and present homework solutions. Exercises will take the form of simple programming tasks.

OBJECTIVES:
After participation to the Module, the student:

    Will know the fundamentals of numerical analysis.
    Will know the basics of the standard imaging analysis methods in research and the industry.
    Will have an overview of the state of the art in many fields of imaging physics.
    Will have developed skills to identify the technique appropriate to a given problem.
    Will have had the chance to apply the learned techniques in hands-on programming exercises.

Title: Bildverstehen - Aktuelle Ansätze des Maschinellen Lernens
Description:
CONTENT:
In this course, we will review selected aspects of current machine learning research. To this end, we will discuss a selection of influential work from the ML research community. Later, we will form groups and try reproducing some of these concepts.

OBJECTIVES:
After successful completion of this course, participants will be able to:
- understand, comprehend, reproduce and evaluate machine learning methods,
- search relevant literature on their own,
- write scientific papers on an international level, and
- create new concepts.

Title: Bioelectronic Interfaces and Devices for Neuroengineering
Description:
CONTENT:
This course covers topics related to the interaction between neural tissue and the tools that are used to record from or stimulate them. Starting with concepts of device-tissue interactions and the electrochemistry of the electrode-electrolyte interface we will proceed with optimization strategies for sensing and stimulation applications. The class provides an overview of the main components of a complete neural hardware system comprising bioelectronic recording/stimulation interfaces as well as relevant processing circuitry.  
The course will also address state-of-the-art methods for the design and fabrication of soft and flexible neuroelectronic interfaces and processing hardware for noisy neural recordings including pre-processing (analog low-noise amplifiers and bandpass filters), and application-specific hardware (analog/digital/mixed signal), which is implemented either in an implantable system or external components. Furthermore, stimulation with micro-currents will be discussed and how to use such systems while minimizing negative chronic effects.

OBJECTIVES:
After completion of the module students are able to understand the physical principles of functional neuroelectronic interfaces. Furthermore, they will know available tools to create efficient soft and flexible neuroelectronic interfaces and apply them in the scope of advanced electrical and electrochemical recording and stimulation techniques. They can evaluate and design appropriate methods for diverse application scenarios.

Darüberhinaus werden die Grundbegriffe biogener Polymere in Bezug auf technisch relevante Polymere und ihre Anwendung erweitert. Weiterhin werden die chemische Synthese und Derivatisierung von industriell relevanten Biokunststoffen eingeführt (z.B. Cellulosederivate). Die physikalisch-chemischen Eigenschaften der Biokunststoffe und ihre Charkterisierung sind zentraler Bestandteil der Vorlesung.

Title: Biomaterialcharakterisierung für Ingenieure
Description:
CONTENT:
This lecture discusses experimental techniques that can be used to characterize the structure and mechanics of biomaterials. First, basic imaging techniques such as optical microscopy, electron microscopy, near field and atomic force microscopy will be introduced. It will be shown how these techniques can be adjusted to increase the resolution and contrast of the obtained images so that these techniques can be used for the characterization of biological samples. In a second part, macro- and microscopic techniques for determining the viscoelastic properties of biomaterials are reviewed and the corresponding setups are discussed. In a last part, techniques for micro- and nanostructuring are introduced and it is shown how they can be applied in tandem with optical or mechanical techniques in a microfluidic setup that allows performing complex sorting or analysis steps in a “lab on a chip” device. 
As an additional part of this lecture, virtual lab tours with short demonstrations of state-of-the-art equipment (optical or mechanical measuring setups) will be offered.

OBJECTIVES:
Nach erfolgreicher Teilnahme an der Modulveranstaltung „Experimentelle Techniken zur Charakterisierung von Biomaterialien“ sind die Studierenden in der Lage, verschiedene experimentelle Techniken aus dem Bereich Optik und Mechanik hinsichtlich ihrer Anwendbarkeit auf Biomaterialien zu bewerten. Sie beherrschen die physikalischen Prinzipien, die diesen Techniken zugrunde liegen und können diese bei der Charakterisierung von Biomaterialien anwenden.

Title: Biomaterials
Description:
CONTENT:
This entry-level course is designed for students pursuing a master's degree. It aims to provide the fundamentals of biomaterials, which will provide the necessary background for advanced and specialized courses related to biomedical engineering. We will first cover key definitions and discuss basic concepts related to biomaterials. We will discuss thermodynamics in biological systems, as well as covalent and noncovalent bonding in biomaterials, with an emphasis on polymers and macromolecules. We will then cover the structure of materials, including their mechanical, surface, and bulk properties. We will then study polymers while looking into applications of biomaterials. Finally, we will address biological responses to implanted materials and principles of materials engineering to mitigate undesirable effects.

Course topics:
•	Introduction to biomaterials
•	Thermodynamics in biological systems
•	Covalent and non-covalent bonding
•	Polymers and macromolecules 
•	Structural properties of materials
•	Optical, electrical, magnetic, and mechanical properties
•	Surface and macroscale properties
•	Inflammation and wound healing 
•	Biocompatibility and in vitro testing 
•	Tissue engineering applications

OBJECTIVES:
After participating in this course, the student is able to:
1.	Understand the fundamental working principles of biomaterials 
2.	Analyze different crosslinking strategies and explain their limitations
3.	Apply knowledge of material and fabrication approaches for tissue engineering applications
4.	Evaluate important criteria for smooth device integration with cells and tissue
5.	Apply the generated biomaterials knowledge to other relevant fields for engineering new devices

Title: Biomolecular Electronics Laboratory
Description:
CONTENT:
The objective of the field of biomolecular electronics is to integrate
bioorganic molecules into electronic devices. In particular,
researchers try to exploit the electrical characteristics of
biomaterials to develop future electronic components, such as
sensors for health monitoring and diagnostics. The topic is highly
interdisciplinary, covering aspects of electrical engineering, physics,
chemistry and molecular biology.
In this context, the laboratory course deals with the electrical
characterization of nanometer-thin biomolecular films. The course
will begin with an introduction to biomolecules, their chemical
structure and the relevant charge transport theory. A briefing on the
experimental fabrication and characterization techniques, such as
chemical self-assembly, microfabrication and electrical
measurements, will also be held. The students will then practice the
above in a laboratory, guided by scientific staff. More specifically,
they will:
1. prepare substrates and chemically modify their surface via
self-assembly,
2. grow biomolecular films, in particular protein layers,
3. characterize the films with respect to wettability, thickness
and morphology via water contact angle, atomic force
microscopy and spectral ellipsometry measurements,
4. perform electrical transport measurements, and
5. analyze and interpret the measured current-voltage
characteristics.
After completing the experimental part, students will summarize the
experimental procedures and the obtained results in a
comprehensive lab report and a final oral presentation.

OBJECTIVES:
By the end of this course, students are expected to be able to
1. describe the structure and function of biomolecules, 
especially proteins, 
2. fabricate nanometer-thin biomolecular films on solid 
substrates,
3. characterize thin films in terms of their thickness, 
morphology and electrical behavior, and
4. perform, analyze and model electrical measurements of 
biomolecular layers.

Title: Bio-Nano Grenzflächenverfahrenstechnik
Description:
CONTENT:
The Bio Nano Interfacial Engineering module is a highly interdisciplinary course that combines components of chemistry, chemical engineering, physics, biology, and materials science. The content covered in the module includes:

- Colloids, macroscopic and microscopic interfaces, and interfacial phenomena. 
- Molecular interactions
- Adsorption and adsorption isotherms; (micro)emulsions and suspensions
- Young-Laplace and Kelvin equations; crystallization
- Liquid phase wetting, capillarity, superhydrophobicity
- Electrochemical double layer and colloidal stability
- Nanotechnology - properties of nanoparticle systems
- Biological (macro)molecules - properties and structures
- Interaction of biomolecules with inorganic surfaces  
- Industrial interfacial processes - examples from biotechnology, food industry, agriculture, environmental technology, cosmetics industry, pharmacy, and biomedicine

OBJECTIVES:
After attending the module, students will be able to:
- describe the main concepts of interfacial engineering
- distinguish and compare general characteristics and specific properties of colloidal systems, biological suspensions, and continuous solid phases 
- identify and distinguish different types of molecular interactions that occur when solids interact with biological suspensions
- evaluate the role of different physicochemical variables
- select methods for the specific determination of core properties of materials
- use this knowledge to analyze industrially relevant processes
- identify challenges of current processes
- work out optimization possibilities with regard to complete biomass utilization as well as energy and resource efficiency, circular economy, and recyclability
- develop requirements for innovative, sustainable, and productivity-enhancing process solutions, inter and transdisciplinary, taking into account social aspects
- understand each other's language, justify one's own decisions, and convince with arguments in interdisciplinary teams with students from different disciplines.

- Life at small Reynolds numbers: Navier Stokes equation
- Life in 2D: Physics of lipid membranes
- Elasticity of molecules and networks
- Viscoelastic behavior of polymer solutions
- Mixtures - phase separation
- Mechanical interactions of cells with their environment: Mechanosensing

Major issues are: Model bioreactors (stirred tank and flow tube) - Formal kinetic models of biological reactions – Biological reactions in model bioreactors (steady-state) – Dynamic behaviour of model bioreactors – Assessment of biological model parameters – Metabolic flux analysis – Measurement of biological model parameters – Structured kinetic models of biological reactions – Stirred tank reactors – Bubble Columns- Fixed bed-/ Fluidized bed reactors.

In addition, students are able to understand the properties of major industrial-scale bioreactors.

Title: Block-Course Tools and Practice in Digital Research and Engineering
Description:
CONTENT:
The students learn good practice and tools in digital research and engineering. On the first day, the students are exposed to linux shell usage and learn a set of central commands. In hand on exercises they experience the functionality of a shell. The second day introduces the basics of ssh for remote access and the use of ssh keys for authentication. In hands-on sessions, the students apply these concepts, generate their own ssh keys, and learn how to access remote servers. On the third day, the students learn the concepts of repositories for collaborative development and gain hands-on experience in setting up and collaborating on git repositories. On the fourth day, the students get introduced to continuous integration and unit testing on git platforms (github or gitlab) and gain experience in setting this up for their own projects. The last day covers latex document development including the use of sharelatex and overleaf.

OBJECTIVES:
The students know key commands for linux shell usage and how to generate, deploy, and use ssh keys. The students understand the concepts behind versioning systems, continuous integration, and unit testing. They have gained expertise in applying the concepts themselves and create git repositories for collaboration, continuous integration pipelines, and how to use unit test frameworks. The students also know how to use latex for document processing.

Title: Blutbildende Stammzellen als Modell für somatische Stammzellen
Description:
CONTENT:
Im Rahmen dieses theoretischen Moduls werden spezielle Kenntnise über somatische, und insbesondere blutbildender Stamm­ und Vorläuferzellen und Stromazellen vermittelt.
Es werden 8 Vorlesungen stattfinden, und anschliessend bis 8, von den Studenten vorbereiteten Seminare in dem aktuelle Forschungsbeispiele präsentiert und besprochen werden sollten. Vorlesungen:

1. Einleitung in der Stammzellbiologie, somatische Stammzellen
2. Embryologische Entwicklung des Blutsystems und blutbildenden Stammzellen
3. normale Physiologie der blutbildenden Stammzellen, Teil 1
4. normale Physiologie der blutbildenden Stammzellen, Teil 2
5. Alterung der Stammzellen
6. die Stammzellnischen
7. klinische Relevanz von blutbildenden Stammzellen
8. Maligne Stammzellen

In den Seminaren sollen von den Teilnehmern aktuelle Forschungsergebnisse der Literatur vorbereitet, präsentiert und diskutiert werden. Dabei werden nicht nur Blutstammzellen, sondern auch somatische Stammzellen aus anderen Geweben besprochen in Themen wie:

1 ­ Stammzellidentität und Isolation
2 ­ Stammzellverhalten (Regeneration, Apoptose, Überleben, Proliferation, Differenzierung) 
3 ­ Stammzellnische (Identität, Isolation, Relevanz für das Verhalten der Stammzelle)
4 ­ Maligne Entartungen des Blutsystems und leukämische Stammzellen

ausführlich zur Sprache kommen
Ergänzt werden die Vorlesungen und Seminare durch eine Hausarbeit (in englischer Sprache) in dem die Teilnehmer ihr Verständnisse der erworbenen Kenntnisse beschreiben, Interpretieren und bewerten.

OBJECTIVES:
Nach der Teilnahme an den Modulveranstaltungen besitzen die Studierenden das theoretische Verständnis und spezielle Fachwissen über blutbildenden Stammzellen. Weiterhin haben sie wesentliche Konzepte somatischer Stammzellen integriert, evaluiert und in einer Hausarbeit beschrieben. Sie haben gelernt:
• die Herkunft der somatischen Stammzellen und deren Entwicklung in Embryonen zu verstehen
• grundlegende funktionelle Verhaltensweisen blutbildender Stammzellen zu verstehen
• (Stamm)zellbiologische Fragestellungen und Arbeitstechniken aus aktuelle Forschungsliteratur zu verstehen, kritisch zu evaluieren und fachliche Fragen selbst zu entwickeln.

Title: Bodenphysikalische Methoden
Description:
CONTENT:
Das Modul  vermittelt Studierenden theoretische Grundlagen und experimentelle Methoden, um bodenphysikalische Eigenschaften wie Bodentextur, Korngrößenverteilung, Bodenretentionskurven oder die hydraulische Leitfähigkeit von Böden zu ermitteln. Wasserflüsse im Boden werden unter verschiedenen Bodenwassergehalten mit gängigen Sensoren quantifiziert. Die experimentellen Methoden beinhalten unter anderem:
-	Optische/ haptische Überprüfung der Bodentextur („Schmiertest“).
-	Bodenlagerungsdichte, Wassergehalt und Porosität werden mit Stechzylindern gravimetrisch nach Trocknung im Ofen ermittelt.
-	Bodenwassergehalt mittels Bodenfeuchtesensor (Time-Domain-Reflectometry, TDR) bestimmen
-	Korngrößenverteilung mittels Sedimentation im Messzylinder (Pario-Methode) bestimmen
-	Sandfraktionen werden mittels Nass-Siebung durch DIN-Siebe ermittelt
-	Gravimetrische Analyse der Wasserhalte- und Feldkapazität des Bodens
-	Verhältnis von Bodenwassergehalt und Bodenwasserspannung wird über Druckplatten (Sandbox Verfahren) und im Drucktopf ermittelt
-	Analyse der Daten mit Hilfe von Template-Arbeitsblättern in Excel
Die Übung findet wöchentlich statt, die Studierenden werden dabei in Gruppen aufgeteilt. Am Ende des Semesters werden die erhobenen Daten unter allen Gruppen ausgetauscht und jede Gruppe wird einem Thema zugewiesen (grundlegende bodenphysikalische Eigenschaften, Wasserretentionskurve oder Wasserfluss), das dann in mündlicher und schriftlicher Form präsentiert wird.

OBJECTIVES:
Nach erfolgreichem Abschluss sind Studierende in der Lage:
•	Grundlegende Bodenphysikalische Eigenschaften wie Bodentextur, Bodenwassergehalt oder Bodenporosität selbstständig zu erfassen..
•	Die Wasserhaltekapazität verschiedener Bodenarten zu bestimmen.
•	Wasserflüsse in verschiedenen Böden zu messen.
•	Verschiedene experimentelle Ansätze, wie der Einsatz von Feuchtesensoren, gravimetrische und tensionsgestützte Messverfahren zu verwenden um Wasserverfügbarkeit und Wasserflussdynamiken in Böden sowohl unter Labor- als auch Freilandbedingungen zu quantifizieren.
•	Die gemessenen bodenphysikalischen Werte mit Literaturwerten zu vergleichen und einzuordnen.

Title: Brain, Mind and Cognition
Description:
CONTENT:
The course attempts to motivate the participants to actively think about the topic "Brain, Mind & Cognition" stimulated by reading and discussing books on this topic. 

The seminar is structured like a reading circle. The participants read a book on the subject of "Brain, Mind & Cognition. After some appropriate reading period the group meets and discusses the main points of the book. Besides the oral discussions participants are also asked to put down their thinking in writing, i.e., in the form of short essays on what has been said in the book and what it means to the individual. 

The books are supposed to be jargon-free, interesting or even popular books on the topic, which are mostly with only very limited amount of mathematical notation. The list of books may also include appropriate novels.

OBJECTIVES:
It is the goal of this course to read and digest information, to stimulate new thoughts as well as to improve the spoken and written communication skills.

Title: BS Practical Course on Network Visualization for Competitive Challenges
Description:
CONTENT:
This course focuses on implementing advanced algorithms to participate
in two prominent algorithmic challenges: the Graph Drawing Challenge and
the Parameterized Algorithms and Computational Experiments (PACE)
Challenge. The course aims to deepen students' understanding of graph
theory, algorithm design, and fixed-parameter tractability (FPT).

Students create a visualization of a given network of medium to large scale. The group is divided into several teams for this purpose. During the process, students acquire knowledge in the areas of network analysis, graph drawing and information visualization and practice applying this knowledge. Students also use suitable visualization software packages to create the visualization. The students present the current state of development at regular intervals and give each other feedback.

Throughout the course, students will develop and refine their
algorithms, receive feedback, and compete in real-world scenarios,
preparing them for future research or industry roles in algorithm design
and analysis. By the end of the course, students will have gained
practical experience in solving complex problems related to graph
structures and parameterized algorithms, positioning them to excel in
competitive programming environments.

OBJECTIVES:
Students are able to create a high-quality visualization of a network and can implement suitable algorithms for network analysis. To achieve these goals, students will be able to select suitable visualization techniques for a given graph drawing/network visualization application and extract suitable features from several prototypes and integrate them into a new model. In addition, students can identify the information available for the application and prioritize relations that are particularly relevant for users. Furthermore, students will be able to compare and discuss different approaches and research relevant literature independently.

Title: Building Archaeology I
Description:
CONTENT:

The lecture series Building Archaeology introduces participants to the wide range of topics, methods and problems covered by historic building research as a special discipline of architecture.
Compact lectures and practical workshops will showcase not only the research, analysis, documentation and decryption of complex historic buildings, but also ways of conserving and using them in practice. Students can put their newly gained knowledge of analysis and both analogue and digital methods of building recording to the test in a practical on-site workshop and a short field trip or guided city walks at the end of the seminar.

OBJECTIVES:
After attending the seminar, the students will know about the different problems, methods and types of recording and illustration in the field of building archaeology. 
They will be capable of recording historic buildings in various display modes, at different scales and levels of detail. They will have a keen eye for constructive coherences, historic architectural elements and historical traces that exist on a building and are able to express and communicate these findings in specialised drawings.

Title: Bürgerbeteiligungsverfahren zum Aufbau der Energieinfrastruktur
Description:
CONTENT:
The module contains two parts:
I) For block lectures with 4 hours of lecture
II) A three day long role play in after the lecture period

The first part contains the following parts:
I.1) Theory of democracy, foundations and methods of public participation
I.2) Life Cylce Assessment (LCA) as basis for environmental and health assessments of projects and products
I.3) Methods and tools of LCA
I.4) Design of an LCA as basis for a public participation process by means of examples

Part II is made up of a three-day long role-play. On the first day, a project is identified and the necessary information is collected. Recommendations for a public participation process are prepared.
On the second day, a public assembly is simulated with an expert hearing. A special role is assigned to each participant. Other students are asked to participate as civilians. All discussions are recorded.
On the third day, the recordings are analysed and refinements of the expert materials are discussed.

OBJECTIVES:
Students are able to name different theories of democracy and assign political systems to these theories. Students know the tools of public participation. They have a good understanding of LCA and are able to apply LCA to different projects. The can write an expert opinion based on an LCA, which can be used as material for a public participation process. They can judge the complex situation of a public participation process and learn the limits of scientific arguments in public debates.
Skills: ['Democracy theory', 'Public participation', 'Life Cycle Assessment (LCA)', 'Environmental assessment', 'Energy infrastructure', 'Role-playing']

Title: Business Law I
Description:
CONTENT:

It includes an overview of the legal framework in Germany and Europe, the formation and termination of contracts, selected types of contract (in particular, sale of goods), torts, property law, and company law. The module covers aspects of the German legal framework as well as the common law. This module is a prerequisite for "Business Law 2". It cannot be replaced with "Wirtschaftsprivatrecht 1".

(3.) to analyse legal implications of typical business situations and to identify their options;

Title: Business Research Methods MIM Heilbronn
Description:
CONTENT:
The course provides students with advanced knowledge on business research methods. In an increasingly complex business environment, managers must rely on evidence rather than intuition to address organizational challenges. Mastering business research methods not only improves managerial effectiveness but also contributes to the broader development of management science through the creation of verifiable, generalizable knowledge.

The course reviews important steps to gain credible insight, which can include topics such as formulating research questions, reviewing the state-of-the-art, selecting an appropriate research method, testing hypotheses, or presenting results.

By combining theoretical lectures with practical exercises, students gain hands-on experience in business research methods, preparing them to make well-informed decisions that are backed by solid evidence.

OBJECTIVES:
After this course, students ...:
• are competent in developing research questions for exploration with business research methods
• can evaluate business research methods on their strengths and weaknesses to inform their use
• can design methodologically sound business research projects
• understand the scientific process, criteria, and statistical foundations that underlie the application of business research methods
• can derive insights from data obtained through business research methods
• communicate research effectively

Title: CAD Basics und Innovationsbewertung
Description:
CONTENT:
The exercise course aims to teach students without an engineering background the use of CAD software (Computer Aided Design). Moreover a product development process based on rapid prototyping techniques will be exercised. In doing so, the students get to know a general engineering mindset and the principles of operation in an engineering environment. They will find out how they can contribute their specific knowledge from their previous study programs. The strengthening of interdisciplinary thinking and working is promoted. The students learn how a body can be captured with a 3D scanner and how the scan can be used in a CAD program. For the scanned object, a tailor-made product is to be developed, which will be 3D printed. Additionally the basics of innovation assessment will be taught in the exercise. The new knowledge is used by the students during a visit of a trade fair. The exercise is organized and held in cooperation with MakerSpace (UnternehmerTUM).

OBJECTIVES:
At the end of the module students are able to
- name basic terms of CAD.
- explain the basics of innovation assessment.
- assess the innovativeness of a product.
- demonstrate the handling of a 3D scanner.
- differentiate between various CAD file formats and handle those within a CAD software tool.
- check the quality of a mesh and modify it.
- independently develop a 3D model in CAD.
- prepare a 3D model for 3D printing and estimate the print results. 
- perform a 3D print.

Title: CAD/TD for Aerospace Engineers
Description:
CONTENT:
The course covers the basic principles of technical drawing, CAD, and design theory:
Content technical drawing:
- Fundamentals of engineering drawings (drawing types, scale, line types, lettering)  
- Drawing of engineering components (views, rules view projection, hatching, section views, rules for marking) 
- Dimensioning of engineering components (fundamentals of dimensioning, drawing and dimensioning of threads, dimensioning for manufacture)
- Surface specifications (surface roughness, edge specifications, hardness, knurls)
- Tolerances (fundamentals of tolerances, tolerances of dimensions, positional and shape tolerances)
- Fits (basic concept of fits, ISO tolerance fields, fit selection with standard bore/shaft)
- Joint connections (types of seams/joints and their drawing/dimensioning)
- Standard Parts (drawing of commonly used standard parts, shaft-hub connections, bearings, and gears)


Content CAD:
- Basic principles (history, classification within CAE, differences 2D/2.5D/3D)
- Models (wireframe, surface, volume)
- Elements (points, lines, splines, planes, sketches, surfaces, bodies/solids)
- Operations (block/extrusion, rotation, boolean operators)

Content design theory:
- Basic rules (straightforward, simple, safe)
- Approach (integral/differential, top down-/bottom up-principle)
- Production oriented design (design for welding, casting, forging, and cutting manufacturing)
- Load compliant design (force transmission, basic rules)

OBJECTIVES:
Upon completion of the module, students are able to:
- analyse a complex component drawing of an engineering component.
- analyse the connection between component and assembly drawings.
- create a component drawing of an engineering component.
- describe important basic terms of CAD systems and explain their differences.
- evaluate different engineering components regarding their design strategy.

Title: Campus-Chor Garching
Description:
CONTENT:
Im Rahmen des Campus-Chor Garching wird in der Regel auf ein bis zwei Konzerte zu Semesterende hingearbeitet. Das Themenfeld der ausgewählten Stücke wechselt auf Projektbasis und ist, stetig aktualisiert, auf der Homepage des Chores einsehbar (https://www.ccg.tum.de). Der konkrete Inhalt besteht in der Einstudierung mehrstimmiger Chorstücke, die von chorischer Stimmbildung sowie der Vermittlung grundlegender musikalischer Kenntnisse (Rhythmik, Grundtonbezogenes Singen, ggf. musiktheoretische Grundlagen) begleitet wird. Zusätzlich werden optionale, aber sehr empfohlene, weitere Veranstaltungen angeboten, wie zum Beispiel Ganztagsproben oder Chorseminare (2-3 Tage an musisch-ausgerichteten Seminarstandorten), inkl. weiterführendem Stimmtraining und social networking. Als Abschluss der Probenphase wird mindestens ein Konzert angestrebt, bei dem die eingeprobten Stücke durch den Chor dargeboten werden. Zusätzlich wird ein Grundrepertoire aufgebaut, welches für Aufritte in wechselnden kulturellen Kontexten (Studierendenveranstaltungen, Abschlussfeiern, Stadtfeste, Gottesdienste, etc.) genutzt werde kann.
Im Sommersemester 2025 stehen die Konzerte unter dem Motto "Licht und Schatten". Neben vielen Klassischen Stücken (u.A. von Johann Bach, G.F. Händel, F. Mendelssohn, M. Reger) mit modernen Einflüssen wie etwa aus Northern Lights (O. Gjeilo) oder Moon River (H. Mancini). Vom 23.-25.5 findet ein Probenwochenende statt und die Konzerte sind für das Wochenende 4.-6.7. angesetzt.

Title: Causal Inference
Description:
CONTENT:
The course will cover the topic of how to infer causality from observational data with Machine Learning methods and how to design experiments for causal inference considering potential confounders and theory for assumption modeling. Students will learn to judge the validity of a causality claim, biases,  applicability and options for explainability of different analytical methods.

OBJECTIVES:
> Understanding of the relevance of causal inference for various fields of research
> How to distinguish between correlation and causal effects in published research 
> How causation can be identified through experimental design or Machine Learning methods
> Know different methods for causal inference, including matching and tree-based methods 
> In what cases those methods should and can be applied, limits of the known methods
> How to model the causal assumptions according to previous literature or studies
> Judge how certain analytical findings are and what biases ML models can introduce

Title: CDR
Description:
CONTENT:
Das Seminar CDR: Digital Future Challenge – verantwortungsvolle KI bildet den Rahmen für die Teilnahme der Teams an der Digital Future Challenge. Die Digital Future Challenge (DFC) ist ein gemeinsames Projekt der Deloitte-Stiftung und der Initiative D21 unter der Schirmherrschaft des BMUV, um die Verantwortung von Unternehmen im und durch den digitalen Wandel, sprich Corporate Digital Responsibility (CDR), zu beleuchten. Die DFC 2024/25 stand daher unter dem Motto „Zukunft digital gestalten“. Digitale Technologien sind zentral für die künftige Wettbewerbsfähigkeit von Unternehmen. Dabei dürfen die damit einhergehenden gesellschaftlichen Folgen und Veränderungen nicht außer Acht gelassen werden. Vielmehr sind sie bei einer verantwortungsvollen Entwicklung und Implementierung von Künstlicher Intelligenz (KI) und anderen Technologien stets mitzudenken. Die zentrale Bedeutung die beiden Aspekte, einer innovativen technischen Lösung einerseits und deren ethische, rechtliche bzw. gesellschaftlichen Implikationen andererseits, miteinander zu vereinbaren und in Ausgleich zu bringen, sollen die Studierenden durch die Teilnahme an der DFC im Rahmen des Seminars CDR erlernen.

OBJECTIVES:
Am Ende der Veranstaltungen verfügen die Teilnehmenden über umfassende Kenntnisse im Bereich CDR und sind sich der Herausforderungen und Chancen dieses Themenfeldes bewusst. Sie kennen dabei sowohl die Besonderheiten der juristischen, der politischen, aber auch der wirtschaftlichen Seite und verstehen es sich in diesem interdisziplinären Feld zu bewegen. Sie könne die Potentiale für CDR einschätzen und wissen in welchen Kontexten sie an ihre Grenzen stoßen.

Description:
CONTENT:
This colloquium serves as the regular, internal research forum for members of the CIT Chair of Software Engineering & AI. It is an essential platform for sharing the ongoing progress of their current research projects.

The primary goals of this weekly meeting are to:

Present and Discuss Research Updates: Participants deliver focused presentations outlining their latest findings, methodological approaches, challenges encountered, and next steps in their work related to Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, and their intersection.

Facilitate Collaborative Brainstorming: The colloquium fosters an open, interactive environment for critical discussion and collaborative brainstorming. Researchers receive valuable feedback, explore alternative solutions, and refine their research questions and experimental designs through constructive critique from their peers and the Chair.

Identify Synergies and Future Directions: By gaining insight into the diverse projects within the Chair, participants are encouraged to identify potential synergies between different research threads and collaboratively discuss new, high-impact research ideas and future directions for the group.

Title: ChangeMakers
Description:
CONTENT:
In this module, students will acquire entrepreneurial and design competencies through experiential and scenario-based learning: Set in a future scenario, students will be confronted with signals (based on scientific projections) that make clear what circumstances we may live in in the future. The Impulse Symposium ahead of the project week will provide inspiration and insight to stimulate students' imagination of the future we might live in. During the immersive project week, participants will work in small teams to create a real-life practical solution for a larger societal problem: The first day of the project week creates space to explore what challenges students find relevant and care about, and to explore through design and entrepreneurial methods whether these challenges appear to be worth solving. Throughout the week, students will learn and apply creative problem-solving methods, entrepreneurial thinking and decision-making to work through that challenge they chose. Students will be encouraged to leverage Generative AI tools to illustrate the ideas they create. Students will be guided to apply visualization and prototyping methods as well as reflection techniques that will support them in producing a shareable vision of a livable and lovable future and identify why and how they can contribute to realizing it.
The module is intentionally structured to include an impulse before, as well as iteration and reflection after an immersive project week. In addition, students will receive a reading package. Combining these elements will allow students to start well-prepared, reactive their prior knowledge, inform themselves about relevant methods, and process and appraise new information.

OBJECTIVES:
After successful completion of this module, students will be able to:

● Understand and apply basic entrepreneurial and design competencies, including: Focus for sophisticated problem identification; Courage to take an active role in creating change; Imagination to develop and articulate ideas; Action to take an idea forward towards implementation
● Leverage these competencies to retain hope in the face of critical societal challenges


While developing and articulating solutions in interdisciplinary project teams, students will learn how to plan, manage and conduct a project, mobilize scarce resources, act in the face of uncertainty, collaborate in a team, and present, discuss, and reflect upon their own solutions convincingly. In addition, working with future scenarios will strengthen students' creative confidence and analytical and strategic skills.

Title: Channel Coding
Description:
CONTENT:
This course deals with modern coding approaches for coding and storage. No previous knowledge of channel coding is required.

- Applications of Channel Coding
- Channel Coding Principles:
  Channel Models, Decoding Principles, Hamming Metric
- Finite Fields:
   Groups, Fields, Prime Fields, Extension Fields, Vector Spaces
- Linear Block Codes:
   Definition, Encoding, Coset Decoding, Bounds (Hamming Bound, Singleton Bound, Gilbert- Varshamov Bound), Hamming Codes, Perfect Codes
- Reed-Solomon Codes:
MDS Codes, Definition, Key Equation, Unique Decoding, List Decoding
- BCH Codes:
Minimal Polynomials, Generator and Parity-Check Polynomial, BCH Bound, Efficient Decoding
- Convolutional Codes:
State Diagram, Shift Register, Viterbi Decoding
- Reed-Muller Codes:
Definition, Simplex Code, Plotkin Construction
- Concatenated Codes:
Basic Concepts

OBJECTIVES:
At the end of the course, the students are able to
- state and understand the goal of channel coding,
- name current areas of applications of channel codes and identify the applied code classes,
- to choose a suitable coding scheme, adapt its parameters, evaluate it, and apply decoding algorithms,
- for a known given coding scheme and a given application: to evaluate its error-correcting capabilities and limits, also in comparison to other error-correcting codes and to bounds,
- to understand coding schemes which were not discussed in the lecture after appropriate literature research.

Title: Chromatographie mit ChromX
Description:
CONTENT:
ChromX ist eine vielseitige und leistungsstarke Software die vom Karlsruher Institut für Technologie (KIT) entwickelt wurde, um präparative Chromatographieprozesse für die Proteinreinigung zu simulieren und eine modellbasierte Prozessentwicklung und -optimierung zu ermöglichen. Den experimentellen Anwendungsfall in eine computerbasierte Simulation zu übertragen gewährleistet nicht nur eine große Zeit- und Kosteneinsparung, sondern ermöglicht auch, dass im Labor gängige Trial & Error-Konzept zu umgehen, den Versuchsablauf vorherzubestimmen oder resultierende Ergebnisse zu untermauern. Seitdem die Entwicklung von leistungsstarken Computern rasant voranschreitet, findet auch die Simulation immer größeren Anklang in der Wissenschaft und Industrie. Es ist daher von großem Vorteil Erfahrungen in der Simulation zu sammeln. Um die Vielseitigkeit und den großen industriellen Nutzen des Programms ChromX zu veranschaulichen werden im angebotenen Simulationspraktikum Chromatographie mit ChomX unterschiedliche Anwendungsfälle wie z.B die Aufreinigung von Molkeproteinen mittels Ionenaustauschchromatographie simuliert. Gleichzeitig werden verschiedene Funktionen der Software genutzt um den Prozess zu optimieren, fehlende Parameter durch Schätzung zu ermitteln oder den Einfluss verschiedener Größen zu gewichten. Neben der Simulation mit ChromX werden Schnittstellen zu Matlab und ParaView geschaffen und weitere interessante Anwendungsmöglichkeiten aufgezeigt. Ziel ist es dem Teilnehmer nicht nur Einblicke in die Simulation der Flüssigkeitschromatographie zu gewähren, sondern ein fundiertes Verständnis der Simulationsgrundlagen zu schaffen, so dass diese auf weitere Probleme und Anwendungsfälle übertragen werden können. Das Praktikum wird im Block angeboten.

OBJECTIVES:
Nach der Teilnahme am Praktikum sind die Studenten in der Lage:
- Die Simulationssoftware ChromX Academics zielsicher auf verschiedene präparative Chromatographieprozesse anzuwenden
- Den Einfluss unterschiedlicher Chromatographischer Modelle bewerten und das richtige Modell für den entsprechenden Anwendungsfall zu ermitteln
- Chromatographische Prozesse mithilfe der Software ausgiebig zu analysieren, charakterisieren und optimieren 
- fehlende Parameter mittels einer Schätzungsfunktion zu ermitteln
- durch verschiedene Parameterstudien die Einflussgrößen von Fluid- und Massentransport zu erkennen und zu verstehen
- Die Softwares Matlab und ParaView über eine Schnittstelle einzubinden und zu Analysezwecken anzuwenden

Title: Circuit Theory and Communications
Description:
CONTENT:
The high level of abstraction makes information theory a versatile and powerful tool for the analysis and optimization of a wide variety of communication systems. On the other hand, information theory has no concept of the flow of energy that accompanies the flow of information. Consequently, some important aspects of communication, like transmit power or noise covariance are by no means straight forward. In this lecture, we introduce effective methods which overcome this inherent limitation of information theory. We deal with this problem from a classic circuit theory point of view. This allows correct assessment of the energy flow in communication systems and thereby enables an information theoretic analysis and optimization which is consistent with the underlying physics of the communication system under investigation. After developing appropriate circuit theoretic channel models, we analyze the performance potential of different kinds of multi-antenna radio communication systems. Besides the study of channel capacity, we also develop interesting insight into receive and transmit antenna gain, super-directivity and super-resolution. A knowledge of circuit- and information theory is helpful but not strictly required, as all necessary methods are introduced during the lecture.

OBJECTIVES:
Durch die Teilnahme an den Modulveranstaltungen werden die Studierenden zunächst mit den wesentlichen Inhalten der schaltungstechnischen Mehrtortheorie vertraut gemacht. Anschließend, lernen die Zuhörer wie eine physikalisch konsistente Modellierung von Kommunikationssystem auf Grundlage der schaltungstechnischen Mehrtorbeschreibung erreicht werden kann. Dabei wird als Konkretisierung die Modellierung und Analyse von Mehrantennenkommunikation erarbeitet. Die darauffolgende Systemanalyse offenbart dem Zuhörer dann zum Teil unerwartete Eigenschaften, und eine tiefere Einsicht in das Verhalten und die Optimierung von  Kommunikationssystemen. Der Zuhörer wird in die Lage versetzt, in den benachbarten Disziplinen: Informationstheorie und Signalverarbeitung, eine physikalisch konsistente Kanalmodellierung vorzunehmen.

Title: Data Science for Management Studies II
Description:
CONTENT:
### Description

Database technology is a key technology in practical and applied computer science. The central theme of this course is the modeling, construction, and use of databases.  The specific topics covered in the lecture are as follows:

1. Introduction to Database Systems
2. The Entity Relationship (ER) model and the Enhanced-ER (EER) model
3. The Relational Data Model
4. The Structured Query Language (SQL)
5. Advanced SQL
6. SQL as Data Definition Language (DDL) Data Manipulation Language (DML)
7. Database Programming
8. Physical Database Design
9. Query Processing
10. Concurrency and Recovery
11. NoSQL Databases

OBJECTIVES:
Students are able to apply the essential concepts of relational database systems and can use and evaluate them systematically and in a qualified manner.
The students have the expertise to systematically use a database system starting from the conceptual design to the implementation design to the physical design. They are able to formulate even complex queries in SQL and have a basic understanding of logical and physical optimization based on relational algebra. Furthermore they know how to safe-guard a database application with respect to recovery, concurrency control and authorization.

Title: Climate Change - The complete briefing
Description:
CONTENT:
Based on the newest IPCC report (AR 5) the theoretical background on the physical science basis of climate change, theory and practical application of adaptation and mitigation measures in biological, physical and chemical systems will be presented.

In the accompanying seminar (with Prof. Annette Menzel and Dr. Nicole Estrella, please register for this seminar in TUMonline as well!), selected topics will be intensified in case studies. TUM as a NGO in the UNFCCC process offers an optional possibility also for students to take part in COP and related negotiations.

OBJECTIVES:
After this module, the students can understand the physical basis of the climate system, identify all drivers of climate change and falsify common arguing of "climate sceptics". They can summarize observed changes in the climate system as well as impacts in divers systems and regions. They are able to assess cross-sectorial impacts of climate change in selected areas, to evaluate and develop adaptation and mitigation measures and strategies in biological, physical and chemical systems including an analysis of their effectiveness and cost-effectiveness.

Title: Clinical Applications of Computational Medicine
Description:
CONTENT:
ECTS credits = 6

Computational medicine is a new scientific field in the intersection between mathematics, physics, biostatistics, computer science, electronics, biomedical engineering and medicine. In this lecture we will focus on actual clinical applications of computational medicine using examples from areas like multiple sclerosis, obstetrics, coronary artery disease and sport medicine.

After a short introduction and description about potential and current topics of interest in the medical clinical field the students work in small groups under the guidance of tutors/lecturers/external experts on self-selected projects in the area of "computational medicine". Students are encouraged to build prototypes using the modern technologies available -- sensors, webservices, smartphones, etc -- with the aim to provide solutions to current shortfalls in the clinical practice or in the sports science field.

 

Project topics

Topics of "Clinical Applications of Computational Medicine" are:
1 "Mobile accelerometry" ("Natural Running", "Move Your Heath", "Fall Risk Prediction", "Fall detection")
2 "Fetal Heart Monitoring"
3 "Evidence Based Decision Support in Multiple Sclerosis"
4 "Validation in large Biomedical Databases"

OBJECTIVES:
The objective of this lecture is:
- to gain basic knowledge in selected medical areas (pathology, epidemiology, diagnosis, prognosis, prevention,therapies), in particular multiple sclerosis, obstetrics, coronary artery disease.
- to understand the problems and solutions of biosignal analysis and processing in clinical practice with examples (data acquisition, filtering and anlysis of data from mobile accelerometry, ECG/Physical activity monitoring). 
- to learn how to develop and implement validation studies/clinical studies in the context of intelligent alarm and monitoring systems/ excercise therapy /motivational psychology. 
- to understand the  key success factors for business models in computational medicine with examples.

Description:
CONTENT:
Deep Reinforcement Learning has recently evolved as a vivid field of research that seeps into various industries and applications. In this seminar, we build on the theoretical foundations that we learned in the course "Introduction to Deep Reinforcement Learning" and study a real-world application case in order to understand how to design and implement advanced DRL algorithms to solve use cases of practical interest.

OBJECTIVES:
The objective of this seminar is to provide the students with the necessary skills to conduct independent research in the field of Deep Reinforcement Learning, e.g., in preparation for a successful master thesis or a research stay abroad. Herein, students learn how to i) structure a research question and conduct a literature review, ii) use and develop adequate models, software, and algorithms to solve the research question, iii) write a research paper, especially how to structure and organize results and the corresponding methodology, and iv) work in an academic environment where knwoledge is mostly gained from recent papers and less from standardized books.

Title: Come Together! - Inter/Cultural Practice for Locals, Foreigners and World Inhabitants
Description:
CONTENT:
What does “international” really mean? Beyond stereotypes, we can discover both fascinating diversity and surprising similarities. 
In this seminar, German and international students come together to learn, exchange, and experience cultural diversity in an open and authentic way. Workshops, cultural events, and group projects provide space to explore differences, reflect on them, and build common ground. 
  
Participants strengthen their intercultural sensitivity, learn to navigate challenges in diverse teams, and develop skills for respectful and constructive collaboration. 

  
Key questions we will explore include: 
•	How do unconscious biases and stereotypes shape perception and interaction? 
•	How can I deal with irritating situations in intercultural settings? 
•	How do people build trust and give constructive feedback? 
•	What skills are crucial for intercultural teamwork?

OBJECTIVES:
After the course, participants will be able to… 
•	identify cultural standards and reflect on their own background 
•	recognize and address stereotyping in intercultural contexts 
•	deal more constructively with cultural differences and conflicts 
•	work effectively in diverse teams towards shared goals 
•	use cultural events as opportunities for dialogue and perspective-taking

1. Fundamentals of acoustics (Müller, Vorländer)

CONTENT:

- Digital baseband transmission (pulse shaping, signal detection)
- Passband transmission

OBJECTIVES:
After completion of the course, the students can apply the theoretical foundations of “Nachrichtentechnik” and “Nachrichtentechnik 2” in computer simulations. In addition, the students can characterize and compare communication systems on the basis of pre-defined performance indicators.

Title: Community Ecology
Description:
CONTENT:
The module "Concepts and Methods in Ecology" is divided into two parts:
Introduction to Ecology
Community Ecology

The lecture “Introduction to Ecology” (see separate entry in TUMonline) is dedicated to the basics of ecology and includes sessions on auto-, population-, community- and functional ecology as well as global material cycles.

“Community Ecology” is a combination of lecture inputs and excercises, and addresses various aspects of community ecology in more depths, from our current understanding what a community is, methods to study ecological communities, to patterns of communities on earth and the underlying mechanisms, in particular interspecific interactions. In the course, there will be emphasis on both theoretical concepts as well as examples from the field or practise.

The general structure is that the first two hours are devoted supervised work of the students in the form of paper discussion or running simulation models, followed by input lectures. A detailed plan will be available in Moodle shortly before the start of the semester.

Title: Competition Law and Entrepreneurial Strategies
Description:
CONTENT:
Competition law is concerned with the legal and economic assessment of entrepreneurial strategies on markets. Competition law intends to prohibit behavior that is not an expression of superior business acumen or superior technological capabilities, but represents a restriction of freedom of competition or an abuse of market power. The legal assessment of a corporate strategies essentially depends on an analysis of its positive and negative economic effects on the market. Thus, competition law represents one of the areas of law most permeated by economic thinking. At the same time, competition law and its enforcement by national and European authorities and courts exhibits a strong international and European dimension.
The course will first introduce into the objectives of antitrust law, the basics of competition economics, the legal rules and their enforcement. The concept of undertakings and the delineation of markets will be discussed. Further, the prohibition of cartel agreements and of coordinations between enterprises is dealt with, as well as possible justifications, in particular through the European block exemption regulations. In particular, vertical distribution agreements are also addressed. Then, market power and the prohibition of abuses of market power are discussed.
Have a look what antitrust law is about (1:57) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5M4Ypcqcazw and (10:16) https://youtu.be/Sb_-wfmJnHA.

OBJECTIVES:
Upon completion of the module, students are able to,
(1.) understand the basic principles of European and German antitrust law,
(2.) grasp the economic effects of entrepreneurial competition and innovation strategies on markets and on economic actors and possible efficiencies,
(3.) comprehend the legal framework for the evaluation of entrepreneurial competition and innovation strategies,
(4.) apprehend the interplay of the economic and legal evaluation of entrepreneurial strategies and innovation activities,
(5.) To distinguish business strategies based on superior business acumen or technological capabilities from those strategies that constitute an abuse of market power or impair freedom of competition, and to use this to devise effective entrepreneurial strategies.
(6.) identify situations and legal remedies when a company or a start-up is harmed by cartel agreements or abuses of market power, is impeded from competing or participating in a market, or is restricted in its economic freedom.
(7.) assess concrete competitive situations and real life scenarios legally and economically.

Title: Compliance and Anti-Money Laundering
Description:
CONTENT:
The module aims to provide students with an overview of the main areas of compliance within the European Union. Legal requirements for companies are explained and discussed on the basis of the applicable regulations within the European Union. Case studies are also used for explanation.

In terms of content, the following will be discussed:
- General principles of compliance requirements for companies as well as risk management, e.g. corporate governance, internal control system, four-eyes-principle, risk management, risk analyses).
- Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and counter terrorist financing (CTF), incl. requirements regarding "Know-Your-Customer (KYC)" procedures for the identification of customers and their beneficial owners
- Current methods and typologies of money laundering, especially in the international and digital context (e.g. in connection with blockchain and crypto assets) and their detection
- Data protection (incl. General Data Protection Regulation)
- Supply chain due diligence (including human rights compliance), as the main areas of "ESG compliance".
- Protection of whistleblowers

OBJECTIVES:
After succesfully attending the course, students will be able to,
(1.) understand and explain important principles and the significance of compliance, especially regarding anti-money laundering,
(2.) comprehend, analyse and apply the legal principles of the individual compliance areas that regulate entrepreneurial activity (especially in relation to anti-money laundering).
(3.) recognise and classify the legal implications of typical compliance situations and derive necessary business processes from them,
(4.) present the results of their analysis in a strctured way and in written form.

Title: Components of Flight Control Systems
Description:
CONTENT:
The module Components of Flight Control Systems provides an insight in to state-of-the-art and the future of flight control systems/functions, system architectures, and components. It describes the functions to required by flight control system components, as well as the principles of flight control system architectures. 
In combination with the module “Safety and Certification of Avionics and Flight Control Systems” students receive an overview of the complete product lifecycle of an airborne system with consideration to the specific challenges (e.g. safety, weight, cost) and harsh environments of aerospace applications.
Content:
•	Introduction to flight control system/functions, its components, related aerospace standards, and development processes
•	Principles of aircraft flight control systems (e.g. mechanical, fly-by-wire, etc.) with respect to aircraft categories, flight control automation, and specific failure cases
•	Human-Machine-Interface for flight control systems and the human operator in-the-loop
•	Sensors and navigation systems, working principles, usage, and typical specifications
•	Components and topologies for common primary and secondary flight control actuation systems
•	Flight control computers, their hardware-, software-architectures and toolchains for software development
•	Digital communication in flight control systems 
•	Realization of redundancy and diversity in system architectures, including redundancy management and fault tolerance
•	Verification, integration, and testing as part of the development process for avionics and flight control systems
•	Aerospace recognized standards in the software and hardware development process for airborne equipment
•	Future air mobility concepts, incorporating UAS / UAM-specific aspects of flight control systems and future flight control concepts; (UAS: unmanned aircraft system, UAM: urban air mobility)

OBJECTIVES:
After completing this module, students will have an insight into functions, system architectures, and components of the state-of-the-art and the future of flight control systems. 
In combination with the module “Safety and Certification of Avionics and Flight Control Systems” and its focus on the aerospace development process and corresponding methods, students gain an overview of the whole avionics and flight control systems development process, which is highly relevant for young professionals who want to join the aerospace industry.
After attending the course, students are able to…
•	describe various kinds of flight control systems and their functions
•	name parts of the Human-Machine-Interface, its characteristics and their parameters influencing the human operator in the loop behavior
•	explain the purpose and usage of sensors and navigation systems; interpret sensor specification for component selection
•	list applicable actuation systems for flight controls and describe their topology as well as their failure modes and effects
•	detail the purpose of flight control computers (FCC) and list the advantages and disadvantages of various FCC architectures
•	name different digital communication busses and their topology in flight control systems
•	describe redundancy and diversity concepts in flight control systems as well as redundancy management and fault tolerance 
•	give an overview of verification and testing methods for hardware- and software-components and explain their purpose (e.g. DO-178C, DO-254)
