Title: Entrepreneurship for Students of Information Systems
Description:
CONTENT:
For more details, please see the course syllabus (see course documents at the bottom of this page). The file will be updated regularly.
_____________________

Entrepreneurship, in one form of another, is core to management studies and the backbone of our economy. Not only did every firm have to start from somewhere—entrepreneurship is much more than founding a new firm. Indeed, one of the core aspects of entrepreneurial behavior is that it may happen everywhere, even in the oldest and most established corporations. Entrepreneurship happens everywhere where people dedicate time and effort to create something new and are willing to assume the risk and rewards of such behavior. In addition, large firms need to be able to work with entrepreneurial companies constantly, so a thorough understanding of their workings is needed for every manager and employee.

Entrepreneurial thinking and behavior are also often seen as key to work with uncertainty. It is often said that successful entrepreneurs have been able to beat their low odds and make something out of nothing. Putting it differently: if there is one area of management that could teach us anything about how to “manage” a company through this pandemic, it should be entrepreneurship. But note how already before the pandemic, strategist from all areas (e.g., business, politics, military, …) had noted that the world seemed to be become increasingly uncertain, as captured by the acronym VUCA.

In the context of the digital industries, entrepreneurship takes on a special meaning. Given how IT-related business often require significantly less upfront investment, we have seen a flurry of innovation in and entry into sectors that were considered mature and possibly even boring, such as AirBnB in hotels, or Uber in transportation. Thus, a specific focus of this course will be on understand what IT-based or digital entrepreneurship is, and whether and how it may be different from “normal” entrepreneurship.

OBJECTIVES:
Course objectives
Knowledge Objectives
After the course, students will be able to
- Define and understand entrepreneurship and its variants (e.g., social, corporate, digital)
- Explain steps of the entrepreneurial process and know corresponding tools and risks
- Apply tools to evaluate and realize entrepreneurial opportunities

Skills Objectives
- Improve diagnostic and analytical skills 
- Enhance verbal skills via class and group discussions
- Build up critical thinking and interpretation skills
- Learn how to evaluate different strategic options
- Learn about strategic tools, options, and approaches that may work even under high uncertainty
- Assess and resolve managerial challenges

Learning Objectives
At the end of this course, students will be able to demonstrate understanding, critical assessment, and application of the following:
- The role of entrepreneurs and entrepreneurship in society
- The need for entrepreneurial behavior even inside established organizations
- The risks and rewards of the entrepreneurial journey

Title: Entrepreneurship in Life Sciences
Description:
CONTENT:
The module contains essential subject-specific, methodological, practical, and interdisciplinary aspects for entrepreneurial activity in the field of life sciences. The focus is on the innovation process from idea to market-ready product as well as the specific characteristics of science-based start-ups in the life sciences sector.
Topics covered include:
• Introduction to entrepreneurship and business model development with a focus on life sciences
• Identification of societal challenges and derivation of potential solutions through scientific innovations, based on seminar challenges
• Technology transfer processes and intellectual property (IP)
• Basics of start-up financing, particularly public funding programs and venture capital
• Methods of needs analysis, validation, and user-centered development (e.g., Design Thinking, Lean Startup, Business Model Canvas)
• Development of start-up pitches and communication of complex scientific content for different target groups
The module combines theoretical foundations with practical elements such as case studies, group work, and guest lectures by founders and experts from TUM’s international life sciences ecosystem.

OBJECTIVES:
After successfully completing the module, students will be able to:
•	analyze and assess scientific innovations from the life sciences in terms of their application potential and societal relevance,
•	develop and critically reflect on the central elements of a business model in the life sciences context,
•	identify and evaluate entrepreneurial opportunities and challenges in the field of life sciences,
•	understand and take into account regulatory and market-specific framework conditions for science-based ventures,
•	practically apply methods such as Lean Startup, Design Thinking, and Business Model Canvas to develop and validate business ideas,
•	prepare complex scientific content in a target-group-oriented manner and present it convincingly, particularly in a pitch format,
•	develop entrepreneurial solutions independently as well as in interdisciplinary teams.

Title: Entrepreneurship
Description:
CONTENT:
Entrepreneurship provides students with knowledge of the theoretical concepts and models of entrepreneurship. The set up of this first part is twofold:
(1) Students will acquire in-depth theoretical knowledge on:
- Definitions, regional aspects, and special forms of entrepreneurship in a complex and uncertain environment
- Entrepreneurial individuals, including their personality, creativity, idea development, cognition, opportunity recognition, decision making, and affect
- Entrepreneurial firms, including their growth strategies, strategic alliances, and resources.
(2) Beyond that, students will engage in break out group workshops to personally experience the process of opportunity recognition and development. In these workshops they will work in teams and apply theoretical models from academic literature to real world entrepreneurial problems. Furthermore, students give presentations to the audience and discuss their results.

Strategic and international management targets long term decisions and the sustainable development of the company. In the course of globalization, it is crucial to consider the international dimension of management. Strategic and international management skills are not only important in the management of companies that are doing business across borders, but also within single business functions when shaping competitive strategy. In detail, this module discusses the following aspects:
- Foundations of management
- Stakeholders, objectives, and governance
- Strategic decision making and performance
- Strategy analysis
- Competitive strategies
- Strategy implementation

OBJECTIVES:
First, students will know and be able to explain basic concepts of entrepreneurship including basic definitions, psychological processes and characteristics of the person of the entrepreneur, and potential development paths of young firms. Second, students will transfer this basic knowledge to real world cases. Thus, students will be able to solve entrepreneurial problems in real world settings drawing on theoretical frameworks of the entrepreneurial

Title: Entwicklung Methodischer Forschungsfragen
Description:
CONTENT:
At the Chair of Architectural Informatics, no predefined topics are offered. Each student should apply with their preferred topic one year before their graduation date. During the first semester, students will participate in the course “Methodische Entwicklung von Forschungsfragen,” which will guide them to specify their topics and write their Expose. It is expected to be approx. 10 pages and elaborate on the chosen topic and methodology. During the second semester, the students will write their thesis. Example theses can be found here: https://www.arc.ed.tum.de/ai/lehre/gallery/masterthesen/
If you want to write your thesis at the Chair of Architectural Informatics, please contact Ivan Bratoev, Nick Förster, or Ilayda Memis respective to their research fields.

OBJECTIVES:
A written 5-10 pages expose, presenting the master topic that the student will do in the following semester.

Title: Entwicklung modularer robotischer Systeme
Description:
CONTENT:
Modular robots offer the possibility to quickly and flexibly design and implement solution concepts. In the seminar the handling of Series-Elastic-Link robot modules and their programming in Matlab is learned in small groups. Based on the fundamentals, these are then applied to a wide variety of tasks.

- introduction to robotic actuators using the example of series elastic actuators
- reading and processing sensor data
- PID-controllers in the context of robotic actuators
- mobile robots
- serial robot kinematics, application of direct and inverse kinematics
- design and structure of modular robots consisting of standard elements
- trajectory generation
- computer vision in the context of robotic systems

OBJECTIVES:
After successfully completing this course, students are able to implement robotic projects on their own. The students can differentiate various kinematics and standard configurations. Furthermore, they can use algorithms for direct and inverse kinematics. Students can configure and use PID-controllers. Students understand the principles of series elastic links and can construct and control robotic systems with torque control.

Title: Entwicklungsgenetik der Pflanzen 1
Description:
CONTENT:
This lecture series covers the following topics: polarity, embryogenesis, root development, seedling development, cell cycle, apical meristems, lateral organs, cell morphogenesis, hormones and their role in development.

OBJECTIVES:
This lecture series introduces the advanced student to a critical discussion of basic concepts and ideas in plant developmental biology. It also aims at furthering the independent scientific thinking of students and will provide a solid basis for scientific approaches in other related areas of study.

Title: Entwurf Baukonstruktion
Description:
CONTENT:
Der Entwurf richtet sich an Studierende der Fakultäten für Architektur und Bauingenieurwesen und fördert das integrative Arbeiten der eng verknüpften Disziplinen.
Es wird das konstruktive Entwerfen anhand einer jährlich wechselnden Entwurfsaufgabe geübt, die in Teams von zwei oder drei Studenten aus den beiden unterschiedlichen Disziplinen bearbeitet wird. Jeder bringt seine speziellen Kenntnisse in den Entwurfsprozess ein, um von Anfang an gemeinsam ein detailliertes Projekt zu entwickeln.
Die Gruppen werden von den Assistenten der zwei beteiligten Einrichtungen betreut. Für die zu vertiefenden Bereiche Tragwerk, Brandschutz und energieoptimiertes Bauen stehen Experten zur Unterstützung zur Verfügung.

Der Entwurf ist üblicherweise in drei Phasen aufgeteilt:
- Konzeptphase: Präsentation alternativer Konstruktionen und ihrer Vor- und Nachteile
- Dimensionierung: Detaillierte graphische und numerische Ausarbeitung der verfolgten Planungsvariante, Präsentation von Schichtaufbauten der Regeldetails
- Detaillierung und Ausführungsplanung: Überarbeitung des bisherigen Standes, Detaillierung der Anschlüsse

Zu Beginn des Entwurfs wird eine entwurfsbezogene Exkursion durchgeführt.

OBJECTIVES:
Die Studenten lernen

- Gebäude bzw. Konstruktionen zu planen, zu entwerfen und zu detaillieren und dabei divergierende Anforderungen aus unterschiedlichen Disziplinen zu integrieren
- Planungskonzepte aufzustellen, auf der Basis von Plausibilitätsüberlegungen vielversprechende Varianten herauszudestillieren und schließlich eine Planunslösung in einem fortschreitenden Prozess bis zur Ausführbarkeit zu detaillieren
- ihre Ergebnisse präzise und klar mit Hilfe der üblichen Präsentationsmittel (Vortrag, Pläne, Berichte, Modelle) darzustellen

Title: Entwurf digitaler Systeme mit VHDL und SystemC
Description:
CONTENT:
The course is very work intensive, since three models need to be built. There is no time to attend other seminars, work on a thesis or do an internship in the period of the course.

The return of assignments must be via Moodle according to schedule. Groups with up to 4 students may be formed to build the model. The contribution of each student to the model must be documented in the model.
Delivery deadlines are:
	Memory Model	tbd
	CPU Model		tbd
	RTL Model		tbd

The simulation of the models is essential, the tool Vivado from Xilinx can (and must) be downloaded for that purpose.
Models will be reviewed and contribute overall 50% to the final grade. 

The final oral examination will be done in groups of two students. Schedules will be arranged case by case. The duration of the examination is 30-45 Minutes.

The content of the lecture covers the Hardware description languages VHDL and SystemC, design methodology with VHDL and SystemC, VHDL/SystemC modeling, VHDL/SystemC simulation and VHDL register-transfer synthesis. There will be  computer lab exercises in VHDL/SystemC modeling, automatic synthesis and selected synthesis methods.

OBJECTIVES:
The students will learn the abstraction, modeling and design techniques. Furthermore, the students will be familiar with an industrial design system and the modeling language VHDL (WS) and System C (SS).

Title: Entwurf Holzbau
Description:
CONTENT:
Der Entwurf richtet sich an Studierende der Fakultäten für Architektur und Bauingenieurwesen und fördert das integrative Arbeiten der eng verknüpften Disziplinen. Es wird das konstruktive Entwerfen anhand einer jährlich wechselnden Entwurfsaufgabe geübt, die in Teams von zwei bis vier Studenten aus den unterschiedlichen Disziplinen bearbeitet wird. Jeder bringt seine speziellen Kenntnisse in den Entwurfsprozess ein, um von Anfang an gemeinsam ein detailliertes Projekt zu entwickeln. Die Gruppen werden von den Assistenten der zwei beteiligten Einrichtungen betreut. Für die zu vertiefenden
Bereiche wie Tragwerk und Brandschutz stehen Experten zur Unterstützung zur Verfügung. Die Tragwerksplanung soll den Entwurf, über die gesamte Dauer aufgeteilt, in drei Phasen begleiten:
- Tragwerkskonzept (Entwurfsplanung): Darstellung und Erläuterung der gewählten Primärtragsysteme für die einzelnen Gebäudeteile sowie Abgrenzung und Wertung gegenüber optionalen Tragsystemen
- Ausarbeitung und Dimensionierung (Genehmigungsplanung): Gliederung des Tragwerks/Positionierung; Ermittlung der Einwirkungen, Lasten und Schnittgrößen auf das Tragwerk; Bemessung und Dimensionierung des Primärtragsystems der Turnhalle sowie Vordimensionierung der Tragsysteme der übrigen Gebäudeteile; Darstellung sowie Bemessung und Dimensionierung des Aussteifungssystems; Bemessung und Dimensionierung von ausgewählten Detailpunkten
- Darstellung, Detaillierung und Bauplanung (Ausführungsplanung): Grundriss, Ansichten, Schnitte, ggf. Axonometrie und Präsentationsmodell des Trag- und Aussteifungssystems, Darstellung der 3-5 ausgewählten Detailpunkte, Erläuterungen zu Vorfertigung, Transport und Montage, Erläuterungen zu Möglichkeiten der Demontage/Wiederverwendbarkeit und des Recyclings.
Es ist eine dreitägige Exkursion zum Zwecke der Vorstellung von beispielhaften Bauten und der Gruppenbildung vorgesehen.

OBJECTIVES:
Nach der Teilnahme am Modul Entwurf Holzbau sind die Studierenden in der Lage, die folgenden maßgebenden Anforderungen zu verstehen und im Planungsprozess eines Bauwerkes anzuwenden:
- Gebäude bzw. Konstruktionen zu planen, zu entwerfen und zu detaillieren und dabei divergierende Anforderungen aus unterschiedlichen Disziplinen zu integrieren
- Planungskonzepte aufzustellen, auf der Basis von Plausibilitätsüberlegungen vielversprechende Varianten herauszudestillieren und schließlich eine Planungslösung in einem fortschreitenden Prozess bis zur Ausführbarkeit zu detaillieren
- ihre Ergebnisse präzise und klar mit Hilfe der üblichen Präsentationsmittel (Vortrag, Pläne, Berichte, Modelle) darzustellen.

Title: Entwurf unbemannter Flugsysteme
Description:
CONTENT:
The module covers the following topics:
- Introduction to UAVs: terminology, historical development, and classification schemes
- Overview of relevant civil and military regulations, such as EASA standards and LufABw (German Military Aviation Authority) requirements
- UAV missions, roles, and system categories (ranging from Micro UAVs to HALE, including UCAV and VTOL configurations)
- Payload configurations and their comparison to manned aviation systems
- System components of a UAS, including communication systems, ground control stations, launch and recovery systems, and support equipment
- Detailed analysis of UAV components, such as structural elements, aerodynamics, propulsion systems, and onboard sensors
- Design methods and tools for small UAVs, including conceptual design strategies and software applications like XFOIL
- Reliability and safety considerations, with a distinction between safety (technical integrity) and security (operational protection)
- Human-machine interaction, addressing interface design, ethical considerations, and societal acceptance
- Future perspectives, such as swarming technology, autonomous systems, and alternative navigation methods

OBJECTIVES:
After successfully completing this module, students will be able to:
- understand regulatory requirements and framework conditions for UAVs, including current European regulations and military standards (e.g. STANAG 4706);
- classify UAV missions and operational scenarios, such as MALE/HALE, VTOL, and UCAV systems;
- evaluate different UAV payloads and their integration into the overall system architecture;
- describe the structure and functional principles of an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) and the complete unmanned aircraft system (UAS);
- apply specific design methods for small UAVs (below 150 kg), including performance estimation, propulsion system selection, and the use of design tools such as XFOIL;
- reflect on aspects of system reliability, operational safety, and human-machine interaction in the UAV context.

Title: Entwurf und Wissenschaft
Description:
CONTENT:
Inhalt und Aufbau des Seminars 	
Landschaftsarchitektur, die sich über die bisher gängigen Lösungswege der Profession hinausbewegt, trifft auf ein offenes Feld entwerferischer und wissenschaftlicher Methoden. Das Seminar Entwurf und Wissenschaft vermittelt Bachelorstudierenden hierfür Grundlagen der allgemeinen Wissenschaftstheorie und beleuchtet vor allem methodische Gemeinsamkeiten und Unterschiede von Forschen und Entwerfen.
Anhand von Wettbewerbsverfahren, Projektbeispielen oder thematisch vertiefender Literaturarbeit wird eine Übersetzung in die Profession der Landschaftsarchitektur überprüft und diskutiert. Das Seminar Entwurf und Wissenschaft bereitet damit auch eine spätere methodische Vertiefung und Anwendung im Seminar Research by Design im Masterstudium vor und eröffnet einen Ausblick in die methodische Arbeitsweise eines Promotionsstudiums. 

Block I:
Im ersten Block werden die Grundlagen wissenschaftlichen Arbeitens anhand einzelner Schlüsselbegriffe und in Gruppenarbeit behandelt und präsentiert. 
Der Focus liegt dabei im Zusammenführen bzw. qualifizieren der bereitgestellten und empfohlenen Veröffentlichungen und Materialien sowie dem eigenen Suchen und Integrieren weiterer Veröffentlichungen.

Block II:
Im zweiten Block überprüfen wir mit Hilfe der erarbeiteten Grundlagen aus Block I eine Theorie bzw. (entwerferische) Haltung aus der Profession Landschaftsarchitektur anhand von Veröffentlichungen, Entwürfen und Projekten. 
Die währen der Gruppenarbeit gefunden Wettbewerbsergebnisse, Publikationen und realisierten Projekte werden aufbereitet, präsentiert und beispielhaft mit Blick auf mögliche Theoriebildung, Schlussfolgerungen oder gar weiterführende Hypothesen reflektiert. Während der Arbeit an Block II übernehmen die Seminarteilnehmer Patenschaft für ihre, in Block I vorgestellten wissenschaftlichen Grundlagen und Begriffe. 

Themenreflexion:
Die abschließende schriftliche Themenreflexion jedes Seminarteilnehmers dient der Einordnung der eigenen Themen aus Block I und II in das Gesamtthema und der (eignen) Überprüfung gelernter Bezüge zwischen den Themenblöcken.

Title: Erfolgreiche Innovationen - Netzwerke, Finanzierung und Management
Description:
CONTENT:
The future viability and resilience of national economies is determined more than ever by their innovative capacity in technological, ecological and social dimensions. Successful knowledge and innovation systems make a significant contribution here. In these systems, dedicated minds of students, researchers and entrepreneurs drive technology-based ideas (inventions) in networks of universities, research institutions and private industry with appropriate funding in a targeted manner to impact-oriented innovations. How these ideas, knowledge and research results can be successfully applied and successfully solve challenges such as climate change and demographic change, and what framework conditions are necessary here, especially with regard to the networks to be involved, financing and management, is the content of this lecture.

OBJECTIVES:
The students understand the societal value (economic, ecological, social) of a successful innovation. Furthermore, they will gain a deeper understanding of the necessary framework conditions to develop their technological invention (Invention) into a successful innovation in application. The path and access to networks and funding opportunities for collaborative research with large companies, medium-sized companies or start-ups on a national and international level can be understood. The relevance to protect one's research ideas, intellectual property exploitation oriented and the role in successful technology transfer is understood. Furthermore, the course participants will gain the understanding of which steps are necessary for a successful innovation via a technology-based spin-off.

Title: Ernährung und Symptomatik der Ernährungsstörungen von Pflanzen in hydroponischen Systemen
Description:
CONTENT:
Das Modul Ernährung und Symptomatik der Ernährungsstörungen von Pflanzen in hydroponischen Systemen befasst sich mit der Zusammensetzung von Nährlösungen und der Steuerung der Nährstoffversorgung in hydroponischen Systemen sowie der Phänologie typischer Ernährungsstörungen am Beispiel von ausgewählten gartenbaulichen Kulturen.

Wichtige Inhalte sind:

- die Zusammensetzung von Nährlösung aus Einzelsalzen basierend auf Wachstumsfaktoren (Biomasse, Transpiration, Einstrahlung) herzuleiten und zu berechnen,
- das Herstellen von Nährlösungen durch Stammlösungen z.B. nach dem „A-/B-Bak-Prinzip“,
- das Aufstellen und Durchführen eines Demonstrationsversuches für Ernährungsstörung inkl. Vorkultur der Versuchspflanzen,
- die Symptome von typischen Ernährungsstörung an verschiedenen Kulturpflanzen im geschützten (Mangel/- Überschuss) zu beschreiben, zu diagnostizieren und zu dokumentieren,
- ausgewählte Verfahren der quantitativen Analytik für wässrigen Lösungen bei Nährlösungen kennenzulernen, eigenständig anzuwenden (Bsp.: pH, EC, N, P, Cl und Wasserhärte) und unter Anleitung zu interpretieren,
- Pflanzenwachstum zu erfassen und mit den Ergebnissen der analytischen Verfahren in Beziehung zu setzen, Ergebnisse aus den Beobachtungen und Messungen aufzubereiten und zu präsentieren.

OBJECTIVES:
Nach erfolgreicher Teilnahme an der Modulveranstaltung, verstehen Studierende die Zusammensetzung von Nährlösungen für die Pflanzenproduktion in hydroponischen Systemen und können diese eigenständig aus Einzelsalzen bzw. Säuren berechnen und ansetzen.
Im Hinblick auf eine bedarfsgerechte Pflanzenernährung verstehen sie die Bedeutung von verschiedenen Einzelsalzen und physikalisch-chemischen Nährlösungsparametern für die Verfügbarkeit von Nährelementen im Nährlösungssystem und können hierfür wesentliche Einflussfaktoren sowie Maßnahmen zur Steuerung dieser Verfügbarkeit

Title: Ethical and moral aspects of intercultural corporate management
Description:
CONTENT:
The seminar aims at a management-oriented ethical-moral foundation and values in entrepreneurship. Morality is shaped by our beliefs and values. People make decisions or react based on their conscious but also unconscious value system. What is allowed and what is forbidden? And does that fit with our own expectations and alignments? Personality formation as a reflected social construct refers to our moral canon. The value orientation and standard systems are not only decisive for the development of individual leadership skills, but they also cultivate a successful corporate culture. During the seminar, students learn to question and reflect on critical processes. 
The consequences of globalization can be found in many areas of everyday life. The effects of globalization are particularly evident in the increase and acceleration of international communication processes. Furthermore, there are extensive changes in society in many areas: politics, economy, culture. In this regard, new forms of organization are emerging in the economic context, and international cooperation is increasing.
In the context of today's globalization processes, intercultural competence seems to be more important than ever. In international companies, in non-governmental organizations as well as at the political level. This strength combined with a well-founded professional qualification is the tool for success. Whether as a manager, head of department or expert, shaping the future depends on successful communication, and successful communication requires the ability to think outside the box.
The fact that we talk to each other no longer means that we communicate with each other. Against the background of various theories, the seminar will also show what constitutes communication, how it succeeds or when it fails and how culture creates the basis for the inner cohesion of a society.
In this context, a special role is assigned to intercultural communication, which focuses on the peculiarities of understanding between different cultures.
Because it is not only the language that distinguishes countries and cultures from each other. The gestures, facial expressions, tone of voice, physical distance and posture also vary depending on the culture. 
The content of the block seminar provides a transdisciplinary approach to processes of social communication and individual education in societies that are caught between globalization processes, increasing socio-economic and political-cultural diversification and the associated effects of an ambivalent culture of debate, which are based on a moral and ethical canon.

OBJECTIVES:
On the technical side, the participants should deepen their knowledge and skills in width and in a special field. In addition, their methodological and analytical skills, in particular their ability to process complex problems, should be recessed. The seminar introduces students to interdisciplinary perspectives and working methods and prepares them for areas of application across the entire spectrum of responsible corporate management.

This includes, in particular, the ability to model a value-based leadership role and the ability to quickly familiarize yourself with new areas of application. The participants gain an overall view of a complex topic, which enables them to recognize interdisciplinary and intercultural connections.

In addition to technical qualifications, the seminar also deepens key qualifications. Great importance is attached to the ability to make presentations, to self-reliance, the ability to work in a team, knowledge and experience in project management and, within the scope of the possibilities to personal management qualifications.

The ability to critically reflect on one's own work and the willingness to take responsibility for the results of this work are promoted. Students are made aware of the need to consider technical, economic, and ethical and moral conditions when using digital systems.
Skills: ['Ethical awareness and data responsibility', 'Business ethics', 'Cross-functional collaboration', 'Stakeholder and requirements management', 'Critical thinking and decision-making']

Title: Ethics & Responsibility
Description:
CONTENT:
Discussions about ethics – about what we ought to do – can be found everywhere. These discussions range from dull to sensational, from abstract to vivid. In this course, we explore some of the main approaches to ethics, starting with more systematic philosophical accounts, and then looking at ethical issues in the context of the environment and technology. These issues cross the boundaries of philosophy, sciences, and humanities, and raise questions about our roles as humans in the universe we inhabit. 
Questions we will discuss include: can we use abstract theories to help us decide what to do? Is it possible or desirable to be ethically consistent? Do we have a moral obligation to non-human or non-living things? How important are co-operation and competition in human lives, and in nature more broadly? Is technology ethically neutral? What are the ethical risks of emerging technologies? What is the relationship between ethics and science? Is the internet dead? How much control do we and should we have over our own attention span?

OBJECTIVES:
By exploring both traditional ethical theories, and a range of examples related to the environment and technology, you will learn to:
-	Explain, analyse and evaluate well-known theories about ethics
-	Understand and defend a view on the applicability of ethical theories to different contexts
-	Identify, understand and articulate key ethical issues across a range of topics 
-	Develop an understanding of the relationship between ethics, science, and technology; and more broadly between facts and values.
Skills: ['Ethics', 'Moral philosophy', 'Environmental ethics', 'Critical thinking and decision-making', 'Research-oriented mindset']

Title: Ethics of AI
Description:
CONTENT:
Das Modul befasst sich aus philosophischer Perspektive mit den vielfältigen Problemen der Künstlichen Intelligenz (KI). Sowohl historisch als auch systematisch werden die grundlegenden Begriffe, Konzepte und Strömungen der KI-Entwicklungen und deren Einflüsse auf gesellschaftliche Transformationsprozesse reflektiert und ethisch bewertet. Anhand ausgewählter Fallbeispiele sollen diese Unterscheidungen und Bewertungen dann auf grundlegende gesellschaftliche Spannungsfelder im Einsatz von KI-Systemen angewendet werden, um daran einen verantwortungsvollen Umgang mit dieser Schlüsseltechnologie zu ermöglichen. Im Einzelnen geht es um Themen wie die folgenden:
• Systematisch-historische Einbettung der Künstlichen Intelligenz im geschichtlichen Kontext von Technologieentwicklungen
• Begriffliche Bestimmung und Ausdifferenzierung von KI in den verschiedenen Bedeutungs- und Verwendungsweisen
• Kritische Reflexion der KI in unterschiedlichen Anwendungsbereichen (z.B. Medizin, Mobilität, Militär, Arbeitsmarktentwicklung, Mensch-Maschine-Schnittstelle etc.)
• Ethisch-moralische Bewertung aktueller KI-Entwicklungen und deren verantwortungsbewussten Anwendungen
• Reflexion und Bewertung von zukünftigen Entwicklungen von KI-Systemen: Möglichkeiten und Grenzen dieser Schlüsseltechnologie

OBJECTIVES:
Das Modul vermittelt Grundkenntnisse in der Philosophie der Künstlichen Intelligenz (KI). Danach besitzen die Studierenden die Fähigkeit, über die verschiedenen Begriffe und Anwendungsbereiche von KI kritisch zu reflektieren und diese Technologie in einen umfassenden gesellschaftlich-sozialen Gesamtkontext einzubetten. Die Studierenden sind in der Lage, in der Auseinandersetzung mit der Fachliteratur die jeweiligen Chancen, aber auch Grenzen dieser Schlüsseltechnologie sinnvoll beurteilen zu können und einen aufgeklärten Umgang mit aktuellen Entwicklungen zu gewinnen. Sie sind imstande, Ihre Werturteile argumentativ zu begründen und bei Bedarf erforderliche Abwägungen zu treffen.
Skills: ['Ethics', 'Artificial Intelligence', 'Machine Learning', 'Societal impact', 'Critical thinking and decision-making', 'Ethical awareness and data responsibility']

Title: Ethics of Generative AI
Description:
CONTENT:
Digital technology is always getting more complex, and it becomes more interwoven with the human lifeworld. The problems of understanding the nature and implications of digital technology express in radically different and often contradictory conceptions. The module examines the major conceptions of digital technology in view of Generative AI and the respective ethical consequences they imply. A particular emphasis is on the changes Generative AI brings to the perception, action, and thinking of individuals and their social relations. Using selected examples, not only concepts for understanding (digital) media and models of ethical argumentation are presented, but also options for evaluating and dealing with ethical conflicts are discussed.

OBJECTIVES:
Upon successful completion of this module, students will be able to:

describe the prevalent and often implicitly presupposed conceptions of digital technology 

explain the ethical issues entailed by the respective conception

read and analyze philosophical texts

apply philosophical and ethical considerations to concrete case studies 

present and discuss academic papers on this complex interdisciplinary topic 

improve their skills in text analysis, group work, and presentation to an interdisciplinary and international online audience
Skills: ['Ethics', 'Artificial Intelligence', 'Digital technology', 'Generative AI', 'Critical thinking and decision-making', 'Ethical awareness and data responsibility']

Title: Ethik für Nerds Campus Heilbronn
Description:
CONTENT:
Topics comprise:
* Information and communication technologies whose invention and also the timing of their invention have had a lasting impact on our society. From this point of view, today's technologies such as the World Wide Web or social media will be considered from an ethical point of view and a look into the future will be taken.

* How dependent are we on emerging technologies? Safety critical systems are by no means always safe, which can be well observed in numerous incidents. What happens, for example, when self-driving cars are controlled by third parties due to a security vulnerability? Is such dependence even justifiable from an ethical point of view?

* What influence do the new media have on the individual?What drives young people to give everything to look good in a virtual world?

* How should the influence of social media on politics and society be looked at? After the initial euphoria, critical voices are increasingly being raised.

* Within this context, it is worth taking a closer look at the topic of ''fake news'' within the context of image and language manipulation.

* How justifiable is it at all to work on information technology for modern weapons systems?

* The gambler of tomorrow: What is happening ''thanks to computer science'' on the international financial markets?

OBJECTIVES:
After the successful completion of this module, students are able to judge a computer scientists relevance to society from an ethical perspective and are able to better judge on their decisions.
Skills: ['Ethics', 'Information and communication technologies', 'Web technologies', 'Social media', 'Future studies', 'Ethical awareness and data responsibility', 'Critical thinking and decision-making']

Title: Evidenzbasierte Entscheidungen auf der Grundlage von Big Data Analytics
Description:
CONTENT:
ATTENTION: In the winter term the course is held in English and in the summer term in German.

The module starts with a virtual kick-off event (webinar). Afterwards, students will have access to the electronic learning content, which is available in form of interactive scripts as well as access to a data center where the course-specific data sets are stored. In addition, they can view video tutorials on the e-learning platform Moodle about the use of open source tools (e.g. the statistics software R) in order to acquire core competencies for data analysis processes. In the accompanying case studies, the basic steps of data preparation, which are necessary for Big Data analyses, are carried out on the basis of case studies. For this purpose, a webinar will be created that explains these central steps in a comprehensible manner and motivates the students to learn independently through immediate application.  
For the case study specific evaluations, the students fall back on R and have to evaluate various data sets with the help of the described procedures and visualize their results visually. 
The case studies consist of the following elements, whereby individual elements are emphasized more strongly and the degree of difficulty increases over the semester:
1. economic theory/questions (including interviews with practitioners)
2. data preparation and explorative data analysis
3. targeted data processing (model estimation and analysis)
4. interpretation of the results with regard to 1. (but also dangers of the analyses, e.g. sham causalities, or ethical aspects connected with the analyses, etc.)

According point 4. additional online offers are made available via the learning platforms and students are encouraged to discuss the ethical problem cases in internal forums. These discussions are moderated by the tutors. At the end of the semester a current outlook will be given. This should enable the tutors to set specific current priorities in this rapidly developing topic area. At this time, a questionnaire-based evaluation will also be carried out, which is intended to make the acquisition of basic IT skills measurable within the framework of Big Data analysis.

OBJECTIVES:
After completing the course "Evidence-based decisions based on Big Data Analytics" students should be able to
(1) Contrast the characteristics of big data analysis with traditional business theories/decisions/methods (especially regarding data creation, data storage, data preparation),
(2) Evaluate (application) possibilities of Big Data for economists,
(3) Implement basic methods of data collection, -preparation and evaluation,
(4) Assess challenges in using Big Data (e.g. data protection, data security, ethical considerations, etc.),
(5) Identify possible trends and developments of Big Data Analytics and use them for their future activities or for starting a business.
Skills: ['Big Data', 'Data Analytics', 'Evidence-based decision making', 'Statistical analysis', 'Data visualization', 'Python', 'R']

Title: Experimental Creation
Description:
CONTENT:
Titel: On the move – on searching, travelling, hunting, losing, longing, travelling again
Lecturer: Ute Heim

Since the beginning of what we call humanity, our species has always moved, wandered about, sometimes settled down and then moved on again. What makes us move? What form does movement take? Where does this longing or necessity to move originate in? In this course you will explore and experience these questions through artistic methods and research. 

This Winter semester offers an intensive artistic journey through exploring performance, spatial installation and other media. By using workshop formats, studio sessions and critiques, paired with critical research on the subject, participants will develop artworks that are finally shown in a public exhibition.

OBJECTIVES:
Unser Kurs gliedert sich in drei Phasen: Explorations-, Realisierungs- und Werkpräsentationsphase. In der ersten Phase erforschen Sie das Semesterthema und finden Ihren ganz eigenen Zugang dazu. In der zweiten Phase werden Sie eine künstlerische Arbeit realisieren, die Ihre Erfahrungen widerspiegelt. In der dritten Phase suchen und finden Sie einen Weg, Ihr Kunstwerk im Ausstellungsraum zu installieren.

Title: Experimental investigation of space propulsion phenomena
Description:
CONTENT:
•	Aufbau und Funktionsweise von Prüfständen für flüssige Bi-Prop Raumfahrtantriebe 
•	Wiederholung Physikalische, Thermodynamische und Fluidmechanische Grundlagen:
o	Ziolkowski-Gleichung
o	Eindimensionale, reibungsfreie Strömung im Bezug auf adiabatische Expansion in Laval-Düsen
o	Schub, spezifischer Impuls, Schubkoeffizient
o	Charakteristische Geschwindigkeit (c*)
o	Expansionsverhältnis, Wirkungsgrad und Effizienz
o	Treibstoffauswahl, Mischungsverhältnis
o	Kompressible Strömung
•	reale vs. ideale Prozesse
•	Testumgebungen:
o	Unterschiede zwischen Boden- und Vakuumtests
o	Testbench vs. Flugsysteme
•	Sicherheitsaspekte:
o	Handhabung von Wasserstoff (Versprödung, Leckage, Explosionsgefahr)
o	Sauerstoffsicherheit
•	Versuchsplanung:
o	Methoden der Versuchsplanung
o	Erstellung von Testsequenzen und Prüfstandsvorbereitung
o	Steuerung und Monitoring des Versuchsablaufs
•	Messtechnik:
o	Messkette, Auswahl und Kalibrierung von Sensoren
o	Fehlerfortpflanzung, Unsicherheiten in der Messdatenerhebung
o	Grundlagen der Messdatenverarbeitung (Post-Processing)
•	Einführung in LabVIEW zur Prüfstandssteuerung

OBJECTIVES:
Nach erfolgreicher Teilnahme am Seminar sind die Studierenden in der Lage:
•	einen Versuchsplan für eine experimentelle Testkampagne auf Basis wissenschaftlicher Fragestellungen eigenständig zu erarbeiten,
•	die grundlegende Funktionsweise sowie Aufbaukomponenten eines Prüfstands für flüssige Bi-Prop Raumfahrtantriebe zu beschreiben und zu verstehen, einschließlich Mess- und Steuersystemen,
•	sicherheitsrelevante Aspekte beim Umgang mit gefährlichen Stoffen, insbesondere Wasserstoff und Sauerstoff, zu analysieren und zu bewerten,
•	experimentelle Einschränkungen kritisch zu reflektieren und bei der Planung zu berücksichtigen,
•	Messergebnisse strukturiert auszuwerten und sowohl schriftlich als auch mündlich im wissenschaftlichen Kontext zu präsentieren.

This course covers the basics and essentials of classical mechanics for first-semester physics bachelor students. Title: Experimentelles Gestalten I
Description:
CONTENT:
Titel: Time-based Presence
Lecturer: Elke Dreier

Presence is understood as something that arises dynamically through movement, interaction, and shifting attention, rather than as a fixed state. It can be experienced, activated or mediated physi-cally, emotionally, or through directed attention. In this course, students develop artistic projects that focus on physical and spatial experiences. By examining the interplay between bodies – space – perception, various modes of presence will be explored.

A central focus lies on the multimodality of perception and embodied experiences. Alongside the question of what makes presence come alive, the course investigates how mixed realities trans-form states of presence and what new layers emerge – both spatially and in the ways individuals engage with environments.

Through time-based artistic projects, students explore how presence can be experienced, staged, and reconfigured. Works in all artistic media are welcome. 
Students develop individual or group projects, which will be exhibited at the end of the semester. Group meetings take place on a weekly basis.

OBJECTIVES:
Nach der Teilnahme ist die/der Studierende in der Lage, Qualitäten und Eigenheiten eines Objektes, einer Form oder eines Materials selbstständig aufzuspüren und zu benennen. 
Sie/er kann künstlerische Qualitäten einer Arbeit wahrnehmen und benennen. 
Sie/er ist in der Lage, aus ihren/seinen Beobachtungen eigene kreative Herangehensweisen zu entwickeln und in einer gestalterischen Arbeit zu visualisieren. 

Sie/er ist in der Lage kreative Lösungswege selbst zu entwickeln. 
Die Wahrnehmungsfähigkeit und Selbstkritik gegenüber der eigenen gestalterischen Arbeit hat sich geschärft.

Title: Exploring Heart Development & Regeneration – Stem Cells in Action
Description:
CONTENT:
According to a report from the European Society of Cardiology published in 2020, cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of mortality in Europe. Animal models, such as mice and rats, have been valuable in the investigation of the etiology and pathogenesis of CVDs. However, interspecies differences limit the translation of the findings from basic research to the clinic. To overcome these obstacles, complex three-dimensional cardiac tissues have been developed advancing basic as well as pre-clinical research studies. Professor Moretti's lab has established a novel protocol that enables the generation of cardiac organoids from human induced pluripotent stem cells. These organoids, the so-called epicardioids, show self-organization of highly functional ventricular myocardium and epicardium, providing a platform for investigating human cardiac development and the pathogenesis of CVDs in a dish. As part of the research internship, participants work under supervision on current research projects of the Chair of Regenerative Medicine of Cardiovascular Diseases. The internship focuses on hiPSC culturing, cardiomyocyte differentiation techniques, generation of epicardioids, and the analysis of their molecular and cellular properties. The general aim is to gain a deeper insight into stem cells as a model for cardiovascular diseases.

Title: Fabrication and characterization of single-photon detectors
Description:
CONTENT:
This practical training deals with the fabrication and characterization of single-photon detectors, a component that detects single photons with high efficiency and which is essential for photonic quantum technologies. After a theoretical introduction to the topic, the students will under supervision carry out all the nano- and micro-fabrication steps which are needed to fabricate single-photon detectors. Next, they will characterize the fabricated devices electrically as well as optically. Finally, the efficiency of the fabricated detectors is determined.

OBJECTIVES:
After successful completion of the module the students are able to: 
- Assess the theoretical background of single-photon detectors and their applications in quantum technologies
- Perform the fabrication of superconducting films via sputtering
- Perform nano- and micro-fabrication (electron beam lithography, optical lithography, reactive ion etching, e-beam metallization, …)
- Characterize components with applications in quantum technologies (electrically and optically)
- Assess the metrics of single-photon detectors

Title: Facilitation Skills for Transdisciplinary Work Processes
Description:
CONTENT:
Moderation and facilitation are a crucial aspect of outcome-oriented professional communication. The word ‘facilitation’ stems from the Latin word ‘facile’, which means ‘easy’. A facilitator’s task is it to enable groups of people to become constructively active and to ease them into finding consensus (or at least a smallest common denominator) so that they can find ways to engage with a task at hand in a way that is feasible for all stakeholders. This is especially important in study and workplace settings where participants with a diverse set of knowledge, values, and motivations come together and work towards a shared goal, such as in multi- ,inter- and transdisciplinary professional contexts. The workshop provides participants with methods and techniques to design, implement, and reflect successful meetings, workshops, field activities and group processes.

OBJECTIVES:
Participants will have the following learning outcomes
•	An introduction to contemporary communication theories and an overview of current approaches in facilitation: classical, agile, and digital 
•	A deep understanding of the role of the moderator and the fundamental techniques of engagement that all fruitful facilitation is based on: active listening and asking questions in a constructive way
•	Values, value-neutrality and status in facilitation processes
•	An understanding of the different kinds of moderation tasks and processes (team meeting, team building, planning larger processes with diverse stakeholders )
•	Techniques that help to structure and visualize group discussion processes
•	Best practices of planning, conducting, reviewing, and documenting a facilitation/moderation process
•	An outlook into eco-facilitation as well as creative and ludic moderation methods

Title: Family Matters. Eine literarische Lese- und Schreibwerkstatt
Description:
CONTENT:
Welche Erinnerungen wiegen schwer? Welche müssen wir immer wieder erzählen? Der stolze erste Schultag. Der ständige Streit am Mittagstisch. Das Schweigen. Angst, Scham, Beistand. Was heißt es heute, Tochter zu sein? Oder Vater? Die Familie ist die kleinste gesellschaftlicher Zelle. Deshalb sind Familienerzählungen, wir werden einige lesen, niemals nur privat. Mit dem Erfolg autofiktionaler Werke sind Herkunftsgeschichten in den letzten Jahren vermehrt und neu erzählt und publiziert worden. Wo komme ich her, wer bin ich? Ein Leben lang justieren wir die Antworten auf diese Fragen neu. Hier wollen wir das schreibend versuchen. In sehr gezielten Übungen – dem Porträt, dem Konflikt, der Erinnerung – wollen wir uns erproben und in den Spuren sehr alter Erzählungen gehen.

OBJECTIVES:
Eine Schreibwerkstatt gibt denen, die schon länger schreiben, die Gelegenheit, eigene literarische Texte in einer geschützten Öffentlichkeit vorzustellen und zu besprechen, um deren Stärken und Schwächen klarer zu erkennen. Zudem bietet sie all denen, die an kreativen Prozessen interessiert sind, die Möglichkeit, sich selbst in Schreibübungen auszuprobieren. Rückgekoppelt an ausgewählte literarische Lektüren sollen sich Lesen und Schreiben verschränken. Wichtig sind zudem die praktischen Übungen, die Impulse für eigene Geschichten und die eigene Ausdrucksfähigkeit geben und einen bewussteren Umgang mit Sprache fördern.

Title: Faser, Matrix- und Verbundwerkstoffe mit ihren Eigenschaften
Description:
CONTENT:
Various fibre types and matrices exist with different properties resulting in diverse mechanical properties in the composite component. The lecture will give an introduction in these fibre types and their production as well as in the various types of matrix systems (thermoset and thermoplastic), their synthesis and properties. Additionally, the carbon yarns, also known as rovings, undergo a textile process to improve their handling ability and their following process ability. These textile processes and their finished products, i.e. woven fabrics, non crimped fabrics, braidings and tailored fibre placements, will be addressed to.

OBJECTIVES:
Nach der Teilnahme an der Modulveranstaltung "Faser-, Matrix-, und Verbundwerkstoffe mit ihren Eigenschaften" sind die Studierenden in der Lage, Unterschiede zwischen den Ausgangsmaterialien und deren Herstellung bzw. Weiterverarbeitung zu Komponenten zu verstehen und Faser bzw. Matrixmaterialien anhand ihres mechanischen Eigenschaftsprofils und ihrer Kostenstruktur auszuwählen und zu bewerten. Die Studierenden können unterschiedliche Verarbeitungstechnologien in der Textil- und Infusionstechnik zu beschreiben und nach technologischen und wirtschaftlichen Gesichtspunkten zu evaluieren. Außerdem können sie die Potenziale der Faserverbundwerkstoffe erkennen und die Möglichkeiten innerhalb der Verarbeitungsprozesskette einschätzen und neue Herstellkonzepte auf Bauteilebene entwerfen.

• apply effective prompting techniques to get the needed support from AI.

• integrate AI into their personal study routines to optimize time management and learning outcomes.

Title: FE-Modelling, Simulation and Validation
Description:
CONTENT:
Modelling and Simulation of structural problems with the Finite Element Method (FEM). This course has a strong focus on hands-on exercises in the computer room using a commercial FEM software (e.g. Ansys). Topics will be (example list): plane stress problems, 3d analyses, use of symmetry, stress singularities, convergence study, validation of results and plausibilty, modelling of nonlinear material behaviour (elasto-plasticity), nonlinear structural behaviour (buckling), geometric nonlinearities (contact), optimization, thermal analysis.

OBJECTIVES:
Upon completion of this course the student will be able to perform numerical simulations with a FEM tool for structural problems. This includes modelling of the physical problem, simulation of problems like panel/plate/shell and continuum structures, as well as validation of results.

Title: Fernraketen in Entwicklungsländern
Description:
CONTENT:
The lecture investigates the conflict between technology and its use for weaponry. Furthermore an overview of rocket science especially with respect to ballistic missiles in so called "problem countries" is provided. The following topics are covered in detail: An overview of the relevance of weapons and their political dimension plus proliferation, technical aspects, history, analysis and reconstruction of the performance of such systems, aspects of project realization, existing systems and weapons of mass destruction and their classification, systems for missile defense.

OBJECTIVES:
Goal of the lecture is a better understanding of the general problem of ballistic missiles, both technical and political/strategic relevance. After participating in this lecture the student should be able to analyze the relevance of those weapons in the context of potential threats and the risk of a military conflict. The students are able to evaluate the systems with respect to their technical performance and status even with insufficient information. Furthermore they are able to provide useful contributions to debates about threats posed by countries in possession of ballistic missiles.

Title: Fertigungstechnologien
Description:
CONTENT:
The lecture introduces the great variety of production technologies to manufacture ready to use machine parts. Metal casting, forming, cutting and joining technologies and their specific applications, their properties and their limits are taught. The production chain is completed by coating principles and an overview of technologies for changing material properties by heat treatment is given.

OBJECTIVES:
Nach Teilnahme an den Modulveranstaltungen sind die Studierenden in der Lage,
• die 6 Hauptgruppen nach DIN 8580 zu nennen und diesen die einzelnen Fertigungsverfahren zuzuordnen.
• die den Fertigungsverfahren zugrundeliegenden Funktionsprinzipien zu erklären, deren Möglichkeiten und Limitierungen zu erläutern, die verwendeten Anlagen, Werkstoffe und Werkzeuge zu beschreiben, typische Schadensbilder zu klassifizieren und Zusammenhänge herauszuarbeiten.
• technische und wirtschaftliche Berechnungs- und Bewertungsmethoden anzuwenden, um die Grundlage für den Vergleich einzelner Fertigungsverfahren zu bilden und eine fertigungsgerechte Bauteilauslegung abzuleiten.
• einzelne Prozessschritte einer Fertigungskette hinsichtlich der Kriterien Wirtschaftlichkeit, technische Umsetzbarkeit und geforderte Bauteileigenschaften zu bewerten und den Anforderungen entsprechend auszuwählen.
• aktuelle Trends in Forschung und Entwicklung zu nennen und den Unterschied zum industriellen Stand der Technik darzulegen.

Title: Festkörper-, Halbleiter- und Bauelementephysik
Description:
CONTENT:
Quantenmechanische Grundlagen der Atom-, Molekül- und Festkörperphysik; Aufbau der Materie; Bändermodell des Festkörpers; Elektronische Eigenschaften; Mechanische und thermische Eigenschaften; Magnetische Eigenschaften; Optische Eigenschaften; Ladungsträger- und Wärmetransport; Halbleiterphysik (Materialien, Kristallstruktur, Bandstruktur, Dotierung, Ladungsträgerstatistik, Generation und Rekombination); Grundlegende Bauelementestrukturen (p-n-Übergang; Feldeffekt-Transistoren; Bipolar-Transistoren; Optoelektronische Bauelemente)

OBJECTIVES:

Wir arbeiten mit einfachen, aber wirkungsvollen Übungen zur mentalen Selbststeuerung, die dir helfen, in stressigen Lernphasen präsent, ruhig und konzentriert zu bleiben. Ganz ohne Fachjargon – dafür mit klaren Tools, die du direkt in deinen Alltag integrieren kannst.

OBJECTIVES:
Nach dem Workshop:
• hast du ein neues Verständnis von Konzentration und Aufmerksamkeit.
• kannst du alltagstaugliche Tools zur mentalen Fokussierung anwenden.
• kennst du kurze Tiefenübungen zur sofortigen Anwendung.

Description:
CONTENT:

The subject area "Fluid mechanics basics" conveys the basics of the mechanics of gases and liquids. OBJECTIVES:

Title: Fluid Mechanics Lab
Description:
CONTENT:
The fluid mechanics lab is quite theoretical for  this kind of course. This is induced by the sophisticated measuring methods used: laser-based velocity measurements, particle image velocimetry (PIV) and laser doppler anemometry (LDA). Before these techniques can be applied basics in laser and camera respectively photomultiplier technology need to be gained. As both measurement techniques are optical and therefore contact-free particles, so called tracers, have to be added to the flow. The dynamics of these tracing particles are of significant importance for the measurement results. Thus some time is to be spent on the dynamics and light scattering characteristics of these particles. For the analysis of the PIV pictures cross correlation and sub pixel refinement as well as several validation algorithms are introduced. In the context of LDA different averaging techniques are outlined. At last also high-precision pressure measurements are introduced. As a laser of class 4 is used in this course also laser prevention takes a significant value.

OBJECTIVES:
After completion of this course students are able to design fluid mechanical experiments and perform high-precision tests using the messurement techniques described above.
Skills: ['Fluid mechanics', 'Laser Doppler Anemometry', 'Particle Image Velocimetry', 'Measurement techniques']

Title: Fluoreszenz Lifetime Imaging - Theorie und Funktion
Description:
CONTENT:
Das Arbeiten mit Lifetime-Messgeräten gekoppelt an Konfokalen Laser Scanning Mikroskopen stellt zunehmend ein wichtiges Arbeitsfeld in der modernen Molekularbiologie dar. Gegenstand der Veranstaltung ist die Vermittlung des Verständnisses wie Fluorophor-Lifetime-Messungen in der Theorie zu verstehen sind und mit welchen Mitteln und wie diese praktisch erreicht werden können. Dabei werden auch die Eigenschaften von Molekülen (Protein-Fluorophor-Fusionen) vermittelt, die für diese Messungen relevant sind bzw. sich auf selbige auswirken. Die Studierenden lernen dabei das Prinzip wie die dazu notwendige Gerätschaft aufgebaut ist und wie das Konfokale LSM mit der Lifetime-Messeinheit zusammenarbeitet.
Die Studierenden erlernen die theoretischen Prinzipien der Lifetime-Messung, des 
Fluorescence Lifetime Imaging (FLIM), des Förster Resonanz Energytransfer (FRET), Anisotropie und Fluorescence Correlation Spectroscopy (FCS).
Vermittelt wird der Einsatz bzw. Erkenntnisgewinn, den FLIM bei zell- und molekularbiologischen Experimenten ermöglicht.
Sie erwerben die Kenntnis welche Protein-Fluorophor-Fusionen am besten für ein FRET-Experiment ausgewählt werden, z. B. um einen Ernergietransfer bei echter Nachbarschaft zweier Proteine zu optimieren.
Ein besonderer Punkt ist die Vermittlung wie ein kombiniertes Lifetime-Messgerät mit Konfokalem LSM im Prinzip und praktisch eingestellt bzw. eingesetzt wird.
Es werden Präparate mit verschiedenen Fluoreszenz-Marker-Proteinen (z. B. GFP-, YFP-, mRFP-, mCherry-Fusionen) eingesetzt. Es werden ausgewählt Kern-, zytoplasmatische bzw. (polare) Plasma-Membran-Proteine untersucht.

OBJECTIVES:
Die Übung ist eine Kombination aus Theorie und Praxis.
Mit dem erfolgreichen Abschluss des Moduls erwerben die Studierenden folgende Kompetenzen und Fähigkeiten:
1. Grundlagen und Methoden des Fluorescence Lifetime Imagings (FLIM) mit Hilfe der Konfokalen Laser Scanning Mikroskopie zu verstehen. Einige der Fragen und Aspekte, die hier im Vordergrund stehen betreffen z. B.:
- das Entstehen der “decay“-Kurve eines Fluorophors; 
- die möglichen Veränderungen von Lebenszeiten (Lifetimes) Fluorophor-gekoppelter Proteine in unterschiedlichen Zellkompartimenten und unter unterschiedlichen physiologischen Bedingungen und die Möglichkeit dies in zellbiologischen Untersuchungen einzusetzen, 
- die Technik mittels Förster Resonanz Energietransfer (FRET) und FLIM die unmittelbare Nachbarschaft und Interaktion zweier verschiedener Proteine in vivo zu untersuchen; 
- die Auswahl von geeigneten Protein-Fluorophor-Fusionen für FRET-Experimente unter Berücksichtigung spezieller FRET-relevanter Aspekte wie ihre Tendenz zur Mono- gegenüber Di- oder Multimerisierung oder zu monoexponentiellen gegenüber di- oder multiexponentiellen “Decay“, 
- die Möglichkeit “cluster“ bzw. die Interaktion von zwei oder mehr Einheiten desselben Proteins mittels Anisotropie-Änderungen verursacht durch HomoFRET zu ermitteln; 
- das Diffusionsverhalten von Propteinen in verschiedenen Zellkompartimenten z. B. Proteinen in der Zellmembran.

2. Die Studierenden erhalten in diesem Fall eine hoch-entwickelte, sehr spezielle Kompetenz. Sie erwerben die Fähigkeit an einem fortgeschrittenen System zweier international tätiger, ko-operierender Hersteller FILM- und Anisotropie-Messungen durchzuführen. Sie erwerben weiterhin die Kenntnis, wie überhaupt, mittels gepulster Laser und modernsten “high-end“-Detektoren, Lifetime-Messungen von Fluorophoren ermittelt werden können. Die Erweiterung zur Messung von Lifetimes von Flourophor-markierten Proteinen am hiesigen Konfokalen Laser Scanning Mikroskop (LSM) ist noch sehr neu und stammt von einer der wenigen weltweit operierenden Firmen auf diesem Gebiet, die mit einem der weltweit führenden Hersteller von Konfokalen LSMs zusammenarbeitet.

Aus letzterem ergibt sich, dass die Studierenden eine zunehmend gefragte aber noch nicht sehr verbreitete Kompetenz erwerben. Diese wird es ihnen erlauben in der Forschung in nachgefragten, sehr fortgeschrittenen Gebieten der Molekularbiologie tätig zu werden. Es liegt auf der Hand, dass dies auch eine hochqualifizierende Kompetenz darstellt, die in der angewandten Forschung bzw. Industrie zunehmend nachgefragt werden wird.
Die erlernte Kompetenz wird es den Studierenden bei Pflege der erworbenen Kenntnisse erlauben, ähnliche Geräte und Techniken nach Einweisung schneller und besser zu verstehen, d. h. die Einweisung zu verkürzen.

Title: Football Analytics Hackathon
Description:
CONTENT:
The technological innovations of recent years - in particular, advances in the field of position tracking – lead to enormous amounts of data in soccer. In this module students will have to solve challenges given by an expert group including sport data scientists, professional soccer clubs and sports data companies. Students will be organized interdisciplinary workgroups including students students from computer science as well as from sport science. 

Challenges are related to soccer performance. The refer to an technical or tactical concept in soccer such as pressing, passing quality, line break, build up play, circle play, movements to receive, tactical formation, physical effort passing lines and much more. Based on these concepts the students will have to 
•	specify the concept from the perspective of sport science (e.g., what is pressing?) 
•	specify the concept from the perspective of computer science science (e.g., how can we model pressing in a mathematical way?) 
•	develop a technical solution for detecting this concept in raw data (e.g., identifying the timespans, in which pressing occurs). 
•	validate the detection quality based on video analysis (e.g., did you found the right timespans?). 
•	calculate performance indicators based on these concept (e.g. number of successful and non-successful pressing situations).  
•	use appropriate methods from visual analytics to make the numbers be interpretable in an easy and intuitive way (e.g. by visualizing indicators in relation to context variables). 
•	interpret the results from the perspective of performance analysis (e.g. ,how can the results be used by a coach?)

OBJECTIVES:
The general aim of the module is to introduce students to the research field of soccer analytics. After successfully completing the project, students will be able: 
-	to understand typical professional sport competition data (spatiotemporal tracking data, event data) and their characteristic.  
-	to apply methods and paradigms of computer science such as network analysis, machine learning and visual analytics for modelling phenomena in soccer.  
-	to develop sports data products for mass media, competition information provider and  top level sports.

Title: FOPRA-Versuch 104
Description:
CONTENT:
In superconducting quantum circuits, such as quantum bits, information is processed and transferred in the form of microwave quantum signals. Moreover, at the end of quantum information protocols, these signals have to be recorded by room temperature electronic devices. Since microwave quantum signals typically consist of very few photons, they must be ampliﬁed in order to achieve reasonable signal-to-noise ratios. Therefore, low-noise ampliﬁcation of quantum signals is crucial. Modern low-noise microwave ampliﬁers are built upon superconducting Josephson parametric devices, such as a ﬂux-driven Josephson Parametric Ampliﬁer (JPA), which allows to reach the standard quantum limit of ampliﬁcation and even go beyond it. The current JPA is formed by a superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID) combined with a superconducting coplanar waveguide resonator. The combined system acts as a tunable nonlinear microwave resonator, whose frequency can be varied in-situ via an external magnetic ﬁeld. A mechanical analogue would be a pendulum of variable length, allowing one to tune its eigenfrequency. Tunability of the nonlinear microwave resonator can be exploited to parametrically pump the JPA via application of a strong microwave signal at twice the resonant frequency. This, in turn, can result in a strong parametric ampliﬁcation of weak quantum signals incident at the JPA. The same parametric ampliﬁcation mechanism can be exploited further for generation of genuine quantum signals in the form of squeezed vacuum states.

Title: FOPRA-Versuch 16
Description:
CONTENT:
You will perform a low temperature experiment at liquid helium temperature (4.2 K) to investigate a superconducting tunnel junction - a so-called Josephson junction - consisting of two Nb 100 nm thick electrodes separated by a thin aluminium oxide (AlOx) layer (about 17 nm thick). The junction area is a square with an edge length L of about 20 μm. Josephson junction feature a finite supercurrent (Josephson current) through the tunneling barrier at zero voltage drop between the two junction electrodes. You will measure the maximum Josephson current I_c by recording the IV-characteristics of the junction. 

The zero-voltage Josephson current across a Josephson junction is proportional to the sine of the phase difference varphi of the macroscopic wave functions describing the two superconducting junction electrodes: I_s = I_c sin(varphi). This phase difference is modified by a magnetic field applied parallel to the tunneling barrier. This results in a characteristic magnetic field dependence of the maximum Josephson current, corresponding to the diffraction pattern of a slit in optics.  You will record this pattern and derive the Josephson penetration depth from the period of the pattern. 

From the experiment you will get basic insights into the phasics of Josephson junctions and in techniques used to perform low temperature experiments.

Title: FOPRA-Versuch 22
Description:
CONTENT:
Determination of the potential of maximum entropy (PME), related to the potential of zero charge (PZC), is of importance to understand the mechanism of various electrode processes. In this lab course, laser-induced current transient (LICT) technique is implemented to fulfil the determination of the PME. This technique utilizes the so-called temperature jump effect to heat the electrode surface, resulting a sudden temperature change then to identify the sign of the electrode surface charge.
The PME, useful in the assessment of stiffness of the interfacial water layer, is a potential at which the entropy of the double layer formation reaches its maximum. In the vicinity of PME, species can move through electric double layer (EDL) more easily and reaction should proceed quite fast, whereas the solvent structure is more rigid at potentials more remote from PME. In this case, one can correlate the PME measurements with the activity towards catalytic reactions, e.g. the hydrogen
evolution reaction (HER).
In this lab course, you have the opportunity to learn how to perform this LICT technique and understand the activity towards the HER correlation with the PME results.

Title: FOPRA-Versuch 85
Description:
CONTENT:
This advanced lab course introduces you to observational astronomy.  It involves observing star clusters with a telescope (weather permitting), analyzing the data, and deriving properties of the star clusters including their relative ages.

There are two types of star cluster in the Galaxy. Open clusters are loose collections of typically a few hundred stars in the galactic disk. These clusters tend to be young with ages of several million to a billion years. Typical cluster masses range between
100 - 1000 solar masses and their diameters are 1 - 10 parsec (where 1 parsec is ~3.3 light years). In our Galaxy more than 1100 open clusters are known. The estimated total number of Galactic open clusters is ∼ 2 x 10^4.

Globular clusters, on the other hand, are tightly bound collections of a few hundred thousand to a few million stars, typically located in the Galactic halo. These clusters are generally old with ages of a few billion years. The diameter of a typical globular cluster is about 40 parsec. 

In this project, you will construct colour-magnitude diagrams of two open clusters. Using these colour-magnitude diagrams you will investigate the differences in morphology in these clusters and explain them in terms of their relative ages.

OBJECTIVES:
Basic knowledge on stars and astronomy.  Experience and competence in astronomical observations, data analysis and interpretations of results.

Title: Formal Methods for Cyber-Physical Systems
Description:
CONTENT:
In many modern systems, computing elements are tightly connected with physical entities for which the term "cyber-physical systems" has been established in recent years. Examples are automated vehicles, surgical robots, smart grids, and collaborative human-robot manufacturing.

Because cyber-physical systems are becoming increasingly safety-critical due to the ongoing trend towards deeper autonomy, formal methods that prove the correct behavior of systems are gaining importance. This lecture teaches state-of-the-art formal methods by combining theory and hands-on programming sessions.

•	Preliminaries: Set representations and operations, including interval arithmetic and Taylor models
•	Formal verification using reachability analysis; considered system classes: linear systems, nonlinear systems, hybrid systems
•	Online verification in uncertain and dynamic environments
•	Safe reinforcement learning 
•	Correct-by-construction controller design
•	Robust model predictive control
•	Set-based observers: set-membership approach and interval-observer approach
•	Conformance checking for system identification: observer-based approaches and reachability-based approaches

OBJECTIVES:
After attending the module, you are able to verify, control, observe, and identify cyber-physical systems in a provably correct way by using formal methods. The material is taught at a level that enables you to apply the methods for real problems or start a research project on formal methods for cyber-physical systems. In particular, you will acquire the following skills:

•	You understand the benefits of formal methods compared to conventional methods which do not prove properties.
•	You can apply interval arithmetic and bound evaluations of functions using Taylor models.
•	You can construct set representations for intervals, zonotopes, ellipsoids, polytopes, and non-convex sets.
•	You can convert set-representations exactly or in an over-approximative way.
•	You can compute set-based operations, such as linear maps, Minkowski sum, or convex hull.
•	You can write software to propagate reachable sets of linear, nonlinear, and hybrid systems. 
•	You can abstract dynamical systems to simpler descriptions and compute the associated abstraction error.
•	You can create solutions to verify cyber-physical systems during runtime.
•	You can safeguard reinforcement learning techniques using formal methods.
•	You can automatically synthesize formally-correct controllers adhering to input and state constraints.
•	You can integrate reachability analysis in model predictive control to design robust and adaptive controllers.
•	You can estimate the set of possible states using set-based observers. 
•	You understand the difference between the set-membership approach and the interval-observer approach for set-based observers.
•	You can check whether a model encloses all real behaviors.
•	You can program solutions to add uncertainty to models so that they include all observed behaviors.

Title: Forschungsmethoden in der Wirtschaftspädagogik
Description:
CONTENT:
Es werden grundlegende forschungsmethodische Verfahren thematisiert und auf bereitgestellte Unterlagen und Forschungsdatensätze angewandt. 
Inhalte in der Vorlesung sowie dem Seminar sind:
- Grundlagen wissenschaftlichen Arbeitens (Aufbau wissenschaftlicher Fachartikel, Basics der Literaturrecherche, Quellenarbeit und Zitationen)
- Forschungslogische Abläufe im Forschungsprozess (z.B. Anlässe von Forschung)
- Formulierung von forschungsleitenden Fragestellungen
- Überführung der fachlich-inhaltlichen Grundlagen in statistisch prüfbare Verfahren
- Hypothesenerstellung mittels bestehender Theorien mit Bezug zum aktuellen Forschungsstand und -prüfung
- Unterschiede quantitativer und qualitativer bzw. hypothesenprüfender und -generierender Forschung
- Arten von Gütekriterien für quantitative und qualitative Forschung

Beispiele möglicher Verfahren:
- Deskriptive Datenanalyse
- T-Test / Varianzanalyse
- Korrelationen & verschiedene Regressionsanalysen
- Mediator- & Moderator-Analysen (PROCESS Makro für SPSS)
- Faktorenanalysen (explorativ)
- qualitative Inhaltsanalyse (QCAmap)
- Güteprüfungen qualitativer Kodierungen: Inter- & Intra-Rater-Übereinstimmungen

Die Schwerpunktsetzung der thematisierten Methoden hängt in hohem Maße mit der zugrundeliegenden Fragestellung und dem Datenformat zusammen.

OBJECTIVES:
Die Studierenden kennen aktuelle, relevante Themen und Probleme aus dem Bereich der ökonomischen und beruflichen Bildung. Die Studierenden sind in der Lage, die Ergebnisse von Softwarepaketen zu bewerten und kontextspezifisch zu interpretieren. Neben quantitativen Methoden kennen sie auch die Grundlagen qualitativer Forschungsmethoden (z.B. Inhaltsanalyse, Kodierung offener Antwortformate) und können Berechnungen zur Inter-Rater-Übereinstimmung durchführen, auswerten und interpretieren. Sie sind in der Lage, Forschungsfragen unter Bezugnahme auf verschiedene wissenschaftliche Theorien selbstständig zu bearbeiten. Sie sind in der Lage, eigene Forschungsfragen zu formulieren, eigene Hypothesen zu formulieren und mit geeigneten statistischen Methoden zu überprüfen. Die Studierenden sind in der Lage, vorhandene qualitative und quantitative Daten zu nutzen und mit Hilfe von Softwarepaketen zu analysieren. Insbesondere sind sie in der Lage, zielgerichtet statistische Standardanalysen durchzuführen und die generierten Ergebnisse zu verstehen, zu interpretieren und kritisch zu bewerten. Sie können die Grenzen der Forschung aufzeigen und Rückschlüsse auf die Theorien und den Stand der Forschung ziehen.

Title: Fortgeschrittene Halbleiterphysik
Description:
CONTENT:
NOTE: This module begins in WS25/26 on 20th October !!  

This module provides an introduction to the structural, electronic and optical properties of modern semiconductor materials and their associated nanostructures. The scientific and economical importance of semiconductor physics as a cross-cutting part of modern solid-state physics is briefly outlined. Then, an introduction to the different methods for the fabrication and deposition used for ultrapure semiconductor materials, alloys and mixed crystals as well as heterostructure will be given. The main body of the module deals with the material, electronic, vibrational and optical properties of the most commonly used semiconductors. This includes elemental semiconductors such as silicon, germanium and diamond, as well as compound semiconductors like group-III arsenides, antimonides and nitrides used for optoelectronic devices.  We will understand the detailed origins of the electronic bandstructure, and discuss the resulting properties of effective mass electrons, holes and other relevant quasiparticles such as excitons and polarons. Equilibrium charge carrier statistics in intrinsic (undoped) semiconductors are then explored before discussing how doping can be used to controllably modify the electronic properties. We will then explore methods to obtain high carrier mobility in semiconductors, from which we will explore semi-classical and quantum transport of charge carriers in nanostructure materials.  This is followed by a discussion of the electronic properties of semiconductors under application-related non-equilibrium conditions, such as illumination in solar cells or photo-detectors, or voltage biasing in diodes or transistors. To this end, the basic properties of semiconductor/semiconductor-, semiconductor/metal-, and semiconductor/insulator-hetero-interfaces will be discussed, providing a sound basis for exploring quantum electronic and photonic devices in other modules.

OBJECTIVES:
After participation in the Module the student is able to:
1. Describe the crystal structure and explain the principle fabrication methods for the most prominent semiconductor materials
2. Explain and calculate the electronic bandstructure of these materials and its dependence on material composition.
3. Understand the terms "two-dimensional", "one-dimensional" and "zero-dimensional" semiconductor nanostructure and explain the influence of quantum confinement on the electronic properties of semiconductors.
4. Understand and explain the physics of charge carrier statistics and scattering governing electrical conductivity in bulk semiconductors and low dimensional nanostructures.
5. Understand and explain the optical properties of semiconductors, in particular optical absorption and recombination of non-equilibrium charge carriers.
6. Understand and explain the basic properties of semiconductor surfaces and interfaces with device-relevant applications to Schottky diodes, solar cells and heterojunctions in optoelectronics.
