Title: Fortgeschrittene Statistik in R
Description:
CONTENT:
*** ATTENTION: In future, the course will be offered in the winter semesters only ***

The course will be offered in a hybrid format. The lectures are available asynchronously via video in Moodle. The exercises will be conducted in presence.

This course introduces advanced methods of analysing biological data in theory and practical application using the statistical programme R. The specific contents of the course are advanced programming in the statistical programme R, analysis of complex data structures in mixed-effect models, generalised linear models (GLM) and an introduction to multivariate statistics.

OBJECTIVES:
After participating in the module course, students are able to statistically test even detailed biological hypotheses and to correctly evaluate even complex data. Students understand the prerequisites for linear models, can recognise violations of these prerequisites in their data and apply generalised linear models and mixed effect models when necessary. Students also understand the difference between univariate and multivariate hypotheses and analyses. Students can present the results of their analyses graphically and in writing.

Title: Fortschritte in der Festkörperphysik
Description:
CONTENT:
Within the seminar, students give talks on current topics in condensed matter physics. The seminar aims to give a closer look at new developments in condensed matter physics and to show how these developments can be transferred into applications. The seminar focuses on spin electronics, spin dynamics, solid-state quantum information processing, the physics of solid-state nanostructures, and high temperature superconductivity. These topics are in the focus of several research projects of WMI and collaborative research programs in the Munich area (e.g. the Excellence Cluster "Munich Center for Quantum Science and Technology (MCQST)", the Munich Quantum Valley e.V., as well as several BMBF and EU projects).

The seminar is relevant for the special courses on Quantum Science and Technology, Superconductivity and Low Temperature Physics as well as on Magnetism and Spintronics. It is suitable for bachelor students in the 5th semester or higher and for master students.

OBJECTIVES:
You will become familiar with recent advances in condensed matter physics that have been published recently in top journals such as Nature, Science, Physical Review Letters, etc.. You will present the physical and technological background of the advancement and the specialized content of the selected paper in a presentation.

Title: Foundations and Applications of Graph Neural Networks
Description:
CONTENT:
A graph is a data structure able to capture relations between data points, e.g. connections within a social network, citations of scientific papers or traffic networks. As graph-structured data is all around us and allows us to intuitively capture a lot of real-world problems, techniques to learn on those graphs have been developed. Like this, assessments on graph-, node- or edge-level can be made. Since traditional machine learning models cannot easily be applied to graphs, the so-called Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have been developed. In this seminar, we will focus on different GNN architectures and optimizations as well as various fields of application. Students will be able to deep dive into a specific GNN problem and present ideas on how to solve it. The topics consist of conducting literature research and/or coding your own prototype.
The preliminary meeting will take place on 15.07.2025 at 11:00am via https://tum-conf.zoom-x.de/j/61699533144?pwd=SpLLQdMzrWVGYA1Sb8n2p0pWeaPbI8.1
Slides: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1zQWA8bJEIxm788SWgAhOZ0-GyBp8UEPfjQfGDwGj-I8/edit?usp=sharing

OBJECTIVES:
By the end of the seminar, students have studied a specific problem in the graph machine learning domain and presented ideas on how to solve it (experimentally or with literature).
In the seminar, students will learn about scientific paper writing techniques, the peer review process, and presentation of results.
Learn how to answer a research question.
Learn how to read and judge scientific papers.
Learn how to build prototypes of algorithms.
Learn how to present scientific work.
Learn scientific writing skills.
Deep dive into a practical graph machine learning topic.

Title: Foundations in Data Engineering
Description:
CONTENT:
Data organization, efficient analysis of large data sets, distributed data storage (depending on system architecture, e.g. multi-core systems, multi-processor systems, clusters), distributed and parallel data analysis, statistics-backed optimization of analytical processes (z.B. by dimensionality reduction), map/reduce techniques and their generalization for distributed query processing, applications in systems as Hadoop and NoSQL systems, effects on society, importance of privacy protection

OBJECTIVES:
Students are able to apply and characterize basic concepts of distributed data storage. They know analysis algorithms for very large, distributed data sets and are able to use, implement and assess them in a systematic and qualified fashion. They are able to assess and combine optimization techniques for analysis processes and are able to tailor these techniques to specific preconditions (e.g. data characteristics, system architecture). They are aware of the societal relevance of data engineering techniques.
Skills: ['Data engineering', 'Data organization', 'Distributed data storage', 'Parallel data analysis', 'MapReduce']

Title: Foundations of Design Practice
Description:
CONTENT:
This module offers a foundational understanding of design as a discipline and practice, with a focus on human-centered design. Students will explore the history, definitions, and practical applications of this methodology through various design processes and research methods. The seminar will also critically assess the current value and limitations of design, along with emerging approaches.

In the practical component of the course, students will work on a specific brief. Participants will define a preliminary design problem, develop a design research plan, and apply various design research methods to gather insights relevant to their design problem. Through collaborative work, participants will learn to differentiate between insights that are merely interesting and those relevant to their solutions. Students will then reframe their design brief, develop initial design hypotheses, and generate ideas to address the identified problems. They will use iterative prototyping to test concepts and ideas, gather feedback from potential users, and refine their designs accordingly. The process will focus on engaging with and gathering insights from a human-centered point of view.

Through reflective practice, students will gain exposure to human-centered design methodology and develop a foundational theoretical understanding of design as a discipline. They will identify aspects of design practice relevant to their future studies and consider how to explore these areas further.

OBJECTIVES:
After successfully completing this module, students will be able to:

• Articulate a clear understanding of human-centered design as both a discipline and a practice.
• Articulate an understanding of design as a discipline and methodology.
• Develop empathy by applying qualitative design research methods, such as interviews and observations.
• Practice synthesis using qualitative data to identify opportunity areas.
• Apply creative problem-solving techniques, including ideation, prototyping, and concept testing.
• Think expansively to generate bold, imaginative, and inspiring solutions that reframe known problems in unexpected ways.
• Collaborate effectively with peers in multi- and transdisciplinary teams.

Title: Foundations of Entrepreneurial Business
Description:
CONTENT:
The module introduces students into basic principles of the topic of entrepreneurship from a global and international perspective. Students will be equiped with basic knowledge on:
- definitions, regional aspects, and special forms of entrepreneurship
- entrepreneurial individuals, including their personality, creativity, idea development, cognition, opportunity recognition, decision making, affect, and moving forward from failure
- entrepreneurial firms, including their growth strategies, strategic alliances, and resources.
Beyond that, students can engage in break-out group work to personally experience the process of opportunity recognition and development while applying concepts from academic literature to real-world entrepreneurial problems.

OBJECTIVES:
Students will know and be able to explain basic concepts of entrepreneurship including basic definitions, psychological processes and characteristics of the person of the entrepreneur, and potential development paths of young firms. Further, students will transfer this basic knowledge to real world cases. Thus, students will be able to solve entrepreneurial problems in real world settings drawing on theoretical frameworks of the entrepreneurial process.

Title: Fragestellungen aus Wissenschaft und Gesellschaft in Architektur und Städtebau
Description:
CONTENT:
Teaching Assignment: Aktuelle Fragestellungen aus Wissenschaft und Gesellschaft (Current Issues in Science and Society) 
Lecturer: Sandra Cabrales 

Winter Term 2025/26: Communication, Power and Role Models in Architecture 

While narratives and role models fundamentally shape architecture, they determine which perspectives
drive both discourse and the built environment. This seminar examines how communication, power, and
role models operate within the discipline, questioning architecture's dominant narratives. By critically
examining mainstream perspectives, we explore feminist architecture as a practice that centers all users
and incorporates their viewpoints as fundamental to shaping our built environment.
The seminar integrates theory with practice through exercises, debates, and analysis, examining historical
and contemporary communication patterns, narratives, stereotypes, representation, and invisibilities within
architectural discourse, as well as unconscious bias and its impact on the field.
Students then apply these insights to their own academic experience, critically analyzing communication
patterns, role models, collaboration, and task distribution within their projects and study environment.
Through this combination of theory, analysis, and practice, students develop an understanding of how
these dynamics affect both the broader discipline and built environment, as well as individual practice in
daily planning work.

Title: Französisch A1.1
Description:
CONTENT:
In this module, students gain basic knowledge of French as a foreign language, enabling them to successfully manage basic everyday situations with minimal language skills, e.g introducing themselves and others; talking about free-time activities; asking for information and for directions; shopping. Grammar topics include: present tense of regular and irregular verbs; personal pronouns; definite, indefinite and partitive articles; questions; and adjective declension. Moreover, opportunities will be made available for students to more effectively organize the process of learning French as a foreign language and thus to improve their own learning abilities.

OBJECTIVES:
The module is aimed at level A1 "Elementary Language Use" of the CEFR (Common European Framework of Reference). Students gain basic knowledge of French as a foreign language with a general language orientation while taking into consideration intercultural and cultural aspects. After completion of this module, students will be able to ask and answer questions about familiar topics. They can interact in a simple fashion, provided that their counterpart speaks slowly and clearly and is willing to help; they can briefly describe themselves in writing.

Title: Französisch A1.1 + A1.2 intensiv
Description:
CONTENT:
In dieser LV werden Grundkenntnisse in der Fremdsprache Französisch vermittelt, die es den Studierenden ermöglichen, sich in alltäglichen Grundsituationen trotz noch geringer Sprachkenntnisse zurechtzufinden. Dabei werden interkulturelle und landeskundliche Aspekte berücksichtigt. 
Der/Die Studierende lernt z.B., einfache Fragen zu Person und Familie zu stellen und zu beantworten sowie über Themen wie Studium, Beruf, Freizeit, Essen in einfachen Sätzen im Präsenz und Perfekt zu berichten. Es werden u.a. folgende grammatische Themen behandelt: Präsenz, Passé Composé, Futur proche, Artikel, Possessivbegleiter, direkte und indirekte Objektpronomen, Präpositionen, Fragesätze. Es werden Strategien vermittelt, die eine Verständigung trotz noch geringer Sprachkenntnisse in alltäglichen Grundsituationen ermöglichen. 
Außerdem werden Möglichkeiten aufgezeigt, den Lernprozess in der Fremdsprache Französisch effektiver zu gestalten und die eigene Lernfähigkeit zu verbessern.

OBJECTIVES:
Die LV orientiert sich am Niveau „A1 – Elementare Sprachverwendung“ des GER. Der/die Studierende erlangt nach der Teilnahme an der Modulveranstaltung Grundkenntnisse in der Fremdsprache Französisch mit allgemeiner Orientierung unter Berücksichtigung interkultureller und landeskundlicher Aspekte. Er/sie ist in der Lage, einfache Fragen über vertraute Themen zu stellen und zu beantworten. Er/sie kann sich auf einfache Art verständigen, wenn die Gesprächspartnerinnen oder Gesprächspartner langsam und deutlich sprechen und bereit sind zu helfen. Er/sie kann einfache schriftliche Mitteilungen zur Person machen.
Sowohl im mündlichen als auch im schriftlichen Sprachgebrauch ist der/die Studierende in der Lage, situationsadäquat, bzw. der A 1-Stufe entsprechend, Wortschatz und Grammatik korrekt anzuwenden.

Title: Französisch A1.2
Description:
CONTENT:
In this module, students expand their basic knowledge of French lexis and grammar for simple oral and written for every-day communication situations. They learn, for example, to pose questions to others about themselves and their families and to answer similar questions, to make arrangements as well as reservations in hotels, to report on free time and holiday activities, to describe past events and habits. Grammar covered will include: Passé Composé, Futur proche, quantities, possessive pronouns, direct and indirect object pronouns. Strategies will be taught enabling students with minimal language skills to successfully manage basic everyday situations. Moreover, opportunities will be made available to more effectively organize the learning process of French as a foreign language and to improve the ability to learn.

OBJECTIVES:
The module is aimed at level A1 "Elementary Language Use" of the CEFR. Students gain basic knowledge of French as a foreign language with a general language orientation while taking into consideration intercultural and cultural aspects. After completion of this module, students will be able to use and understand everyday expressions and very simple sentences. They can interact in a simple fashion, provided that their counterpart speaks slowly and clearly and is willing to help; they can write short, simple reports in French using fixed phrases.

Title: Französisch A2.1
Description:
CONTENT:
In this module, students gain additional basic knowledge of French as a foreign language, enabling them to successfully manage everyday situations, e.g. while travelling, at the doctor, while looking for a place to live, or while talking to colleagues, friends and neighbors. More grammar will be covered, e.g. use of the Passé Composé und Imparfait, the conditional, relative pronouns, en + y pronouns, comparatives and the superlative. Students will learn strategies for successfully communicating in day-to-day situations with minimal language skills. Additionally, opportunities will be made available to more effectively learn French as a foreign language and thus to improve the student's ability to learn.

OBJECTIVES:
The module is aimed at level "A2 - Elementary Language Use" of the CEFR. Students gain basic knowledge of French as a foreign language with general language orientation while taking into consideration intercultural and cultural aspects. After completion of this module, students will be able to understand and use simple sentences and expressions on a broader spectrum of familiar topics. Students can, for example, describe where they live, their health status and free-time activities. They are able to communicate while searching for a place to live and in important situations while on holiday or travelling and describe the resulting experiences or events. They can use and understand standard expressions in familiar communication situations both orally and in writing.

Title: Französisch A2.1 + A2.2
Description:
CONTENT:
In dieser Lehrveranstaltung werden Grundkenntnisse in der Fremdsprache Französisch intensiv aufgebaut, die den Studierenden – trotz noch geringer Sprachkenntnisse - ermöglichen, sich in Alltagssituationen zurechtzufinden. Die Studierenden lernen/üben (u. a), wie man über Erfahrungen spricht und sie bewertet, wie man Meinungen äußert und darauf reagiert, wie man über die Ursachen und Folgen von etwas spricht, wie man Anweisungen, und Ratschläge gibt. Dabei werden interkulturelle und landeskundliche Aspekte berücksichtigt. Die grammatischen Strukturen werden weiter aufgebaut. Folgende grammatischen Themen werden behandelt, wie z.B. Verwendung von Passé Composé und Imparfait, Konditional, Relativpronomen, „en + y“ Pronomen, Komparativ und Superlativ.
Es werden Strategien vermittelt, die mündlich wie schriftlich eine Verständigung trotz noch geringer Sprachkenntnisse ermöglichen. Außerdem werden Möglichkeiten aufgezeigt, den Lernprozess effektiver zu gestalten und damit die eigene Lernfähigkeit zu verbessern. Ferner werden Möglichkeiten aufgezeigt, den Lernprozess in der Fremdsprache Französisch effektiver zu gestalten und damit die eigene Lernfähigkeit zu verbessern.

OBJECTIVES:
Die LV orientiert sich am „A2 – Elementare Sprachverwendung“ des GER. Nach Abschluss dieser LV kann der/die Studierende einfache Sätze und Redewendungen zu einem erweiterten Spektrums an vertrauten Themen verstehen und gebrauchen. Dabei handelt es sich um grundlegende Informationen zu alltäglichen oder studien- bzw. berufsrelevanten Themen. Sie erfassen die Bedeutung von kurzen, klaren und deutlich artikulierten Mitteilungen und Durchsagen. Der/die Studierende kann standardsprachliche Ausdrücke in vertrauten Kommunikationssituationen sowohl in mündlicher als auch in schriftlicher Form verstehen und verwenden und dabei Wortschatz und Grammatik korrekt anzuwenden.

Title: Französisch A2.2
Description:
CONTENT:
In this module, students gain further basic knowledge of French as a foreign language, enabling them to successfully deal with every-day situations. Listening and reading comprehension as well as speaking will be practiced with various listening exercises and texts (the world of work, new media, environmental protection, culture). The review and extension of grammar refers to communicative learning goals (emphasis: the future, gerunds, indirect speech, past perfect, the subjunctive). Students will learn strategies for successfully communicating orally and in writing with minimal language skills. Additionally, opportunities will be made available to more effectively learn French as a foreign language and thus to improve the student's ability to learn.

OBJECTIVES:
This module is aimed at level "A2 Basic Language Use" of the CEFR. Students gain further basic knowledge of French as a foreign language with general language orientation while taking into consideration intercultural and cultural aspects. After completion of this module, in discussions students will be able to understand and use familiar sentences and figures of speech on an expanded spectrum of topics, such as basic information on every-day topics or topics relating to the university and careers. They can understand longer texts and letters on familiar topics in which contemporary but simple every-day and business language is used and in which expected information is found. Students are able to write short, informative texts or reports on every-day situations and the university.

Title: Französisch B1.1
Description:
CONTENT:
In this module, knowledge of French as a foreign language will be further developed, enabling students to function/persuade/express themselves in French independently and confidently in familiar situations, e.g. in the classroom, at work, in free time and with the family, on topics of general interest when standard French is spoken. Students expand their cultural knowledge of a great variety of current topics in French life. They increase their vocabulary as well as consolidate and deepen the French grammar focused on thus far.

OBJECTIVES:
The module is aimed at level "B1 Independent Language use" of the CEFR. Students acquire knowledge of French as a foreign language at the standard language level with a focus on intercultural, cultural and academic aspects. Following completion of this module, students can communicate confidently in familiar situations encountered at school or work, in free-time activities or while travelling in French-speaking countries. They can understand the essential content of simple, authentic texts on every-day topics and can take part in discussions on familiar topics. Students are capable of describing personal experiences and impressions in writing in longer texts.

Title: Französisch B1.2
Description:
CONTENT:
In this module, knowledge of French as a foreign language will be further developed, enabling students to express themselves in French independently and confidently in familiar situations, e.g. in the classroom, at work, in free time and with the family, on topics of general interest, e.g. films, music, sports, etc, when standard French is spoken. Students expand their cultural knowledge of a great variety of current topics in French life. They increase their vocabulary as well as consolidate and deepen the French grammar focused on thus far.

OBJECTIVES:
The module is aimed at level B1 of the CEFR. Students acquire knowledge of French as a foreign language at the standard language level with a focus on intercultural, cultural and academic aspects. Following completion of this module, students can confidently communicate in most situations they are likely to encounter in school, at work, during free-time or while travelling in French-speaking countries. They can understand and describe the essential content of simple specialist texts, radio or television programs, and literary texts and spontaneously take part in discussions of familiar topics of general interest. They can write simple, formal and longer personal letters and texts, report in a structured fashion on a general topic of personal interest and take a logical position on a current topic, if support is offered.

Title: Französisch B2 - Cours de conversation
Description:
CONTENT:
In diesem Modul werden Kenntnisse in der Fremdsprache Französisch aufgebaut und vertieft, die es den Studierenden ermöglichen, aktiv und mit einem gewissen Grad an Flüssigkeit über Themen von allgemeinem Interesse oder von vertrautem Fachgebiet mit einem Muttersprachler zu diskutieren und eine Argumentation gut verständlich ausführen.
Ein besonderes Merkmal wird in diesem Modul auf die Entwicklung von Lesestrategien von allgemeinen und fachbezogenen Texten, auf Wortschatzarbeit und die Entwicklung von Hörstrategien gelegt. Zur Festigung der mündlichen und schriftlichen Fertigkeit werden Schwerpunkte der Grammatik wiederholt und vertieft.

OBJECTIVES:
Das Modul orientiert sich am Niveau „B2- Selbständige Sprachverwendung“ des GER. Der/die Studierende kann den wesentlichen Inhalt von Artikeln und Berichten sowie Texte aus dem eigenen Fach- und Interessengebiet selbständig verstehen. 
Er/sie kann längere Redebeiträge und Vorträge zu aktuellen Themen folgen, sofern sie klar vorgetragen werden. 
Er/sie ist in der Lage Texte zu aktuellen Themen zu schreiben und dabei auch zu einem gewissen Grad komplexe Satzstrukturen zu benutzen. 
Er/sie kann zu vielen Themen aus seinen/ihren Interessen- oder Fachgebieten klar in mündlicher Form kommunizieren.

Title: Französisch B2 - Cours de préparation à un échange universitaire
Description:
CONTENT:
Die LV bereitet auf ein ausländisches Studium oder Praktikum in einem frankophonen Land vor, indem es verschiedene Aspekte der Kultur und der Gesellschaft aufgreift. und somit die interkulturelle Kompetenz und Performanz erhöht werden.

-	Vermittlung von Umgangsstrategien mit fremden Strukturen und Formen (Hochschullandschaft, Lehr-und Lernformen, Kommunikationsformen)
-	Schärfung des Bewusstseins für interkulturelle Aspekte
-	Bewerbung
-	Entwicklung von Hörstrategien
-	Einführung in die Praxis schriftlicher akademischer Arbeit
Zur Festigung der mündlichen und schriftlichen Fertigkeit werden Schwerpunkte der Grammatik wiederholt und vertieft.

OBJECTIVES:
Die LV orientiert sich am Niveau „B2- Selbständige Sprachverwendung“ des GER. Der/die Studierende ist in der Lage, durch situationsrelevantes interkulturelles Wissen über Universitäten und Berufswelt im französischen Sprachraum angemessen zu kommunizieren und einen Studien-, Projekt- oder Forschungsaufenthalt, ein Praktikum oder Weiterbildungsmaßnahmen im französischen Sprachraum zu absolvieren.
Skills: ['Clear technical and non-technical communication', 'Cross-functional collaboration', 'Stakeholder and requirements management']

Title: Französisch B2 Le francais pour la profession
Description:
CONTENT:
In this module, students will increase their knowledge of French as a foreign language, enabling them to discuss with a native speaker topics of general or professional interest actively and with a certain degree of fluency and to argue for a position in a comprehensible fashion. On the one hand, the module provides an introducation to the French business world and, on the other hand, prepares students to study in a French-speaking region. Particular attention will be devoted to the development of communication skills and intercultural competencies. Certain grammatical structures will be reviewed and studied in greater depth to consolidate oral and writing skills. In this module, applying for jobs in France is a central focus.

OBJECTIVES:
The module is aimed at level "B2 Independent Language Use" of the CEFR. Students acquire knowledge of French as a foreign language at the standard language level with a focus on intercultural, cultural and academic aspects. Following completion of this module, with their intercultural knowledge, students can communicate appropriately about the university and the business world in French-speaking regions and seek a professional training program or further education in those regions.

Title: Französisch B2/C1 La France actuelle
Description:
CONTENT:
In this module, knowledge of French as a foreign language will be further developed, enabling students to communicate with a native speaker actively and with a certain degree of fluency on topics of general interest or in familiar specialist areas and to argue a point understandably. In order to consolidate speaking and writing skills, certain French grammatical structures will be reviewed and extended. This module offers a cross-section of contemporary French culture, in which social tendencies, as reflected in newspaper articles, and radio and television programs, will be discussed. Topics suggested by students for examination are welcome. Students must independently prepare and deliver a short presentation on a cultural, social or scientific topic connected with France and then answer questions afterward.

OBJECTIVES:
The module is aimed at level B2-C1 of the CEFR, depending on the level of the student's knowledge. Students acquire knowledge of French as a foreign language at the standard language level with a focus on intercultural, cultural and academic aspects. Following completion of this module, students can report on texts in detail and coherently, summarize information, describe their impressions, and defend their positions. They can describe the content of texts, discussions, or television programs and offer their opinions. They are capable of spontaneously and fluently expressing themselves, without obviously having to search for words. Students can communicate clearly and in a structured fashion, both orally and in writing, on many topics in their areas of interest or specialization.

Title: Französisch C1 - s'exprimer à l'écrit comme à l'oral
Description:
CONTENT:
In dieser LV werden Kenntnisse in der Fremdsprache Französisch erarbeitet, die es den Studierenden ermöglichen, schriftlich wie mündlich in Themenbereichen aus Alltag, Beruf und Kultur situationsadäquat zu handeln (agieren und reagieren).

Sie lernen, Textsorten und Schreibstile zu unterscheiden und situationsadäquat anzuwenden. Sie üben, komplexe Sachtexte auch außerhalb des eigenen Fachgebietes zu analysieren, zu komprimieren und kritisch schriftlich sowie mündlich zu kommentieren.

Diese LV orientiert sich an Niveau "C1-Kompetente Sprachverwendung" des GER. Nach der Teilnahme an der Lehrveranstaltung kann der/die Studierende auf sehr hohem Niveau in unterschiedlichsten Situationen schriftlich und mündlich kommunizieren. Er/Sie ist in der Lage, die Fremdsprache mündlich und schriftlich sowohl im Auslandsstudium als auch im Beruf wirksam und flexibel zu gebrauchen. Er/Sie kann ein breites Spektrum anspruchsvoller, längerer Texte verstehen und auch implizite Bedeutungen erfassen. Er/Sie kann sich spontan und fließend ausdrücken, ohne öfter deutlich erkennbar nach Worten suchen zu müssen. Er/Sie kann sich klar, strukturiert und ausführlich zu komplexen Sachverhalten äußern und dabei verschiedene Mittel zur Textverknüpfung angemessen verwenden.

Title: From General to Clinical
Description:
CONTENT:
This seminar will explore the foundations and capabilities of foundation models, with a
focus on pretraining strategies, representational generalization, and efficient adaptation
methods. We will examine state-of-the-art foundation models and discuss how they can
be adapted to downstream tasks, especially in medical imaging, through techniques such
as self-supervised learning, cross-domain transfer, and parameter-efficient tuning.

OBJECTIVES:
We will review state-of-the-art foundation models and their practical adaptations for
medical imaging and cover: (i) What to adapt: identify which model parameters to adapt, explore common strategies for adaptation (ii) How to adapt: The various strategies by which the models can be adapted to the target data (iii) Evaluation for clinical context: discuss methods for handling diverse distributional shifts that mirror real-world clinical scenarios.
Skills: ['Python', 'TensorFlow', 'PyTorch', 'Machine Learning and AI', 'Analytics', 'Data Science and Analytics', 'Research-oriented mindset', 'Ability to learn complex systems quickly']

Title: From Invention to Patent
Description:
CONTENT:
Research results are important sources for new products and services in the era of Open Innovation for business
and industry. But how can research results be protected and commercialized?

A practice-oriented introduction to intellectual property rights, with a special focus on university inventions:
In addition to patents, other relevant areas of intellectual property (IP) — such as design protection, domain and trademark protection, and utility models — are thoroughly covered by experts in each field.

The course explores the path from invention to obtaining the respective IP right, its legal enforcement in court, and the economic
exploitation of the IP right, particularly in the context of university spin-offs. Students will then deepen their understanding of patenting opportunities in their specific technical disciplines through practical case studies, working in separate groups based on their fields of study.

OBJECTIVES:
After participating in the course, students will be able to assess whether a technical development or research result is eligible for patent protection. They will also be capable of drafting an invention disclosure for their own invention. Participants will understand how to obtain patents both nationally and internationally, how to enforce them legally, and how to commercially exploit them.
Skills: ['Intellectual property', 'Patent', 'Business software applications', 'Research-oriented mindset', 'Business and product-oriented thinking']

Title: From Lab to Market
Description:
CONTENT:
Germany is globally recognized as a powerhouse in patenting groundbreaking technologies. However, significant challenges remain in translating these innovations into successful market-ready products. This module addresses this critical gap, equipping students with the necessary skills and insights to bridge academic research and industry realities effectively.
Participants will explore key concepts of deep-tech commercialization, including technology validation, intellectual property strategy, market analysis, business model innovation, and fundraising strategies for startups. Through a balanced combination of theoretical frameworks and real-world case studies, students will learn proven methodologies to transform cutting-edge research into viable commercial applications.

OBJECTIVES:
The module, offered in collaboration with TUM Venture Labs Robotics, provides a unique opportunity to engage with leading experts and real-world case studies, preparing participants for impactful careers in academia, startups, and industry.

Students will finish this module equipped with a robust understanding of how to successfully navigate the complex journey of translating scientific research into market-impacting technologies. Upon completion of the module, students will:
• Understand the essential steps for transitioning technology from lab-scale prototypes to market-ready products.
• Develop insights into business model creation and intellectual property strategies specific to deep-tech startups.
• Gain practical knowledge of market validation, customer discovery, and effective communication strategies for technology pitches.
• Learn directly from successful founders who have navigated the commercialization journey from academia to industry.
Skills: ['Business and product-oriented thinking', 'Project planning and prioritization', 'Market research', 'Product development']

Title: From "New Atlantis" to "Blade Runner" - Utopias and Dystopias in Culture, Literature and Film
Description:
CONTENT:
What would an ideal society look like? What political order and what laws would this utopian state have to be based on? And when does a utopia become a dystopia? 
In this interdisciplinary seminar we will look at various fictional utopian texts and discuss real-world concepts and attempts to create ideal societies. In addition to different utopias, we will also look at the representation of dystopias in different media (novels, films, computer games) and examine the role of science and technology in both genres. Additionally, participants will work in groups to design their own utopian and dystopian societies and stories.

OBJECTIVES:
Students read literary texts from different eras, watch films and other media relevant to the topic and analyze them according to previously discussed criteria and methods. They research current discourses on the topic of the course and critically analyze them. 
Students also learn how to create and present an academic poster.

Title: Führen und Verantwortung tragen - Menschen und Teams entwickeln
Description:

In the area of methodological competence:

- Apply aspects of feedback interviews, development interviews and coaching elements in interviews.

Title: Führung durch Motivation in der Schule
Description:
CONTENT:
In dem Seminar werden die Themen "Führung und Motivation" in der Schule eingehend besprochen. Diese Themenfelder sind auf verschiedenen Ebenen in der Schule relevant: Eine zentrale Aufgabe einer Lehrperson ist es, SchülerInnen zu motivieren. Die Lehrperson nimmt insofern eine Führungsaufgabe wahr. Aber auch die Lehrperson muss in der Lage sein, sich selbst zu motivieren und zuführen, und sie kann diese Fähigkeiten auch ihren SchülerInnen vermitteln. In diesem Seminar wird ein forschungsbasiertes, in der Praxis verschiedener Organisationen erprobtes Konzept vermitteilt. Schwerpunkte der Veranstaltung "Führung durch Motivation" sind (1) Das 3K-Modell der Arbeitsmotivation, (2) Ziele und Motive, (3) Selbstüberwindung und Wille, (4) Intrinsische Motivation und Flow, (5) Transformationale Führung und Motivation und (6) Authentische Führung und Charisma.

OBJECTIVES:
Nach erfolgreichem Abschluss des Seminars sind die Studierenden in der Lage, wissenschaftlich fundierte Modelle, Befunde und Techniken aus Motivationspsychologie und Führungsforschung abzurufen, zu verstehen, und praktisch im Schulkontext anzuwenden.

Title: Fundamental Electrochemistry
Description:
CONTENT:
The lectures and the accompanying exercises of this module consist of two parts. In the first part, Prof. Hubert Gasteiger provides a comprehensive overview on the most commonly used electroanalytical methods and the underlying phenomena that govern the corresponding electrochemical reactions: Beginning with the thermodynamics, Prof. Gasteiger first introduces electrochemical cells, the electrochemical potential, and the concept of reference electrodes. This is followed by a detailed explanation of the ionic conduction in electrolytes, electrochemical kinetics, as well as mass transport and diffusion effects. Finally, Prof. Gasteiger applies this knowledge to electroanalytical methods, including cyclic voltammetry, rotating disk electrode experiments, micro-electrodes, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. In the second part, Prof. Tom Nilges introduces thermoelectric materials and discusses the transport phenomena in solid electrolytes. He complements the analytical toolkit by further spectroscopic methods.

OBJECTIVES:
Upon successful completion of this module, students will be able to identify relevant research literature and critically review publications in the field of electrochemistry. The students will be able to make suggestions and develop experiments to address specific questions in related areas of research, e.g., electrical energy storage and energy conversion. The module provides them with a comprehensive overview of the most commonly used electroanalytical techniques (e.g., cyclic voltammetry, rotating disk electrode experiments) and describes the underlying phenomena that govern the corresponding electrochemical reactions (e.g., ionic transport, electrode kinetics, electrochemical potential).
Skills: ['Electrochemistry', 'Thermodynamics', 'Analytical thinking and structured problem solving', 'Research-oriented mindset']

Title: Fundamentals of Aircraft Operations
Description:
CONTENT:
The course "Fundamentals of Aircraft Operations” covers a multi-disciplinary range of relevant topics in the field of aircraft operation with focus on commercial air transport. Starting with a review of the history of civil aviation, the course presents important players, operating processes and procedures, and boundary conditions of the air transport system and additionally portrays the future perspectives of new technologies and their potential impact on aircraft operation. The following topics are depicted: history of civil aviation, overview of the aircraft design process, aircraft operators, airports, air traffic control, commercial aircraft operation, environmental impact of aviation, electric aircraft, unmanned aerial vehicles (military aircraft operation, aircraft maintenance).

OBJECTIVES:
At the end of the course, students are able to understand all important aspects as well as their mutual interaction in the field of aircraft operation, and to evaluate them in the context of the development of modern aviation systems.

Title: Fundamentals of Artificial Intelligence
Description:
CONTENT:
- Task environments and the structure of intelligent agents.

- Solving problems by searching: breadth-first search, uniform-cost search, depth-first search, depth-limited search, iterative deepening search, greedy best-first search, A* search.

- Constraint satisfaction problems: defining constraint satisfaction problems, backtracking search for constraint satisfaction problems, heuristics for backtracking search, interleaving search and inference, the structure of constraint satisfaction problems.

- Logical agents: propositional logic, propositional theorem proving, syntax and semantics of first-order logic, using first-order logic, knowledge engineering in first-order logic, reducing first-order inference to propositional inference, unification and lifting, forward chaining, backward chaining, resolution.

- Bayesian networks: acting under uncertainty, basics of probability theory, Bayesian networks, inference in Bayesian networks, approximate inference in Bayesian networks.

- Hidden Markov models: time and uncertainty, inference in hidden Markov models (filtering, prediction, smoothing, most likely explanation), approximate inference in hidden Markov models.

- Rational decisions: introduction to utility theory, utility functions, decision networks, the value of information, Markov decision processes, value iteration, policy iteration, partially observable Markov decision processes.

- Learning: types of learning, supervised learning, learning decision trees.

- Introduction to robotics: robot hardware, robotic perception, path planning, planning uncertain movements, control of movements, robotic software architectures, application domains.

OBJECTIVES:
After attending the course, you are able to create artificial intelligence on a basic level using search techniques, logics, probability theory and decision theory. Your learned abilities will be the foundation for more advanced topics in artificial intelligence. In particular, you will acquire the following skills:

- You can analyze problems of artificial intelligence and judge how difficult it is to solve them.

- You can recall the basic concepts of intelligent agents and know possible task environments.

- You can formalize, apply, and understand search problems.

- You understand the difference between constraint satisfaction and classical search problems as well as apply and evaluate various constraint satisfaction approaches.

- You can critically assess the advantages and disadvantages of logics in artificial intelligence.

- You can formalize problems using propositional and first-order logic.

- You can apply automatic reasoning techniques in propositional and first-order logic.

- You understand the advantages and disadvantages of probabilistic and logic-based reasoning.

- You can apply and critically asses methods for probabilistic reasoning with Bayesian networks and Hidden Markov Models.

- You understand and know how to compute rational decisions.

- You have a basic understanding on how a machine learns.

- You know the basic areas and concepts in robotics.

Title: Future Making & Creativity
Description:
CONTENT:
The slogan “everything is interconnected” has gained widespread resonance in recent years. For some, it emerges from spiritual traditions or engagements with Eastern philosophies. Others encounter it through the study of quantum physics, systems theory, or process philosophy. Still others arrive at this insight through patterns observed in everyday life. While such ideas were once confined to the esoteric margins of Western thought, today even fields grounded in empirical science increasingly acknowledge the entangled, relational, and distributed nature of life, agency, and planetary transformation.

Scientific paradigms are shifting: “nature” is no longer understood solely as a mechanistic system to be governed or predicted, but increasingly as a complex assemblage of dynamic, distributed, and emerging relationships - systems in which humans are not merely participants, but also constitutive elements. Historically, science often sought to develop increasingly refined analytical tools to examine such patterns in human relations with nonhuman entities, thereby frequently reinforcing an ontological separation between humans and the world they observe. As a response, more-than-human studies aim to challenge these anthropocentric assumptions and illuminate the multiple, often subtle ways in which human life is entangled with ecological, social, and multispecies systems.

Yet a persistent epistemological and affective question remains: How can we come to “know” what lies beyond our sensory and cognitive capacities? How might we relate to beings and processes whose temporalities, chemistries, and intelligences do not align with human perception? And just as importantly, how might we become aware of the unconscious scripts, shadows, and resistances that shape our relationships with the more-than-human world?

This experimental laboratory investigates these questions by integrating artistic and ethnographic methodologies to engage with more-than-human worlds. Students will critically examine... (see document attached)

Title: F1TENTH
Description:
CONTENT:
The course offers the opportunity to learn the basics of autonomous driving and robotics through hands-on experience with the F1TENTH vehicle. We will first teach the basics of autonomous driving by teaching the theory of perception (Perception), path planning (Planning) and regulation (Control) and their programming. After the theory, we will further deepen the most important software modules in a practical way in this practical course. This software must then be implemented and optimised by the students on real vehicle hardware. The central element here is the F1TENTH vehicle, a 1:10 vehicle platform that is equipped with sensors (camera, lidar), computer hardware (Nvidia Jetson) and further electronics to be able to drive fully autonomously.  The goal of each term is to implement the theoretically learned algorithms on the real vehicle and then have the vehicle drive fully autonomously.

OBJECTIVES:
After attending the module, students will have a comprehensive overview of the algorithms used in autonomous driving in the areas of perception, path planning and control. They will be able to select the appropriate method and algorithm for various problems in autonomous driving and implement them with the corresponding code. Furthermore, you will be able to develop and program the software in such a way that it can efficiently and safely move a real, 1:10 autonomous model vehicle. In doing so, students will learn the basics of software development for real hardware use. Based on this, students will then be able to develop inter- and transdisciplinary approaches to combine the three elements (environmental, social and economic development).In addition, students will learn how to improve and optimise existing software and algorithms using real vehicle measurement data. By working together in teams of their own discipline, but also beyond that in interdisciplinary teams, students are able to understand each other's language, justify their own decisions and convince with arguments.

Title: Game Physics
Description:
CONTENT:
Concepts and methods from the areas:
- Foundations of animation and animation technologies
- technical mechanics (kinematics, dynamics, contact), and rigid body modeling
- methods for collision detection
- deformable bodies and springs
- fluid modeling and simulation
- basics of numerical simulation
- particle systems

OBJECTIVES:
Participants acquire knowledge of the physical simulation of real phenomena, and effects which are increasingly prevalent in computer games. Numerous physical models are discussed, and corresponding numerical approaches for solving them are demonstrated. The focus of these methods are interactive environments for real-time applications.
An additional goal of the curriculum is the ability to implement simulation algorithms and integration methods with the C++ programming language.

Title: Game Theory - Lecture
Description:
CONTENT:
Subject-specific content
• Strategic interaction in economic and managerial contexts
• Conflict, cooperation, and incentives in multi-agent settings
• Decision-making under complete and incomplete information
• Applications to negotiation, pricing, entry deterrence, signaling, reputation, or related concepts

Methodological content
• Formal modeling of static and dynamic games
• Equilibrium concepts (Nash, subgame perfect, Bayesian, sequential)
• Quantitative analysis and logical reasoning in strategic environments

OBJECTIVES:
Upon completion of the module, students can
• formally analyze strategic interactions using foundational models of game theory,
• evaluate the suitability of different equilibrium concepts for modeling competitive and cooperative behavior,
• assess the implications of information structures and incentives in static and dynamic games,
• and critically examine strategic situations in economics and management using formal tools of game-theoretic analysis.

Title: Games mit Bewegung- Dein Körper als 3D Nutzerinterface
Description:
CONTENT:
This module introduces current techniques for sensing, tracking and interacting in three-dimensional space. Subsequently, issues and problems in user interactions with 3D user interfaces will be discussed. 
During the seminar, practical tasks targeting 3D user interfaces and mixed reality applications are set and continued in small project teams in the second half of the semester. A project task is implemented here in terms of conceptual design and implementation in an interactive three-dimensional application. The progress of the project is monitored in an agile and iterative manner to be able to give feedback on the progress in a timely manner. Finally, the projects are analyzed using user-centered evaluation methods and discussed in pair reviews between the individual groups.

OBJECTIVES:
After completing this module, students will be able to use a selection of novel interaction devices currently available on the market for motion capturing in interactive applications. They will also be able to implement simple animated characters. They know software systems for interpreting motion data, as well as components of a pipeline for learning selected gestures. Through practical use of these systems, they can differentiate between the levels of difficulty of selected ideas for interactive applications. As well as implement them with available interaction devices and gesture interpretation software. They can classify basic problems in 3D user interactions and derive and implement their relevance in connection with the techniques discussed.

Title: Gender Studies in Architecture
Description:
CONTENT:
Gender Studies in Architecture: "Strollology - Spatial Choreographies"
Lehrbeauftragte: Henriette Lutz

«Ich lebe in Städten. Sie sind mein Zuhause. Der urbane Raum ist mein Alltag. Ich
bewege mich durch ihn wie durch mein Wohnzimmer. Ich kenne seine Ecken und
Kanten, seine Kuschelorte. Ich kenne die Straßen, viel befahren, viel begangen, auch von
mir. Er ist Teil meines Denkens, meiner Welt.»
Dündar, Özlem Özgül u.a. (Hg.), Flexen . Flâneusen* schreiben Städte, Berlin 2019., S. 11.

Der Kurs orientiert sich an der Theorie der Spaziergangswissenschaften von Annemarie
und Lucius Burckhardt. Demnach wird (Stadt-)Landschaft als Konstrukt verstanden. Die
Wahrnehmung der (gebauten) Umwelt ist abhängig von individuellen Erfahrungen, der
eigenen Sozialisierung und somit auch von Bildung, Kultur, Herkunft, Geschlecht, Alter,
etc.

Anhand experimenteller Wahrnehmungsspaziergänge in Kombination mit theoretischen
und/oder literarischen Texten, sowie eigener Feldforschung wird die Wechselwirkung
geschlechtsspezifischer Perspektiven in Bezug auf Stadträume analysiert. Das
forschende Gehen dient als Methode, um die alltägliche Lebenswelt zu reflektieren und
kritisch wahrzunehmen.
Dabei wird unter anderem, über Zugänglichkeit, Sicherheit, Sichtbarkeit und Aneignung
öffentlicher Orte diskutiert. Ziel ist es, ein erweitertes Verständnis von Raum zu
entwickeln, das Gender, soziale Gerechtigkeit und Diversität in der Stadtplanung und
Stadtnutzung berücksichtigt.

Das Seminar findet grundsätzlich in einem zweiwöchigen Turnus ganztägig statt und
umfasst experimentelle Spaziergänge, kollektiven Lesungen, Diskussionen,
Recherchen, Schreiben, Skizzieren, um nur einige Aktivitäten zu nennen. Von allen
Kursteilnehmenden wird erwartet, dass sie bei allen Seminarsitzungen anwesend sind,
sich aktiv an den Spaziergängen beteiligen und bereit sind einen öffentlichen
Spaziergang als Semesterabschluss mitzugestalten.

OBJECTIVES:
Die Methoden aus den Spaziergangswissenschaften unterstützen eine Sensibilisierung in Bezug auf eine diverse Wahrnehmung von Raum. Nach Absolvierung sind die Studierenden in der Lage den Stadtraum im Hinblick auf bestehende Geschlechterrollen und die eigene Wahrnehmung kritisch zu hinterfragen. Die Spaziergangswissenschaft kann als angewandte Methode, auch im weiteren Studienverlauf und in der beruflichen Praxis selbstständig angewandt werden, um komplexe Fragestellungen sichtbar, diskutierbar und kommunizierbar zu machen.

Title: Genderkompetenz als Schlüsselqualifikation
Description:
CONTENT:
Der „kleine Unterschied“ ist bei den einen größer als gedacht, die anderen reden ihn klein. Das Bundesverfassungsgericht hat währenddessen das 3. Geschlecht (divers) eingeführt. Die Ehe für Alle wurde als wichtiger Schritt zur Gleichberechtigung gefeiert, wenn auch nicht von allen. Es tut sich was in der Gesellschaft und schon länger in der Wissenschaftsgemeinde.

Doch wie geht Mensch mit den neuen Optionen und Anforderungen um? Welche Rollenerwartungen ergeben sich für Mitarbeitende und Leitung in Wirtschaft und Wissenschaft.
Geschlechterrollen beeinflussen unser alltägliches Verhalten und unsere Wahrnehmung. Höchste Zeit, dass wir uns diese Einflüsse bewusst machen.

Was erwartet die Teilnehmenden?
Der Workshop läuft über 2 Tage und im Anschluss gibt es selbstorganisierte Gruppenarbeiten als Hausaufgabe. Inhaltlich gehen wir auf die aktuelle Genderdiskussion ein und klären Fragen nach Definitionen, Theorien und Kompetenzgrundlagen. Gleichzeitig sensibilisiert der Workshop für eigene Vorbilder, strukturelle Ungleichheit, den Einfluss von Kultur und genderspezifischen Handlungsmustern.
Darüber hinaus werden interaktive Workshop-Module dafür sorgen, dass wir ergebnisoffen und interessenorientiert an einem verbesserten Umgang zwischen den Geschlechtern arbeiten. Ziel des interaktiven Lern- und Forschungsprojekts sind spannende Forschungsarbeiten (Gender-Pacers), die von den anderen Teilnehmenden eingesehen werden können und das Wissen weiter vertiefen helfen.

Title: Generalized Linear Models
Description:
CONTENT:
The main topic of this course will be regression methods for non-normal response data. These generalized linear models (GLM) include regression models for binary, count, nominal and positive response data. Applications of these models can be found in finance, insurance, economics, medicine and biology. In addition to classical GLM's such as logistic, probit, Poisson, Gamma, and log-linear models, we will discuss extensions to adjust for overdispersion and models with random effects. Both theory and practice will be emphasized. Statistical software knowledge of R is expected.

OBJECTIVES:
Upon completing this module, students will understand, analyze, apply the theory of modern regression methods, such as explorative data analysis, model fitting and validation, and interpret the results. Furthermore, they will select appropriate regression models to a given data set using the statistical software R.

Title: Geographic Text Analysis
Description:
CONTENT:
Text data sources can be a very helpful in answering geodetic and geographic questions, and can complement remote sensing data in various ways. In particular, social media has emerged as a novel source of geodata, but other text sources like news items or governmental streams are also valuable. In this lecture, students will learn how to analyze text data sources on a large scale using techniques from classical Natural Language Processing and state-of-the-art machine learning for tasks such as filtering, classification, and geocoding. These methods are demonstrated on news sources and large social media corpora. Approaches for fusion with other geodata sources, in particular remote sensing data, are highlighted. Questions of privacy, ethics, and trustworthiness are also discussed. The lecture will also include examples from real-world applications such as disaster management, building function detection, land usage, etc.

OBJECTIVES:
By completing this module, students will understand the geographic information to be gained from text data, particularly social media data. They will be able implement methods for retrieval and storage, and to apply models from natural language processing and machine learning for the automated analysis of large text data sets. Students will be able to judge how and when to use such data, as well as analyze results and evaluate the employed approaches on a variety of real-life applications.

Title: Geometrisch exakte Balkentheorien
Description:
CONTENT:
The focus of the lecture lies on geometrically exact beam theories as an example for nonlinear models in structural mechanics. Slender beam- or fiber-like components represent essential constituents of mechanical systems in countless fields of application and scientific disciplines. Examples are high-tensile industrial ropes and webbings, fiber-reinforced composite materials or synthetic polymer materials. On entirely different time and length scales, such slender components are relevant when analyzing the supercoiling process of DNA strands, the characteristics of carbon nanotubes or the cytoskeleton of biological cells, a biopolymer network of highly slender filaments that crucially influences the mechanics of cells. Often, these slender components can be described by means of geometrically fully nonlinear beam models. In many cases, the interaction between these beam- or fiber-like components—such as through mechanical contact or intermolecular forces—plays an important role.

In this lecture, the so-called geometrically exact beam theory will be considered, which is based on a fundamental kinematic assumption and accounts for large rotations and strains in a consistent manner, i.e., without additional approximations. In particular, the geometrically exact Simo-Reissner beam theory (kinematic assumption: beam cross-sections remain plain; nonlinear counterpart of the linear Timoshenko beam theory) and the geometrically exact Kirchhoff-Love beam theory (kinematic assumption: beam cross-sections remain plain and normal to the centerline; nonlinear counterpart of the linear Euler-Bernoulli beam theory) will be introduced as well as their interpretation as a 1D Cosserat continuum, i.e., a continuum theory with three translational and three rotational degrees of freedom.

Since the presence of large rotations is an inherent characteristic of fully nonlinear structural theories, the theory of larger rotations (in particular the theory of the special orthogonal group SO(3)) will be introduced in the beginning. Based on these fundamentals, the geometrically exact beam theory will be postulated as a nonlinear Cosserat continuum theory consisting of (translational and rotational) strain measures, stress resultants, constitutive relations and mechanical equilibrium conditions (in spatial and material form, respectively). In addition, it will be shown that the geometrically exact beam theory can be derived from the equations of nonlinear continuum mechanics supplemented by the fundamental kinematic assumption (e.g., plain beam cross-sections). For this purpose, a summary of the nonlinear continuum mechanics theory of solids (3D Boltzmann continua) will be presented, among others underlining the structural similarities with the geometrically nonlinear beam theory (1D Cosserat continuum).

Eventually, the lecture provides an overview of modeling approaches for mechanical contact interactions between beam- or fiber-like structures (e.g., in ropes or fabrics) and the embedding of such structures in a 3D Boltzmann continuum as required, e.g., for the fiber-scale modeling of fiber-reinforced composite materials. Finally, relevant numerical discretization and solution methods (in particular discretization schemes based on the Finite Element Method - FEM) will be presented. In a dedicated lab session, students will apply these methods using a FEM software developed at the institute to analyze selected problems of fully nonlinear beam mechanics.

OBJECTIVES:
Upon successful completion of this module, students can define the most important fundamental concepts of geometrically exact beam theories. They understand the interplay between underlying modelling assumptions and describing differential equations and the relation to linear beam models as conveyed in the Bachelor studies, which can be identified as special cases of the more general nonlinear theories. Moreover, the students acquire the ability to analyze, compare and assess different solution approaches and methods for geometrically exact beam theories and to apply and transfer these solution strategies to specific problems, e.g., the calculation of geometrically nonlinear deformation of (beam) structures.

Title: Georg Friedrich Händel
Description:
CONTENT:
Händels (1685 – 1759) bedeutende musikalische und finanzielle Karriere in England ist nicht nur seinen herausragenden musikalischen Fähigkeiten geschuldet, sondern verdankt sich in vielfältiger Weise auch den besonderen gesellschaftlichen und politischen Konstellationen des politischen Systems Englands (UK) zu Beginn des 18. Jahrhundert.  
Mit der Thronbesteigung 1714 von Georg I (König von Großbritannien und Irland aus dem Hause Hannover (Welfen) sowie seiner Gattin Karoline) war ein Förderer Händels zur politischen Macht gelangt, der in einem gesellschaftlichen und politischen Umfeld agierte, das von einem einflussreichen Philosophen, gemeint ist John Locke (1632 – 1704), weitreichend beeinflusst worden war. 
Mit „A letter concerning Toleration“, „Two Treatises on Government“, „An Essay Concerning Humane Understanding“ argumentierte Locke u.a., dass eine Regierung nur Legitimität besitzt, wenn sie die Zustimmung der Regierten aufweist und die Naturrechte Leben, Freiheit und Eigentum schützt. John Locke entwarf das Modell eines selbstbewussten, emanzipierten Individuums, eine autonom liberal und individualistisch agierende politische Person, die, auf sich selbst verwiesen, ihre eigene Welt und ihr eigenes (ökonomisches) Schicksal gestaltet.
Und G. F. Händel? Händels Existenz repräsentiert die Realisation dieses Lockeschen Entwurfs einer Person. Gerade dieser Entwurf hatte für Händel die größte Anziehungskraft. Schon als Kind mit zwölf Jahren charakterisiert sich Händel im Trauergedicht auf seinen Vater als den „freyen Künsten ergebener“ und sein ganzes Leben als Künstler wird geprägt sein durch künstlerisches, ökonomisches und politisches Handeln in selbstbewusster Eigenständigkeit, manchmal wird dieses Handeln aber auch kompromisslos und stur sein.
In diesem Seminar wird das gemeinsame Nachdenken über die Philosophie der „Fairest Isle“ ergänzt durch die Betrachtung der politisch-philosophisch inspirierten Werke Georg Friedrich Händels, vor allem seiner englischsprachigen Oratorien.

OBJECTIVES:
Grundlegende Kenntnisse der Musikgeschichte, philosophischer Ideengeschichte und deren Anwendung zur Analyse musikalischer Werke.

Title: Geschichte und Geschichten
Description:
CONTENT:
Was bietet uns heute (noch) die Beschäftigung mit Persönlichkeiten aus der Vergangenheit? Was fangen wir mit ihren Texten an, was leiten wir daraus für unsere Gegenwart ab? Am Beispiel von Erika Mann (1905-1969), dem „kühnen Kind“, wie Literaturnobelpreisträger Thomas Mann (1875-1955) seine älteste Tochter bewundernd nannte, stellen wir uns diesen Fragen und versuchen, uns damit der Geschichte gegenüber zu positionieren. 

Erika Manns Leben verläuft geradezu exemplarisch an den entscheidenden Schnittstellen des 20. Jahrhunderts entlang: von der Rebellin und „neuen Frau“ der 1920er Jahre über die kompromisslose Streiterin für Frieden und Freiheit in den 1930/40er Jahren bis zur konservativen Nachlassverwalterin für den Vater und ihren Bruder Klaus nach dem Zweiten Weltkrieg. Nie wollte sie sich dem „Familienfluch Schreiben“ beugen, eignete sich ihn jedoch auf ganz eigene Weise an. 
Schlagworte wie Queerness, Cultural Clash, Exilerfahrung oder Female Heritage können auf sie und ihr vielseitiges Werk ausprobiert werden, greift sie in ihren mitunter sehr modern klingenden Schriften Themen auf, die auch für uns heute (wieder/ noch) aktuell sind – politisch, gesellschaftlich, kulturell. 

Das gemeinsame Lesen und Diskutieren ausgewählter Texte soll den Zugang zu Erika Manns Lebenswelt erfahrbar machen. Zugleich soll deutlich werden, inwieweit die persönliche Perspektive die Bewertung der Vergangenheit beeinflusst. Durch das Schreiben und Referieren eigener Texte, die von Erika Manns Werk und/ oder ihrer Biographie inspiriert sind, werden diese Beobachtungen auf einer weiteren Ebene reflektiert.

Erika Manns literarisches Schaffen umfasst Feuilletons, Reiseberichte, Glossen, Kabaretttexte, Reden, politische Bücher über Hitler und den Nationalsozialismus sowie Kinderbücher und ein riesiges Konvolut Briefe. Es ist größtenteils digital über das Literaturarchiv Monacensia zugänglich. Ein Besuch dort wird vorstellen, wie ein solches Erbe betreut und für nachfolgende Generationen bewahrt, aber auch wie damit recherchiert und gearbeitet wird.

OBJECTIVES:
Die exemplarische Beschäftigung mit Biographie, Werk und Wirken einer historischen Persönlichkeit ermöglicht, diese zeitgeschichtlich einzuordnen und ihre Bedeutung für die Gegenwart zu hinterfragen. Die subjektive und kontextuelle Prägung eines solchen Vorgehens wird herausgearbeitet. Zugleich eröffnen literarische Schreibübungen eine neue Reflexionsebene.

Title: Gestaltung der künstlichen Intelligenz unter gesellschaftlichen und juristischen Vorgaben
Description:
CONTENT:
Ziel der Vorlesung ist es, die Teilnehmer in das moderne Forschungsgebiet der Gestaltung der künstlichen Intelligenz (engl. Artificial Intelligence - AI) unter gesellschaftlichen und juristischen Vorgaben einzuführen. Die enorme Bedeutung dieses Forschungsgebietes leitet sich aus der wissenschaftlichen Erkenntnis der New Institutional Economics (NIE) ab, dass die völlig unregulierte Entwicklung der AI durch wenige Tech Companies mit zweifelhaften Geschäftsmodellen bereits zu starken gesellschaftlichen Fehlentwicklungen geführt hat. Auch die moderne Gesellschaft hat bereits reagiert und eine erste progressive Entwicklung zur Regulierung von AI gestartet [1- 5]. In der Vorlesung wird eine Einführung in die NIE gegeben und das Prinzip der Shared Prosperity als Optimierungskriterium zur Steuerung der gesellschaftlichen Entwicklung eingeführt [6-8]. Das Wirken des Prinzips der Shared Prosperity wird anhand der aggregierten Produktionsfunktion erklärt. Im Anschluss werden die NIE Mechanismen zur Gestaltung einer gesellschaftlich progressiven Entwicklung der AI eingeführt. Diese NIE Mechanismen werden dann mit der Computing-Theorie und der Informationstheorie der AI verbunden. Es werden auf diesem Weg in der Vorlesung die allgemeinen wissenschaftlichen Grundlagen der Gestaltung der AI unter dem Optimierungsprinzip der Shared Prosperity entwickelt. Anhand dieser wissenschaftlichen Grundlagen werden erste Anwendungen für die AI Technologie Entwicklung entsprechend [9-11] in der Vorlesung vorgestellt.

OBJECTIVES:
Am Ende der Veranstaltung ist der Student mit den wissenschaftlichen Grundlagen zur zukünftigen Gestaltung von AI vertraut. Er kann u.a. auch die behandelten Mechanismen der NIE in der Entwicklung bzw. im Entwurf von zukünftigen AI Anwendungen und AI Algorithmen einsetzen.
Skills: ['Artificial intelligence', 'Ethical awareness and data responsibility', 'Research-oriented mindset']

Title: Getränkemikrobiologie und biologische Betriebsüberwachung
Description:
CONTENT:
Der Inhalt des Moduls setzt sich wie folgt zusammen:
• Mikroorganismen allgemein: Sterilisation/Gefährdungsklassifizierung – Zellmorphologie von Bakterien, Hefen und Schimmelpilzen
• Kultivierung von Mikroorganismen – Anaerobiose – Vermehrung + Wachstum – Lebendkeimzahlbestimmung – Physiologisch-Biochemische Tests – Bestimmung des physiologischen Zustands von Hefen – Färbemethoden – Identifizierung von Mikroorganismen (Schlüsseltests) 
• Brauereimikrobiologie: Eigenschutz der Getränke – Schädlichkeitskategorien -Hefetaxonomie – unter- und obergärige Kulturhefen – Wilde Hefen – Hefedifferenzierung – Bierschädliche Bakterien (experimenteller Nachweis)
• Nachweismedien für Bierschädlinge – Stufenkontrolle – Nachweissicherheit Filter bis Füller – Mikrobiologische Stabilität – Luftkeimanalyse
• Wasser: Verkeimung – Bakterien – Trinkwasser – Mineralwasser
• Mikrobiologie alkoholfreier Getränke

OBJECTIVES:
Nach der erfolgreichen Teilnahme am Modul Getränkemikrobiologie und Biologische Betriebsüberwachung sind die Studierenden in der Lage:
- Getränkespezifische Kultur- und Schadorganismen zu benennen.
- Getränkespezifische Kultur- und Schadorganismen anhand ihrer Eigenschaften, Kultivierungs- und Nachweismethoden nachzuweisen. 
- Schnellnachweis-Methoden verschiedener mikrobiologischer Techniken und Technologien fachlich korrekt selbstständig anzuwenden.
- Die wichtigsten mikrobiologischen Identifikations- und Nachweismethoden zu erläutern. 
- Kultur- und Fremdhefen anhand detaillierter Kriterien zu unterscheiden
- Schadorganismen, die in der Getränkeindustrie (Bier, Wasser, alkoholfreie Getränke)) anfallen zu differenzieren.

Sie sind zudem in der Lage Problemfelder und Gefahren in den Verfahrensabläufen einer Getränkeproduktion zu erfassen, zu analysieren und Lösungsansätze zu erarbeiten. Dazu stehen ihnen die theoretisch erlernten und praktisch erprobten Methoden, wie beispielsweise selektive Kultivierung von Mikroorganismen, Membranfiltration und Anreicherung mittels Gussplatten, von Stufenkontrollen und biologischem Qualitätsmanagement zur Verfügung.

Title: GIS-Applications for Urban Studies
Description:
CONTENT:
The course will introduce mapping as a critical research and design method, and not just a technical tool. We will investigate how spatial data reveals urban growth, highlights social and infrastructural inequalities, and visualizes the everyday experiences shaping cityscapes. 

Working with existing datasets (such as land use and land cover, administrative and cadastral data), any field-collected data, and ethnographic insights we will produce layered maps that help reveal complex spatial narratives. Producing schematic map/series of visualizations from this analysis.

OBJECTIVES:
After successful participation in the module, students are able to
1.	Utilize a GIS program (QGIS) to conduct quantitative and/or qualitative analysis (specifically data handling and spatial analysis).
2.	Understand the morphology of urban spaces and represent them graphically.
3.	Move beyond technical GIS to understand mapping as a situated and imaginative act that is integral to design justice and urban transformation.
4.	Continuously reflect on the methods and knowledge they have acquired with regard to sustainable ecological, social and economic development, incorporating context-dependent and individual perceptions of sustainability.
5.	Create presentations communicating this data analysis and visualization.

Title: Globale Zusammenhänge erkennen
Description:
CONTENT:
Im Studium bzw. der Arbeit sind wir in globale Zusammenhänge eingebunden. Diese mit Bezug auf den Arbeitskontext der TeilnehmerInnen aufzuzeigen, Hintergründe und Bedingungen zu hinterfragen und die Konsequenzen darzustellen ist Ziel dieses Kurses. 

Inhalt 
Anhand bestimmter Rohstoffe (z.B. Aluminium) und Produkte (z.B. Computer) werden beispielhaft globale Zusammenhänge aufgezeigt, die im alltäglichen Gebrauch dieser Stoffe üblicherweise ausgeblendet werden. Diese finden sich auf menschenrechtlich-individueller Ebene genauso wieder wie auf der politischen, sie sind auf einen nachhaltigen Umgang mit der Umwelt genauso bezogen wie auf die Wirtschaft. Die Ursachen dafür sind teilweise struktureller Natur, die Konsequenzen aus der teilweise ungerechten Vernetzung sind genauso global wie auch deren Ursachen. 
Anhand von den zukünftigen Arbeitsfeldern der TeilnehmerInnen werden theoretische Modelle praktisch aufgezeigt.

OBJECTIVES:
Nach der Teilnahme an der Veranstaltung sind die Studierenden in der Lage, selbstständig über die Auswirkungen ihrer privaten und beruflichen Handlungen in Bezug auf globale Verbindungen zu recherchieren und zu reflektieren. Sie können globale Güterketten von Produkten und Rohstoffen analysieren und auf ihre Auswirkungen hin hinterfragen. Am Ende des Kurses können die TeilnehmerInnen das Modell des ungleichen Tausches anwenden und verstehen die sich daraus ergebende Ungleichverteilung von Wohlstand in der Welt. Die StudentInnen können verschiedene Lösungsansätze für eine global gerechtere Welt erinnern und sie auf ihre Vor-, Nachteile und Realisierbarkeit untersuchen.

- Ambiguity resolution using undifferenced phase measurements.
- Analysis and assessment of different ODTS results.
- Application of the Bernese GNSS software package.

OBJECTIVES:
Precise GNSS satellite orbit, clock, and bias products are fundamental for precise positioning, navigation, and timing services. This module provides advanced knowledge and a practical tool to compute and evaluate these GNSS satellite products. This course combines theoretical lectures with group-based lab exercises, enabling students to deepen their understanding through hands-on experience and self-assessment. The use of the Bernese software package and the focus on advanced topics will equip students with valuable skills directly applicable to industry or research.

Upon successful competition of this module, students will be able to:
- Recall GNSS constellations, attitudes, observations and relevant data files (RINEX SP3, CLK, Bias).
- Understand the principles of ODTS.
- Comprehend various solar radiation pressure models (analytical, empirical and semi-analytical).
- Interpret ambiguity resolution (AR) using undifferenced measurements.
- Apply the Bernese software package in lab exercises.
- Analyze input and output files in the practical scenarios.
- Evaluate and discuss lab results effectively.

Title: Governance
Description:
CONTENT:
Transport planning is much more than paperwork. It is working with people, institutions, companies and any kind of stakeholders being involved into a (planning) process. 
It is also about bargaining and negotiating for better and more effective solutions to transport problems. The pathways to sustainable transport demand management and mobility at the regional level go along with new concepts of power management and government.
Governance is one of the major catchwords to describe the fundamental changes in the relations of political, economic and civil society actors in cities and regions. 
This seminar gives insights into concepts of governance and discusses empirical experiences with local and regional actors. 
It will introduce students to state of the art theories in governance and the methodological toolbox behind governance processes to involve stakeholder or engage citizens.

OBJECTIVES:
After attending the module, students are able to
- Identify, actively communicate and apply key concepts and stakeholder groups of
governance
- Be aware of the range of concepts and theoretical approaches concerning the topic of
governance
- Be able to analyze actual policy problems and case studies using a governance
perspective and to formulate relevant insights.
- Be able to apply empirical (participation) methods.

Title: Gravitationslinseneffekt
Description:
CONTENT:
Imagine a galaxy that lies behind another galaxy.  Will you see the galaxy in the back?  If you think not, think again.  The gravitational field of the galaxy in the front will bend the light from the background source, so that the background source appears to be distorted, magnified and can even have multiple images.  This phenomenon is gravitational lensing. 
Gravitational lensing is now a powerful astrophysical tool to study planetary systems, black holes, galaxies, clusters of galaxies and cosmology.  This course presents the underlying theory of gravitational lensing and the various astrophysical applications.

Course webpage with more info:
http://www.mpa-garching.mpg.de/~suyu/teaching/ph2242.html

OBJECTIVES:
After successful completion of this module, the student is able to
- understand the working principle of gravitational lensing.
- apply gravitational lensing as an astrophysical tool to study current puzzles in astronomy - such as how galaxies form and evolve, what is dark matter and what is dark energy.
- use gravitational lensing to detect matter and weigh galaxies.
- use gravitational lensing to probe the dark matter halo of the Milky Way.
