Title: Machine Learning and Optimization
Description:
CONTENT:
The course introduces the theory and practice of advanced machine learning concepts and methods (such as deep neural networks). In particular, we will discuss (statistical) learning theory, (deep) neural networks, first-order optimization methods such as stochastic gradient descent and their analysis, the interplay of learning and optimization, empirical risk minimization and regularization, and modern views of machine learning in the overparameterized regime with deep neural networks. We also discuss automatic hyperparameter optimization, active learning, and aspects beyond performance such as fairness. We will start the lecture with a very brief review of the foundations of machine learning such as simple regression and classification methods so that all students are on the same page.

OBJECTIVES:
Upon successful completion of the module students know the theoretical foundations of (advanced) machine learning algorithms and common optimization methods for machine learning, and how to develop and analyze such algorithms. Students are able to (i) apply advanced and build new machine learning methods by modifying existing ones (for example deep neural networks), (ii) develop and tune optimization algorithms for training such models, (iii) rigorously analyze their performance both with computational experiments as well as by proving generalization bounds and analyzing the convergence/computational complexity of training algorithms. Also, upon successful completion, students are familiar with concepts beyond the traditional supervised learning setup, in particular active learning and aspects such as fairness.

Title: Machine Learning and Uncertainty Quantification for Physics-Based Models
Description:
CONTENT:
Machine learning and uncertainty quantification (UQ) are ubiquitous in modern science and engineering applications. In the last two decades, UQ for complex physical processes has been developed rapidly with a focus on grid-based process models, such as finite element models, which are well-established in engineering applications. On the other hand, machine learning techniques have not traditionally been applied to physics-based models. The recent surge in data-driven models based on machine learning techniques such as deep learning is changing the computational science and engineering landscape. Novel hybrid models based on neural networks are emerging and are already enhancing traditional methods. In this seminar, we discuss theoretical and computational aspects that arise from combining PDE-based models and neural networks, e.g., neural networks for PDE approximation, molecular simulations, and fluid dynamics.

OBJECTIVES:
Upon successful completion of the module, students will:
•	become familiar with the recent advances in the area of Machine Learning and Uncertainty Quantification for Physics-Based Models
•	be able to understand the main ideas of various Machine Learning methods
•	be able to compare and evaluate different methods in terms of their area of application, advantages/disadvantages, limitations, etc.
•	gain experience in scientific presentations

Title: Machine Learning for Electronic Design Automation and Manufacturing
Description:
CONTENT:
The complexity of modern chips significantly impacts the cost and capabilities of design and manufacturing for traditional Design Automation Toolkits. This issue is exacerbated by the increased relevance of software and applications running on modern SoCs and their co-design. Current Design Automation methodologies often struggle to fully capture and optimize complicated designs or reduce them to the initial specification. However, advancements in data-driven algorithms, particularly in Machine Learning, can address these shortcomings. This course teaches how to apply Machine Learning to enhance and improve the chip design process.

This module provides an in-depth exploration of machine learning for design automation, including:
* Theory and application of machine learning algorithms
* In-depth exploration of recent machine learning methods suitable for design automation tasks
* Overview of topics, areas, and current industrial pain points in the semiconductor chain where a great availability of data exists
* Detailed coverage of data structures and state-of-the-art tools for tackling design automation
* Hands-on experiences of machine learning algorithms applied to design automation tasks

OBJECTIVES:
By the end of the module, students will 
* gain detailed insights into how machine learning can aid in the development, design, testing, and manufacturing of chips,
* understand which problems in chip design/manufacturing can be approached by data-driven methodologies and how to do so, and
* have learnt the essential requirements and best practices for introducing machine learning in a chip design/manufacturing industrial setting. 
The course will also cover different data structures and core methods that may form the basis for AI-based software methodologies. Through hands-on experience, students will implement and adapt machine learning algorithms for design automation and manufacturing tasks.

Title: Macromolecular Coatings for Biomedical Devices
Description:
CONTENT:
The characterization of soft, biological materials requires different techniques than the characterization of hard, inorganic materials. Almost every biological material shows a viscoelastic material behavior, i.e., they combine elastic and viscous characteristics. Moreover, the surfaces of biological materials are often very complex with roughness on different length scales (macro-, micro-, and nano-roughness). Such surfaces show a wide range of tribological behavior when biological, macromolecular lubricants are employed on them. 
In this lab course, the students will perform selected experiments, in which the complex material behavior of mucosal systems (i.e., mucin solutions, surface-attached mucin coatings, and mucin hydrogels) can be studied. The characterization methods used here quantify the viscoelastic, tribological, and selective properties of different biological materials. The experiments are divided into four parts:
1.	Generation of macromolecular coatings
2.	Rotational tribology
3.	Cell culture & microscopy
4.	Spectroscopy

OBJECTIVES:
After successful completion of the module the students are able to:
-	perform data recording, analysis, and evaluation
-	investigate the properties of biological materials
-	document the experiments including methods, results, and discussion fulfilling the requirements for a scientific publication
-	perform literature research

Title: Magnetism
Description:
CONTENT:
The module teaches the physical fundamentals of magnetic materials with a focus on applications relevant to engineering.
As a starting point, magnetic vector fields are introduced, followed by dia- and paramagnetic properties of materials. Building on this, magnetic order states in solids are discussed, in particular those with long-range order such as ferromagnetism, antiferromagnetism, and ferrimagnetism. The behavior of magnetic materials under the influence of magnetic fields and electric currents, as well as micromagnetic phenomena such as domains and domain walls, is analyzed. A particular focus is placed on the discussion of order phenomena that can be reproduced and understood through magnetostatic and magnetodynamic simulations. In addition, experimental methods for characterizing magnetic properties and technological applications of magnetism in sensor technology, storage technology, and signal processing are discussed. The interactions of currents with magnetic materials, often subsumed under the term “spintronics,” with phenomena like spin-transfer-torque (STT) or spin-orbit-torque (STO) are studied. A central topic is the application of magnetoresistive effects, i.e., AMR, GMR, and TMR, as they are used in modern magnetic memory devices and sensors. Furthermore, research-related topics such as spin-waves (collective excitations in a system of spins, showing resonance phenomena and nonlinear dispersion), or topologically protected magnetic structures such as Skyrmions (rather robust and ion-beam tunable swirling spin textures in ferro- and ferrimagnets) are discussed.

Title: Magnetismus
Description:
CONTENT:
This module provides an introduction to the various manifestations of magnetism. After a contextual and historical motivation, it begins with an introduction to the fundamental relations describing quantitatively the response of matter in an externally applied magnetic field. It describes the types of magnetism present in isolated atoms or ions and discusses the influence of the crystallographic environment. Afterwards, magnetism originating from the free electrons in a solid are discussed. Additionally, various coupling mechanisms of magnetic moments, collective effects, magnetic ordering and phase transitions are studied.

OBJECTIVES:
After participation in the Module the student is able to:
1) Evaluate the response of magnetic materials when applying a magnetic field,
2) Evaluate the magnetic properties of isolated ions and atoms,
3) Understand the influence of a crystallographic environment on ions and atoms,
4) Analyze the magnetic properties of free charge carriers in solids,
5) Understand the various coupling mechanisms between magnetic moments,
6) Understand magnetic ordering and phase transitions, and
7) Analyze the results of experimental data with respect to manifestations of magnetism

Title: Magnetohydrodynamische Phänomene - eine Einführung
Description:
CONTENT:
The most important phenomena in ideal fluid dynamics, magnetohydrodynamics and plasma physics will be explained in an visually accessible way using illustrative examples and some experiments. Examples are the magnetic fields in the solar system, dynamo effect in the sun, plasma confinement in controlled nuclear fusion experiments. Apart from plasma and astro physics, the basics of fluid mechanics and electrodynamics are discussed and revisited:
- solar wind
- heliosphere
- reconnection
- dynamo effect
- magnetic forces
- magnetic levitation
- plasma equilibria
- single particle picture / collective picture
- instabilities
- turbulence

Title: Magnetresonanztomographie
Description:
CONTENT:
Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is a widely used medical imaging technique with exclusive soft-tissue contrast to non-invasively depict anatomical structures and physiological processes in the human body. A multitude of novel contrast mechanisms that are being investigated in preclinical and clinical research are constantly expanding MRI's capabilities towards quantitative and functional imaging of biological processes on a cellular and molecular level.
This course will give you insights into the basic operation of an MRI scanner and state-of-the-art applications in a preclinical and clinical context.
First you will get familiar with the components needed for signal generation in a magnetic resonance imaging experiment on a preclinical MRI scanner: the main magnetic field, the radiofrequency coils and the magnetic field gradients. You will perform pre-scan adjustments (Tuning, shimming, pulse calibration) that are important for good image quality. Second, fundamental properties of the magnetic resonance signal will be studied in experiments investigating relaxation mechanisms and chemical shift. Third, choosing the MRI pulse sequence and tuning the sequence parameters is crucial for obtaining the best contrast within an image. You will get familiar with different families of pulse sequences and will learn how different pulse sequence parameters and reconstruction settings influence image contrast.
Finally, you will get familiar with advanced methods of magnetic resonance imaging in preclinical and clinical contexts, such as molecular imaging techniques that allow for the characterization of metabolic processes or quantitative imaging methods that enable image-based fat-water separation.

Title: Making a Mess with Methods
Description:
CONTENT:
Over the last 30 years, Science and Technology Studies (STS) have developed a specific take on research methods. The field not only applies (mostly qualitative) research methods to produce claims and cases about science, technology, and society, but methods for knowledge production (of different scientific disciplines) are also an important object of investigation for STS. 
This course will introduce students to a range of different qualitative research methods relevant for STS research. We will get to know different methods for data gathering (such as interviews and participant observation), different methods for analyzing data (e.g., coding procedures, iconography), different approaches that guide the research process as a whole (such as grounded theory, discourse analysis, and ethnography) and gain an understanding how neighboring disciplines (history, law) explore the interactions between science, technology and society. We will develop an understanding of the whole qualitative research process from developing a research interest, choosing adequate methods to gathering and analyzing the data. The focus of the course is both on acquiring hands-on knowledge about different methods and a reflexive understanding about their theory, practices and politics. We will do a lot of practical exercises in and out of class, but also discuss what the exact nature, societal role and the politics of methods are. E.g., are they best understood as giving insights into a (social) reality exterior to them, or are they better understood as being themselves part of making the social and technical relations we call society? The goal of the seminar is to provide students with an overview and first hand-on experience over different qualitative research methods, with a comprehensive understanding of the research process, and with the necessary conceptual tools to critically reflect upon and interrogate the practices, politics and ethics of doing qualitative research.
The course has an irregular rhythm. It will consist of two parallel groups, one taught by tba, and one by Georgia Samaras. It will be taught in seminar room 270 and 370.

OBJECTIVES:
Upon successful completion of this module students will know different methods of STS. The students are able to choose between them to gather and analyze data. They understand methodological foundations of research in the humanities and social science, they understand the character of data and the links between methods and conceptual frameworks. The students can apply different methodological approaches and have fundamental skills for developing research designs for STS projects.

Title: Making Comics
Description:
CONTENT:
In diesem Workshop zur visuellen Narration werden wir uns gemeinsam dem umfangreichen Medium Comic widmen, um ein tieferes Verständnis für diese Erzählmethode zu erhalten und selbst bildsprachliche Geschichten erstellen zu können.
Beginnen werden wir unsere Webinare mit ein paar einfachen, praktischen Übungen zur Lockerung der Handgelenke und Gedanken. Daraufhin widmen wir uns jedes Mal einem theoretischen Block, in welchem sowohl gestalterische Grundlagen, verschiedene Erzähltheorien als auch beispielhafte KünstlerInnen und Werke besprochen werden. Im Weiteren wird an jedem Termin eine Besprechung der Hausaufgaben stattfinden, die jeweils darin bestehen, ein an die vorangegangene Stunde angelehntes Thema in ein bis maximal vier Paneln festzuhalten. Dabei ist freigestellt, ob es sich beispielsweise um eine bloße inhaltliche Zusammenfassung oder eine anknüpfende Erzählung handelt, auch eher assoziative Fortführungen sind dabei legitim.
Zum Abschluss ist eine gemeinsame Publikation am Semesterende geplant.

OBJECTIVES:
Nach der Teilnahme am Modul CLA21212 sind die Studierenden in der Lage:
- visuelle Alphabete und bildsprachliche Grammatik zu gebrauchen
- die Grundlagen der Visual Literacy sowohl auf Einzel- wie auch Mehrbildfolgen anzuwenden
- narrative Muster und Erzählstrukturen zu erkennen und zu vergleichen
- visuellen Lesefluss zu prüfen und Storyboards zu erstellen
Nach Teilnahme am Modul CLA31212 sind die Studierenden darüber hinaus in der Lage:
- Figuren und Themen für Bilderzählungen zu entwerfen
- Konzepte für den Transfer von Themen an der Schnittstelle von Wissenschaft, Technik und Gesellschaft verständlich zu präsentieren

Title: Management - Geschichte, aktuelle Herausforderungen, Perspektiven
Description:
CONTENT:
Schwerpunktthema dieses Semester: Intellekt, Intellektualität, Persönlichkeit - Wie gebildet müssen Manager sein?

„Es gibt schlechterdings gewisse Kenntnisse, die allgemein sein müssen, und noch mehr eine gewisse Bildung der Gesinnungen und des Charakters, die keinem fehlen darf. Jeder ist offenbar nur dann ein guter Handwerker, Kaufmann und Geschäftsmann, wenn er ohne Hinsicht auf seinen besonderen Beruf ein guter anständiger, aufgeklärter Mensch und Bürger ist“. (Wilhelm von Humboldt)

„ich wüsste nicht, wessen Geist ausgebreiteter wäre, ausgebreiteter sein müsste, als der eines echten Kaufmanns“. (Johann Wolfgang von Goethe)

Schon Helmuth Plessner und auch Peter Drucker warnten vor mehreren Jahrzehnten, dass das Bildungswesen der modernen Gesellschaft die Gefahr in sich birgt, gelehrte Barbaren zu produzieren („Fachmenschen ohne Geist und Genußmenschen ohne Herz“. Max Weber 1905). Für den österreichischen Philosophen Konrad Paul Liessmann ist für unsere „Wissensgesellschaft“ der „flexible Mensch“. der vorherrschende Sozialcharakter . Hierzu schreibt er in seinem Buch -Theorie der Unbildung-: „Der flexible Mensch, der, lebenslang lernbereit, seine kognitiven Fähigkeiten den sich rasch wandelnden Märkten zur Disposition stellt, ist nicht einmal mehr eine Karikatur des humanistisch Gebildeten, wie ihn Wilhelm von Humboldt in seiner knappen – Theorie der Bildung des Menschen – skizziert hatte, sondern dessen krasses Gegenteil. Bei allem, was Menschen heute wissen müssen und wissen können – und das ist nicht wenig! –, Fehlt diesem Wissen jede synthetisierende Kraft. Es bleibt, was es sein soll: Stückwerk – rasch herstellbar, schnell anzueignen und leicht wieder zu vergessen“.Diese Kritik am heutigen Bildungsniveau schließt natürlich Defizite der Konzepte von Managementbildung und Managemententwicklung mit ein. 
Die Fähigkeit des Bürgers frei und verantwortlich in der Gesellschaft zu agieren, ist das Leitbild des Humboldtschen Bildungsideal. Ausgehend von diesem Verständnis von Bildung steht im Mittelpunkt des Seminars die Frage, inwieweit die gegenwärtige Managementbildung das Fundament für den Manager, speziell für den Wirtschaftsmanager liefert, um die Herausforderungen seiner gesellschaftlichen Verantwortung zu bestehen und das in Zeiten ,in denen Krisen zumNormalfall gehören. 
Die hier vertretene These lautet in Abwandlung eines Adorno Wortes: – gebildete Manager allein schaffen noch keine funktionierende Gesellschaft, doch ohne gebildete Manager ist keine funktionierende Gesellschaft möglich! –

Erörtert werden im wesentlichen folgende Fragen:
– Weche Defizite weist die gegenwärtige Managementbildung auf?
– In welchen Schwerpunkten bedarf die Managementbildung Erneuerung, Ergänzung und Weiterentwicklung?
– Welche Konzepte sind hierzu erforderlich?

Title: Management of Renewable Resources
Description:
CONTENT:
Lectures are divided into three sub-areas. These topics differ somewhat in their content, but they all deal with various facets of renewable resource economics.
1. Production and logistics
Introduction to selected management planning problems in production and logistics such as inventory management, lot sizing, project management and transport planning as well as the economic evaluation
2. Renewable resources economics
Resources of agriculture and forestry; exploitation costs of renewable resources, potential for re-use as energy and material (e.g. biodiesel, bioethanol, biogas, solid fuels; lubricants); economic feasibility of selected conversion routes; derivation of CO2 reduction costs specific to certain procedures; perspectives
3. Markets for renewable resources 
Description of various markets for renewable resources. These are divided into material (biolubricants, raw materials, chemical compounds and fine chemicals) and energy use (heat, electricity and transport)

OBJECTIVES:
After their participation, students can explain the basic methods of resource economics and land use in terms of resource protection in individual case examples. Students also understand business and market connections in the production and processing of renewable resources and they can discuss current deveopments. In addition, students are able to describe and compare the various marketing strategies and factors in the field of renewable resources.

Title: Management Science Lecture - Campus Straubing
Description:
CONTENT:
Management Science is about modeling, solving and analyzing business adminstrations and management problems using mathematial concepts. Management Science is used across different industries, departments and organizations. The lecture will treat the Management Science approach to decision making in general and the following topics in particular: Linear Programming, Mixed-Integer Programming, Graph Theory, Netwerk Flow, Dynamic Programming and Decision Theory.

OBJECTIVES:
After successfull completion of the module students are capable of modelling mathematical optimization models for business problems, of solving  small problems manually, of interpreting derived solutions and translating them into management actions. Furthermore, the knowledge is the foundation for the the elective module "Modeling, Optimization and Simulation" where students will learn how to use commerical software in order to come up with solutions for large real-world optimization problems.

Title: Management weltweiter Geschäftsaktivitäten in der Praxis
Description:
CONTENT:
Elements characteristic of the management process of global activities will be presented: How to derive a consistent strategy for many, at times hundred and more business units, located in a multitude of countries? How to align market requirements in varying countries with the use of company-wide synergies? How to detect threatening developments to the enterprise early, across the globe? How to coordinate measures in a way that despite different, often contrary objectives of individual agents the overarching goal of increasing the value of an enterprise will be achieved? And much more.

In the second part, substantial tools and concepts which early on indicate the need for an enterprise to take action (e.g. benchmarking, portfolio-techniques, break-even-analysis, source of change) will be discussed. Central measures to increase the value of a company will be presented (e.g. complexity management, pricing, redesign of global value-chains, mergers & acquisitions). It will be discussed, how to secure the implementation of value-increasing measures, how to detect the need for action within a changing business environment or during implementation interferences, and how to initiate countermeasures.

The perspective of the lecture is that of a general manager. The lecture is focused on the holistic optimization of the enterprise, the development of competitive advantages, and the sustainable increase of the enterprise value. Accordingly, it is centered around tools, which have proven to be effective in practice. Across all topics, the focus is rather on the integration into the overall process and its use in practice, than on ‘technical' details of these tools.

OBJECTIVES:
The course aims at giving students an overview on how to steer global activities of an enterprise in practice. Furthermore, an understanding of the application of essential concepts and tools of an executive in the cooperate world shall be acquired.

Title: Managing Challenges in the BioTech Industry
Description:
CONTENT:
The chair for Management Accounting offers different courses for "Advanced Topics in Finance & Accounting" which are mainly offered in cooperation with companies or guest lecturers with a long standing experience in management positions. The courses cover problems and questions which are highly relevant in practice. This course will broadly cover challenges for successful management, particularly with regard to R&D budgets, effective boards, and corporate social responsibility. In addition, it will highlight the special features of automation and innovation in a BioTech company.

OBJECTIVES:
At the end of the module, students will have thorough knowledge of the topics covered by the chosen seminar. Students understand daily challenges of firms, the relevance as well as causes of problems faced by firms in practice.They are able to apply basic concepts and theories in practice to solve these problems and to compare and evaluatedifferent approaches for solving these problems. These concepts and theories consider processes and anaylses ofthe firm as well as increases in firm value.

Title: Market Strategy
Description:
CONTENT:
It explores how strategy is done by companies with special focus on marketing, growth, market entry and M&A. Following specific case studies (e.g. how an American fast food restaurant chain plans to grow in the German market) we will get a deep understanding what data to analyse, how to evaluate ideas and how to steer implementation. Two deep dives wiill be into sustainability as new requirement of any strategy and into M&A (when does it make sense, how to derive a fair value, post merger management)

OBJECTIVES:
By the end of this course, students will be familiar with the key frameworks of market strategy (Porter, Blue Ocean, where to grow/how to grow, sustainability etc.) and be able to apply them, as we will do many real life case studies. Specific focus will lie in the marketing aspects of strategy, such as customer research, market segmentation etc.

Title: Marketing
Description:
CONTENT:
The module introduces the goals, tasks, and instruments of the marketing mix and introduces to fundamentals of marketing theory and practice. The module outlines why marketing plays a central role for every company and its success. The module also addresses how marketing tasks and instruments are continuously changing in the context of the digital transformation and how to consider ethical aspects when deciding on marketing activities. The module is structured as follows:
• Subject and basic concepts of marketing
• Branding
• Product policy and product innovation
• Pricing policy
• Communication policy and social media marketing
• Distribution policy

OBJECTIVES:
After successfully completing the module, participants have gained the following competences:
• Ability to summarize the core elements of the marketing management process
• Ability to apply important theories, models, and strategies for building brand equity
• Ability to explain and apply goals and instruments of product policy and new product development
• Ability to explain and apply characteristics and elements of pricing policy, communication policy, and social media marketing
• Ability to design distribution systems
• Ability to apply data science and artificial intelligence to analyze consumer behavior, optimize marketing strate-gies, and enhance customer engagement
• Ability to discuss and argue for alternative ways of organizing, developing, and implementing practical marketing projects and to consider environmental and ethical effects
• Ability to reflect on and discuss central aspects in relation to the marketing research literature

Title: Marketing Mobility with Generative AI
Description:
CONTENT:
In this hands-on seminar (Digital Marketing × Mobility Policy), student teams tackle a real-world GenAI marketing challenge from an industry partner and design a multi-modal GenAI-enabled marketing campaign they pitch at the end. This semester, Flughafen München will provide the marketing challenge.

First, we cover the essentials of marketing, mobility policy, and GenAI tools and limits. After the content day, teams enter a self-study/project work phase in which they develop their campaign independently and receive feedback from us in a coached feedback session. Seminar days are held at the Lab Campus at Munich Airport and include an airport tour with insights into the world of aviation. Further, additional lectures on the aviation industry and marketing in the aviation sector are provided at the Lab Campus.

- Foundations: key marketing concepts; core mobility-policy ideas (demand, externalities, user vs. system optimum).
- GenAI toolkit: trends & state-of-the-art tools across modalities (text, image, video, audio, code).
- Responsible AI: biases, legal/ethical issues, energy & sustainability considerations.
- Project work: independent team project work between blocks with a structured feedback session; build partner-ready marketing concept, assets, and KPI plan.
- Field visit & context immersion: airport/Lab Campus tour and expert insights.

OBJECTIVES:
By the end, students can plan and produce a GenAI-enabled marketing concept for a mobility provider, grounded in policy realities and measurable outcomes.

- Apply core mobility-policy concepts (derived demand, externalities, user vs. system optimum) to marketing decisions.
- Prompt and evaluate state-of-the-art generative models across modalities; prototype creative assets.
- Define KPIs, test variations and reason about impact vs. constraints.
- Identify AI risks (bias, IP/safety, energy) and propose mitigations.
- Pitch a coherent campaign to executives with clear narrative and ROI logic.

Title: Marketing Research
Description:
CONTENT:
The course connects experimental work with data analysis. As such, it is fundamental for doing further marketing lectures as well as for doing a master thesis. In the first block, students learn about experimental design in the consumer research and marketing context (including collecting data using eyetracking and virtual reality). The introductory lectures cover the design of variables and measures, factors influencing experimental designs, the formulation of research hypotheses, how to use the literature for hypotheses formulation as well as moderation and mediation as concepts. In the second block, students learn about how to analyze data collected from experiments using a range of multivariate statistical techniques that allow for the testing of group differences, the classification of observations, the modeling of categorical outcomes, the examination of associations between variables, and the evaluation of complex decision-making processes. Emphasis is placed on understanding the logic behind each method, selecting appropriate techniques based on research questions, and interpreting results in a theoretically grounded and managerially relevant way.

OBJECTIVES:
Key learning goals are:
•Learn about basic principles of experimental design for consumer research and marketing phenomena.
•Learn about important models and methodologies that can be applied to analyze marketing research data.
•Learn about how to apply experimental and analytical methods to real-world marketing problems.
•Be able to explain and design experiments.
•Be able to evaluate the impact that design decisions have on which data analysis can be applied.
•Be able to use marketing research methods, which includes choosing an appropriate method, using statistics programs to do calculations and explain the results.
•Be able to explain limitations of experiments and data analysis.
•Be able to think critically about research questions and methodological choices in marketing research.
•Be able to communicate research findings clearly (experiments as well as data analysis results) to expert audiences and defend the own work.

Title: Maschinelles Lernen für die Produktentwicklung
Description:
CONTENT:
Machine learning is intensely used in computer science, e.g., for image classification, autonomous driving, and generating new text. The impact of machine learning with its advantages and applications is well known in those domains. For engineers, though, it is often difficult to grasp how machine learning methods can be exploited for developing mechanical systems and where their limitations are. This lecture will demonstrate different machine learning methods that can be used for modeling, characterizing, optimizing, and monitoring mechanical systems, and identify their limitations. Various real case scenarios are highlighted, and simplified examples will be studied in computer exercises.

OBJECTIVES:
The module’s goal is to provide a general understanding of different machine learning methods and their implementation for product development. Students will also study basic probability theory and apply it to different product development tasks. 
After participating in the module, students are able to: 
•  understand the fundamentals of machine learning,
•  apply these fundamentals in the context of product development in order to, for example,
  o  quickly evaluate different designs,
  o  leverage large language models (e.g., chatbots) for own data and projects,
  o  analyze uncertainties associated with a design, and
  o  use probabilistic models for predictive maintenance and accelerating experiments,
•  and clearly present and discuss their results.

Title: Maschinelles Lernen im Energiemanagement
Description:
CONTENT:
The energy transition leads to new challenges in controlling energy systems. In particular, the deployment of distributed energy generation from renewables (e.g., wind and solar) and sector-coupling flexible loads (e.g., heat pumps and electric vehicles) requires new energy management systems that must leverage modern computer science techniques to be effective. At the core of these new energy management systems (EMS) are data-driven forecasting, and control methods. These methods enable next generation EMS to automatically adapt energy systems to their dynamic environment based on measured data and make optimal decisions to achieve higher energy efficiency and more efficient use of variable renewable power.

In this course, we provide knowledge and examples on where and how data-driven techniques can be used in next generation energy management systems. The lecture is divided into two parts: the first part focuses on prediction and forecasting techniques. Each is explained formally and then applied to selected energy management problems. The second part focuses on data-driven control. Again, the fundamental concepts are first introduced and then applied to practical problems. The lecture sessions are accompanied by exercises that further deepen the student’s knowledge on the introduced techniques. The exercises focus rather on methodological understanding than on coding skills.

Methods being taught in this course include machine learning techniques for supervised prediction, e.g., linear and non-linear regression, decision trees, ensemble methods, and neural networks. Due to their importance in energy management, one focus of the course is on applications of ML to system estimation and time series forecasting. A second focus of the course is on using ML-based techniques in the optimization and control of energy systems. Starting from control basics, this part introduces data-driven control techniques, including model predictive control and deep reinforcement learning. Use cases introduced in the course include load and renewables forecasting as well as data-driven estimation of selected energy system dynamics, e.g., buildings.

OBJECTIVES:
• Understand selected machine learning techniques both conceptually and formally,
• Understand how machine learning techniques can be applied in energy management,
• Learn to apply and evaluate machine learning algorithms in selected energy management use cases,
• Understand selected methods for data-driven control both conceptually and formally,
• Learn to apply and evaluate data-driven control in selected energy management use cases,
• Continuously reflect on the methods and knowledge learned regarding sustainable ecological, social, and economic development,
• Develop inter- and transdisciplinary approaches to link the three elements (environmental, social, and economic development).
Skills: ['Machine Learning and AI', 'Energy management', 'Renewable energy systems', 'Control systems']

Title: Maschinelles Lernen in Lebensmittel- und Biotechnologie

In particular, students are familiar with the mathematical background of important machine learning techniques, which helps them to decide which technique is best suited to which problem. Learning one of today's most powerful yet simple programming languages, Python, together with knowledge of a ground-breaking technology such as machine learning will make students more attractive to future employers and enhance their academic potential.

Title: MA-Soziologische Theorie
Description:
CONTENT:
Die Biomedizin ist ein Zweig der medizinischen Wissenschaften, der biologische und physiologische Prinzipien nutzt, um verschiedene Zustände von Gesundheit und Krankheit zu erklären. Sie kann im weitesten Sinne als der Bereich definiert werden, in dem sich Biologie und Medizin überschneiden. Und doch ist die Biomedizin weit mehr als das. Sie ist ein Rahmen, ein bestimmter Denkstil und ein wissenschaftliches Paradigma, das eine Reihe von disziplinierenden Instrumenten hervorbringt. Die Biomedizin kann als eine mächtige Organisation beschrieben werden, die Individuen und Populationen reguliert. So kann sie beispielsweise als eine globale Institution agieren, die in die westliche Kultur und ihre Machtdynamik eingebettet ist. Gleichzeitig können biomedizinische Errungenschaften und Innovationen, wie etwa genetische Testungen, eine ermächtigende Wirkung auf den Einzelnen und die Gesellschaft haben. 
Die Biomedizin, wie wir sie heute kennen, ist weit davon entfernt, ein geschlossenes System zu sein, das nur innerhalb des medizinischen Sektors wirkt. Im Gegenteil, wie die Soziologie und benachbarte Disziplinen herausgearbeitet haben, entfalten sich biomedizinische Praktiken in sozialen, kulturellen und historischen Kontexten: Soziale Normen und Werte prägen die Biomedizin in ihrer (Forschungs-)Praxis und als Institution. Gleichzeitig beeinflusst die Biomedizin die Art und Weise, wie wir Leben, Gesundheit und Krankheit wahrnehmen und wie wir unseren Körper erleben und mit ihm umgehen: Individuen und Kollektive wenden biomedizinisches Wissen und Praktiken an, bestreiten oder verhandeln sie. Um diese Dynamiken analytisch zu fassen, hat der französische Philosoph Michel Foucault die Begriffe der „Biopolitik“ und der „Biomacht“ vorgeschlagen, welche es erlauben, produktive Machtformen, die auf die Erzeugung, Sicherung, Verwaltung und Optimierung des menschlichen Lebens, seiner Körper, Prozesse und Formen kritisch zu durchleuchten.
Im Laufe des Seminars werden wir uns ein Repertoire an kritischem Bewusstsein und Denken aneignen, das sowohl die Möglichkeiten als auch Herausforderungen und Vorbehalte des biomedizinischen Wissens und der Technologien berücksichtigt. Zu den Fragen, die wir stellen werden, gehören: Wie hat sich die Biomedizin historisch entwickelt, und inwieweit ist diese Entwicklung mit (Bio-)Politik verbunden? Wie prägt und verändert biomedizinisches Wissen soziale Identitäten, soziale Beziehungen und Kategorien wie Geschlecht oder Verantwortung? Wie wird biomedizinisches Wissen produziert, und was sind seine Vorstellungen und Beziehungen zu politischem Handeln und sozialer Gerechtigkeit? Um diese Fragen zu beantworten, werden wir verschiedene empirische Fallstudien in Form von Referaten diskutieren.
Des Weiteren führt dieses Seminar in die Diskursanalyse ein, welche eine zentrale Analysemethode der Soziologie darstellt und in den Seminararbeiten auf ein Falleispiel der Biomedizin angewendet werden soll. Nach Abschluss des Seminars können die Teilnehmenden zentrale Konzepte der Gesundheitssoziologie (Biopolitik, Biomacht, Medikalisierung) verstehen und auf einen selbstgewählten Fall anwenden.

Title: MA-Spezielle Soziologie
Description:
CONTENT:
Krisendiagnosen haben in der Gegenwart Konjunktur, ob nun von Klimakrise oder Covid-19 die Rede ist. Obwohl der Krisenbegriff sowohl im akademischen als auch im medialen und politischen Diskurs omnipräsent ist, bleibt seine konkrete Bedeutung häufig diffus. Vor diesem Hintergrund widmet sich das Seminar folgenden Fragen: Was ist das Besondere an der oder den historischen oder gegenwärtigen Krise(n)? Was rechtfertigt überhaupt die nicht nur politisch interessierte, sondern soziologisch fundierte Rede von Krisen? Wie lassen sich Krisen und potentielle Lösungsmöglichkeiten soziologisch beschreiben und erklären? Um diese Fragen zu adressieren, verfolgt das Seminar drei Ziele: 
•	Der erste Teil dient der Einführung in die Thematik und widmet sich der historischen, begriffs- und theoriegeschichtlichen Annäherung sowie der systematischen Begriffsklärung. 
•	Im zweiten  Teil geht es um die Kartierung von gesellschaftlichen Krisen mit Hilfe von Konzepten (aus der Politischen Soziologie, Risiko-, Organisations- und Umweltsoziologie). Eingehender betrachtet werden wirtschaftliche „Krisen“, großtechnische und ökologische Risiken (wie Tschernobyl und Fukushima). Das Ziel besteht darin, systematisch zu klären, welche soziologischen Konzepte zur Verfügung stehen, um die entsprechenden 'Krisen' wissenschaftlich zu erfassen und verstehen. 
•	Der dritte Teil des Seminars widmet sich in zeitdiagnostischer Absicht konkreten Krisendiagnosen der Gegenwart, wobei der Schwerpunkt  Umwelt-/Klimakrise und der Corona-Pandemie liegt. Ein besonderes Augenmerk wird auf die aktuelle Situation und die pandemiebedingten Krisenentwicklungen gelegt. Je nachdem, wie sich die politische Großwetterlage verändert, können tagesaktuelle Themen (4. Welle …) in das Seminar einbezogen werden. 
Sog. Krisen fordern immer wieder zu Reflexionen über das Verhältnis von Wissenschaft und Politik heraus. Krisendiagnosen werden häufig als Anlass und Grundlage herangezogen, um eine Standortbestimmung der Soziologie als wissenschaftlicher Disziplin anzuregen. Abschließend geht es auch um die Frage, welche Rollen Soziolog:innen in aktuellen Diskussionen spielen können und sollen.

OBJECTIVES:
Die Studierenden verfügen über vertiefte Kenntnisse im Hinblick auf Konzepte und Begriffe einer Speziellen Soziologie und können mit deren Hilfe gesellschaftliche Krisenphänomene (wie die Pandemie) bearbeiten und diese vermitteln. Die Seminarthemen wechseln und erstrecken sich von Theorie/ Begriffsgeschichte auf Politische Soziologie, Risiko- und Technik-Soziologie und sowie auf Umwelt- und Nachhaltigkeitssoziologie. 
Am Ende des Moduls haben die Studierenden
- Grundkenntnisse in sozialwissenschaftlicher Krisenforschung,
- Kompetenzen, die gesellschaftlichen Ursachen, Merkmale und
Folgen von Krisen zu erfassen
- Fähigkeiten, ausgewählte Konzepte auf
konkrete Probleme anzuwenden (Extremereignisse, Kritische
Infrastruktur, Pandemie, Digitalisierung) und ihre Kenntnisse kritisch reflektieren sowie im Unterricht zu vermitteln.

Title: Mathematical methods for uncertainty quantification in hydrology MOOC
Description:
CONTENT:
The lecture with integrated exercises is offered as MOOC. 
A series of lectures (recorded and always available on Moodle) will introduce uncertainty quantification methods and their application in hydrology. This part will cover about 30 h of on line lecture material including practical work (e.g., how to develop phython scripts step by step and providing them on line). Topics covered are:

- Introduction about uncertainties in hydrology
- Rating curves and their uncertainties
- Uncertainties in surface water - groundwater interaction
- Uncertanties in lumped hydrological models
- Sensitivity analysis of hydrological models
- Introduction about uncertainty quantification methods
- Basics of python programming
- Markov Chain Monte Carlo
- Bayesian inversion for linear and non linear models
- Active subspace method
- Presenting uncertainties to an interdisciplinary audience
- Presenting the results on an interdisciplinary project to an interdisciplinary audience

OBJECTIVES:
The students will: LO1. understand the relevance of uncertainty quantification for practical hydrological problems,LO2. be able to apply uncertainty quantification methods to hydrological problems, LO3. be able to critically analyze the results of the applied methods, LO4. be able to effectively work in an interdisciplinary team, LO5. be able to effectively present and communicate the results to an interdisciplinary audience.

Title: Mathematical Modeling of Materials
Description:
CONTENT:
Linear finite element analysis: two- and three-dimensional formulations in elasticity. Mixed FEMs and volume locking. A posteriori error estimators (ZZ estimator, residual-based, goal-oriented). Selection of nonlinear finite element analysis: geometric, material nonlinearities, contact problems. XFEM: partition of unity, enrichment functions, interface description by level-set functions. Energy functionals over Lebesgue and Sobolev spaces. Weak and strong topologies. Necessary and sufficient conditions for lower semicontinuity of integral functionals under several assumption on the energy densities. Gamma-convergence. Atomistic to continuum limits for phase transition and fracture problems.

OBJECTIVES:
At the end of the module students can carry out linear and nonlinear finite element analyses for PDE-based mathematical models in continuum mechanics. This consists of the problem formulation (weak form), discretization by finite elements, and the solution of the associated equations. Students are also introduced to advanced finite element techniques, e.g. mixed FEMs, a posteriori error control, and extended FEMs, and can apply these techniques using suitable advanced software packages, e.g. FEniCS. In a second part of the course the students will learn about variational formulation of model problems in continuum mechanics, phase transitions and fracture mechanics in the antiplanar case. In particular they will familiarize with the direct methods of the calculus of variation and with the notion of Gamma-convergence.

Title: Mathematical Models in Biology 1
Description:
CONTENT:
Introduction in theory and application of dynamical systems and stochastic processes: linear compartmental models, Markov-chains, Galton-Watson processes, birth-death-processes, population models, spatial models and age structured models. 
The emphasis of the module is to teach the understanding of the importance for different model approaches for one single biological system.

OBJECTIVES:
After successful completion of the module, the student is able to evaluate the connection of different results related to different model approaches (stochastic/deterministic, discrete/continuous) and to choose the appropriate level for the description of the system under observation. Furthermore they are able to formulate mathematical models for biological systems on the basis of analytic, stochastic or discrete mathematical structures.

Title: Mathematische Kontinuumsmechanik
Description:
CONTENT:
The lecture contains the conservation laws of continuum mechanics. These include the equations for mass, momentum, and energy. Their significance is demonstrated using concrete examples from physics.


General contents:
————————
- Conservation laws
- Distributions
- Conservation of mass and momentum
- Coordinate transformation
- Fundamentals of elasticity
- Observer transformations
- Objectivity of balance laws
- Objectivity of constitutive equations
- Energy equation
- Entropy principle
- Free energy inequality

For a better understanding, distributions are introduced. They make it possible to represent point mechanics as a subfield of continuum mechanics and to derive from the conservation laws the Newton's axioms for a mass point. Furthermore, distributions are essential when dealing with different media that meet at an interface.
Note: Knowledge of distributions is not necessary to successfully complete the course.

A fundamental requirement of the theory is objectivity, i.e. observer independence. For this purpose, a theorem on invariance under coordinate transformations is proven. This can be applied to general transformations, to polar and cylindrical coordinates, to reference coordinates, and to classical observer transformations.

After this general part, we will then focus on specific models (ca. 6 weeks before the end of the semester).

Selection of special models:
-------------------------------------
- Fluid equations (included in the curriculum as standard)
- Navier-Stokes equations
- Euler equations
- Elasticity theory
- Chemical reactions
- Self-gravity
- Liquid crystals

You can make a suggestion to a special model; an impression of this you can get in the lecture notes:
https://www.moodle.tum.de/pluginfile.php/5842019/mod_resource/content/1/alt-continuum%2027-5.pdf

There is a separate lecture notes for students interested in distributions:
https://www.moodle.tum.de/pluginfile.php/5842021/mod_resource/content/1/alt-distributions.pdf

In the following summer semester, a continuation on relativity will be offered using the theorem of invariance under coordinate transformations.

OBJECTIVES:
-----------
After successful completion of the module students are able to understand and apply
mathematical methods, which describe physical laws.

After the lecture, there is the possibility to prepare a Master's thesis.
This thesis consists of a topic that is taken from the follow-up lecture.
This lecture will take place in the following semester.
-----------

+ Review of multimodal registration, visualization and user interfaces.
+ Real-examples using head mounted display (HMDs), Camera augmented mobile C-arm (CamC) and, intraoperative gamma probes coupled with AR capabilities, AR magic mirror for anatomy education. 
+ Includes visits to the Navigated Augmented Reality Visualization Systems Laboratory, Chirurgische Klinik und Poliklinik Innenstadt; and IFL: Interdisziplinäres Forschungslabor, Klinikum rechts der Isar.

Exercises (every two weeks):
+ Using Unity3D, C#, Python or C++
+ Implementation of lecture course topics with students in small groups.

OBJECTIVES:
In-situ visualization in medical augmented reality (AR) enables the registered view of virtual data such as a 3D CT scan, with a video view of the real anatomy of a patient. Data can be aligned with the required accuracy such that surgeons do not have to analyze data on an external monitor in the operating room. Instead, surgeons get a direct view onto and into the patient. Mental registration of medical imagery with the operation site is not necessary anymore. Augmenting medical images and virtual surgical instruments within the body provides the most intuitive way to understand the patient’s anatomy within the region of interest. This allows for the development of completely new generations of surgical navigation systems. The objectives of this lecture are to have students learn the theoretical basics and practical aspects of augmented reality solutions related to the medical field. The content of the lectures are outlined below.
Skills: ['Augmented Reality (AR)', 'Virtual Reality (VR)', 'Medical imaging', '3D modeling', 'Computer graphics', 'User interface design']

Title: Medical Instrumentation and Computer Aided Surgery
Description:
CONTENT:
The interdisciplinary course "Medical Instrumentation and Computer Aided Surgery" is organized by the Research Group MITI at the TUM University Hospital Rechts der Isar.

The aim of the course is to demonstrate the technical fundamentals of medical instruments and systems in clinical use and research, as well as the relations between different clinical fields and current research directions. The course is taught by a team of distinguished lecturers with technical and medical expertise, as well as industrial partners. 

The course covers the following topics:
	- Medical Devices for Surgical Techniques
	- Clinical and Surgical Robotics
	- Navigated Surgery
	- Medical Data Science
	- Training, Simulation and Additive Manufacturing in Surgery

In addition, students will learn background information about clinical developments, cutting-edge research projects and might even meet their future employer. For industrial partners, the presentation of actual developments could be the basis of future cooperative research projects together with students and clinical partners.

OBJECTIVES:
Technical fundamentals of medical instruments and systems in clinical use and research.
Skills: ['Medical instrumentation', 'Computer Aided Surgery', 'Medical devices', 'Surgical robotics', 'Biomedical engineering']

Title: Medical Technology 1 - an organ system based approach
Description:
CONTENT:
During the semester, we offer visits to Munich clinics in the disciplines cardiac, visceral and plastic surgery. The students will be able to follow surgical, minimally invasive or robot-assisted interventions in the operating rooms (ORs), where they will be guided by the expert team.  The OR team will also provide the rules of conduct in the OR as well as explanation of the of the pathology and the therapy, so that the students will benefit from the experience in the most comprehensive way, complementing the theoretical knowledge gained in the lecture.
Each lecture comprises a Q&A session and integrates exercises for knowledge transfer where the lecturer will intentionally go beyond the content of the lecture in order to stimulate the active participation of the students in a larger context as well as the historical developments of medical technology.

Title: Medientechnik
Description:
CONTENT:
Fundamentals of multimedia information processing, information retrieval, fast text - and image retrieval, image creation, camera models and camera coordinates, relationship of world and pixel coordinates, camera calibration, Stereo camera systems, image synthesis, Rasterization of lines, geometric scene composition and modelling, polygon meshes, parametric curves and surfaces, B-splines, rendering of polygon meshes, rendering of parametric surfaces, local lighting models, rendering pipeline, image-based scene modelling, analog video, color television signals, color television norms, digital video.

OBJECTIVES:
After participation, the student will be able to understand the fundamentals of digital media (real and synthetic images, videos) and the processing chain of selected media types from recording over retrieval to displaying. Moreover, the student will learn the mixture of real and synthetic scenes in a studio scenario.
Skills: ['Multimedia processing', 'Image processing', 'Computer vision', '3D modeling', 'Camera calibration', 'Geometric modeling']

Title: Medienwelt und Mediennutzung reflektieren
Description:
CONTENT:
Wie sich unsere Medienwelt entwickelt, ist eine Frage, die gesellschaftlich für uns alle eine tragende Rolle spielt. Die Studierenden erkunden, wie und wie viel ihrer Welt sie durch Medien wahrnehmen. Sie beschäftigen sich mit Voraussetzungen und Arbeitsweisen unterschiedlicher Medien. Sie reflektieren, wie und warum sie verschiedene Medien nutzen. Ihre eigenen Erfahrungen und ihr Wissen sind in dem Projektseminar die Basis, um eine zukünftige Medienwelt zu entwerfen – welche Wünsche richten sich an Medien, welche Funktionen sollen sie in Zukunft idealerweise erfüllen, welchen Einschränkungen sollen sie ggf. unterliegen? Welche Arten der Nutzung sind möglich, welche sind wünschenswert? Die Zukunftsentwürfe zur Medienwelt, welche die Studierenden zu diesen Fragen entwickeln, präsentieren und diskutieren sie zum Abschluss mit professionellen Kommunikatoren.

OBJECTIVES:
Sie reflektieren, welche Rolle Medien in verschiedenen Kontexten spielen und zugleich ihre eigene Mediennutzung. Indem Sie selbst einen Zukunftsentwurf zur Medienwelt gestalten, bringen Sie Ihre Ideen und Ihre Lösungsansätze ein.

Title: Medizin I
Description:
CONTENT:
Ziel der Module Medizin I und II ist eine Einführung in die
Medizin mit dem Erwerb eines allgemeinen medizinischen
Grundverständnisses, verbunden mit dem Verständnis der
Informationsverarbeitung in der Medizin.

übersetzen zu können. Thema hier ist:

- Aufbau und Struktur der medizinischen Fachsprache

OBJECTIVES:
Die Studierenden

- besitzen Grundkenntnisse über den Aufbau der Zelle und
  die wichtigsten physiologischen Vorgänge
- kennen die Topographie der Organsysteme

- sind in der Lage, die wichtigsten physiologischen Abläufe

Title: MedTech Culture - Modular Trainings
Description:
CONTENT:
The course will bring participants in touch with experts in Med Tech industrial development. The contents will be presented in a modular setup. While some of the modules will be obligatory, students can select others from a panel of offered modules according to their interests and prior knowledge. 
The moduls will train students in project manangement, patent issues, contract and legal issues, ethical issues, business economics, reimbursement in the health sector, health politics, industrial designing, quality issues, product admission and regulatory issues, health politics, entrepreneurship.
These topics will be illustrated with examples from MedTec. Specific Med Tech engineering issues will also be treated in the context of recent industrial development projects such as imaging, microelectronic body implants, digital designs, in-vivo and in-vitro sensing technologies, processing and handling of personal, health-related data.  
A particular emphasis will be on the training of soft skills such as presentation techniques, virtual working style, teamwork organisation.

Title: Memory Technology for Data Storage
Description:
CONTENT:
Without memory technologies we would not be able to live our connected lifestyle. Memory is the core of our tablets, PCs, smart phones, servers, cloud services, deep learning hardware and the basis of almost all complex electronics. Understanding how different memory technologies work and where their limitations are is crucial for most applications.

Memory technology operates at the forefront of semiconductor technology and production. Memory technology uses the most advanced lithography tricks and the latest transistor designs in combination with novel electronic materials. Therefore, you will touch base with the latest challenges in nanoelectronics and learn how to live with them or how to mitigate them. 

The lecture will discuss technology details, limitations and challenges along the memory hierarchy in data storage systems.
Outline:
semiconductor memories:
-SRAM
-DRAM
-HBM / SOCAMM
-Soft errors (SER)
-Flash
-FeRAM
-MRAM
-PCRAM (3D XPoint)
-OTP like e-Fuse, Antifuse, eMemory, Kilopass, Synopsis, NSCore
Emerging Memories:
-resistive memory technologies (Memristor etc.)
-3D memory technologies
-mechanical and magnetic memories:
-magnetic tape storage
historical memory devices

OBJECTIVES:
After completion of this course, the student
- understands advanced patterning, litho and layout techniques
- understands advanced transistor concepts like FinFet, Gate-all-Around FET, FD-SOI and MCBFETs
- knows the economic and performance aspects of the memory hierarchy (evaluate)
- is able to evaluate pros and cons of different memory technologies
- knows which memory to choose for a given application (apply)
- knows what technology to choose for having memory w/o extra masks (apply)
- knows a metric how to benchmark different memory technologies (evaluate)
- knows the physical limitation for each memory technology (evaluate)
- knows the physical challenges for each technology (evaluate)
- understands the basic physics and technology for semiconductor memories
- understands the basic physics and technology for magnetic storage
- understands the basic physics and technology of insulators, high-k and metal gate materials
- understands the basic physics and technology for phase-change materials for data storage
- knows architecture-based limitations of certain memory technologies (evaluate)
- has an overview of current nano-electronic challenges

Title: Memristive Memory Technology
Description:
CONTENT:
The block course will introduce memristive devices for various future electronic applications. We will first cover basic principles of achieving a memristive effect and its possible applications. We will then give an in-depth introduction in the characteristics of memristive devices and how they are fabricated and characterized. The students will apply their knowledge by fabricating and measuring several memristive devices. This interdisciplinary course covers aspects of electrical engineering, physics and materials science.

Course topics: Introduction to memristive devices, hands-on introduction into fabrication processes: sputtering, plasma oxidation, rapid thermal annealing, metal evaporation using thermal and e-beam sources, optical characterization of thin films with ellipsometry; electrical characterization of memory devices using a probe station, analysis of measurement results.

OBJECTIVES:
After participation in this course, the students are able to 1. describe the relevance of memristive systems for future electronics, 2. describe the different physical phenomena that lead to resistance switching, 3. fabricate memristive devices using suitable semiconductor fabrication processes, including post-processing, 4. plan, execute and analyze electrical measurements of memristive devices, 5. evaluate the performance of memristive devices, 6. present the process from experiment to evaluation in a comprehensive way.

Title: Menschenwürde im Zeitalter der Künstlichen Intelligenz
Description:
CONTENT:
Sind wir Cyborgs? Die Technik geht uns unter die Haut, wenn wir das Handy 2600-mal am Tag streicheln. Dass Maschinen uns helfen, dass Smartphones unser Suchen auf Stadtplänen ersetzen, dass sie uns beim Einkaufen helfen, dass Chat GBT uns beim Formulieren unserer Gedanken hilft, alle diese Hilfen sehen wir als problemlos und moralisch erlaubt an. Die bereits jetzt erkennbare Abhängigkeit 
von Technik und KI projizieren wir in eine weite Ferne, und Formen der Versklavung des Menschen durch Computer wurden bisher nur in spannenden Unterhaltungsfilmen vorgeführt. 

Die wirkliche Sklaverei von Menschen durch Menschen wurde in der Geschichte, weil sie zunehmend moralisch falsch und verwerflich erschien, überwunden. Ein dramatischer Höhepunkt für die Herabwürdigung des Menschen durch den Menschen war die Katastrophe des Zweiten Weltkriegs mit ihrem menschenvernichtenden Holocaust. Inzwischen verblassen die Erinnerungen an die Notwendigkeit der Anerkenntnis der Menschenwürde, und die Logik der Selbsterhaltung des Staates setzt auf Machterhaltung des Staates durch geopolitische Bedingungen und Künstliche Intelligenz.

Entscheidend für eine Entwicklung zum Frieden ist der Umgang mit dem Computer. Die bereits jetzt sichtbaren Veränderungen, die die Organisation der Arbeit für das Verhältnis von Arbeitgebern und Arbeitenden hervorbringt, müssen ebenso in den Blick kommen wie die Veränderungen beim Verständnis der Macht der Staaten und bei den Versuchen, diese mit den Notwendigkeiten des gemeinsamen Überlebens aller Menschen in Einklang zu bringen. 

Es muss neu einsichtig werden, dass die kollektive Autorität nicht allein aus dem Machtbegehren eines Individuums oder einer Gruppe, sondern aus der Zustimmung der der Macht unterworfenen Individuen hervorgeht. Auch ist die Gesellschaft und ihr ökonomisches Verständnis neu zu denken.

OBJECTIVES:
Das Ziel der gemeinsamen Diskussionen kann nicht in fertigen Resultaten bestehen, sondern im Erarbeiten der Perspektiven eines digitalen Humanismus, zu dem nicht nur Konzepte des Venture Capitals, der Automatisierung, der Gewinnmehrung und schließlich neuer Waffensysteme gehören sollten, sondern auch die Besinnung auf das unverfügbar Eigenste des Menschen, die Menschenwürde. 

Auf der Basis einer offenen, aber mit Gründen geführten Diskussion sind die Studierenden in der Lage, die Menschenwürde als Grundlage der Menschenrechte zu verstehen. Sie sind ferner in der Lage, aktuelle Konfliktlagen auf der Basis politikwissenschaftlicher und philosophischer Erkenntnisse zu erörtern.

Title: Messgrößen von Gesundheit
Description:
CONTENT:
Durch die Kooperationen im Netzwerk Deutsche GesundheitsRegionen e. V. soll das Bild der Gesundheitswirtschaft geschärft werden – sowohl in der nationalen Wahrnehmung wie vor allem auch in der außenwirtschaftlichen Perspektive. Gesundheitsregionen stellen sich als Top-Regionen für die Zukunft der Gesundheit auf und sorgen für frischen Wind und Zusammenarbeit bei Erneuerungen im Gesundheitsgeschehen (aus: http://www.deutsche-gesundheitsregionen.de).
Im Kern dieses Kurses geht es um die Erarbeitung einer Bewegungsintervention für Kinder in Zusammenarbeit mit Fit- und Clever. Die Intervention wird durchgeführt in der Gesundheitsregion plus im Berchtesgadener Land und in der Gesundheitsregion München.

Jede Gruppe wird einen Tag vor Ort sein und mit Schülern der Hauptschule bzw. des Sonderpädagogischen Förderzentrums arbeiten. Die Termine in München sind vom 02. bis 06. Dezember, auch hier wird jede Gruppe einen Termin übernehmen.

OBJECTIVES:
Nach erfolgreicher Teilnahme am Modul sind die Studierenden in der Lage:
- eine Intervention zu planen, durchzuführen und zu evaluieren. 
- die verschiedenen Größen, an denen sich Gesundheit qualitativ und quantitativ messen lässt, zu kennen und anzuwenden
- Gesundheitsregionen mit ihren diversen gesundheitsbezogenen Angeboten und Passung auf diverse Zielgruppen mit unterschiedlichen Handlungsfeldern zu benennen

Title: Metal additive manufacturing
Description:
CONTENT:
Metal Additive Manufacturing (MAM) is revolutionizing production by building up components layer by layer. In contrast to traditional subtractive manufacturing, which causes enormous waste through material removal, MAM offers a sustainable alternative. This technology not only enables customized productions but also the integration of complex geometries into functional products, which reduces resource-intensive inventory. As a result, MAM is recognized by many leading publications as a pioneering technology. To familiarize EuroTeQ students with this innovative technology, this introductory course in Metal Additive Manufacturing is offered. The course covers all essential aspects of MAM and provides the necessary knowledge to develop functional products using this technology. It contains the modules 1. introduction to MAM, 2. design and topology optimization, 3. process and material simulation, 4. powder bed based MAM processes, 5. directed energy deposition, 6. post-processing, 7. quality and failure analysis, 8. applications, 9. sustainability, digitalization and business models in AM. In addition to the technical basics, this course also covers the sustainability potential of MAM. Practical examples, presented by our industry partners, will be used to illustrate the ecological and economic benefits of this technology. This introductory course provides a comprehensive and practical introduction to metal additive manufacturing and prepares students to succeed in one of the most exciting and dynamic areas of manufacturing technology.

OBJECTIVES:
After completing the module, students will be able to, 
1. explain the basics of the most popular additive manufacturing processes for metals, process workflows, design principles, material selection, post-processing, testing methods and applicability in an industrial context, 
2. classify the importance of materials engineering, characterization, and modeling in the field of metal AM, 
3. apply the principles of topology optimization and design guidelines as well as numerical material and process mapping for the design of additively manufactured products and services with added value, 
4. assess the suitability of additive manufacturing as a replacement or complementary technology to conventional manufacturing, 
5. assess the sustainability potential of additive manufacturing with metals and develop ecologically compatible manufacturing and business models.

Title: Methoden der Personalauswahl und -entwicklung
Description:
CONTENT:
The module "Methods of Personnel Recruitment and Development" consists of two parts "Methods of Recruitment" and "Methods of Personnel Development".

In the course "Methods of Recruitment", application-related contents of recruitment are taught. The whole process of recruitment is dealt with, starting with the analysis of requirements (competence models, operationalization, etc.) through the various selection methods (interview, psychological test procedures, behavioral observation) to the preparation of an expert opinion.

In the course "Methods of Personnel Development", application-related contents of personnel development, differential psychology, and social psychology are taught. 
In particular, personality and competence development, coaching, communicative competence, and team development are dealt with. Emphasis is placed on the assessment of one&#x27;s own and others&#x27; competencies.

OBJECTIVES:
After participating in the module, students are able to understand and apply methods and measures of personnel recruiting and development.

After successful completion of the course "Methods of Recruitment", students are able to independently replicate the process of recruitment, i.e. to create a requirements analysis, to validly and reliably examine central competencies with the help of suitable selection methods, to make a well-founded personnel decision, and to record the result in an expert report.

After successful completion of the course "Methods of Personnel Development", students know the basics of differential and personality psychology and are able to evaluate and apply practical personality and competence models. They know important models of communication psychology and can use them to improve their individual communicative competence in the professional environment. They can use social psychological processes for communication, coaching, mentoring, and team development.

Title: Methoden der Produktentwicklung
Description:
CONTENT:
The aim of the lecture is to convey key methods and approaches for the systematic and successful development of technical products. The focus is on structured approaches to the analysis, planning, and design of products and product families.
The course covers methods for requirements analysis and generation (e.g., using benchmarking and solution spaces), modeling and structuring complex systems with Design Structure Matrices (DSM) and Attribute Dependency Graphs (ADG), as well as development of solutions using techniques such as morphological charts or target cascading, and systematic evaluation and decision-making methods such as FMEA and utility evaluation.
In addition, various process models of product development (e.g., the V-Model) are introduced. Agile approaches are also considered as modern practices in product development.

OBJECTIVES:
After completing the course, students will be able to:
• Describe the essential steps of a generic product development process, applicable to all technical disciplines
• Select appropriate methods for particular product development scenarios.
• Generate and analyze requirements for complex systems
• Model product architectures, functions and properties and their dependencies
• Apply methods for solution generation, systematic evaluation and decision making
• Transfer the acquired knowledge to new product development scenarios.
Skills: ['Product design software', 'CAD (SolidWorks, AutoCAD, CATIA)', 'Simulation software', 'Mechanical design', 'Project management software']

Title: Methoden der Proteinbiochemie
Description:
CONTENT:

We will first address the legal issues concerning the work with genetically modified organisms. 
The major topic of the lecture will be the explanation of laboratory methods for genetic madifications in bacteria with the focus on maximizing the yield of the desired protein.
The basics of fermentation will be presented as well as methods for protein purification.

OBJECTIVES:
After this lecture students should be able to set up a project plan for producing and purifying a recombinant protein in a preparative scale.

Title: Methoden eines digitalen Berufsschulunterrichts – Praktische Umsetzung eines hybriden Unterrichtsbeispiels
Description:
CONTENT:
Im Rahmen des Seminars soll in Gruppenarbeit (je ca. 3–5 Studierende) eine sog. Hybride Lernlandschaft (kurz: HLL) entwickelt werden. HLL sind Lernumgebungen, in denen digitale Möglichkeiten so genutzt werden, dass ein herkömmlicher Klassenunterricht beruflicher Schulen räumlich und zeitlich überschritten werden kann. Grundidee hierbei ist, dass alles, was zum Lernen benötigt wird, auf einer Lernplattform verfügbar ist und die Lernenden im Klassenzimmer, Zuhause oder auch im Betrieb selbstorganisiert lernen können.

Im Seminar werden zunächst die Möglichkeiten der Lernplattform Moodle und deren Features erkundet und ausprobiert. Anschließend erfolgt eine selbstorganisierte Lernphase zu relevanten Bezugskonzepten sowie zur HLL-Theorie als theoretische Basis. Im nächsten Schritt wird jeder Gruppe eine Konzeptionsmatrix (Unterrichtskonzeption) zur Verfügung gestellt. Anhand dieser gilt es zu klären, welche Medien und Materialien in welcher Form sinnvoll digitalisiert werden sollen und welche Struktur der Moodle-Kurs bzw. dessen Themen-/ Lerngebiete haben sollen. Im letzten Schritt wird der Moodle-Kurs erstellt und mit Inhalten gefüllt. Das schließt die konkrete Erstellung von eigenen Arbeitsanweisungen, Erklärvideos, Informationstexten, Arbeitsblättern, entsprechenden Lösungshinweisen, usw. mit ein.

Hinweis zum Wintersemester 25/26:

Title: Methoden zur Analyse und Regelung von Smart Grids
Description:
CONTENT:
Die massiven Installationen erneuerbarer Energien, die fortschreitende Elektrifizierung und Digitalisierung, bzw. die daraus resultierende veränderte Netznutzung, ändern die Anforderungen an die Stromnetze fundamental: Bisher waren Energieflüsse fast ausschließlich von wenigen großen Kraftwerken hin zu vielen, statistisch gut beschreibbaren Verbrauchern gerichtet. Nun finden auch horizontale Austausche innerhalb der unteren Spannungsebenen statt. In bestimmten Situationen können die Verteilnetze in die Übertragungsnetze zurück speisen. Sogar komplett (unter Umständen temporär) entkoppelte, lokale Inselnetze sind im Einsatz. Die Änderungen in unserer Energieinfrastruktur beschränken sich nicht allein auf die Stromerzeugung, hinzu kommen neue Verbrauchsmuster - beispielsweise durch das Laden von Elektrofahrzeugen oder Stromspeichern induziert - und der massiv ansteigende Strombezug durch Künstliche Intelligenz. Um in dieser Situation einen technisch wie ökonomisch stabilen Betrieb gewährleisten zu können, müssen sich die Strukturen und der Betrieb der Verteilnetze von hauptsächlich passiven Systemen hin zu aktiven Smart Grids entwickeln. Dazu werden zahlreiche Analyse- und Regelungstechniken benötigt.

Diese Vorlesung beschreibt die Herausforderungen, denen die Smart Grids gegenüberstehen, sowie die nötigen Maßnahmen, um diesen Herausforderungen gerecht zu werden. Im Zentrum der Veränderungen steht das Stromverteilnetz, die Vorlesung behandelt, aber auch wichtige angrenzende Netzstrukturen, beispielsweise Wärmenetze oder cyber-physische Systeme.

Sie gibt einen Überblick über grundlegende Techniken zur Analyse, Automatisierung und Optimierung von Energienetzen. Anhand von Beispielen wird dies anschaulich demonstriert. Die Vorlesung soll erste solide Grundlagen in diesem Feld vermitteln.

Behandelte algorithmische Grundlagen: Optimierung, Statistische Modellierung, Regelung. Smart Grid Anwendungsbeispiele werden aufgeführt und dem Studenten nähergebracht.

OBJECTIVES:
Der Studierende ist nach der Teilnahme an der Veranstaltung in der Lage:
- das Themengebiet Smart Grids zu verstehen,
- die Strukturierung von Smart Grids, bzgl. Regelung, Kommunikation und Märkten anhand von algorithmischen Grundlagen zu bewerten und
- einen Überblick über verschiedene Elektrizitätsmarktmodelle, Frequenz- und Spannungsregelung und Stabilität von Elektrizitätsmärkten zu geben.

CONTENT:

In the seminar, the students will apply the six steps of the Intervention Mapping Framework to create their own health promotion program. The seminar involves discussions, group work as well as feedback on planning a health promotion program.

- Differentiation of prevention and (mental) health promotion in the field of psychology
- Differentiation of mental illness and mental health
- Models of attitude and behavior change in general and in health-related behavior

- to understand and describe main methods and approaches in the psychology of prevention
- to discuss and evaluate approaches in health promotion and the prevention of disease from a psychological perspective

- to apply the Intervention Mapping Framework within program planning.

Title: Microeconomics
Description:
CONTENT:
The module introduces to the essential concepts of microeconomics. It deals with the behavior of individual econom-ic units (e.g., households, companies, and public institutions) and how these economic units interact to form markets and industries. Important questions discussed in the module:
• How can consumer decisions be explained and how can aggregate demand be derived from consumer choice?
• Which are the factors that determine the production decisions of companies?
• How do equilibrium prices emerge in competitive markets and how in monopoly markets?
• What is the effect of government interventions in markets?
• How does market power affect social welfare?
• Which factors lead to market failure?

OBJECTIVES:
After successfully completing the module, participants have gained the competence to:
• describe economic tradeoffs, in particular of consumers and companies in scarcity situations,
• solve tradeoffs and to apply these approaches to new situations,
• explain fundamental economic mechanisms underlying specialization and trade,
in particular in the context of technological progress,
• predict governmental interventions and how they affect simple competitive markets,
• explain why certain industries are prone to market concentration and how market power affects social welfare, and
• distinguish which types of goods are efficiently provided on free markets and which not.
