Title: Business Ethics
Description:
CONTENT:
The contrast between the unique ability of capitalism to create prosperity and its side-effects, scandals, pollution etc. raises the question; is the capitalism a blessing or a plague? Can we extract the benefits and reduce the side-effects?

In the first part of the course we will venture into the history of ethics, concentrating on the concept of duty, on consequentialism, on the virtues of Aristotle, Adam Smith, and modern management virtues. The historical background conveys an essential understanding of current ethical dilemmas. In the second part we will concentrate on corporate social responsibility and corporate governance. We will discuss the significance of these concepts in the light of globalisation, the financial crisis of 2008 and major corporate scandals. The third part of the course is dedicated to two specific subjects: The first is power; the combination and coexistence of sympathy and the power struggle in professional life and interaction. The second subject is consumer ethics. Here, we will investigate religious, bourgeois and intellectual values and their relationship to hedonistic consumerism. We will look at the contrast between mainstream society and anti-consumerist morality. The course is concluded with a discussion of capitalism, freedom and responsibility.

OBJECTIVES:
Students shall be able to reflect upon ethical issues in business, apply theories and understand the ethical gist of economic theories.
Skills: ['Analytical thinking and structured problem solving', 'Research-oriented mindset', 'Critical thinking and decision-making', 'Ethical awareness and data responsibility']

Title: Portugiesisch - Português para hispanofalantes A1
Description:
CONTENT:
In diesem Modul werden Grundkenntnisse der Fremdsprache Portugiesisch unter Berücksichtigung plurikultureller, plurilingualer und landeskundlicher Aspekte vermittelt, die es den Studierenden ermöglichen, mit Unterstützung ihres Repertoires in anderen romanischen Sprachen, hier insbesondere Spanisch, vertraute und alltägliche Ausdrücke und einfache Sätze zu verwenden und zu verstehen.
Sie lernen/üben grundlegendes Vokabular zu Themen wie Familie, Beruf, Freizeit, Einkaufen, Wohnen, Reisen und Gesundheit, einfache Gespräche in alltäglichen Situationen zu führen und in Hauptsätzen Alltägliches in Vergangenheit, Gegenwart und Zukunft zu äußern, unter Verwendung von Nomen, Verben, Pronomen und Possessivartikeln, Modalverben, Imperativ und grundlegender lokaler und temporaler Präpositionen.
Es werden Möglichkeiten aufgezeigt, den Lernprozess in der Fremdsprache eigenverantwortlich und effektiv zu gestalten. Die Studierenden üben soziale und interkulturelle kommunikative Kompetenz durch kooperatives Handeln und Mediation (auch online).
Im Unterricht wird zugleich auf die grammatikalischen und phonetischen Unterschiede zwischen Sprachvarietäten des Portugiesisch als auch im Vergleich zum Spanischen eingegangen.

OBJECTIVES:
Das Modul orientiert sich an den Niveaustufen A1 des GER. 
Nach Abschluss dieses Moduls sind die Studierenden in der Lage Ausdrücke und einfache Sätze zu verwenden, die auf die Befriedigung konkreter, in der Bewältigung des Alltags wesentlicher Bedürfnisse zielen. Sie sind in der Lage, seine spanischen Vorkenntnisse beim Erlernen der portugiesischen Sprache nützlich einzubringen.
Sie können einfache Fragen in alltäglichen Situationen stellen und beantworten, Tagesabläufe in Vergangenheit und Gegenwart beschreiben, Absichten ausdrücken und einfache schriftliche Mitteilungen zur Person machen, Verabredungen treffen und in grundlegenden alltäglichen Situationen beispielsweise beim Einkauf oder im Restaurant ihre Wünsche erfolgreich kommunizieren, sofern die Gesprächspartner deutlich sprechen und Wiederholungen anbieten, wenn es erforderlich ist. 
Die Studierende können einfache, vorhersehbare Informationen von unmittelbarem Interesse übermitteln, die in kurzen, einfachen Texten wie Schildern und Notizen, Postern und Programmen enthalten sind. Die Kommunikation kann mit Hilfe von Internationalismen und verwandten Wörtern/Gebärden aus anderen Sprachen erfolgen.

Title: Portugiesisch A1
Description:
CONTENT:
In this module the basics of the Dutch language are taught so students can express themselves in everyday situations.
Focus is laid upon intercultural and geographical aspects; the students learn how to ask questions about somebody else's family, how to count, to understand prices and time expressions, a basic vocabulary is created and used in easy present tense or present perfect main clauses.

The teaching strategy used will enable the students to communicate in the Dutch language despite of their small vocabulary.
Furthermore, tactics in order to learn the language more efficiently are shown.
Differences between the Portuguese spoken in Brazil and Portugal are shown.

OBJECTIVES:
The lecture is aimed at level A1 of the CEFR (Common European Framework of Reference). Students gain basic knowledge of Portuguese with a general language orientation while taking into consideration intercultural and cultural aspects. Students acquire teamwork skills through collaborative work in multinational mixed groups. After completion of this module, students will have acquired knowledge of everyday expressions and very simple sentences aimed at fulfilling the concrete needs of everyday life. Students can introduce themselves and others, ask others about themselves and answer similar questions, give simple descriptions of their day-to-day lives and briefly describe themselves in writing. They can communicate their wants and needs to counterparts who speak clearly and slowly and are willing to help.

Angestrebte Lernergebnisse: Das Modul orientiert sich am Niveau B1.1 des GER.
Nach Abschluss des Moduls sind die Studierenden in der Lage sich in den meisten Situationen, denen man in Studium, Beruf und Freizeit im Sprachgebiet begegnet, sicher zu verständigen und zu alltäglichen Themen eine persönliche Meinung äußern und widersprechen bzw. für und gegen etwas argumentieren. 
Sie können sich über kulturelle Unterschiede und Sprache austauschen; Ratschläge, Warnungen und Meinungen aussprechen und schreiben; die meisten Situationen bewältigen, denen man auf Reisen und im Sprachgebiet begegnet; über Erfahrungen und Ereignisse berichten, Träume, Hoffnungen und Ziele beschreiben und dies auch begründen oder erklären; über persönliche Themen, und zu Ihrem Studienumfeld, kurze Texte schreiben.
Die Studierenden können andere Menschen einladen, ihr Fachwissen, ihre eigenen Erfahrungen und Sichtweise einzubringen. Sie können Informationen in klaren, gut strukturierten Texten zu Themen übermitteln, die ihnen vertraut oder von persönlichem oder aktuellem Interesse sind, obwohl der begrenzte Wortschatz gelegentlich zu Formulierungsproblemen führen kann.

Title: Portugiesisch B1.2
Description:
CONTENT:
In diesem Modul werden Kenntnisse in Portugiesisch gefestigt und erweitert, unter Berücksichtigung plurikultureller, plurilingualer und landeskundlicher, studienbezogener Aspekte, die es den Studierenden ermöglichen, sich in vertrauten Situationen (Studium, Arbeit, Freizeit und Familie) und zu Themen von allgemeinem Interesse  wie z. B. Kunst, Geschichte, soziales Engagement, selbständig und sicher in der Zielsprache zu äußern und zu verstehen, wenn Standardsprache der verschiedenen Varietäten des Portugiesisch verwendet wird.
Die Studierenden erarbeiten ein erweitertes Spektrum an Vokabular und Redewendungen, erfassen und benutzen ein grundlegendes Repertoire an logischen Haupt- und Nebensatz-Strukturen mit Konjunktiv. Sie lesen selbständiger Texte über Ihrem Studienumfeld und weitere globale, wissenschaftliche und literarische Texte und äußern sich schriftlich und mündlich darüber. Dazu werden entsprechende hierfür notwendige grammatikalische Themen erlernt und angewendet.
Es werden Möglichkeiten aufgezeigt, den Lernprozess eigenverantwortlich effektiv zu gestalten und damit die eigene Lernfähigkeit zu verbessern. Die Studierenden üben soziale und interkulturelle kommunikative Kompetenz durch kooperatives Handeln und Mediation (auch online).
Im Unterricht wird zugleich auf die grammatikalischen und phonetischen Unterschiede zwischen Sprachvarietäten des Portugiesisch eingegangen.

OBJECTIVES:
Das Modul orientiert sich am Niveau B1 des GER. 
Nach Abschluss des Moduls sind die Studierenden in der Lage sich in den meisten Situationen, denen man in Studium oder Beruf, Freizeit und auf Reisen im Sprachgebiet begegnet, sicher zu verständigen. Sie können z.B. Informationen aus Zeitungstexten weitergeben, über lebenswerte Städte diskutieren, Personen und Dinge genauer beschreiben, Meinungen äußern und argumentieren.
Sie können wesentliche Inhalte in einfachen, authentischen Sachtexten, literarischen Texten und in Fernseh- oder Radiosendungen verstehen und wiedergeben und sich spontan an Gesprächen zu Themen von allgemeinem Interesse beteiligen. Sie können einfache formelle E-Mails und längere persönliche Briefe verfassen und von persönlichen Erfahrungen berichten.  Sie können die wesentlichen Punkte langer Texte übermitteln, die in unkomplizierter Sprache zu Themen von persönlichem Interesse formuliert sind, sofern man die Bedeutung einzelner Wendungen überprüfen kann.

Title: Positionen des modernen Designs
Description:
CONTENT:
Design works! Die bewusste Gestaltung von Objekten für den täglichen Gebrauch zeigt sich in allen Lebensbereichen. Ob iPhone, BMW oder Wagenfeldleuchte – gutes Design ist überall präsent. Dabei steckt in der Auseinandersetzung mit Gestaltung ein entscheidendes Potential für die individuelle und kulturelle Entwicklung und den wirtschaftlichen Erfolg von Produkten. 

Der Workshop richtet seinen Fokus auf die Design-Entwicklung des 20. und 21. Jahrhundert und bespricht ihre wesentlichen Positionen. Er gibt einen Überblick über modernes Industrie-, Fahrzeug-, Graphik-, Möbel-, IT- und Schmuckdesign, dem sich die Neue Sammlung – The International Design Museum in der Pinakothek der Moderne auf einzigartige Weise widmet.

Thematische Beispiele: Alvar Aalto, Ron Arad, Peter Behrens, Marcel Breuer, Luigi Colani, Charles und Ray Eames, Eileen Gray, Konstantin Grcic, Josef Hoffmann, Shiro Kuramata, Charles Rennie Mackintosh, Alessandro Mendini, Gaetano Pesce, Jean Prouvé, Dieter Rams, Richard Riemerschmid, Aldo Rossi, Ettore Sottsass, Gerald Summers, Michael Thonet, Henry van de Velde, Wilhelm Wagenfeld, Frank Lloyd Wright

OBJECTIVES:
Der Kurs vermittelt  die unterschiedlichen Positionen des modernen Designs. Nach der Teilnahme haben die Studierenden ihre Kenntnisse in der Designgeschichte erweitert. Durch die Diskussionen und Referate wird das Thema interdisziplinär beleuchtet und das Wissen vertieft.

Title: Positionen
Description:
CONTENT:
The seminar "Positions" covers topics, fundamentals, and methods of urban planning studies at TUM. The introduction focuses on familiarizing students with the structure of TUM, the School of Engineering & Design, and the urban planning program, as well as the right contact persons for various issues. It also provides an overview of the course schedule and tasks and helps students identify their own interests in the discipline. 
In the following sessions, the professors and chairs of Urban Design (Prof. Ben Boucsein), Sustainable Urbanism (Prof. Mark Michaeli), and Spatial Planning & Development (Prof. Lindsay Howe) present their respective positions and specific perspectives on the subject for discussion in lectures and jointly prepared discussion rounds. The perspective will then be expanded in three jointly prepared discussion rounds by the positions of other professors and lecturers. 

Suitable methodological approaches will be taught on an ongoing basis through input and individual exercises. We do not view methods merely as ready-made tools with which we can explore and describe spatial and social processes in the city and become active in them ourselves. The methods themselves can also be designed, modified, and adapted to our needs.

Finally, participants will design a possible course of study for themselves.
The overarching content-related goal of the course is to gain an overview of the structure, staff, and positions in the Urban Design program at TUM, to learn about methods and approaches that enable students to meet the complex challenges of the polycrisis in the field of urban design, and, on this basis, to sharpen their own interest in the discipline of urban design and to design their own course of study in a targeted manner.

OBJECTIVES:
Disciplinary knowledge of urban development, urban planning, the functioning of urban systems, and the challenges these systems face in the polycrisis. Language requirements exist insofar as contributions can be made in spoken and written English, but a significant part of the discussions will take place in German. A high degree of interest and initiative in shaping the content of the course is expected.  

Expected learning outcomes and acquired skills up to 3500 characters

After participating in the module, students will be able to 
-	Plan their own course of study in urban studies
-	Determine their future professional profile
-	Identify and understand the dimensions of the polycrisis and derive possible responses to it
-	Understand the range of courses offered by TUM across departments and schools.
-	Know and apply basic working methods of urban studies, adapt them to specific requirements, and develop your own sets of methods.
-	Consider the inextricably linked ecological, economic, and social impacts of their actions.
-	Continuously reflect on the methods and knowledge learned with regard to sustainable ecological, social, and economic development.
-	Develop interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary approaches to combine the three elements (ecological, social, and economic development).
-	Incorporate context-dependent and individual perceptions of sustainability.
-	In teams within one's own discipline, but also in interdisciplinary teams, understand each other's language, justify one's own decisions, and convince others with arguments.

Teaching and learning methods (transfer of skills) Workload for students up to 2000 characters

The skills are taught through the joint preparation of guest lectures in the form of moderated discussions and debates (in groups, with each group preparing one event). There are also reading texts for each event, which are read by everyone and prepared for discussion.

The methods are taught through exercises, with each event involving the individual application of a method and its documentation on an A4 sheet of paper. 

For final submission, see "Examination."
Skills: ['Urban planning', 'Project management software', 'Team leadership and mentoring', 'Independent work and self-direction']

Title: Post Shannon Theory
Description:
CONTENT:
Many new applications such as machine-to-machine, human-to-machine systems and the tactile internet demand ultra-reliable low latency. Achieving the demanding capabilities for those applications
requires the incorporation of essential features such as low latency, resilience, and robust data security directly into the physical domain.
In contrast to the classical Shannon transmission, the so-called Post Shannon Communication models can lead to significant performance improvements. For instance, the identification scheme, introduced by Ahlswede and Dueck, can bring about notable enhancements in performance. In the identification paradigm, the receiver only wants to decide whether the sender has sent a relevant message or not. Of course, the sender has no prior information about the messages that the receiver considers important.  Furthermore, substantial improvements in performance can be achieved by effectively exploiting the common randomness resource within the identification framework.
This module introduces this new research field and discusses the significant performance improvements.

OBJECTIVES:
At the end of this module, the students will be familiar with the different information-theoretic models for identification and common randomness generation.  They will be able to derive the capacity for each of the proposed models.

Title: Power Electronics for Distributed Energy Systems
Description:
CONTENT:
The following contents will be covered in the module:
1. Context and requirements for the application of grid-connected power electronic converters in modern energy systems (solar photovoltaic, wind energy conversion systems, energy storage systems, HVDC).
2. Converter topologies and modulation strategies for grid-connected two-level and multilevel converters.
3. Instantaneous power theories.
4. Converter-to-grid synchronization strategies.
5. Dynamic modeling and control of three-phase inverters connected to the grid in grid following and grid forming modes.
6. Analysis of impedances of static converters.
7. High power DC-DC converters for energy storage systems and PV applications.

OBJECTIVES:
After participating in the module events, students will be able to:
- identify the requirements and the use of Power Electronics concepts to enable static power conversion in modern energy systems,
- understand the principles of power flow control through the use of power converters in an energy system,
- evaluate which power converters are appropriate for specific applications in the context of modern energy systems,
- model, analyze, and evaluate the compatibility and the behavior of a power converter in an energy system,
- calculate and simulate grid-connected converter systems and their controls in grid connected applications,
- understand the advantages and disadvantages of using different power converters in modern energy systems.
Skills: ['Power electronics', 'Electrical engineering', 'Renewable energy systems', 'Control systems', 'Simulation software']

Title: Power Management Integrated Circuits
Description:
CONTENT:
Introduction & Use Cases
– The role of PMICs in electrical systems: placed between the energy source and the electronics
– Key requirements: size, efficiency, reliability, noise performance, cost
– Fundamental topologies:
• Linear regulator (resistive approach)
• Inductor-based DC/DC converter (switch + inductor)
• Switched-capacitor converter (switch + capacitor)
• Hybrid converters (switch + capacitor + inductor)
– Power-management system architectures: multiple rails (e.g., Li-ion battery → DC/DC → analog LDO + digital LDO)
Power Devices & Components
– Power-stage configurations: low-side switch, high-side switch, half-bridge, full-bridge
– Non-ideal effects: RDSon, dropout, parasitic capacitances, body diode
– Loss mechanisms: conduction losses, switching losses
– Passive components: MOS, MOM, MIM capacitors; planar inductors
– Power transistors: DEMOS, DMOS; SOI technologies; latch-up; safe-operating area (SOA); dead-time generation
Linear Regulators – Basics
– Principle: voltage-controlled resistance
– Architecture: power transistor, sense resistor, reference voltage, error amplifier
– Dropout voltage (~100 mV)
– DC metrics: power efficiency, current efficiency, line regulation, load regulation
– Error amplifier specs: gain, slew rate, PSR
– Transient response: step changes in input voltage and load current
Linear Regulators – Advanced Topics
– Voltage-mode vs. current-mode control
– PMOS vs. NMOS power devices
– Stability analysis: poles/zeros, Miller compensation, zero-canceling resistor
– Slew-rate enhancement & dynamic biasing
– Noise & power-supply rejection considerations
– Over-charge protection, capacitor-less LDO designs
Protection & Reference Circuits
– Overvoltage, undervoltage, and overtemperature protection
– Bandgap voltage & current references
– Start-up circuits and power-on-reset
– Short-circuit and over-current protection
Switching Regulators – Fundamentals
– Comparison of switching vs. linear regulation
– Converter topologies: LC vs. capacitive-only
– Synchronous vs. non-synchronous DC/DC
– Voltage-mode vs. current-mode, Buck vs. Boost, PFM vs. PWM, CCM vs. DCM
– Inductive vs. inductorless operation
– Stability considerations
LC Buck Converter
– Inductor sizing & current ripple
– Schematic & operating principle
– Line & load regulation
– Efficiency, stability, noise & PSRR analysis
– Compensator design (Type I/II/III)
LC Boost Converter
– Inductor sizing & current ripple
– Schematic & operating principle
– Line & load regulation
– Efficiency, stability, noise & PSRR analysis
– Comparison to Buck topology
Capacitive Buck Converters (SCVR)
– Series-parallel topologies (Dickson, ladder, Fibonacci)
– Equivalent output resistance
– Flying-capacitor and switch sizing
– Efficiency and regulation methods
Capacitive Boost Converters (Charge Pumps)
– Diode-based vs. transistor-based charge pumps
– Stage cascading & closed-loop control
Near-Field Wireless Power Transfer
– Principles: electromagnetic vs. electrostatic induction
– Basic architectures & operating frequencies
– Near-field vs. far-field applications
Far-Field Wireless Power Transfer & RF Energy Harvesting
– RF energy harvesting for low-power IoT: impedance matching, rectification, MPPT
– RF path loss and power budgeting
– Full chain: RFEH → Boost → MPPT → Buck → LDO
– Far-field application examples

OBJECTIVES:
Upon successful completion of the module, students will be able to:
Understand fundamental PMIC concepts and architectures:
Grasp the operating principles and block‐level structures of power‐management ICs, including low‐dropout regulators(LDOs), switching converters, charge pumps, power sequencing and protection circuits.
Connect theoretical models to real‐world behavior:
Develop insight into how small‐signal and large‐signal models predict regulator dynamics, stability margins andtransient response, and relate these models to measured circuit performance.
Describe the interplay between specifications, sizing and topology:
Explain how key requirements—output accuracy, load/regulation transients, efficiency and noise—drive choices intransistor sizing, passive component selection (inductors, capacitors) and overall PMIC topology.
Skills: ['Power electronics', 'Analog electronics', 'Circuit analysis', 'Simulation software', 'Semiconductor device physics']

Title: Practical Course - Algorithms for Programming Contests
Description:
CONTENT:
Programming contests are competitions for solving problems with the help of computer programs. By taking part in these contests one may improve skills in using algorithms and data structures as well as in problem solving, software development and teamwork through fun and games. Important topics in computer science are combined with the fun in programming.

There are plenty of programming contests by now, each of them having a different mode and focus. The exercise problems in this course will be similar in style to the ones used in the International Collegiate Programming Contest (ICPC), an international programming contest for students which is run by the Association for Computing Machinery (ACM) since the 1970s. In this contest, groups of up to three students each need to solve eight to ten problems in five hours using one computer only. The Computer Science Department of TUM has been participating in the ICPC with multiple teams for several years. A sample problem of our practical course gives an impression of the problems we are going to solve in this course. [1]

As the course doesn't require previous contest experience, and the tasks are solved by each student individually, the course uses easier problems than ICPC.

There will be a lecture where we explain algorithms for a new topic each week. During the following week, the participants need to solve problems related to this topic. Solutions, different ideas and remarks regarding the problems will be presented in the next lecture. The problems differ in the level of difficulty: There will be problems asking for straightforward implementations of the presented algorithms as well as harder problems taken from several contests.

[1] https://teaching.model.in.tum.de/2021ss/conpra/sample_problem.pdf

OBJECTIVES:
Goals of this course are

- a better understanding of fundamental algorithms and data structures through practice,
- getting to know specialized algorithms,
- improved skills in problem solving and problem analysis,
- practice in recognizing needed algorithms for given problems on one's own,
- practice in adapting algorithms for specific use cases,
- improved capacities in teamwork by taking part in team contests,
- the application of important mathematical techniques as well as
- preparing the participants for programming contests.

Title: Practical Course - Analysis of new phenomena in machine/deep learning
Description:
CONTENT:
Deep neural networks produce state-of-the-art results on a wide range of machine learning problems. While deep learning still remains elusive to rigorous theoretical analysis, its phenomenal performance has shaken the mathematical foundations of machine learning—contradicting many conventional beliefs of classical learning theory and the fundamental understanding of how algorithms can successfully learn patterns. However, the past few years have seen an exciting combination of mathematical and empirical research, uncovering some of the mysteries of modern machine/deep learning and development of formal theories to explain them, such as:
1. Generalization: Why do classical theories fail to explain generalization in deep networks?
2. Over-parameterization: When overfitting can be good for learning?
3. Kernel behavior: When do neural networks behave identical to kernel methods?
4. Robustness: Why are some neural networks more robust? Why can specific changes in data trick the predictions of neural networks?

This course will familiarize the students with empirical practices used to explain surprising phenomena in deep learning. In particular, the students will be asked to reproduce empirical findings of recent papers from top ML conferences (Neurips, ICML, ICLR and AISTATS) and empirically extend these observations to more complex problems/models.

OBJECTIVES:
Upon completion of this module, the students will have gained
1. hands-on experience on reproducing and extending of modern ML algorithms / deep neural networks
2. critical analysis of empirical findings in relation to provided theoretical results

Title: Practical Course - Business Process Prediction, Simulation, and Optimization
Description:
CONTENT:
Organizations strive to optimize their business processes by developing data-driven prediction, simulation, and optimization strategies. For example, in the healthcare domain, clinics aim to predict and simulate surgical processes to optimize the planning of nursing and medical staff capacities. In manufacturing, organizations simulate production lines to explore new ways of improving efficiency. In the financial domain, prediction and simulation is used to optimize loan application processes. This practical course covers prediction, simulation and optimization of business processes. The goal is to strengthen students’ knowledge in machine learning, business process management and operations research to optimize data-driven, real-world business processes. Business process prediction includes forecasting the entire sequence of events. Business process simulation tries to create a “virtual twin” of a real-world process. Business process optimization seeks to improve running processes. All three concepts can be combined, for instance, using prediction to support simulation and simulation outcomes to guide optimization for process redesign.
Participating students will be assigned a task that addresses the prediction, simulation and optimization of a specific aspect of an existing business process. For each process, an event log and relevant background information will be provided. In the first half of the course, students will implement and apply state-of-the-art business process prediction and/or simulation models. In the second half of the course, students will implement different policies to optimize the process based on their prediction and/or simulation model. Upon completion, students will present results and discuss the benefits, implications and limitations of their approach in the context of a real-world business process.

OBJECTIVES:
Course participants will learn to create business process prediction and simulation models from existing event logs.
They will learn how to implement optimization policies based on prediction and simulation results and test their applicability.
Participants will learn how to work self-dependent towards accomplishing the assigned task and to present and discuss their results.
Skills: ['Business process management', 'Data analysis', 'Predictive modeling', 'Simulation software', 'Optimization', 'Python', 'Analytics', 'Independent work and self-direction']

Title: Practical Course - Deep Learning for Human Modelling
Description:
CONTENT:
This praktikum focuses on different aspects of modelling humans from a technical or medical point of view. The praktikum will involve different sets of tasks including multimodal analysis of the human body, and its visualization. The interface development tasks are mainly designed for B.Sc. students, while the advanced computer vision and machine learning problems are tailored for the level of M.Sc. students.

Title: Practical Course - Human-Centered Computing
Description:
CONTENT:
This module brings together practical approaches from the fields of human-centered data science, which considers societal contexts and ethical concerns for data analysis, and computational social science, which leverages large-scale data to discover theories and patterns of societal behavior. Work in these areas matters as solving the hard and pressing problem of our and future generations requires teams that combine the how (data, algorithms, tools) with the why (societal implications, culture, ethics) of computing with human-centered data and/ or for applications that impact people’s lives. We will use concepts, theories, methods, algorithms, and evaluation methods from the fields/ domains of natural language processing, network science, statistics, machine learning, AI, and the social sciences. This module entails: 1) implementing data analysis and/ or software (sub)project in teams, 2) practicing methods and models of computational data analysis and/ or software development and/ or programming from the outlined areas, and 3) practicing techniques for planning, documentation, assessing, and presenting process and (intermediate) results.

OBJECTIVES:
Completing this module and its requirements should enable students to acquire the following knowledge and skills: 
-	Conceptualize, plan, design, implement, and evaluate a computational data analysis and/ or software project in a team-based manner.
-	Apply methods and models from different disciplines to work through the various stages of the project. 
-	Assess risks and common problems encountered in computational data analysis and programming projects and be able to trouble shoot them. 
-	Consider context, culture, and ethics throughout computing projects. 
-	Communicate their work including process and outcomes.
-	Improve their academic and professional communication and interaction skills.
Skills: ['Human-centered data science', 'Computational social science', 'Data analysis', 'Python', 'Data ethics', 'Societal impact analysis']

Title: Practical Course - JavaScript Technology
Description:
CONTENT:
In this practical course, participants will be provided with hands-on experience in designing and building modern JavaScript-based web applications in an agile development environment. Partnering with renowned industry professionals, the course creates an industry-like atmosphere where participants learn about modern web development practices, project and stakeholder management. 
Students work as software developers on meaningful problems in fast-paced Scrum teams, collaborating with 12-15 other developers over the course of 12 weeks. In the end, participants present their final project results in a live demo.

OBJECTIVES:
This course aims to prepare students for a successful career in web-based software engineering by familiarising them with modern, industry-relevant web technologies like React, Node, SQL and No-SQL data storage solutions (e.g., PostgreSQL and MongoDB), as well as modern cloud providers like AWS and GCP. The course emphasizes code quality using Linters and code analysis tools and highlights the importance of proper documentation. Moreover, participants explore project management tools like Notion, Linear, and Slack, enhancing their collaboration and organizational skills. The course also introduces product, system, and UI design principles to teach students to go beyond solving just the base problem and instead build scalable and beautiful software systems.
Skills: ['JavaScript', 'Web application software', 'Agile development', 'Modern web development practices', 'React', 'Angular', 'Vue.js', 'HTML', 'CSS', 'Node.js']

Title: Practical Course - Technical Project Leadership
Description:
CONTENT:
In this practical course, you will lead an international team of 12-18 other developers in designing and building a modern JavaScript-based web application within an agile development environment from start to finish. Hereby, you’ll be involved in all critical processes from goal definition, and requirements elicitation to final implementation and deployment. Through your technical leadership, you will inspire and enable participants to excel as developers, ensuring their growth and success throughout the course as well as the success of the overall project. You’ll exchange with other technical project leads regularly during the course to share progress and learnings.

OBJECTIVES:
The practical course is designed to enhance participants' proficiency in technical project leadership. It offers a comprehensive learning experience in project, people and stakeholder management, and agile methodologies, enabling participants to effectively lead, support and motivate teams in overcoming challenges in a technical environment. Participants will gain hands-on experience in real-world project scenarios, fostering the skills to navigate complex dynamics and drive successful outcomes.
Skills: ['Project management', 'Team leadership', 'JavaScript', 'Web application software', 'Agile development', 'Requirements elicitation', 'Implementation', 'React', 'Angular', 'Vue.js']

Title: Practical Course
Description:
CONTENT:
The lectures will provide extensive theoretical aspects of neural networks and in particular deep learning architectures, specifically for advanced methods in the field of Computer Vision. 
The practical sessions will be key, students shall get familiar with Deep Learning through hours of training and testing. They will work with PyTorch and implement advanced network architectures. The project will have a focus on visual computing, including the following topics: 
- neural rendering 
- generative neural networks (GANs)
- neural radiance fields
- deep fake generation
- media forensics (forgery detection)
- scene reconstruction (multi-view, depth sensors, etc.)
- generative geometric models
- semantic scene understanding (object detection, instance segmentation, semantic segmentation)
- 3D scene understanding for autonomous driving (e.g., with Lidar/Radar)
- reinforcement learning (e.g., for 3d modeling, 3d auto-scanning, 3d navigation)
- natural language processing (NLP) for scene understanding

OBJECTIVES:
Upon completion of this module, students will have acquired extensive theoretical concepts behind advanced architectures of neural networks, in particular in the context of computer vision tasks in visual computing. In addition to the theoretical foundations, a significant aspect lies on the practical realization and training of neural networks.

- Written test of 60 minutes at the end of the course (for lecture)
- The lecture will have reading assignments (e.g., from the DeepLearning book and recent CVPR/ICCV/ECCV papers)
- After each practical session, the students will have to provide the written working code to the teaching assistant for evaluation. The students will be awarded a bonus in case they successfully complete all practical assignments.
- In the written exam, we will ask questions regarding lecture theory
- In addition, to the written exam, the results of the projects will be evaluated; we will evaluate projects on a (bi-)weekly basis including reports (33.33%), oral presentations (33.33%), and code/submissions (33.33%).

Title: Practical Course Advanced Robocup@Home
Description:
CONTENT:
1. Introduction
1.1. Introduction to Robocup@home competition

OBJECTIVES:
Analytical Skills and Technical Knowledge: Through writing reports on Technical Review and Requirements Analysis, students gain an in-depth understanding of the technologies and strategies used in previous RoboCup@Home competitions. This process enhances their ability to analyze, evaluate, and understand complex technical solutions.
Practical Robotics Skills and Team Collaboration: The hands-on experience of completing a final project in teams teaches students practical application of theoretical knowledge in robotics. It includes working on object detection, recognition, manipulation, and task planning, fostering teamwork and collaborative problem-solving skills.
Individual Technical Proficiency: Students are assessed on their individual contributions to the final project, focusing on their ability to devise technically sound solutions and implement them effectively using software like ROS.

Communication and Presentation Skills: The course requires students to present their project solutions, honing their ability to communicate complex ideas effectively. The live demonstration and question session further develop their skills in articulating and defending their technical decisions.
Comprehensive Understanding and Reporting: Writing a detailed final project report enables students to demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of the course material, applying their knowledge to a practical challenge. Overall, students emerge from the course with a blend of theoretical knowledge, practical robotics skills, analytical abilities, teamwork experience, individual technical proficiency, and strong communication skills.

Title: Practical Course Atomically Thin 2D Transistors and LEDs
Description:
CONTENT:
The practical course offers an introduction to 2D materials, their fabrication, properties, and applications in electro-optical devices. The participating students get hands on experience in fabricating atomically thin 2D materials using the mechanical exfoliation technique, the assembly of different materials into heterostructures by dry stamping, connecting to electrical circuits, and in measuring their opto-electronic characteristics. Two exemplary experiments are the fabrication and characterization of atomically thin field effect transistors and atomically thin LEDs. The devices that the students fabricate represent the ultimate atomic limit how small these devices can be miniaturized. The materials involved are graphene, transition metal dichalcogenides, and hexagonal boron nitride.

OBJECTIVES:
After successful completion of the module, the students will be able to fabricate, characterize, and handle 2D materials, as well as to build heterostructure devices based on these materials. They have also developed the skills needed to understand the limitations and potential advantages of such materials for next-generation nano-electronics. In addition, the students will have obtained the skills to present their results in an academic environment.

Title: Practical Course Atomistic Simulation of Nanomaterials and Electronic Devices
Description:
CONTENT:
The practical course offers an introduction to modern atomistic simulation tools, such as density functional theory (DFT). The participating students get hands on experience using these tools to calculate material properties and electronic devices. The topics include 2D and other nanomaterials; semiconductor heterostructures; quantum LEDs; batteries and energy storage; among others.

OBJECTIVES:
After successful completion of the module, the students will be able to perform modern atomistic simulations and can calculate properties of (e.g., semiconducting) nanomaterials and electronic heterostructure devices. They have also developed the skills needed to understand the limitations of such computational methods and can assess the reliability of simulation results.
Skills: ['Atomistic simulation', 'Density functional theory (DFT)', 'Nanomaterials', 'Electronic devices', 'Quantum simulation', 'Material properties calculation', 'Python', 'Simulation software']

Title: Practical Course Biological Life Support System
Description:
CONTENT:
The practical course introduces the topic of microalgae cultivation as a fundamental part of life support systems and covers the following aspects:

• Design and operation of microalgae culture.
• Planning and execution of experiments with microalgae.
• Maintenance of optimal cultivation conditions.
• Operation and set up of photobioreactor for microalgae cultivation.
• Periodic investigation of the status and condition of the microalgae culture with special attention to growth, pigment content or nutrient concentration, among others.

OBJECTIVES:
After participating in the practical module, students have a deep knowledge of the utilization and cultivation of microalgae for use mainly in life support systems (LSS) applications. This includes cultivation of microalgae culture for possible future solutions for long-duration human spaceflight missions. With all this, students will be able to design and prepare a microalgae culture for space applications from the beginning, analyze microalgal cultivation and growth as well as other characteristics for a specific mission design, based on the specific requirements of the mission, as a fundamental part of life support systems.
Skills: ['Microalgae cultivation', 'Life support systems', 'Experimental design', 'Bioreactors', 'Cultivation optimization', 'Scientific protocol writing']

Title: Practical Course Electronic Power Conversion
Description:
CONTENT:
The following contents will be covered in the module:
1. Basic principles of power converters.
2. Principles of power semiconductor devices and switching losses.
3. Control oriented modeling of power converters.
4. Three-phase power converters (power circuits and modulation strategies).
5. Power factor correction (single-phase and three-phase).
6. High performance DC-DC converters.
7. Basics on the design of magnetic components for power converters.
8. Modern applications of high-power converter systems (renewable energy, electric mobility, and advanced power supplies).

OBJECTIVES:
After participating in the module events, the students will be able to:
- model, analyze, and evaluate the compatibility and the behavior of a power converter in different applications, with a focus on the modernization of power systems and of the electrification occurring in several fields of technology,
- calculate, simulate and design power converter circuits and controls,
- understand the advantages and disadvantages of different power converters in the context of specific technical requirements,
- identify the typical implementation of converters in power systems.
Skills: ['Power electronics', 'DC/DC converters', 'Power semiconductor devices', 'Control systems', 'Power factor correction', 'Simulation software', 'Hardware-software interfacing']

Title: Practical Course Methods of Biomedical Engineering
Description:
CONTENT:
The contents of the course are 
•	the rules of scientific protocol writing and good laboratory practise,
•	basic laborartory methods (such as pipetting, weighing, stoichiometric calculations, pH measurements, microscopy)
•	basic statistical methods of planning and evaluating experiments 
•	methods of cell- and tissue culture, cell assays
•	basic amplifier circuits for recording of biosignals and for sensors, 
•	basics and applications of bioimpedance measurements.
Skills: ['Biomedical engineering', 'Scientific protocol writing', 'Laboratory methods', 'Statistical methods', 'Cell culture', 'Tissue culture', 'Experiment design and evaluation']

Title: Practical Course Power Electronics DC/DC Converter
Description:
CONTENT:
This module consists of a series of hands-on laboratory experiments with the following content being covered:
• Understanding the working principle of a buck-converter by measuring and testing a working prototype (12V-to-5V converter)
• Designing and building a magnetic coil for a boost converter and including this coil in an existing setup
• Analyzing an industrial DC/DC converter and its design criteria
• Experimental evaluation of a state-of-the-art load resonant converter (LLC)
• Experimental comparison of the different topologies regarding efficiency, electromagnetic compatibility, thermal behavior, and topology-dependent advantages

OBJECTIVES:
After successful participation in the module, the student is able to:
• Work independently and safely in a power electronics laboratory
• Understand the behavior and operating mechanism of switched-mode power converters
• Understand the concept of systematic hardware debugging
• Understand the concept of electromagnetic compatibility analysis of DC/DC converters
• Apply the concept of efficiency analysis of DC/DC converters
• Evaluate different DC/DC converter topologies regarding efficiency, cost, electromagnetic compatibility
• Create a magnetic coil for a simple DC/DC converter
Skills: ['Power electronics', 'DC/DC converters', 'Buck converter', 'Boost converter', 'Magnetic coil design', 'Circuit analysis', 'Hands-on laboratory experiments']

Title: Practical Course Power Electronics for Distributed Energy Systems
Description:
CONTENT:
The following contents will be covered in the module:
1. Context and requirements for the application of grid-connected power electronic converters in modern energy systems (solar photovoltaic, wind energy conversion systems, energy storage systems, HVDC).
2. Converter topologies and modulation strategies for grid-connected two-level and multilevel converters.
3. Instantaneous power theories.
4. Converter-to-grid synchronization strategies.
5. Dynamic modeling and control of three-phase inverters connected to the grid in grid following and grid forming modes.
6. Analysis of impedances of static converters.
7. High power DC-DC converters for energy storage systems and PV applications.

OBJECTIVES:
After participating in the module events, students will be able to:
- identify the requirements and the use of Power Electronics concepts to enable static power conversion in modern energy systems,
- understand the principles of power flow control through the use of power converters in an energy system,
- evaluate which power converters are appropriate for specific applications in the context of modern energy systems,
- model, analyze, and evaluate the compatibility and the behavior of a power converter in an energy system,
- calculate and simulate grid-connected converter systems and their controls in grid connected applications,
- understand the advantages and disadvantages of using different power converters in modern energy systems.
Skills: ['Power electronics', 'Grid-connected converters', 'Energy systems', 'Converter topologies', 'Modulation strategies', 'Simulation software']

Title: Practical Course Simulation of Life Support Systems
Description:
CONTENT:
- Introduction to Life Support Systems for Human Spaceflight and the corresponding subsystems
- Simulations of Life Support Systems with various tools

OBJECTIVES:
After finishing the practical course, the students should be able to

- compare LSS configurations for specific mission scenarios using trade-off analysis 
- understand the interaction of subsystems within an LSS
- interpret simulation results of an LSS and its subsystems

Title: Practical course
Description:
CONTENT:
This course provides comprehensive knowledge and skills in the field of topology optimization. Upon completion of the course, you will be able to understand the fundamentals and principles of topology optimization and apply numerical methods for topology optimization in 2D. You will learn to write numerical codes in MATLAB to solve topology optimization problems and will be able to interpret and evaluate the results of topology optimization. Furthermore, you will develop mechanical models and surrogate models for optimized structures and generate measures to improve the structural stiffness and strength through topology optimization.

The course includes theoretical foundations as well as practical exercises in which participants independently solve small topology optimization problems and go through the entire process chain from the optimized component to the manufacturable component. This also includes an introduction to a commercial software tool for optimizing more complex systems. The exercises are conducted using MATLAB to apply the learned methods and principles in a practical manner. Additionally, you will learn to recognize and develop practical applications of topology optimization in real engineering projects.

OBJECTIVES:
You are able to
- understand the fundamentals and principles of topology optimization.
- apply numerical methods for 2D topology optimization.
- write numerical codes in MATLAB to solve topology optimization problems.
- interpret and evaluate the results of topology optimization.
- develop mechanical models and surrogate models for optimized structures.
- generate measures to improve structural stiffness and strength through topology optimization.
- identify and develop practical applications of topology optimization in real engineering projects.
Skills: ['Topology optimization', 'MATLAB', 'Numerical methods', 'Finite Element Analysis (FEA)', 'Computational mechanics', 'Algorithm implementation']

Title: Practical Course Wearable Robotics
Description:
CONTENT:
In this course we introduce students to the fundamentals of robotics and control to develop wearable robotics. The course consists of theoretical lectures, hands-on tutorials, and a final project. The lectures introduce selected topics on robotics, sensors, and actuators by connecting it to neuromechanics and motor control in humans, and their application to upper-limb exoskeletons with a special focus on rehabilitation of patients with neurological disorders. The hands-on tutorials guide the students to program the robotic control of a single joint upper limb exoskeleton using robot skin developed in our laboratory as a sensory interface. Each group of students will receive a hardware setup to work with in the tutorials and project phases. In the final part of the course the students are supported in the development of their final projects through regular colloquium with the lecturers. Students are expected to apply what they learned in the lectures and tutorials to implement exoskeleton control routines used in robotics rehabilitation areas.

OBJECTIVES:
At the end of this course, students are able to: 
-	Understand the different wearable robotic technologies, requirements and applications
-	Understand the role of human-robot interaction and human factor in exoskeleton control. 
-	Describe the modelling of the human musculoskeletal system
-	Model kinematics and dynamics of upper limb exoskeletons 
-	Integrate signals from multiple sensors to exoskeleton devices depending on intended therapy outcomes. 
-	Use exoskeleton’s kinematic and dynamic models to design control schemes using multisensory modalities
--

Title: Practicing Research
Description:
CONTENT:
This course is designed to walk you through preparing and setting up an actual research process step-by-step. During this intensive course, you will choose a research topic and develop it into a research proposal which will be the final output (examination) of the course. Upon completion of the course, you will have a research proposal (exposé) which you can then either develop into a full MA thesis project, or use it as guide to design a new one. 

The course will be taught in two separate groups with equal number of participants in each.

OBJECTIVES:
The primary outcome of the seminar is a paper (4000 words incl. references) in which students formulate a research proposal for a potential MA thesis project or a comparable social science research project. In this proposal, students demonstrate that they are able to generate and formulate adequate research questions, do a successful literature search and review state-of-the-art research in relation to their chosen topic, develop an appropriate research design and apply different methods to an empirical case, address ethical issues of their planned research, make realistic plans and present their planned research in a structured way. Besides the written proposal, which will amount to 75% of the overall grade, students will also present their research progress at every session (25% of the overall grade).
Skills: ['Research-oriented mindset', 'Analytical thinking and structured problem solving', 'Project planning and prioritization', 'Documentation and knowledge transfer']

Title: Praktische Datenanalyse am Beispiel von Waldsystemen
Description:
CONTENT:
Das Lernergebnis wird zum einen durch Vorlesungen, zum anderen durch Übungen (einem sog. „blended learning“ Ansatz) sichergestellt. Übungen werden zum Teil in die Vorlesung integriert und ergänzend zur Vorlesung und zum Selbststudium angeboten.
In der Vorlesung werden die Inhalte im Vortrag durch anschauliche Beispiele sowie durch Diskussion mit den Studierenden vermittelt. Die Vorlesung soll den Studierenden dabei auch als Motivation zur eigenständigen Beschäftigung mit den Themen sowie zum Studium der Literatur dienen.
Jeweils passend zu den Vorlesungsinhalten werden in den Übungen Aufgaben und deren Lösungen angeboten, die die Studierenden zur selbstständigen Kontrolle sowie zur Vertiefung der gelernten Methoden und Konzepte nutzen sollen. Nachdem dies anfangs durch Anleitung passiert, wird dies im Laufe des Semesters immer mehr selbstständig einzeln und zum Teil auch in Kleingruppen vertieft.
Die Kombination aus Vorlesung und Übung ist entscheidend, um theoretische Inhalte und Grundlagen zu vermitteln, gleichzeitig muss das neu erlernte Wissen in der Praxis angewendet werden, um den Lernerfolg zu steigern

OBJECTIVES:
Das Modul bietet Anfängern eine solide Grundlage in der Nutzung der Programmiersprache R für Datenanalyse und Statistik.

Nach erfolgreicher Teilnahme am Modul sind die Studierenden in der Lage,
- mit der R-Konsole umzugehen und die Syntax der Sprache zu verstehen
- R-Code und Programme selbst zu schreiben, auszuführen und zu interpretieren
- die wesentlichen Konzepte der R-Programmierung zu differenzieren, darunter Datentypen (Vektoren, Matrizen, Faktoren und Datenbanken (Tabellen), Variablen, Operatoren, Funktionen
- grundlegende Konzepte der Datenverwaltung und -analyse in R anzuwenden, einschließlich des Lesens und Schreibens von Daten, des Zusammenfügens, Sortierens und Transformierens von Datenbanken
- Daten auf verschiedene Art und Weise zu visualisieren
- typische Daten, die in Wäldern für wissenschaftliche und praktische Zwecke erhoben werden, mit Standard- und fortgeschrittenen Verfahren auszuwerten, zu visualisieren und im Hinblick auf typische Fragestellungen zu interpretieren (z.B. Anwendung von Regressionsanalysen zur Erstellung von Bestandeshöhenkurven, die Identifizierung räumlicher Strukturen, die Berechnung von Holzvolumina, Biomassen, Kohlenstoffgehalten und Zuwächsen auf Baum- und Bestandesebene)
- die beschreibende und schließende Statistik zu unterscheiden
- die Bedeutung der Wahrscheinlichkeitstheorie als Grundlage für Verteilungen und Zufallsvariablen zu verstehen und zugehörige empirische Verteilungen zu benennen
- das allgemeine Prinzip eines Hypothesentests zu erkennen und damit die Ergebnisse eines ihnen nicht bekannten Hypothesentests zu interpretieren und richtige Schlüsse zu ziehen
- die Zahl der beobachteten Merkmale und Skalenniveaus richtig zu erkennen und anhand dieser Charakteristika den Lerninhalten richtig zuzuordnen, Formeln und Vorgehensweisen richtig anzuwenden und richtige Schlüsse zu ziehen
- die Bedeutung von R als Statistikprogramm einzuschätzen.

Title: Praktische Einblicke in die Managementberatung
Description:
CONTENT:
Sowohl die Unternehmensberater- als auch die Personalberaterbranche befand sich in den letzten Jahren auf einem kontinuierlichen Wachstumskurs. Für viele Hochschulabsolvent*innen hat der Berufseinstieg in die Beratungsbranche eine hohe Attraktivität, da das Berufsbild sowohl einen Einblick in unterschiedliche Kontexte und damit ein abwechslungsreiches Arbeitsumfeld bietet verbunden mit der Möglichkeit, das eigene Erfahrungs- und Methodenspektrum zügig zu erweitern. Dabei unterscheiden sich die Einsatzgebiete und Berufsprofile von Berater*innen signifikant, abhängig vom Schwerpunkt der angebotenen Expertise. 
In diesem Kurs werden wir den Studierenden ermöglichen, einen Einblick in die Anforderungen, Geschäftsmodelle, Aufgabenbereiche und Usancen der Beratungsbranche zu bekommen und uns dabei vor allem auf den Bereich der Managementberatung konzentrieren.

Der Kurs wird fünf verschiedene Perspektiven zu diesem Thema praxisnah beleuchten. 
•	Wir werden wir uns mit dem Berufsbild, den verschiedenen Einsatzbereichen und dem Geschäftsmodell von Managementberatung auseinandersetzen und sowie den Kundennutzen aber auch die Risiken einer Beratung für Kunden kritisch reflektieren.

•	Ausgehend von den verschiedenen Einsatzbereichen untersuchen wir, welche Anforderungen das jeweilige Einsatzgebiet von dem/der Beratenden erfordert und welche Kompetenzen dafür erworben werden müssen. Von den Studierenden jeweils vorbereitete und durchgeführte Experteninterviews aber auch in die Präsenzphase eingeladende Gäste werden hier einen vertieften Einblick in die Beratungspraxis ermöglichen.

•	Des Weiteren werden wir eruieren, welche unterschiedlichen Beratungsansätze und -tools es gibt und deren Vor- und Nachteile für die Lösung diverser Problemstellungen diskutieren

•	Um ein ganzheitliches Verständnis für den Ablauf einer Beratung zu ermöglichen, führen wir uns gemeinsam die verschiedenen Phasen eines Beratungsprozesses vor Augen und was es in jeder Phase zu beachten gilt.

•	Im Rahmen einer Case Study werden die Studierenden ein praktisches Angebot für eine Managementberatungsleistung erstellen und/oder einen Teil einer Beratungsleistung selbst durchführen.

OBJECTIVES:
Theorie:
Die Studierenden erhalten einen Einblick in die Anforderungen, Aufgabenbereiche, Geschäftsmodelle  und Usancen der Beratungsbranche (insb. Managementberatung): Zum einen, um Entscheidungen für die eigene Karriereentwicklung besser treffen zu können. Zum anderen um Einblick in eine weiterhin zukunftsträchtige Branche zu erhalten. 

Praktische Anwendung:
Die Studierenden verstehen, welche verschiedenen Einsatzbereiche und Anforderungen der Managementberatung existieren und können einen Abgleich mit ihren eigenen Kompetenzen und Interessen vornehmen. Zugleich erhalten Sie Informationen über die Gestaltung von Beratungsprozessen und zu relevanten Beratungstools.

Methode:
Die Studierenden erhalten im Rahmen von Experteninterviews Einblicke in unterschiedliche Einsatzbereiche und in die angewandte Praxis der Managementberatung. Mit der Bearbeitung einer Case Study können sie ihre Kompetenzen in der Strukturierung eines Beratungsprozesses erweitern.
Skills: ['Project planning and prioritization', 'Stakeholder and requirements management', 'Clear technical and non-technical communication']

Title: Praktische Ökotoxikologie
Description:
CONTENT:
Im Rahmen von Mesokosmenstudien oder Aquarienversuchen werden Untersuchungsmethoden zur ökotoxikologischen Bewertung von Umweltstressoren vorgestellt. Es werden physikalische und biologische Parameter erfasst und deren qualitative und quantitative Auswertung erlernt. Die erhobenen Daten werden mit gängigen statistischen Auswertungsmethoden (uni- und multivariate Statistik) bewertet und verschiedene Bewertungsendpunkte werden bestimmt (LC50/NOEC).

OBJECTIVES:
Nach der Teilnahme an der Lehrveranstaltung besitzen die Studierenden vertiefte praktische Kenntnisse zur Risikobewertung von Umweltstressoren mittels komplexer Testsysteme (Mesokosmenstudie, Aquarienversuche). Sie erhalten Einblick in Planung, Aufbau, Durchführung und Auswertung ökotoxikologiescher Testverfahren. Sie erlernen taxonomische Kenntnisse von Zooplankton und Makroinvertebraten und sind in der Lage, Zooplankton- und Makroinvertebratenproben qualitativ und quantitativ auszuwerten. Sie sollen in der Lage sein, ökosystemare Zusammenhänge zu erkennen und die verschiedenen Effektarten und deren Auswirkungen auf die verschiedenen Trophieebenen zu benennen. Sie erhalten einen Einblick in die gängigen ökotoxikologischen statistischen Auswertungsmethoden (multivariat und univariat) und die Bestimmung ökotoxikologischer Endpunkte.

Title: Praktische Softwareentwicklung für komplexe Simulationsumgebungen im Ingenieurwesen
Description:
CONTENT:
In this course basic methods of software development with C++ are treated. These will be developed using the example of a finite element software.
The course consists of three parts

Part 1: (one week towards the middle of the semester)
Lectures on the following topics:
- Basics / Good Practice of Software Engineering 
- Introduction to coding guidelines in C++, 
- Introduction to software management (version control, testing, ...)

Part 2: (one week towards the end of the semester)
Each student gives a presentation on an assigned topic. They can choose between
- a paper (or book chapter) on aspects of software engineering
or
- a content (methodological) paper and its implementation in the form of pseudo code.
In addition, each student prepares a written summary (approx. 1-2 pages) of their presentation.

Part 3: (directly following part 2)
The students receive (as one team or several teams, depending on the number of participants) a programming task and have to implement it independently (incl. group organization).

OBJECTIVES:
After successful participation in the module Practical Software Development for Complex Simulation Environments in Engineering, students are able to name basic concepts of software development and apply them to engineering problems. Furthermore, they are able to develop numerical software with C++ and can apply methods and tools for version control, testing and software development in a team. The learned basic methods contribute to the development of the ability to formulate complex simulation questions in engineering problems and to solve them independently.

Title: Praktisches Deep Learning
Description:
CONTENT:
The lab course is a hands-on introduction to deep learning where students learn through experience fundamental deep learning algorithms. The topics covered are deep neural networks for regression and classification, convolutional networks, sequence modeling with recurrent nets and long short-term memory gates, dimensionality reduction techniques such as autoencoders, and deep generative methods, e.g., generative adversarial networks and variational autoencoders.

OBJECTIVES:
After participating in the module, the students

are knowledgeable in different deep learning algorithms and understand the major differences between them
can explain the basic concepts of training neural networks such as backpropagation, underfitting/overfitting, cross validation, regularization, early stopping, etc.
are able to use the machine learning package PyTorch to apply deep learning to real-world data sets
can design and suggest improvements to deep learning workflows

Title: Praktizierte Technik
Description:

In the seminar Practiced Techniques in Landscape Architecture, fundamental and special techniques of tree planting and tree care are taught in a short lecture series.

Subsequent practical exercises will link theory and practice and apply and deepen the gained knowledge.

OBJECTIVES:

The exhibition will be opened on the 12.03.2025.

Title: Präparative Chromatographie
Description:
CONTENT:
In dem angebotenen Chromatographie-Praktikum sollen die Grundlagen der chromatographischen Trennmethoden verstanden und angewandt werden. Im Vordergrund steht die präparative Aufreinigung eines rekombinanten Proteins mithilfe zweier Chromatographiemethoden. Hierfür werden verschiedene Materialien untersucht, Säulen gepackt, sowie statische und dynamische Bindekapazitäten bestimmt. Ebenso werden die Bilanzierung von Gesamt- und Teilprozessen erlernt. Gearbeitet wird unter anderem mit ÄKTA-Systemen, die auch in Industrie- und akademischen Forschungseinrichtungen häufig zum Einsatz kommen. Zusätzlich wird die Simulationssoftware DSPX genutzt, um die chromatographischen Teilprozesse zu simulieren und anzupassen.

OBJECTIVES:
Nach der Teilnahme am Praktikum Chromatographie sind die Studenten in der Lage:
- ÄKTA-Chromatographiesysteme zu bedienen.
- Statische und dynamische Bindekapazitäten zu bestimmen.
- Ein Scouting geeigneter Prozessbedingungen für die Chromatographie durchzuführen.
- Eine Säule zu packen und deren Güte zu bestimmen (HETP, Asymmetriefaktor).
- Bilanzen des Aufreinigungsprozess aufzustellen.
- Laboranalytische Methoden (BCA, SDS-PAGE) durchzuführen.
- Den Chromatographieprozess mithilfe DSPX zu modellieren.

Title: Präsentation und Diskussion innovativer Ansätze in der Gentechnologie
Description:
CONTENT:
Students are giving English presentations about a very recent (English) publication (dating max. one year back) in the field of gene technology with special attention to gene therapy and gene delivery.
The specific aims of the seminar are:
- to learn to read publications critically (regarding scientific conclusiveness, missing controls,...)
- to present data and background in a concise way (power point presentation)
- to learn to get involved into active discussion during general discussion
- to learn to receive and to deal with critical questions posed to the presenting person
Skills: ['Gene technology', 'Gene therapy', 'Gene delivery', 'Research-oriented mindset', 'Critical thinking and decision-making']

Title: Präsentation und Diskussion innovativer Ansätze in der Gentechnologie Hausarbeit
Description:
CONTENT:
Term paper
In contrast to the seminar, which deals with novel aspects of viral gene technology, the term paper will focus on basics supporting the understanding of techniques that were presented in the seminar.
With this respect an aspect of the paper presented during the seminar will be chosen and will be dealt with in detail (e.g. viral replication cycles, virion structure and organization, etc.). The elaboration will exceed the scientific background of the seminar presentation.
The instructor will choose the topic, to which students will perform literature research. 
The elaboration of the topic will in most cases be based on older literature.
Besides the elaboration the term paper will include a reference list and an explanation how the literature search was performed.

OBJECTIVES:
acquisition of background knowledge in basic viral gene technology

Title: Präsentation und Moderation
Description:

Title: Praxisworkshop Datenschutz für StartUps
Description:
CONTENT:
The seminar is aimed at student start-ups or students with the necessary entrepreneurial spirit. In the seminar, the basics and pitfalls of data protection law are taught in a practical manner and solutions tailored to the concrete needs and business ideas of the students are developed.

Organisational matters:
- The seminar is based on fortnightly dates for the theoretical introduction to the application of data protection law, a written presentation of the results of a data protection law audit of the respective start-up by the students and a block event in which the students can present their business models as well as the concrete implementation of the learned data protection law requirements and work through further data protection law problems in the discussion. The individual dates will probably be held in the period from October to December and the block event on a date in the period from mid-January to early February. The exact dates will be announced later.
- There will be no general preliminary discussion. Interested students are welcome to contact us to arrange an individual meeting date.

Content:
- In the seminar, we will deal with the topic of data protection law and privacy policy in a strongly application-oriented manner. The students will receive a basic introduction to the legal material, especially with regard to questions that regularly arise in smaller internet companies. 
- The students then examine their concrete application, project or (fictitious) business idea to determine which data protection challenges arise from this and how these could be overcome, summarise the results of the investigation in writing and also present the results as part of a block event.

Number of participants and application:
- The seminar is limited to a maximum of ten applications / projects. Several students can apply per application / project.
- Please apply by 15 September 2024 via email to office.elaw@sot.tum.de with the following information: (1) Description of the project, (2) In which phase is the project?, (3) Is there already experience with the topic of data protection law?

OBJECTIVES:
After participating in the module, students understand the basic concepts of data protection law, can relate these concepts to various concrete business models/applications and are familiar with initial approaches to processing personal data in a data protection-compliant manner.

Title: Principles of Economics
Description:
CONTENT:
This course provides an introduction to the basic concepts of economics. It is divided into two parts: micro- and macroeconomics. Microeconomics deals with the behavior of individual agents, such as households, firms, and public institutions and with their interaction on markets. How can market demand be derived from the consumption choices of households? How can market supply be derived from the production decisions of firms? Which mechanisms give rise to an equalization of demand and supply? What are the consequences of market failure, and what can the state do about it? Macroeconomics takes an aggregated perspective; it analyzes the economy as a whole. How can economic activity, inflation, and unemployment be measured? What are the factors that determine economic growth? Which mechanisms give rise to economic fluctuations, and how can these fluctuations be mitigated through fiscal and monetary policy?

Title: Private Equity
Description:
CONTENT:
The lecture has a scientific as well as a practical focus since recent scientific papers but also recent trends in the private equity industry will be discussed.
The topics covered in the lecture can be broadly divided into two sections. The first part gives an overview on the private equity industry and views private equity on a fund-level. This section will be rounded off by the guest lecture from Bain & Company. During the second part, private equity will be analyzed on a deal-level. Therefore, the entire investment process will be covered starting with the deal origination and ending with the harvest (exit) from the perspective of a private equity firm. Finally, a guest lecture by a private equity firm will give the students more practical insights.
During the first part, the tutorial will complement the lecture with in-class calculations, exercises and case studies. Afterwards a LBO model will be discussed in detail.

OBJECTIVES:
After this module students will understand the main characteristics of a private equity fund as well as differences between private equity and public equity. Additionally, they will be able to analyze a deal from the perspective of a private equity firm. Finally, students will be also able to set up an integrated LBO model.

Title: Probability Theory
Description:
CONTENT:
Based on measure and integration theory, in this course the fundamental concepts of probability theory are presented. Of central importance are the different types of convergence, the concept of stochastic independence, and conditional expectations. In addition, the course will deal with the Radon-Nikodym theorem, product spaces and the construction of stochastic processes. For sequences of independent random variables, laws of large numbers and the central limit theorem will be proved. As an important generalization of partial sums of independent random variables, martingales will be introduced and on this basis we will investigate stopping times and prove the martingale convergence theorem.

Title: Problemorientiertes Lernen in der Anwendung
Description:
CONTENT:
Anmeldung über VHB im Oktober!
Problembasiertes Lernen als Methode zur Aneignung flexibel nutzbaren Wissens, zur Entwicklung fächerüberschreitender Kompetenzen und Problemlösefähigkeit.

Die POL Methode (Methodik des 7-Sprunges):
1. Klären unbekannter Begriffe 
2. Themenfindung oder Problemdefinition 
3. Brainstorming zur Hypothesengenerierung 
4. Systematische Ordnung und Bewertung der Hypothesen 
5. Lernzielformulierung 
6. Recherche 
7. Synthese / Ergebnisse zusammen tragen.

Anwendung von POL anhand unterschiedlicher Beispiele aus der Krankheitslehre, um die verschiedenen Sichtweisen im Berufsfeld der Gesundheitswissenschaft zu erforschen.

OBJECTIVES:
Nach erfolgreicher Teilnahme am Modul sind die Studierenden in der Lage die Methode des POL (Siebensprung) zu verstehen und anzuwenden. Dadurch sind sie befähigt unterschiedliche  Sachverhalte aus unterschiedlichen Blickwinkeln zu betrachten und dabei Erkenntnisse aus der aktuellen Gesundheitsforschung zu berücksichtigen und auf den betreffenden Fall anzuwenden.

Title: Problemorientiertes Lernen
Description:
CONTENT:
Die Einschreibung für das Seminar erfolgt ausschließlich über die Virtuelle Hochschule Bayern (vhb) und startet am 01.10.2025.

Name des CLASSIC vhb-Kurses: Lösungsorientiertes Arbeiten und Feedback an Praxisbeispielen in Gesundheit und Pflege

Der Kurs wurde insbesondere für die Zielgruppe angehender (Fachschul-)Lehrkräfte in den Bereichen Gesundheit und Pflege entwickelt. Grundlage bildet der Lehr-Lern-Ansatz des Problemorientierten Lernens. Im Zentrum steht die Bearbeitung von Praxisbeispielen aus den Bereichen Gesundheit, Pflege, Medizin und Schule nach der Methode des Siebensprungs mit den für die Einzelarbeit adaptierten Arbeitsschritten:
1. Klärung unbekannter Begriffe
2. Problem bestimmen
3. Sammlung von Ideen und Lösungsansätzen
4. Systematische Zusammenfassung und Ordnen der Ideen
5. Lernziele formulieren
6. Informationen beschaffen (Recherche)

Title: Process Mining
Description:
CONTENT:
Process mining is a family of new data analysis methods that aims to discover, monitor, and improve business processes. It is increasingly adopted by industry. Process mining analyzes so-called event logs, which capture the real execution data of business processes and are usually collected from one or several information systems supporting their execution. The main difference to traditional data analysis techniques is that process mining explicitly focuses on the process perspective. It aims to reveal the complex order relations among the activities captured in the event log. 
This lecture introduces the field of process mining. After introducing basic formalisms, it provides a detailed and algorithmic perspective on the three key process mining perspectives: process discovery, conformance checking, and enhancement. Furthermore, it discusses how process mining projects are typically executed and how data is extracted. Finally, the lecture shows how process mining is currently used in industrial environments and advanced in process mining research (e.g., visual analytics and process mining).

OBJECTIVES:
After successfully completing this course, students will be able to:
* Explain the principles of process mining and its application area 
* Understand the structure of event logs (the basic input for process mining) and how it is built
* Explain and apply basic process mining algorithms for the different perspectives: discovery, conformance, and enhancement, and explain their strength and limitations
* Know different process mining tools/libraries and apply them to event logs
* Understand how to run a process mining project and explain the different phases and how it is applied in industrial settings
* Know advances in current process mining research

Title: Process Modeling and Control
Description:
CONTENT:
1.	Basics of Modeling: Balances of mass, mole amount, energy, and momentum; steady-state, quasi-steady-state and dynamic modeling
2.	Basics of Process Control: Terminology; input and output variables; steady-state and dynamic behavior of controlled systems; transfer behavior of controllers
3.	Flow Control: Control of liquid flows through inlet and outlet valves
4.	Stirred Tank Reactor: Steady-state and dynamic behavior of a stirred-tank reactor with liquid level control
5.	Controller Types: Mechanical controller as P controller, electric controller as I controller, combined PI controller
6.	Cascade Control: Dynamic and transfer behavior of two stirred-tank reactors with liquid level control in series
7.	Complex CSTR: Modelling of a stirred-tank reactor with temperature control; steady-state design and dynamic behavior; inclusion of chemical reaction
8.	Complex PFR: Modeling of a spatially discretized plug-flow reactor with temperature control and chemical reaction; steady-state design and dynamic behavior
The course further integrates reflection on one's own actions with regard to sustainable ecological and economic development at appropriate points through illustrative examples, thus promoting sensitivity and interdisciplinarity among students.

OBJECTIVES:
Upon successfully completing this module, students will be able to:
-	Identify the steady- state and dynamic behavior of controlled systems
-	Understand the distinction between P, I and D controllers and their combination with respect to their control behavior
-	Apply rules for PID controller tuning 
-	Analyze steady-state characteristics of controlled systems
-	Derive and numerically solve ordinary differential equations to model the dynamic behavior of a system
-	Create systematic solutions to complex control problems with MATLAB Simulink 
-	To consider the inseparable ecological and economic effects of their solutions and to apply the methods and knowledge learned with regard to sustainable ecological and economic development.
-	To practice professional discussion and collaboration in interdisciplinary teams
