Title: The Art of Inhabitation
Description:
CONTENT:
This course explores the design of urbanism and housing in the European city and beyond. The focus is in the design of buildings, interiors and urban spaces from strategy to detail. This is carried out in relation to given themes in a studio environment of discussion and dialogue.
The course will consider the complex ways in which the city can engender dignity on the part of the user. It will try to anticipate the consequences of design decisions in terms of an emotive response. It will seek a rigorous and conceptual understanding of construction.

Title: The Auditory System
The Craft and Art of Leadership
Description:
CONTENT:
This seminar gives students a deeper understanding of the essence, the content, and the function of leadership in organizations. Students will learn how leaders and leadership - both formal and informal - contribute to achieving goals on the individual, team and organizational level. The difference between the management of processes and leadership of people will also be discussed. The seminar will also focus on the influence of leadership on constructive and destructive team and organizational processes. In addition to the discussion of theoretical frameworks, real-world examples of leadership will be presented by the students and will highlight the connection between theory and practice.

OBJECTIVES:
After sucessful participation, students…
(1) understand the importance of leadership for organizational processes and outcomes.
(2) remember different approaches to management and leadership and can apply these to practical contexts.
(3) can analyze the leadership dynamics in teams and organizations.
(4) understand the development of leaders and leadership.

Title: The Dark Side of Entrepreneurship
Description:
CONTENT:
This seminar explores the dark side of entrepreneurship by analyzing cases in which entrepreneurial ventures crossed ethical or legal boundaries. Students will investigate how entrepreneurs can mobilize resources, build legitimacy, and scale businesses while engaging in deceptive, manipulative, or outright criminal behavior. By applying established entrepreneurship frameworks, such as opportunity recognition, resource acquisition, entrepreneurial identity, and institutional work, students will critically analyze these cases and develop counterstrategies for prevention.
Working in teams, students choose one real-world case to examine in depth. Examples could include:
- Elizabeth Holmes (Theranos): Leveraging narrative and social capital to legitimize a non-functional product.
- Travis Kalanick (Uber): Using aggressive market entry strategies to circumvent regulation and establish first-mover advantage.
- Adam Neumann (WeWork): vision-driven entrepreneurial storytelling masking governance and financial mismanagement.
- Anna Sorokin (Delvey): constructing an entrepreneurial identity to gain access to elite networks and capital without a viable venture.
The seminar enables students to explore instructive examples of how entrepreneurial activity can interact with and at times exploit societal blind spots, such as regulatory gaps, cultural narratives of success, or the celebration of disruptive innovation. In their final presentations, students propose prevention or intervention strategies, drawing on insights from frameworks from entrepreneurship theory, business ethics, and policy-making to address the societal conditions that enable unethical ventures to thrive.

OBJECTIVES:
After successful participation, students are able to:
1. Identify and analyze cases of unethical or criminal entrepreneurial behavior based on publicly available materials (e.g., media reports, documentaries).
2. Critically assess the structural, individual, and contextual factors that enabled the misconduct.
3. Reflect on the ethical dimensions of entrepreneurial decision-making and business model design.
4. Develop and justify potential counterstrategies or prevention measures at different levels (e.g., policy, law enforcement, education, organizational culture).
5. Work effectively in teams to synthesize diverse materials and viewpoints into a coherent analysis.
6. Communicate findings effectively in an oral presentation and engage constructively in academic discussion.

Title: The Entrepreneur's Playbook - Fallstudien von VCs und Gründern
Description:
CONTENT:
“The Entrepreneur’s Playbook” offers TUM students the opportunity to gain deep insights into the world of venture capital (VC) firms and entrepreneurship. The course is designed around direct interaction with successful investors and founders, combining theoretical knowledge with practical experience. It includes guest lectures, workshops, and project work. Students collaborate in interdisciplinary teams to develop learning decks, bridging practice and academia, and receive feedback from experienced VCs and entrepreneurs. The course concludes with a pitch session, where students present their work.

OBJECTIVES:
The combination of theoretical knowledge and practical application in The Entrepreneur's Playbook is designed to enhance students’ understanding of venture capital and entrepreneurship. The course aims to equip them with the skills and insights they need to navigate the start-up ecosystem successfully.

Title: The Ethics of Artificial Intelligence Applied to Security
Description:
CONTENT:
This course introduces students to the ethical and social problems of artificial intelligence, particularly when applied to the field of cybersecurity.

OBJECTIVES:
Knowledge and understanding: 
During the course, students will acquire knowledge about Artificial Intelligence (AI) and its functionalities with a focus on applications in cybersecurity. They will also comprehend the ethical and societal consequences of the widespread 
diffusion of AI. The course also provides the basis for understanding the functioning of 
biometric systems and their problems relating to individual privacy. Students will be able to identify and describe the concepts of bias, trust, fairness, explanation, equality and 
empowerment.

Judgement skills: 
The course will allow students to acquire the skills to be able to analyze and identify safety issues in various scenarios involving AI technology.

Communication skills: 
Regarding communication abilities students will become proficient in using AI related terminology within security and ethics contexts. This skill will enable them to convey ideas to both non-technical audiences. Additionally, they will learn how to present their research findings with effective and clear language. ⁤

Learning skills: 
The students will be able to independently deepen their knowledge of the latest research and developments in the field of ethics and security applied to artificial intelligence. The students will be able to learn new methods for the design and analysis of security technologies autonomously.

Title: The EuroTeQ Engineer
Description:
CONTENT:
The workshops take place on 3-4 days in the specified period, on Friday / Saturday, on Monday / Thursday /Wednesday or on Tuesday. 
Future engineers are required to coordinate interdisciplinary projects and to collaborate with specialists from other domains. Aside from professional know how, successful engineering in a European context requires excellent intercultural communication skills and competences. Having said that, what exactly are the ingredients for successful cooperation in multicultural settings? The workshops of the EuroTeQ Engineering University focus on the intercultural agility that is crucial for studying and working in a multicultural environment. 

These intercultural seminars are intended for students in all areas of engineering but are also open to all TUM students. Students who will, in the next academic year, spend time at a EuroTeQ partner university or are presently doing an exchange from one of these universities to the TUM are especially invited to register for this intercultural seminar.

OBJECTIVES:
Together we will explore in this course how our mind set, values, attitudes and personal background shape the way in which we interact with others. We will find ways to widen our perception and change our perspective. 

After this seminar, you will have practical tools at your disposal to experience and analyse complex intercultural situations from a point of curiosity and openness and you will be well on your way to develop the cultural agility that is required in today’s engineering world.

Title: The Munich Entrepreneurial Ecosystem
Description:
CONTENT:
An entrepreneurial ecosystem refers to the interconnected network of individuals, organizations, institutions, and resources that collectively support entrepreneurship and innovation within a specific geographic region or industry. These ecosystems provide an environment where entrepreneurs can start, grow, and sustain their ventures through access to various forms of support, including funding, mentorship, talent, infrastructure, and market opportunities. 
Understanding how entrepreneurial ecosystems function is vital for entrepreneurs, policymakers, investors, and other stakeholders as it facilitates opportunity recognition, resource mobilization, network building, innovation, collaboration, policy advocacy, and adaptation to change, ultimately fostering vibrant and sustainable entrepreneurial communities. In this course, students will learn what constitutes an entrepreneurial ecosystem and how entrepreneurial ecosystems contribute to supporting founders and founding teams. In various site visits, they will get to know different ecosystem participants such as VCs, business angels, industrial companies that work with start-ups, entrepreneurial support organizations such as incubators or accelerators or makerspaces. Students will gain an understanding of the interaction between the various participants in the start-up ecosystem and understand the entrepreneurial journey using Munich as an example.

OBJECTIVES:
After successful participation, students are able to:
- understand how an entrepreneurial ecosystem is structured
- understand and describe the perspectives and goals of individual participants in the ecosystem
- understand what the entrepreneurial journey of a founder (team) through the ecosystem can look like

Students learn to work together in a team, present convincingly, discuss and reflect.

Title: The Psychology of Teamwork
Description:
CONTENT:
This seminar is offered either as part of the Introduction to Psychology and Human Behavior module for M.Sc. Data and Society students or as an elective plug-in open to all TUM students. It examines psychological theories and perspectives that shape organizational life—how work teams and groups form, develop, and perform. The seminar also covers motivation and behavior at work, including managerial perspectives, and shows how these theories inform core organizational processes.

The seminar will take place in a face-to-face format in Room 269 (2nd Floor) at the Marsstraße 20-22 TUM Campus at the following dates:

Thursday, October 16, 13:00-16:30 (kick-off session)
Thursday, October 30, 10:00-15:00 
Thursday, November 06, 09:00-13:30 
Thursday, November 13, 10:00-15:00

OBJECTIVES:
The seminar consists of a kick-off session and three 5-hour blocks, each with its own learning objective. Students will explore classic and emerging topics in organizational psychology and behavior; read, analyze, and synthesize key texts; debate ideas in reflective class discussions; and apply concepts to real-world contexts through activities and presentations. The overarching objective is for students to understand how psychological factors shape organizational processes at both the individual and team levels.

Title: The Science of Creativity
Description:
CONTENT:
Creativity has shaped the world we live in and is often considered unique to humans. We have been able to transform cities, make art, and develop new technologies that extend our lifespan and contribute to our well-being. Encouraging creativity is a crucial success factor in organizations as original and useful ideas are key to their long-term success. The study of creativity is interdisciplinary and requires analysis at multiple levels.
 
This course has theoretical and practical implications for students. They will learn about creativity from psychology and management research fields. Simultaneously, they will (a) foster critical thinking by presenting and discussing scientific articles and (b) develop and implement activities that evaluate and boost the creativity of themselves and others at the workplace and in day-to-day life. In this course, students will be encouraged to generate ideas that tell how improving individuals' skills such as creativity can help address current leadership, entrepreneurship, and management problems.

OBJECTIVES:
Students will 

•	...understand what creativity is.
•	...understand different perspectives on the study of creativity.
•	...understand relevant concepts from psychology, neuroscience and management theories, which relate to creativity and discuss their applicability to the issue at hand.
•	...name methods used to evaluate creativity.
•	...generate ideas how developing creativity and other individuals' skills can help to address current problems in leadership, entrepreneurship and management.
•	...develop and implement activities that improve creativity in management contexts and how to address them to specific groups. 
•	...learn to present scientific papers in a clear, consistent, and attractive manner. 
•	...adopt a critical stand towards scientific articles and presentations.

Title: The Social Life of Chemicals
Description:
CONTENT:
Anthropogenic chemicals are pervasive in modern everyday life. In this seminar, we will deal with social scientific research that investigates this situation as a consequence of the entanglement of (academic) chemistry research and the chemical industry. Particularly, we will discuss how chemicals enter the world through economic markets, how they permeate, inhabit and constitute our bodies, social relations and ecologies, how they are shaped by legal modes of regulation and political decision-making, and how their effects can and cannot be rendered visible by scientific experts. Moreover, we will ask whether and how an alternative chemistry might look like and what our roles as scholars and scientists in such a process might be. 
These questions seem to be of urgent importance in times of the Anthropocene, where the planetary boundaries of the Earth are alarmingly exceeded by the circulation of chemicals, and where increasing prevalences of non-communicable diseases – that seem to correlate with the presence of chemicals in our modern ways of living – are posing serious threats to individual, public and planetary health.

OBJECTIVES:
The seminar intends to foster intensive discussions of scholarly texts based on your reading, written reflections, presentations and active participation. Thereby, you will (1) reflect about the role and responsibility of chemistry in our current societies from social scientific and interdisciplinary perspectives; (2) understand how studying chemicals and chemistry relates to discussions about materiality, the divide between nature and culture as well as sustainability in Science and Technology Studies; (3) practice academic writing on which you will receive valuable (peer) feedback, and (4) improve your reading, discussing, presenting and feedbacking skills.
Skills: ['Sociology', 'Science and technology studies', 'Environmental sociology', 'Chemical industry', 'Social impact']

Title: Theorie und Praxis der Wirtschaftspädagogik und -didaktik
Description:
CONTENT:

OBJECTIVES:
Auf Grundlage des aktuellen Berufsbildungsberichts lernen die Studierenden Chancen und Herausforderungen der dualen Ausbildung aus verschiedenen Blickwinkeln (Arbeitgeber, Berufsschule, Auszubildender) kennen. Die Studierenden diskutieren aktuelle bildungspolitische Maßnahmen und sind in der Lage die berufliche Bildung mit ihren Bildungszielen und Herausforderungen zu definieren. 
Die Teilnehmer arbeiten mit aktuellen Lehrplänen/Lehrplanrichtlinien, leiten Kompetenzbereiche ab und erarbeiten konkrete handlungsorientierte Lernarrangements, die auf umfassende Kompetenzentwicklung abzielen. Sie sind in der Lage auf Grundlage von ausgewählten didaktischen Theorien/Modellen eine Unterrichtsplanung vorzunehmen und zu reflektieren. Möglichkeiten und Grenzen der ausgewählten didaktischen Modelle werden diskutiert. Sie können theoretische Merkmale und unterrichtspraktische Bestimmungsgrößen für handlungsorientiertes Lernen beschreiben. Sie benennen Vorteile und Probleme dieses Unterrichtskonzepts bewerten diese. Insgesamt erfassen die Studierenden die Kennzeichen lernförderlichen und aktivierenden Unterricht und sind sich deren Relevanz für das duale Berufsbildungssystem bewusst. Die Studierenden sind in der Lage zu reflektieren, welche Rolle die Professionalität der Lehrkraft im Unterricht und bei dessen Planung und Reflexion spielt.

Title: Theorie und Praxis der Zukunftsforschung
Description:
CONTENT:
Zukunft betrifft jeden von uns. Aber was wissen wir von der Zukunft? Was kann man überhaupt wissen? Wie kann man zukünftige Situationen beeinflussen? Um Zukunft zu gestalten, müssen Unwägbarkeiten und Nichtwissen bewältigt werden.
Zunächst werden die Teilnehmer/innen mit einem geisteswissenschaftlichen / philosophischen Blick auf das Zukunftsthema vertraut gemacht – wie geht man also mit dem Paradox um: handeln und entscheiden zu müssen ohne über (ausreichendes) Zukunftswissen zu verfügen?
Darüber hinaus vermitteln Experten aus Wissenschaft und Industrie Praxiswissen im Spannungsfeld Zukunft und zum Umgang mit Zukunftswissen, Unsicherheit und Nichtwissen.
Abschließend werden aus den vermittelten Beispielen und den vorgestellten Konzepten Verfahrensregeln und Anleitungen für das Handeln von Individuen im Alltag und Institutionen/Unternehmen unter Bedingungen der Ungewissheit und des Nichtwissens abgeleitet.

Dr. Ulf Pillkahn ist Professor für Technologie- und Innovationsmanagement an der FOM Hochschule. Zuvor bei der Siemens AG im Bereich Corporate Foresight beschäftigt. Ursprünglich Ingenieur für Elektro-  und Informationstechnik, danach MBA und Promotion in Psychologie an der LMU, Masterstudium Wissenschafts- und Technikphilosophie an der TUM

OBJECTIVES:
Nach der Teilnahme an den Modulveranstaltungen sind die Studierenden in der Lage:
- verschiedene Formen von Zukunftsaussagen zu erfassen und deren Wert zu diskutieren
- Kreation von Zukunftswissen in Situationen die durch Ungewissheit und Unsicherheit geprägt sind. 
- Verschiedene Formen von Zukunftswissen zu differenzieren, in der Praxis zu identifizieren und in verschiedenen Kontexten anzuwenden 
- Regeln zur Orientierung und das Handeln trotz Ungewissheit zu nennen.

Title: Thermische Verfahrenstechnik 1
Description:
CONTENT:
This module will teach the thermodynamic and enineering basics of thermal separation processes. Essential contents are: thermodynamics of one-component systems and mixtures with special focus on equilibrium states (chemical equilibrium and phase equilibrium) - practical calculation of gas-liquid-equilibrium (flash-calculation) - phase diagrams of ideal and non-ideal mixtures -distillation processes (open and closed) - rectification processes (binary mixtures) - tray columns - rectification and mass transfer in packed columns.

OBJECTIVES:
After participating in this module the students are capable of analysing and applying thermodynamic models for one-component systems and mixtures. Based on that the students can evaluate and apply the design basics to the thermal separation processes distillation and rectification. Furthermore, the students are capable of understanding the basic principles of the most important thermal separation processes and the column types which are used in process industry.

Title: Thermische Verfahrenstechnik 2
Description:
CONTENT:
The course should deepen und broaden the engineering fundamentals of the thermal separation principles on the basis of the module Thermal Separation Principles I. Essential contents are: absorption and desorption - evaporation - crystallisation - drying - extraction - adsorption.

OBJECTIVES:
After participating in this module students are able to evaluate and to apply the design basics on the following thermal processes: absorption and desorption, evaporation, crystallisation, drying, extraction and adsorption. Furthermore, the students are capable of understanding the basic principles of the most important thermal separation processes and equipment which are used in process industry.

Title: Thermodynamics II
Description:
CONTENT:
The contents of the new Thermodynamics II lectures are:
1) Review of TD1 and outline of TD2,
– Recap: 1st law, 2nd law and applications for different cycles
2) Gas mixtures:
– Composition,
– p-v-T diagrams,
– Properties.
3) Gas-vapor mixtures:
– Specific and relative humidity of air,
– Humid air properties,
– Processes in Air-conditioning (HVAC).
4) Heat transfer processes:
– Basic heat transfer modes,
– Simplified heat transfer consideration in engineering systems.
5) Chemical reactions:
– Ideal and actual combustion processes,
– Enthalpy of formation and combustion,
– First law analysis of a reacting systems,
– Adiabatic flame temperature,
– Entropy change of reacting systems,
– Second law analysis of reacting systems.
6) Chemical and phase equilibrium:
– Criterion of chemical equilibrium,
– Equilibrium for ideal gases,
– Chemical equilibrium for simultaneous reactions,
– Phase equilibrium.
7) Compressible flow:
– Mach number, Stagnation properties ,
– One-dimensional, isentropic flow,
– Shock wave and expansion wave,
– Duct flow with heat transfer.
8) Renewable energies:
– Energy and environmental technologies overview,
– Solar energy,
– Wind energy,
– Geothermal, hydrothermal, biomass,
– Energy storage systems.

OBJECTIVES:
The aim of the course is to advance the knowledge gained from the Thermodynamics I lectures by a few new aspects:
1) towards non-equilibrium and more realistic conditions,
2) towards the consideration of Heat Transfer, Chemical Reactions, and Compressible Flow, and
3) towards applications in aerospace and energy engineering.

Title: Thermodynamics in Energy Conversion
Description:
CONTENT:
This course covers the fundamentals of engineering thermodynamics, with a focus on energy systems. It introduces the basic concepts of thermodynamics and then expands to the application of thermodynamic principles to energy systems and their components. These include gas turbines, steam turbines, steam generators, fuel cells, combustion systems, heat exchangers and refrigeration systems. The concept of exergy, the maximum theoretical net work that can be derived from an amount of energy or an energy flow, is also introduced and applied to the aforementioned systems. Overall, the course should provide the fundamental knowledge for further lectures such as "Thermal Power Plants" and provide an overview of how thermodynamic principles can be applied for the analysis and design of energy systems.

OBJECTIVES:
Goals: Understanding thermodynamics laws and principles and their application. Understanding the thermodynamic function of state of the art energy systems and their components. Understanding the concept of exergy and its application to energy systems. The ability to perform thermodynamic calculations of energy systems.

Title: Thinking, Imagining, and Making Future Environments
Description:
CONTENT:
What can critical environmental thinking contribute to our efforts to understand environmental change? How can we use methodological and theoretical tools from STS and the Environmental Humanities to think more clearly about environmental complexity, dynamic systems, and the diversity of life? 

This seminar explores research and analytical strategies for understanding the social dimensions of environmental change. It draws from the case examples presented by an interdisciplinary group of research practitioners in order to explore contrasts and complementarities in the ways that the natural sciences, social sciences, and humanities approach key environmental questions. Through a weekly series of lectures and seminar discussions, we will grapple with core topics related to environmental sustainability, climate change, and our planetary future. 

The course meets twice weekly: once for lectures and once for a focused seminar discussion. It is conducted in collaboration with the Chair in Environmental Humanities at LMU, opening opportunities for expanding our interdisciplinary conversations and collaborations.

OBJECTIVES:
The course will enhance students’ environmental literacy and open-up multiple perspectives on environments of the past, present, and future.
Skills: ['Research-oriented mindset', 'Critical thinking and decision-making', 'Environmental impact assessment', 'Analytical thinking and structured problem solving', 'Clear technical and non-technical communication']

In doing so, they cooperatively solve challenges that arise from constraints from the different disciplines. They generate suitable market hypotheses and product ideas at an early stage and interact with initial potential customers/users. They iteratively create prototypes and evaluate their hypotheses with them in experiments.
 
For more information, visit www.tms.tum.de.

• examine the relevance of a problem and develop a solution collaboratively in an interdisciplinary team 
• design a prototype based on the acquired design methods and analyzed insights
• lay the foundation for one's own business start-up by identifying a start-up idea or team.

Title: Tierernährung
Description:
CONTENT:
The lecture consists of two consecutive blocks of equal relevance:

1) Basics of nutrition physiology in agricultural livestock animals
Description and analysis of nutrients in the feeds; nutrient digestion in monogastrics and ruminants; metabolism of carbohydrates, lipids, and proteins - basics of energy metabolism and energy evaluation - function and requirement of minerals, trace elements, and vitamins

2) Practical livestock nutrition
Establishing basic concepts to feed agricultural livestock during growth and reproduction (gravidity – lactation; egg formation); quantitative derivation of nutrient requirements; transformation into feeding concepts applicable in practice and environmentally compatible; control of product quality through feeding:
   Pigs for fattening, sows for breeding, piglets
   Poultry (basic aspects)
   Steers for fattening, dairy cows, calves, heifers

OBJECTIVES:
At the end of the lesson students have acquired an understanding of physiological principles of digestion and metabolism of nutrients in order to apply it in practical situations of feeding agricultural livestock. On base of this knowledge students are able to evaluate the animals’ requirements according to their performance for energy and nutrients and to create adequate feeding strategies. Furthermore, students may judge feeding strategies in in view of product quality and environmental compatibility.

Title: Topics in Linear Algebra
Description:
CONTENT:
Generell behandelt Topics in Linear Algebra (CH4502) in Grundzügen alle Teilbereiche der LInearen Algebra und einige spezielle anvancierte Themen aus der Matrix-Analysis.  
Einzelne Inhalte sind:

1. Grundlagen: Lineare Abbildungen über Vektorräumen; Kern und Bild von Homomorphismen; Erzeugendensysteme, Basen; Determinanten; elementare Umformungen von Gleichungssystemen und ihren Matrix-Darstellungen; Dreiecksformen; Inverse einer linearen Abbildung; Normalformen und Diagonal-Darstellungen.

2. Lösbarkeit (und Lösungen) homogener und inhomogener lin. Gleichungssysteme: Abhängigkeit vom Rang; Angabe vollständiger Lösungsmengen (und Bezug zu Vektorräumen im homogenen Fall); Beziehung zwischen Lösungsmengen inhomogener Gleichungssysteme und denen ihrer Homogenisierung. 

3. Eigenwertprobleme:  Unterschiede zwischen Typen von Matrizen (allgemein, normal, hermitsch, unitär, orthogonal, symmetrisch etc); Normalformen; Familien kommutierender Matrizen und ihre simultanen Eigendarstellungen.

4. Singulärwert-Zerlegung (SVD) als Verallgemeinerung der Eigenwert-Zerlegung. Ausblick auf Anwendungen in der Bildverarbeitung, Principle-Component Analyse (PCA) etc.

5. Matrix-Gleichungen: Tensorprodukte und Superoperator-Darstellungen (im Liouville Raum), Anwendung der gelernten Methoden an konkreten Beispielen, z.B. bei der Stabilitäts- und Symmetrie-Analyse dynamischer Systeme.

OBJECTIVES:
Nach der Teilnahme am Modul Topics in Linear Algebra verstehen die Studierenden 
(1) die Grundlagen von linearen Abbildungen, 
(2) homogene und inhomogene lineare Gleichungssysteme und ihre Lösbarkeit, 
(3) den Umgang mit Eigenwertproblemen, 
(4) Familien kommutierender Matrizen von unterschiedlichem Typ und schliesslich 
(5) die Lösung von Matrix-Gleichungen im Superoperator-Formalismus.

Title: Tour de France der Philosophen. Einführung in das philosophische Denken
Description:
CONTENT:
Guillaume Martin gehört zu den besten Radrennfahrern der Welt. Und er ist Philosoph. In »Sokrates auf dem Rennrad« schickt Martin die bedeutendsten Denker der Geschichte in das größte Radrennen der Welt: die Tour de France. Da ist Sartre, der als Teamchef der Franzosen seine Fahrer ermutigt, sich nicht im Peloton zu verstecken. Da ist Marx, der sich um die ungerechte Verteilung der Prämien sorgt. Da ist Kant, der schlucken muss, als er erfährt, dass das Rennen nicht in seinem geliebten Königsberg stattfindet… 
Eigenes Erleben des Profis, das einen Blick hinter die Kulissen des realen Radsportzirkus gewährt, wird mit grundlegenden philosophischen Fragestellungen in einem fiktiven Kampf um das gelbe Trikot verwoben. 
Mit dieser einführenden Veranstaltung in die Philosophie sollen sowohl Radrennenthusiast: innen als auch werdende Philosoph: innen angesprochen werden. Wer Sartre für einen Radrennfahrer hält oder Wout van Art für einen Philosophen sollte sich deshalb jedoch nicht ausgeschlossen fühlen. „Niemand wird als Radsportsportler oder Philosoph geboren, oder als Radsportler-Philosoph; man muss es werden.“ wie Martin sagt, und „[…] trotz des strengen Habitus mit dem sich Philosophie manchmal umgibt, ist sie auch [wie der Radrennsport] eine Form des Spiels.“ 
Anhand des Textes von Guillaume Martin wollen wir uns mit ausgewählten philosophischen Problemen und den damit verbundenen Argumenten auseinandersetzen. Dabei sollen u.a. folgende Themen behandelt werden:  
• Unterscheidung von Körper und Geist (Körper-Geist-Problem) 
• Ockhams Rasiermesser 
• Das aristotelische Argument der Irreduzibilität des Guten 
• Die Pascal'sche Wette

OBJECTIVES:
Nach der Teilnahme erlernen Studierenden folgende Kompetenzen:
a. Argumente interpretieren: Studierende erkennen und verstehen philosophische Argumente.
b. Argumente evaluieren: Studierende evaluieren die Stichhaltigkeit und Gültigkeit von Argumenten.
c. Argumente entwickeln: Studierende entwickeln eigene Argumente und formulieren sie klar und überzeugend.

Title: Tractor Engineering Fundamentals
Description:
CONTENT:
The lecture gives a broad insight into the design fundamentals of modern tractors and emphasizes a high practical relevance. It deals with the historical development in tractor construction and shows functions and application limits of the machines. Both the overall concept and the individual components are covered. Economical aspects are discussed, general principles of product planning and project management are presented by using tractors as an example. The outer and inner mechanics of the whole vehicle are explained and the gear concepts including their design/dimensioning are dealt with. The design of typical drive elements, aspects between human beings and machinery (environmental factors, basics of industrial medicine, noise reduction) and the basics of tractor hydraulics including methods of industrial tests are explained and their use is shown by giving examples.
Theoretical engineering fundamentals (e.g. gearbox calculations, tyre selection, steering geometry, power and traction requirements and ergonomic design principles for the driver) are applied in exercises, by calculation with formulas and equations with provided data sets.

OBJECTIVES:
After participating in the module courses, students are able 
-	to understand the tractor environment and market and know the development process of tractors.
-	to analyse individual components such as diesel engines, transmissions and axles, brakes and hydraulic systems and to demonstrate their functionality. 
-	to describe the requirements for technical solutions for tractors, which arise due to the special relationship in professional mobile machinery.
-	to adapt on the basic principles of integrity of operation, ergonomics and process control for tractors.
-	to solve basic problems in designing tractor details using known mathematical and physical models.

Title: Traffic Impacts, Evaluation of Transport and Logisic Processes
Description:
CONTENT:
A. Transport and Air Pollution Air pollution in different parts of the world, sources of emission and health / environmental effects of Lead, Sulphur dioxide, Carbon monoxide, Volatile organic hydrocarbons, Nitrogen oxides, Particulate Matter and Ozone
B. Vehicle Emissions Standards How is emission standards measured? What kind of emission standards exist worldwide? Emission reduction with catalytic converters, Vehicle CO2-emission / fuel economy regulations in the world
C. Noise Definition of sound and noise, health effects of noise, noise mitigation
D. Consumption of energy Worldwide energy consumption till now and future development of energy consumption
E. Climate change / Kyoto Protocol Types of greenhouse gases and emission sources, effects of greenhouse gases, ways of greenhouse gases emission stabilization, Kyoto-Protocol
F. External cost of transport / internalization methods What are “external costs of transport”, examples for external costs of transport, amount of external costs in Western Europe, How should we deal with external costs of transport?
G. Sustainable transport What does sustainable development mean – introduction of the concept, definition of a sustainable transportation system, consequences for sustainable transportation policies / some German objectives
H. Why do we need assessment methods? – Introduction: Elements of assessment methods, target system / indicators / aggregation
I. Cost-benefit analysis (CBA) Flowchart / elements of a CBA, indicators included into a CBA, monetarisation of indicators, discounting and sensitivity analysis, exercise: Cost-benefit analysis (CBA)
J. Multi criteria analysis (MCA) Multi criteria analysis (first generation): flowchart, conversion of the original values into utility values, weighting, aggregation, Multi criteria analysis (second generation): relevance tree, preference matrix, exercise: multi criteria analysis (MCA) and assessment of urban effects
K. Balancing and Discussion Method Principle of this method and examples
L. Other Assessment Methods Ranking, Compatibility Assessment, Elimination method, Cost – Efficiency –Analyse, Combination of different methods
M. Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) 
Aims and objectives of an EIA, limitations of EIA, common EIA processes

OBJECTIVES:
Transportation systems, as a rule, strongly contribute to the overall emission of a country and consume considerable amounts of natural resources. Furthermore, transportation systems influence the quality of human lives. This module will introduce the interrelation between transport and the environment. Moreover, this module will represent the concept of a sustainable transportation system. Some strategies for archiving such sustainable transportation system will be worked out and discussed with the students. The second part of this module introduces the basic principles and concepts of an assessment and evaluation of transport and logistics systems. The assets and drawbacks of different assessment methods (Cost-benefit analysis, Multi criteria analysis, Balancing and Discussion Method, Environmental Impact Assessment, Ranking, Cost – Efficiency – Analyse etc.) will be introduced, including application areas and initial constraints of specific assessment procedures will be discussed.

Title: Translationale Onkologie
Description:
CONTENT:
This is a 3 ECTS lecture about topics in Translational Oncology given in English only.
Translational Oncology is an interdisciplinary field that focuses on transferring scientific discoveries in cancer research into clinical applications. This course provides an overview of the latest advancements in translational cancer research and their relevance for improving cancer diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis, with a specific focus on childhood cancer.
The lectures will cover fundamental molecular and cellular mechanisms of tumor development as well as modern therapeutic approaches. A particular focus will be on targeted therapies, immuno-oncology, and innovative preclinical model systems. This includes adoptive cell therapies, immune modulation, oncolytic viruses, and novel strategies to overcome tumor-induced immune tolerance. Additionally, an overview of preclinical tumor models, including animal models, iPSC-based systems, and organoids, will be provided, as they play a crucial role in the development of new therapeutic agents.
Another key aspect of the course is genetic cancer predisposition, modern screening strategies, and personalized oncology, particularly through the use of genomic and immunological biomarkers. Furthermore, recent advances in hematopoiesis, immunotherapy, and the interaction between cancer cells and the immune system will be discussed.
Finally, participants will be introduced to a potential career path in biomedical research, with discussions on the challenges and opportunities of pursuing a career at the interface of research and clinical translation. The goal of the course is to provide a comprehensive understanding of the translational process in oncology and to highlight future directions in the field.

OBJECTIVES:
Understanding the basic properties of cancer cells
Mechanisms of tumor development and progression
Fundamentals of translational research in oncology
Importance of multi-omics approaches for personalized cancer therapies
Role of hematopoietic stem cells in cancer development
Concepts of immune surveillance and immune tolerance
Advantages and disadvantages of different preclinical models for cancer research
Genetic factors and hereditary cancer risks
Basics of immunotherapy against cancer
Basics of gene editing with CRISPR-Cas9
Applications for the modification of cancer genes
How CAR-T and transgenic TCR therapies work
Importance of the tumor microenvironment for cancer growth
Mechanisms of immunogenic cell death and their therapeutic relevance
Principles of oncolytic virus therapy
Development and use of cancer vaccines

Title: Tribology Technologies for Sustainable Drivetrains
Description:
CONTENT:
Tribology is an interdisciplinary science. In drivetrains, it concerns friction, lubrication and wear of interacting surfaces in relative motion in machine elements like gears and bearings. Approx. 23 % of the world’s energy consumption results from tribological contacts. Out of this, up to approx. 40 % can be saved by implementing new technologies complying with the principles of green tribology.
The number of publications on tribology increases from year to year. Many different research fields like classical tribology, green tribology, biotribology or nanotribology are related to various trends like vehicle electrification, multiscale modelling, machine learning and superlubricity (ultra-low friction).
This interactive seminar addresses the ability to distinguish relevant from non-relevant information of scientific publications and to grasp and summarize the essentials quickly. The ability is trained by studying recent tribology technologies and its impact on the sustainability of drivetrains. The seminar also prepares for writing student theses and scientific publications.
The following contents will be covered in the module:
• Basics of tribology and drivetrains
• Sustainable development aspects
• Selected tribology technologies
• Circle of research and publication structure
• Searching and reading scientific publications
• Writing and reviewing scientific publications

OBJECTIVES:
After participating in the module, students will be able to
• remember tribology technologies for drivetrains,
• discuss its impact on environmental sustainability,
• understand circle of research and publication structures,
• analyze scientific literature and create key statements efficiently,
• evaluate recent tribology technology independently regarding energy efficiency, environmental sustainability and technology readiness
• present and discuss scientific results,
• work in a team of one’s own discipline but also beyond that in interdisciplinary teams,
• justify one's own decisions and to convince with arguments.

Title: Trustworthy Distributed Learning
Description:
CONTENT:
This course explains the recently introduced federated learning setting and its multiple challenges. It will focus on data privacy, robustness against malicious client attacks, and the challenge of reducing the communication cost. The course will give an overview of the setting of decentralized learning and some of its challenges. A deep study of the recent machine learning algorithms and their fundamental properties, used to guarantee privacy, robustness, and communication efficiency, will be carried out.

More precisely, the course covers the following topics
- An introduction to distributed learning in its centralized, federated, and decentralized forms and the respective challenges arising.
- Basics of machine learning algorithms: gradient descent, stochastic gradient descent, linear and logistic regression, and basic neural network architecture
- Data privacy in distributed learning and the main tools to guarantee privacy, e.g., information-theoretic privacy through secret sharing and differential privacy.
- Schemes ensuring information-theoretic privacy in federated learning, their advantages and shortcomings.
- Combination of information-theoretic privacy and differential privacy in federated learning.
- Malicious client attacks in federated learning: known attacks and defense mechanisms.
- Designing robust federated learning schemes.
- Joint privacy and robustness in federated learning: challenges and schemes achieving them.
- Communication cost and model/gradient compression.
- A primer on decentralized learning and the challenges arising.
- An overview of schemes allowing robust and private decentralized learning and open problems for future research.
- A semester-long project requiring the students to implement state-of-the-art machine learning algorithms of their choice (fine-tuning LLMs, CNN, gradient descent ...) and making them privacy-preserving and or robust against attacks, and test the change in performance

OBJECTIVES:
Upon successful completion of the course, the students will be able to:

- Identify the challenges of modern distributed learning systems and tackle them using tools from coding theory and distributed learning literature
- Understand the challenges of federated and decentralized learning systems
- Analyze and assess the privacy and performance guarantees of methods applied to privacy-preserving distributed learning
- Analyze and assess the robustness and performance guarantees of methods applied to federated learning challenged by state-of-the-art malicious attacks
- Design privacy-preserving and robust federated and decentralized learning methods
- Understand how to reduce the communication cost of distributed learning
- Implement state-of-the-art algorithms explained in a research paper of the students' choice (ICML, NeurIPS, ICLR...), produce their own observations, and critically analyze the findings of the paper
- Prepare and present a poster (or a paper) within the standards of international conferences/workshops

Should the student decide to engage in a follow-up Master thesis (some topics will be offered by the lecturer), this will be an opportunity to get familiar with the world of scientific research.

Title: TUM Climate Ventures

CONTENT:
Building climate ventures that have impact can be a very complex and demanding challenge. Often this requires an expanded skillset of how to identify, assess, analyze, design, build, and launch climate-tech ventures, as well as high team effort, and very strong leadership. In addition, dynamic markets, technological uncertainties and grand challenges create additional pressures on novel ventures understanding their impact. This module provides a holistic view of the climate venture process in a real-world project. It introduces you to theories, concepts, and frameworks for climate ventures. Students will gain hands-on experience in the startup process, learning how to identify, assess, analyze, design, build, and launch climate-tech ventures.

Emphasis will be placed on effective collaboration within interdisciplinary teams to tackle real-world climate challenges. The course will help students build a strong climate-tech network and community, providing opportunities for collaboration and support. Students will work on creating new companies aimed at addressing high-impact climate problems, from ideation to market entry.

Exploration of breakthrough technologies and their potential applications in solving global climate issues will be a key component of the course. Students will understand the fundamentals of economic and technical evaluations specific to the climate-tech industry. The course will teach customer-centric approaches to developing climate solutions, emphasizing the importance of understanding and addressing customer needs.

Das Modul startet mit einem Kickoff-Termin (Einführung in das Modul und erste konkrete Projektideen vorstellen) und zwei einführenden Workshops: Projektmanagement und Teamkommunikation in der Praxis. Gearbeitet wird, soweit möglich, anhand bereits vorliegender konkreter studentischer Projektideen einzeln oder im Team.

Darauf aufbauend planen die Modul-TeilnehmerInnen ein eigenständiges Projekt und führen es im Laufe des Semesters durch. Dabei stehen ihnen MentorInnen zur Seite. Nach Projektabschluss ist der Projektbericht in Form eines Lernportfolios bei der Carl von Linde-Akademie einzureichen. Außerdem wird das Projekt mit einer kurzen Präsentation in der Abschlussveranstaltung vor den anderen Teilnehmern vorgestellt. 

Inhalte
- Grundprinzipien der Kommunikation in einem Team und der Führung und Motivation eines Teams
- Grundlagen der Projektorganisation (Planung,  Durchführung und kritischen Evaluation)

Die spezifischen Inhalte hängen vom gewählten Projekt ab, wie Planung eines Seminarwochenendes, Leitung eines Arbeitskreises oder Organisation eines Events, z.B. die „Langen Nacht der Uni“.

OBJECTIVES:
Nach der Teilnahme an dem Modul 
- kennen die Studierenden die Grundprinzipien der Organisation von Projekten und sind befähigt, diese anzuwenden, indem sie Projekte mit Unterstützung durch eine/n MentorIn effektiv organisieren und durchführen.
- können die Studierenden Projektmanagement-Abläufe kritisch reflektieren und evaluieren.
- kennen die Studierenden die Grundprinzipien der Führung und Motivation von Teams und können sie anwenden.
Skills: ['Project planning and prioritization', 'Team leadership and mentoring', 'Clear technical and non-technical communication', 'Teamwork']

Title: TUMpaedagogicum Einführung Berufliche Bildung
Description:
CONTENT:

Die darauf aufbauenden Veranstaltungen werden in Seminarform wöchentlich angeboten. Siehe weitere Lehrveranstaltungen "TUMpaedagogicum Vorbereitungsseminar"

Title: TUMpaedagogicum I
Description:
CONTENT:
This module is mandatory for the following module TUMpaed II. It contains a 10-day internship at one of the TUM Referenzgymnasien (between 1st and 2nd semester), which is pedagogically, didactically and methodically supplemented by a kick-off meeting (1st semester) and a wrap-up meeting (2nd semester).

OBJECTIVES:
This module provides the opportunity to gain first vocational experience and to reflect one’s choice of profession.

Title: TUMpaedagogicum IIa
Description:
CONTENT:
This module is based upon the module TUMpaed I. Topics are classroom observation, introduction into lesson planning and sampled teaching methods, coping with classroom interferences and conflicts, as well as relevant aspects of school laws and specific demands of the teaching profession.

OBJECTIVES:
The goal of this module is to prepare practical education. By participating in TUMpaed II, students attain basic skills in the topics mentioned above.
Skills: ['Clear technical and non-technical communication', 'Pedagogy', 'Lesson planning', 'Conflict resolution']

Title: TUM.wood Lecture Series
Description:
CONTENT:
The lecture series provides a comprehensive overview of the interrelationships of the entire wood value chain. This holistic approach beyond the boundaries of the individual disciplines deepens the understanding of the ecological, economic, socio-cultural and technical aspects of the topic "Building with Wood".

OBJECTIVES:
The lecture series provides an overview of the interconnections within the entire wood value chain. TUM.wood’s holistic, interdisciplinary approach aims to deepen the understanding of the ecological, economic, sociocultural, and technical aspects of building with wood. The lecture is designed for students from various disciplines who work with wood across the value chain, fostering interdisciplinary exchange and collaboration
Skills: ['Environmental impact assessment', 'Life cycle assessment', 'Ecological aspects', 'Economic aspects', 'Socio-cultural aspects']

Title: Turing Berechenbarkeit für Kommunikationsnetze und Informationstheorie
Description:
CONTENT:
Ziel der Vorlesung ist es, die Teilnehmer an die Turing Berechenbarkeit und deren Anwendung für die Berechnung von Kommunikationsnetzen heranzuführen - ein Forschungsgebiet, welches sich insbesondere in den letzten Jahren rasant entwickelt und etabliert hat. Die Turing Berechenbarkeit liefert das stärkste Modell für Simulationen, die auf einer perfekten digitalen Hardware implementiert werden kann. Sie liefert damit auch die Grundlage für Software Defined Networking (SDN) und Network Function Virtualization (NFV). Neben einer grundsätzlichen Einführung in die Turing Berechenbarkeit und Gödelschen Theorie der rekursiven Funktionen werden weitergehende Zusammenhänge zu SDN und NFV und fundamentale Grenzen für SDN und NFV vermittelt.

OBJECTIVES:
Nach dem erfolgreichen Abschluss des Moduls ist der Student mit den Grundlagen der Turing Berechenbarkeit vertraut. Er kann auch die behandelten Algorithmen in der Entwicklung bzw. im Entwurf von SDN- und NFV-Systemen einsetzen.

Title: Türkisch - Kommunikation A2
Description:
CONTENT:
In diesem Modul steht die mündliche Kommunikation in der Fremdsprache Türkisch im Vordergrund. Es werden Kenntnisse vermittelt, die es den Studierenden ermöglichen, im einfachen Kontext, d. h. in verschiedenen alltäglichen Situationen und zu Themen von allgemeinem Interesse zusammenhängend und verständlich zu kommunizieren. 
Dabei wird ein Spektrum an Vokabular, Redewendungen und Dialogmustern erarbeitet; interkulturelle und landeskundliche Aspekte berücksichtigt; Schwerpunkte der Grammatik gemäß der Niveaustufe (insbesondere die Tempus-Formen Präsens, Präteritum und Futur sowie Nebensatzkonstellationen) wiederholt bzw. vertieft und gefestigt. Die aktive Mitarbeit der Studierenden wird erwartet und gefördert.

OBJECTIVES:
Nach Abschluss des Moduls können die Studierenden auf A2-Niveau sich an leichteren Gesprächen im Alltag beteiligen bzw. einfach und zusammenhängend in alltäglichen Kommunikationssituationen verstehbar reagieren und Ansichten kurz begründen oder erklären, sofern sie in klarer Standardsprache vorgetragen werden und die Thematik vertraut ist.

Title: Türkisch A1.1
Description:
CONTENT:
Nach ersten Einblicken in die Beschaffenheit/Spezifität der Sprache  (Agglutination, Vokalharmonie, Satzbau, Fehlen des grammatischen Ge-schlechts) werden in diesem Modul Grundkenntnisse der Fremdsprache Türkisch vermittelt, die den Studierenden ermöglichen, sich in alltäglichen Grundsituationen zurechtzufinden. Dabei werden interkulturelle und landeskundliche Aspekte mit einbezogen. Die Studierenden ler-nen/üben einfach strukturierte Hauptsätze zu formulieren  und im bestimmten Präsens zu erzählen. Zum Beispiel: Angaben  zur eigenen Biografie zu machen oder zur Biografie einer Person Fragen zu stellen und zu beantworten, bezogen auf Namen, momentanes Befinden, Herkunft, Nationalität, Familienstand, Alter, Wohnort, Arbeitsplatz, Studium, Sprachen, Beruf; Zahlen zu verstehen und zu benutzen. Dazu werden entsprechende, hierfür notwendige grammatikalische Themen behandelt. Es werden Strategien vermittelt, die eine Verständigung trotz noch geringer Sprachkenntnisse (in alltäglichen Grundsituationen) ermöglichen.

OBJECTIVES:
Dieses Modul orientiert sich am Niveau „A 1 Elementare Sprachverwendung“ des GER. Nach der Teilnahme an der Modulveranstaltung sind die Studierenden in der Lage, vertraute alltägliche Ausdrücke und sehr einfache Sätze zu verstehen und zu verwenden, die auf die Befriedigung konkreter, in der Bewältigung des Alltags wesentlicher Bedürfnisse zielen. Er/sie kann sich und andere vorstellen, anderen Leuten Fragen zu ihrer Person stellen und auf Fragen dieser Art Antwort geben. Der/die Studierende kann sich auf einfache Art verständigen, wenn die Ge-sprächspartnerinnen  oder Gesprächspartner langsam und deutlich sprechen und bereit sind zu helfen.

Title: Türkisch A1.2
Description:
CONTENT:
Aufbauend auf die Spezifität der Sprache  und unter Einbeziehung der fortdauernden Modernisierung der türkischen Sprache (Sprachreform Atatürks und Europäisierung des Wortschatzes) werden in diesem Modul erweiterte Grundkenntnisse der Fremdsprache Türkisch vermittelt, die den Studierenden ermöglichen, sich in alltäglichen Grundsituationen zurechtzufinden. Dabei werden interkulturelle und landeskundliche Aspekte mit einbezogen. Die Studierenden lernen/üben einfach strukturierte Sätze in Präsens und Vergangenheit zu formulieren und zu verstehen. Die Angaben zur eigenen Lebensgeschichte und zu anderen Personen erweitern sich um die Themen Einkauf, Bezahlen, Bedarf, Kleidung, Benutzung von Verkehrsmitteln, Bestellung im Café, Vorlieben,   Lern-motivation, Fremdsprachenkenntnisse. Dazu werden entsprechende, hierfür notwendige grammatikalische Themen behandelt. Schwerpunkt des Moduls ist die sichere Verwendung von Dativ, Akkusativ, Lokativ und Ablativ. Es werden Strategien vermittelt, die eine Verständigung trotz einfacher Sprachkenntnisse (in alltäglichen Grundsituationen) er-möglichen und das Hörverstehen der Agglutinationen schulen.

OBJECTIVES:
Dieses Modul orientiert sich am Niveau „A 1 Elementare Sprachverwendung“ des GER. Nach der Teilnahme an der Modulveranstaltung sind die Studierenden in der Lage, vertraute alltägliche Ausdrücke, Redewendungen und einfache Sätze zu verstehen und zu verwenden. Dabei han-delt es sich um grundlegende, kurze Informationen zu alltäglichen oder Studien- bzw. berufsrelevanten Fragen und vertrauten Tätigkeiten und Themen.  Er/sie kann sich und andere vorstellen, anderen Leuten Fragen zu ihrer Person stellen und auf Fragen dieser Art Antwort geben. Der/die Studierende kann sich auf einfache Art verständigen, wenn die Ge-sprächspartnerinnen  oder Gesprächspartner langsam und deutlich sprechen.

Title: Türkisch A2.1
Description:
CONTENT:
Aufbauend auf den Grundkenntnissen aus A1 und unter Einbeziehung interkultureller und landeskundlicher Aspekte und der fortdauernden Modernisierung der türkischen Sprache werden in diesem Modul das Hörverstehen trainiert und vertieft und die Verflüssigung der Ausdrucksfähigkeit im aktiven Sprechen gefördert. Der Übungsschwerpunkt liegt in der richtigen Auswahl und Anreihung der Agglutinationen, der Endungsanalyse beim Hören und Lesen von Informationen. Die Studierenden lernen/üben Sätze im Präsens (Şimdiki Zaman), Perfekt (dili Geçmiş Zaman) und Futur (Gelecek Zaman) zu formulieren und zu verstehen. Die Angaben zur eigenen Lebensgeschichte und zu anderen Personen erweitern sich um die Themen Familie und Freundeskreis, Kindheit, Uhrzeit und Tagesablauf, Jahreskreis und zeitliche Orientierung, Reisen und Briefe/Postkarten schreiben. Dazu werden entsprechende, hierfür notwendige grammatikalische Themen behandelt. Schwerpunkt des Moduls ist die sichere Verwendung von Genitiv und Possessiv und den Genitiv-Possessiv-Verbindungen in allen 6 Fällen.

OBJECTIVES:
Diese LV orientiert sich am Niveau „A2 - Elementare Sprachverwendung“ des GER. Nach der Teilnahme an der Lehrveranstaltung sind die Studierenden in der Lage, vertraute Sätze und Redewendungen zu einem erweiterten Spektrum an Themen zu verstehen. Dabei handelt es sich um grundlegende Informationen zu alltäglichen oder Studien- bzw. berufsrelevanten Themen. Die Lernenden erfassen die Bedeutung von klaren und deutlich artikulierten Mitteilungen. Der Austausch von Informationen erfolgt kurz, aber mühelos zu vertrauten Tätigkeiten und Themen.  Der/die Studierende ist in der Lage mithilfe feststehender Wendungen kurze, informative Texte oder Mitteilungen zu verfassen.

Title: Tutor Academy
Description:
CONTENT:
The Tutor Academy is a course designed to train student assistants to teach a successful tutorial. In addition, student teachers (tutors) are often expected to support instructors in the preparation and implementation of online teaching and have access to relevant training modules. The course is fully online, with optional in-person workshops shortly before the start of the semester. Both employed student assistants, as well as unemployed students, can join the Tutor Academy.

OBJECTIVES:
Upon completion of the Tutor Academy, students will be able to 
(1) reflect on and describe their role as a tutor.
(2) describe learning theories and principles.
(3) apply learning theories and principles in the design of course content and to their teaching practice.
(4) visualise and present content to their own students in an accessible way.
(5) deescalate conflicts that may arise between students and tutors and among students.

CONTENT:
The lab course spans from the theory of propeller and rotor performance modeling to the design and testing of a real propeller.

Title: Überblick über die Vegetationszonen der Erde
Description:
CONTENT:
Die globale Vegetationsgliederung wird beschrieben inklusive der sie steuernden klimatischen, edaphischen und anthropogenen Faktoren. Dazu gehören die Vegetationszonen der Tropen und Subtropen, der gemäßigten Breiten sowie der arktischen Gebiete und Gebirge. Dabei werden jeweils kennzeichnende Pflanzenarten, wesentliche ökologische Prozesse, biologische Ressourcen sowie Möglichkeiten und Grenzen ihrer Nutzung dargestellt.

Diese Veranstaltung findet zeitgleich mit der Vorlesung "Vegetation der Erde" satt. Details siehe dort.. Teilnehmer der "Vegetation der Tropen und Subtropen" müssen nur den allgemeinen Teil der Vorlesung besuchen, der die jeweils ersten beiden Stunden umfasst.

Die Vorlesung findet im aktuellen Semester online statt.

Title: Überfachliche Grundlage
Description:
CONTENT:
Participants in this course can choose from three different projects: Hacker School, ReDi, and TUM LearnLabs. Participants inspire school students with programming courses at a basic level. Through small programs and games, they give young people insights into digital topics, strengthen their IT skills, and share their passion for their chosen field of study. Participants work in teams and independently supervise young people in a school class. They improve their communication skills on IT topics with young people who have no IT experience, apply presentation techniques, practice moderation skills, and train their creativity in new situations. The course instructors prepare participants for their assignments with tried-and-tested, didactically sound concepts for programming courses in different languages and topics, such as Scratch, HTML, Python, Bash, and Swift.

OBJECTIVES:
Upon successful completion of the module, participants will be able to:
- Communicate enthusiasm for computer science
- Communicate basic programming skills to people with no IT experience
- Apply digital presentation techniques and online facilitation methods
- Communicate with, collaborate with, and meet the individual needs of people who are not familiar with IT
- Provide self-efficacy to young people as role model
- Teach the importance of basic IT skills, digital literacy, and media literacy
- Pass on the importance of creativity and critical thinking as well as a positive culture of making mistakes

Title: Umfeldsensorik für automatisiertes Fahren
Description:
CONTENT:
Einführung: Basisinformationen zum automatisiertem Fahren, aktuelle Radar- und Lidar Sensorsysteme, Grundbegriffe der Umfeldwahrnehmung, Koordinatensysteme.
Grundlagen: Das elektromagnetische Spektrum, Modelle der Wellenausbreitung, Signale im Zeit- und Frequenzbereich. 
Das Radar- bzw. Lidarziel: Radarprinzip, Radargleichung, Zielmodellierung, Radarrückstreuquerschnitt, Lidar-Reflektivität, Zieldetektion.
Abstandmessung durch Pulsradar und Puls-Lidar: Funktionsprinzip, praktische Umsetzung, Auflösung, Meßgenauigkeit.
Geschwindigkeitsmessung:  Dopplereffekt, Mischer als Schlüsselbaugruppe, Dauerstrich-Dopplerradar, Auflösung, Meßgenauigkeit.
FMCW-Radar: Kombinierte Messung von Abstand- und Geschwindigkeit beim frequenzmodulierten Dauerstrichradar, Auflösung, Meßgenauigkeit.
Winkelmessung: Hertz'scher Dipol und Apertursythese, Antennensysteme,  winkelselektive Antennen, winkelselektive Signalverarbeitung, abtastendende und bildgebende Lidarsysteme.
Systementwurf: Systemdefinition, Komponentendefinition, Technologien, elektrische und mechanische Systemintegration.
Zieldatenverarbeitung: Rohdatenverarbeitung, Zielverfolgung, Objektbildung und -klassifizierung, Datenfusion, Kalman-Filter.

OBJECTIVES:
Nach dem erfolgreichen Abschluss des Moduls hat der Studierende folgende Kenntnisse:
- Grundlegende theoretische Kenntnisse über Radar- und Lidarsensoren
- Kenntnis der Anwendungsmöglichkeiten für diese Sensoren, auch im Vergleich zu kamerabasierten Systemen
- Entscheidungskompetenz hinsichtlich der in Radar- und Lidarsensoren zu Einsatz kommenden Verfahren
- Fertigkeiten zum Entwurf der Hard- und Softwarekomponenten
Skills: ['Radar technology', 'Lidar technology', 'Sensor technology', 'Automated driving', 'Signal processing', 'Electromagnetic spectrum']

Title: Umweltgerechter Gartenbau
Description:
CONTENT:
Bedarfsgerechte Mineralstoffversorgung gärtnerischer Freilandkulturen und resourcenschonende Düngungstrategien; Charakterisierung und Düngung von gärtnerischen Erden und Substraten auf der Basis von Torfen und Torfersatzstoffen; Beurteilung des Ernährungszustandes von Pflanzenbeständen. Title: Umweltsoziologie
Description:
CONTENT:
Umweltsoziologie untersucht, welche Beziehungen Gesellschaft(en) zur natürlichen Umwelt ein-gehen. Ihr Anspruch ist dabei, einen Beitrag zur Aufklärung und Lösung von Umweltproblemen zu leisten. Das Seminar führt in das soziologische Denken anhand von Themen und Fragestellungen aus der Umweltsoziologie ein. Es werden verschiedene umweltsoziologische Theorieansätze behandelt und auf umweltbezogene Handlungsfelder angewendet. Dies sind Landwirtschaft, Energie, Mobilität und Klimawandel. Weiterhin werden Positionen in der Umwelt- und Nachhaltigkeitsdebatte behandelt sowie Studien zu Umweltbewusstsein und umweltbewusstem Alltagshandeln durchgenommen.

Title: Unsupervised Data Mining in Automation and Information Technology
Description:
CONTENT:
The aim of the lecture “Unsupervised Data Mining in Automation and Information Technology” is to provide an overview of established methods as well as current research topics and practical applications of unsupervised data mining methods in engineering and design. The lecture itself addresses the following aspects:
- Introduction of different archetypes of unsupervised data mining methods (e.g. hierarchical or density-based clustering methods)
- Unsupervised data mining methods in the context of high-dimensional feature spaces (e.g. subspace clustering methods)
- The treatment of unsupervised data mining methods in a high-velocity context (e.g. clustering on streams)
- Discussion of the underlying assumptions, the strengths and limitations of the methods as well as the similarities and differences between different methods
- The analysis of different parameter settings of the methods, as well as the challenge of evaluating results in an unsupervised setting

OBJECTIVES:
After participating in the module, students will be able to
1) explain basic characteristics and terminology in the context of unsupervised data mining
2) name and discuss characteristics such as strengths and limitations of unsupervised data mining methods for research and practice based on typical use cases.
3) understand the basics of conceptualizing, implementing and evaluating unsupervised data mining methods.

Title: Unternehmensexzellenz durch Strategie, Führung und Prozesse
Description:
CONTENT:
This lecture will present methods, procedures, and metrics for measuring and assessing business excellence (e.g. according to the EFQM model). This will be illustrated by case studies. Building on that, a way to achieving business excellence will be discussed.
On the example of automotive production, relevant fields of action of business excellence and their practical implications are presented.
The following topics will be dealt with:
- quality management
- processes
- leadership
- values and business excellence

OBJECTIVES:
After participating in the lecture the students are able to apply and explain the methods and procedures of Business Excellence for case studies.
They will able to identify and explain the main characteristics of a successful business excellence model: systemic, writable, holistic, sustainable and process-oriented character.
They can identify the essential core elements of managerial action and, in a holistic corporate management model, assess selected organizations with regard to their holistic entrepreneurial approach.

Sie können den Human-Relations-Ansatz erklären und andere Theorien veranschaulichen. Title: Unterricht und Schule entwickeln - Unterrichtsqualitätsentwicklung
Description:
CONTENT:
Qualitätsmanagement an beruflichen Schulen - QmbS
Qualitätsrahmen: Personalentwicklung, Schulentwicklung, Unterrichtsentwicklung, Organisationsentwicklung
QmbS Grundlagen

-	Praxisbeispiele
Unterrichtsentwicklung als Teil von QmbS
-	Medienentwicklung / Digitale Bildung
-	Individualfeedback
Evaluationsinstrumente

OBJECTIVES:
Die Studierenden können die grundlegenden Begriffe und Zusammenhänge sowie die theoretische Modellierung eines ganzheitlichen Qualitätsmanagements an Schulen erläutern. Sie können wesentlichen Ziele, Fragestellungen und Methoden der Qualitätsentwicklung des Unterrichts und der Schulentwicklung benennen und erklären.
Die Studierenden können die theoretische Modellierung eines Qualitätsmanagements an beruflichen Schulen auf ihre Einsatzschule übertragen und die dort vorhandenen Maßnahmen der Schul- und Unterrichtsentwicklung theoretisch reflektieren. 
Die Studierenden können geeignete Verfahren und Instrumente eines Qualitätsmanagements beschreiben und hinsichtlich ihrer Eignung und ihrer Grenzen einschätzen.
Die Studierenden können einen Qualitätsmanagementprozess im Bereich des Individualfeedbacks in ihrem eigenen Unterricht durchführen und dafür geeignete Verfahren und Instrumente heranziehen.
Die Studierenden entwickeln eine Sensibilität und Bedeutungsbeimessung für Aufgaben der Unterrichts- und Schulentwicklung. Ihnen ist die Bedeutung einer kontinuierlichen Qualitätsentwicklung des Unterrichts und Schulentwicklung bewusst.

Title: Unterrichtsplanung im Staatsexamen Mathematikdidaktik
Description:
CONTENT:
Das Seminar baut auf den theoretischen Grundlagen auf, die die Studierenden in vorangegangenen fachdidaktischen und fachlichen Veranstaltungen erworben haben. Im Mittelpunkt steht die Anwendung dieses Wissens und die Erweiterung um das schulbezogene Fachwissen. Die Studierenden wenden dieses Wissen integriert an, um fachlich fundierte und fachdidaktisch begründete Unterrichtseinheiten zu entwickeln, wie dies etwa im schriftlichen Staatsexamen, aber auch im künftigen Referendariat, gefordert wird. Durch die Entwicklung und Überarbeitung eigener Unterrichtspläne schärfen die Studierenden ihr Bewusstsein für fachliche und didaktische Herausforderungen und erproben gleichzeitig Methoden, um diesen effizient zu begegnen. Inhaltlich beziehen sich die Unterrichtseinheiten auf alle schulrelevanten Themen (Algebra, Zahlen, Funktionen, Geometrie, Stochastik). Dabei wird insbesondere der Aufbau der Schulmathematik vom höheren Standpunkt reflektiert.

OBJECTIVES:
In Ergänzung zu früheren Modulen, in denen die Studierenden erste Unterrichtsskizzen erstellten, liegt der Fokus dieses Seminars darauf, fachliche Inhalte und fachdidaktische Überlegungen in Einklang zu bringen und Unterrichtseinheiten effizient zu planen. Nach Abschluss des Seminars sind die Studierenden in der Lage, das erworbene schulbezogene Fachwissen mit ihrem fachdidaktischen Wissen und ihrem Fachwissen zu integrieren und anzuwenden. Sie nutzen ihr integriertes Wissen, um Unterrichtsentwürfe zu konkreten Themen auf Basis fachdidaktischer und fachlicher Inhalte Analysen zu erstellen. Sie können komplexe mathematische Inhalte in didaktisch angemessener Weise für Schülerinnen und Schüler aufbereiten und dabei sowohl die fachliche Präzision als auch die didaktische Zugänglichkeit gewährleisten. Zudem können sie fundierte Begründungen für ihre methodischen und inhaltlichen Entscheidungen geben.

Title: Urban Theory
Description:
CONTENT:
1. Block 1: What is urbanization? 
This block unpacks the fundamentals of urban theory as a canon. It describes the production of space as a philosophical stance (e.g. Henri Lefebvre). It also includes debates on the “rural” vs. the “urban” conceptualizing urbanization as more than rural-to-urban migration, but rather, as a process of transformation. 
2. Block 2: Global perspectives
This block describes the epistemology of an urbanism grounded in postcolonial perspectives from the Global South and/or East. 
3. Block 3: Methodological Advances
This block engages with alternative and cutting-edge methods in urban research, and new practices in deriving urban theory.

OBJECTIVES:
After successful participation in the module, students are able to:
-	1. Grasp the political, economic, and social processes that underlie the production of the built environment and define what is “sustainable.” 
-	2. Gain familiarity with cutting-edge textual material (e.g. journal articles) in urban theory that shed light into globally and locally interconnected urbanization processes.
-	3. Understand cities and regions as the key sites in which these challenges are staked, resulting in an uneven landscape of resources and opportunities.
-	4. Discuss the responsibility of academics and practitioners to confront climate change, uneven development, migration, economic crises, and social conflicts.
-	5. Become familiar with transdisciplinary engagement and methods for translating scientific knowledge into urban and architectural design and/or policy and governance strategies. 
-	6. Present these reflections and create a “safe space” in which to moderate discussions on these topics with their peers.

Title: Urban Waters in Sustainable Urban Developments and Infrastructure
Description:
CONTENT:
Following the positive experiences with creative interdisciplinary project work in the previous course TUM.stadt, this seminar will also focus on the independent development of freely chosen study projects on the topic of water in urban space. The students will be supported by external supervisors. 

The main steps of the seminar are
- Problem identification with self-organized group formation
- Problem definition
- Development of a solution approach
- Elaboration of the solution approach -> definition of the study project
- Internal presentation and discussion of the study project
- Revision of the study project
- Public presentation of the study project

The seminar is structured as follows:

1. introduction
- Water as a medium of sustainable architecture, urban and landscape planning
- Fields of activity  
- Method of “Design Thinking”
- Networking with experts
- Group formation

2. definition of the study project
- Collaborative development of an initial solution approach
- Elaboration of the solution approach taking into account the NASL lectures
- Internal presentation
- Revision in exchange with the external experts

3. results of the study project
- Elaboration of the results
- If applicable, choice of publication medium (poster/podcast/video) (optional -> 0.3 grade upgrade)
- Elaboration of the presentation
- Elaboration of the report

4. final presentation (dissemination)
- project-based presentations and, if wanted delivery a publication media in form of a  Poster/Podcast/Video
- synopsis of all group results

OBJECTIVES:
After completing the seminar, students will be able to
- recognize and understand the importance of water as a connecting medium for the basic functions of the city in terms of supply, energy and quality of life.
- recognize the importance of water as a natural hazard and know planning measures to reduce or prevent it.
- know and apply the methods of creative, collaborative and interdisciplinary planning.
- examine and evaluate the sustainability of the study project in its overall context.
- work out the resulting study project in concrete terms.
- discuss, reinterpret and, if necessary, revise it in collaboration with experts.
- be able to present and defend it in a presentation.
- be able to present it to the public using a chosen medium.
- be able to describe it in the form of a short report.
Skills: ['Urban water management', 'Sustainable urban development', 'Infrastructure', 'Project management', 'Interdisciplinary studies']

Title: Value Chain Economics
Description:
CONTENT:
The course covers the economics of value chains with a focus the agro-food sector. 
The course provides an overview of the institutional framework in which the EU agro-food sector operates, and covers trends in and challenges to the functioning and performance of the agro-food sectors in the EU, USA and developing countries. The course covers economic models and conceptual frameworks required to analyse the economic effects of various challenges posed by globalization, climate change, growing consumer demand for quality and sustainable products, market power and the imbalance of power within the supply chain. The course introduces students to the EU industrial policy for the agro-food sector and discusses market-based and non-market based solutions to improve the functioning and performance of the agro-food sector, including food labelling and production, processing, and distribution standards, formal and informal coordination and alignment of incentives among different actors of the supply chain.

OBJECTIVES:
After successfully completing the module, students will be able to perform an independent analysis of a value chain. This entails being able to:
(1) describe the main actors, their interactions and the structure of the value chain
(2) describe the institutional environment and the relevant industrial policies 
(3) assess the performance of the value chain and the distribution of generated welfare along the value chain by applying economic models and conceptual frameworks 
(4) assess the effect of the institutional environment (including industrial policies) on the functioning and performance of the value chain by applying economic models and conceptual frameworks
(5) find suitable market-based and non-market based solutions to improve the functioning and performance of the value chain by applying economic models and conceptual frameworks
(6) present in oral form the analysis of a value chain 
(7) draw up a written report of the analysis of a value chain
